`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing to Aleph0

Aleph0 is a research hypervisor: low-level, mostly `unsafe` Rust that runs in
VMX root operation, where a mistake hangs or resets the machine instead of
printing an error. These guidelines keep changes small, explained and
verified. [README.md](README.md) covers building and running;
[ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) says what is done and what comes next.

## Before you start

- Check [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). Work that follows the next open item is the
  easiest to review and merge.
- For anything larger than a fix or a small refactor (a new exit, a change to
  the VMCS setup, the EPT layout or the exit-handler flow), open an issue first
  and describe the approach.
- Read the `docs/` page for the area you touch. Each one explains the
  mechanism the code implements, often with the Intel SDM references the code
  relies on.

## Setup

- Rust stable, edition 2024. `rust-toolchain.toml` installs the
  `x86_64-unknown-uefi` target.
- The host tests need a host target. `cargo test-host` is an alias for
  `cargo test --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; on Linux or macOS, pass your
  own host triple instead, for example
  `cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
- Running the hypervisor itself needs an Intel CPU with VT-x and a VMM that
  exposes nested virtualization. Hyper-V is the tested path (see
  [Verifying on Hyper-V](#verifying-on-hyper-v)).

## Checks before every pull request

```powershell
cargo build                                            # the .efi
cargo test-host                                        # host unit tests
cargo fmt --all --check                                # rustfmt.toml: 120 columns, both packages
cargo clippy                                           # lints for the UEFI build
cargo clippy --features test-guest                     # lints for the regression mode
cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --tests   # lints for the tests
cargo clippy -p ebs-harness                            # lints for the ExitBootServices harness
cargo clippy -p ebs-harness --features set-virtual-address-map
cargo test -p ebs-harness --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc            # its host tests
cargo clippy -p ebs-harness --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --tests  # lints for them
```

All of them must pass without warnings. Use your host triple instead of
`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` on Linux or macOS. The harness (`tools/ebs-harness`)
is the workspace's second package; Cargo commands without `-p` act on Aleph0
alone.

## Code conventions

### `unsafe`

- `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` is on. Every `unsafe` block has a
  `// SAFETY:` comment that says why it is sound here, not what it does.
- Every `unsafe fn` has a `# Safety` section listing what its callers must
  guarantee (for example "VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS current").
- Keep `unsafe` blocks as small as the operation that needs them.

### Separate deciding from doing

Code that executes VMX instructions or touches hardware cannot be unit-tested.
Keep it thin, and put the logic in pure functions that can be:

- The exit handler reads, judges and applies (`src/vmx/vmexit/handler.rs`).
  The judgement, `exit_decision::decide`, is a pure function of the exit
  fields and the handler's state, and is host-tested.
- Decoding and encoding of raw values (RFLAGS, descriptors, control MSRs, EPT
  entries, interruption info) live in pure functions or types with tests.

A new exit or feature should follow the same split: a pure decision with host
tests, and a small `unsafe` part that only carries it out.

### Types and constants

- Give raw hardware values their own types (`EptEntry`, `Eptp`,
  `InterruptionInfo`, `ControlCapability`, ...) instead of passing `u64`
  around, and make invalid combinations impossible to construct where it is
  practical (for example `EptEntry<L>` has only the constructors valid at
  level `L`).
- Define each architectural constant once, with a doc comment naming the bit,
  field or MSR and what it means. Cite the Intel SDM when the reason for a
  check is not obvious.

### Exit context

The VM-exit handler runs with interrupts off, on its own stack, and must keep
working after `ExitBootServices`. In code reachable from it:

- no firmware calls: print with `serial_println!` (or `log!`, which skips the
  console once the handler has set the `VmExit` output phase), never with
  `uefi::println!`;
- no allocation: the crate has no allocator, and the exit handler must not
  call UEFI to get memory;
- no panics on guest-controlled input: an unexpected exit stops the guest
  through the normal stop path instead.

### Style

- `rustfmt` with the repository's `rustfmt.toml` (120 columns).
- Comments explain why, and the hardware behaviour the code depends on. Match
  the comment density of the surrounding code.
- Prefer clear names over abbreviations, except for the SDM's own names
  (`VMCS`, `EPTP`, `GPA`, `CPL`, ...).

## Tests

Unit tests live in `tests/unit/`, which mirrors `src/`: the tests for
`src/vmx/paging.rs` are in `tests/unit/vmx/paging.rs`. Each source file includes its
tests with

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../tests/unit/vmx/ept.rs"]
mod tests;
```

so the tests are a child module that can reach private items, and none of
them ends up in the `.efi`.

Add tests for every pure function you add or change. Name tests after the
behaviour they check (`map_end_past_one_pdpt_is_refused`), not after the
function.

## Verifying on Hyper-V

Host tests cannot prove that VM entry succeeds or that an exit behaves as
planned. A change that affects what runs in VMX operation needs a boot:

```powershell
# From an elevated PowerShell session.
.\scripts\run-hyperv.ps1 -ProcessorCount 1   # the firmware, virtualized in place
.\scripts\run-hyperv.ps1 -TestGuest          # the test guest: the regression mode
.\scripts\run-hyperv.ps1 -InjectNmi          # the test guest, with NMI reinjection
.\scripts\run-hyperv.ps1 -Harness -ProcessorCount 1   # the ExitBootServices harness
```

A default build virtualizes the running firmware: Aleph0 returns to it in
VMX non-root operation, and it runs until an exit Aleph0 does not handle,
which halts after the stop's report. The test guest (Cargo feature
`test-guest`) runs a fixed script, then teardown, and returns `SUCCESS`, so
its exits can be compared run by run. A change to VM exits is checked in
both modes.

VM-exit diagnostics appear only on serial (the PowerShell window and
`run\serial.log`). Put the relevant serial lines in the pull request, and
record what was observed in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) the way existing entries
do: the values printed, not just "it worked".

QEMU with OVMF (`.\scripts\run.ps1`) has no nested VMX. It only exercises the
code that runs before VMXON; say so if that is all a change was tested with.

## Documentation

Update the documentation in the same pull request as the code:

- [README.md](README.md): the summary of what Aleph0 does and the Layout table,
  when files or behaviour change;
- [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md): check items off, with what was observed;
- `docs/`: the page for the mechanism you changed, or a new page for a new
  mechanism, linked from the README's Layout table.

## Commits

- One logical change per commit. Keep behaviour-preserving refactors in
  separate commits (or pull requests) from behaviour changes.
- Subject line in the imperative, capitalized, without a trailing period, for
  example `Emulate RDMSR and WRMSR of intercepted MSRs`.
- Use the body, when needed, for why the change is made and anything a reviewer
  would otherwise have to work out.

## Pull requests

- Branch from `master` and keep the pull request focused on one change.
- In the description, say what changed, why, and how it was verified: which of
  the checks above ran, and the serial output of a Hyper-V boot when the change
  runs in VMX operation.
- Address review comments with new commits; do not rewrite history that a
  reviewer has already seen.

## Scope

The end goal is anti-cheat research (see [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), section 6).
Contributions must stay within that: research only, no deployment against
third-party services, and nothing whose purpose is to evade or defeat
anti-cheat or other security software.

## License

Aleph0 is dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option. Unless you
explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for
inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be
dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

```

`Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "aleph0hypervisor"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"

# The ExitBootServices test harness, its own EFI application
# (docs/RESIDENT.md): `cargo build -p ebs-harness`. Cargo commands run at the
# root still act on Aleph0 alone.
[workspace]
members = ["tools/ebs-harness"]

[dependencies]
uefi = "0.40"

# Switches for the Hyper-V runner (`-Features`, `-TestGuest`); all are off by
# default. A default build virtualizes the running firmware in place.
[features]
# Run the built-in test guest instead: the regression mode, with its scripted
# VMCALLs, teardown and the return to firmware outside VMX operation.
test-guest = []
# The exit handler reads a non-canonical address at the first exit, so the
# host IDT's #GP handler prints the fault and halts.
host-fault-test = []
# The exit handler waits in root operation after main VMCALL #1, so the
# `-InjectNmi` NMI reaches the host NMI handler instead of the guest.
host-nmi-test = ["test-guest"]
# At the first exit under Hyper-V, forward an RDMSR and a WRMSR of
# 0x4000FFFF, which Hyper-V refuses: shows the host fault handler resuming
# a refused forward (docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md section 5).
forward-refusal-test = []
# Print every VM exit in full, with no rate limit (vmexit/policy.rs).
trace-exits = []
# Expect the wrong RAX at main VMCALL #1, so the guest stops there as an
# unexpected exit: the stop report and teardown of a stop nobody planned.
unexpected-exit-test = ["test-guest"]
# Make the Local APIC's PDPT entry W without R, so the guest's read of it is
# an EPT misconfiguration: the stop, and the walk that names the entry.
ept-misconfig-test = ["test-guest"]

```

`README.md`:

```md
# Aleph0 Virtualization Hypervisor

[![CI](https://github.com/alephc0rporation/Aleph0-Virtualization-Hypervisor/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alephc0rporation/Aleph0-Virtualization-Hypervisor/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT OR Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20OR%20Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](#license)
[![Rust 1.85+](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)
[![Target: x86_64-unknown-uefi](https://img.shields.io/badge/target-x86__64--unknown--uefi-informational.svg)](.cargo/config.toml)

An Intel VT-x hypervisor written in Rust and booted as a UEFI application.
Aleph0 is being built to stay resident after `ExitBootServices` and run an
operating system as its guest, with EPT memory isolation and multiple vCPUs.
The end goal is research into game anti-cheat: running below the guest OS,
the hypervisor can watch and protect a game's memory where kernel-mode cheats
cannot reach. The project is also a study of AI-driven development in
low-level `unsafe` Rust, and of AI-assisted reverse-engineering tooling for
the analysis the anti-cheat needs.

## Status

Verified on Hyper-V with nested virtualization:

- [x] Enters VMX root operation and fills in a complete VMCS
- [x] Runs root operation on its own page tables, GDT, TSS and IDT
- [x] Launches a minimal guest and resumes it with VMRESUME after each exit
- [x] EPT identity map of the whole guest-physical address space, with the
      memory types the MTRRs give to RAM and UC for MMIO and everything
      else (1 GiB pages above RAM); a read-only guest page whose write exits
      to Aleph0, which grants the write and retries it; any other EPT exit
      stops with a walk of the GPA through the tables
- [x] Keeps the guest's MTRR writes in a copy, never the CPU's, with the #GP
      of a value the CPU would refuse, and gives EPT the types the copy gives
      (the #GP host-tested only)
- [x] Emulates CPUID, RDMSR/WRMSR and IN/OUT by passthrough, with MSR and I/O
      bitmaps limiting which MSRs and ports exit
- [x] Keeps Hyper-V's interface for its guest: forwards the guest's
      hypercalls and synthetic MSRs to Hyper-V from root operation, and
      gives it the #UD or #GP Hyper-V refuses one with
- [x] Catches an NMI that arrives while the guest runs and reinjects it into
      the guest's own IDT
- [x] Reports every exit over serial, then leaves VMX operation and returns to
      firmware
- [x] Virtualizes the running firmware in place: on Hyper-V it runs as the
      guest, draws its boot screen and answers the keyboard over VMBus
- [x] Stays resident after `ExitBootServices`: a harness exits boot
      services as Aleph0's guest and overwrites every page the OS may
      reclaim, and Aleph0 still handles its exits
- [ ] Hide Aleph0's own memory from the guest through EPT
- [ ] An OS guest on multiple vCPUs
- [ ] Anti-cheat research: guest memory introspection, EPT protection and
      split views, watching privileged changes

See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for the details of each step and what comes next.

## What it looks like

An excerpt of Aleph0's serial output (COM2) from a Hyper-V run, with the
`[Aleph0 Virtualization Hypervisor]` prefix trimmed from each line:

```text
Entered VMX root operation.
Launching the guest with VMLAUNCH; its VM exits are reported on serial only.
VM exit #1: reason=10 (CPUID)
VM exit #1: CPUID leaf=0x1 subleaf=0x0 -> eax=0x00090672 ebx=0x00020800 ecx=0xf7fa3203 edx=0x1f8bfbff (processor ecx=0xf7fa3223); resuming at rip=0x000000007ead4009.
...
VM exit #11: reason=48 (EPT violation)
VM exit #11: EPT violation at GPA 0x000000007ead5000 (linear 0x000000007ead5000): write; page R=1 W=0 X=0.
VM exit #11: write to the protected data page: write granted (W=1), INVEPT single-context; retrying the write at rip=0x000000007ead406c.
...
VM exit #13: reason=18 (VMCALL)
VM exit #13: expected VMCALL (rax=0xa1e1); all 2 planned VMCALLs handled; no NMI arrived.
VM exit #13: emulated exits: cpuid=1 rdmsr=2 wrmsr=2 in=2 out=2 hlt=1.
VM exit #13: stopping the guest; returning to bring-up.
...
Teardown: CR4.VMXE=0 firmware CR3 restored=true firmware GDTR/IDTR restored=true IF=1.
Guest finished after 13 VM exits; VMX operation left.
Returning to firmware with SUCCESS.
```

## Requirements

- Rust stable (edition 2024, Rust 1.85+). `rust-toolchain.toml` installs the
  `x86_64-unknown-uefi` target automatically.
- An Intel CPU with VT-x. VMX instructions only run under a VMM that exposes
  nested virtualization (Hyper-V is the tested path).

## Build

```powershell
cargo build            # produces target\x86_64-unknown-uefi\debug\aleph0hypervisor.efi
```

`.cargo/config.toml` makes the UEFI target the default.

## Test

```powershell
cargo test-host        # alias for: cargo test --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
cargo fmt --all --check   # formatting (rustfmt.toml: 120 columns)
cargo clippy           # lints for the UEFI build
cargo clippy --features test-guest                     # lints for the regression mode
cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --tests   # lints for the tests
cargo clippy -p ebs-harness                            # lints for the ExitBootServices harness
cargo test -p ebs-harness --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc   # its host unit tests
```

All of them pass without warnings, and CI runs them with `cargo build` on every
push to `master` and every pull request. `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` is on,
so every `unsafe` block needs a `// SAFETY:` comment saying why it is sound,
and every `unsafe fn` has a `# Safety` section for its callers.

Unit tests cover the pure logic (RFLAGS decoding, control-value selection,
descriptor encoding/decoding) and run on the host. Nothing that executes VMX
instructions can be unit-tested; that still needs a boot under Hyper-V.

The tests live in `tests/unit/`, which mirrors `src/`: the tests for
`src/vmx/vmexit/handler.rs` are in `tests/unit/vmx/vmexit/handler.rs`. Each source file
includes its test file with `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "..."] mod tests;`, so the
tests stay a child module that can reach private items, and none of them is
compiled into the `.efi`.

## Run

**Hyper-V (VMX available):** from an elevated PowerShell session,

```powershell
.\scripts\run-hyperv.ps1 -ProcessorCount 1   # the firmware, virtualized in place
.\scripts\run-hyperv.ps1 -TestGuest          # the built-in test guest
```

A default build virtualizes the running firmware: the code after Aleph0's
own VMLAUNCH goes on as the guest, and Aleph0 returns to the firmware in VMX
non-root operation. `-TestGuest` builds the regression mode instead (Cargo
feature `test-guest`): the built-in test guest runs its scripted exits, then
Aleph0 leaves VMX operation and returns to firmware with `SUCCESS`.

This turns off and reconfigures the `Aleph0Test` VM and recreates its ESP disk
under `run/`; keep nothing important there. It then streams Aleph0's serial
output (COM2) into the PowerShell window and `run\serial.log`, and saves the
guest's COM1 to `run\guest-serial.log`
(`-NoSerial` skips this; `.\scripts\read-serial.ps1` reattaches later). VM-exit
diagnostics only appear there, not on the VM console. See
[docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md](docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md). `-InjectNmi` runs the test
guest and sends it an NMI after its first VMCALL, and `-Features` builds with the
test-only switches in `Cargo.toml`: `host-fault-test` and `host-nmi-test` (see
[docs/HOST_ENVIRONMENT.md](docs/HOST_ENVIRONMENT.md) section 8),
`unexpected-exit-test` and `trace-exits` (see
[docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md](docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md)), and `ept-misconfig-test`
(see [docs/EPT.md](docs/EPT.md) section 6), and `forward-refusal-test`
(see [docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md](docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md) section 5).
`-ProcessorCount` sets the
vCPUs (2 by default, 1 with `-InjectNmi`).

**The Linux target:** `scripts/linux/build.sh` (Linux or WSL) builds the
kernel that is to boot as Aleph0's guest, as one EFI file in `run\linux\`.
`-Kernel run\linux\linux.efi` puts it on the ESP next to Aleph0, and
`-WithoutAleph0` boots it in Aleph0's place, streaming its console (COM1). See
[docs/LINUX_GUEST.md](docs/LINUX_GUEST.md).

**The ExitBootServices harness:** `-Harness` boots `tools/ebs-harness` in
Aleph0's place, which starts Aleph0, exits boot services as its guest,
overwrites every page the OS may reclaim and checks that Aleph0 still handles
its exits; `-SetVirtualAddressMap` adds that call. See
[docs/RESIDENT.md](docs/RESIDENT.md).

**QEMU + OVMF (no VMX):** put `OVMF_CODE.fd` and `OVMF_VARS.fd` from
[rust-osdev/ovmf-prebuilt](https://github.com/rust-osdev/ovmf-prebuilt) in
`ovmf/`, then run `.\scripts\run.ps1`. Without nested VMX this only exercises the
diagnostics that run before VMXON.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.rs` | UEFI entry point and the `log!` macro; copies the image to resident memory and runs on from the copy |
| `src/resident/` | Staying resident after `ExitBootServices`: the relocated image copy and the `ExitBootServices` event (`mod.rs`), which memory types the OS reclaims (`memory.rs`), PE32+ base relocation (`pe.rs`) |
| `src/vmx/page.rs` | Page allocation in the resident memory types, with the list of resident allocations bring-up checks |
| `src/bring_up/` | The bring-up sequence (`mod.rs`), its errors (`error.rs`), status lines (`report.rs`) and the return to firmware (`teardown.rs`) |
| `src/output.rs` | Output phases and the firmware-free panic handler |
| `src/serial.rs` | Serial logger usable without firmware, on COM2 (`SerialPort`); COM1 is left to the guest |
| `src/port.rs` | in/out of 1, 2 and 4 bytes, for the serial driver and the exit handler |
| `src/vmx/cpuid.rs`, `msr.rs`, `cr.rs` | CPU feature, MSR and control-register access |
| `src/vmx/context_tables.rs`, `segment.rs` | The GDT copy with a TSS that bring-up and the test guest run on, and the TSS layout; gate and descriptor encoding, segmentation state |
| `src/vmx/host/` | What VMX root operation runs on: Aleph0's page tables (`page_tables.rs`), GDT (`gdt.rs`), IDT with interrupt stacks (`idt.rs`) and the NMI and fault handlers (`handlers.rs`) |
| `src/vmx/vmxon.rs` | Entering and leaving VMX root operation |
| `src/vmx/vmcall.rs` | Aleph0's own VMCALLs, told apart by RCX: the end of boot services, and a test call |
| `src/vmx/hyperv.rs` | Hyper-V's interface, which the guest keeps: detecting it, and forwarding the guest's hypercalls and synthetic MSRs from root operation, with the recovery points for those Hyper-V refuses (see [docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md](docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md), the decision and its runs) |
| `src/vmx/region.rs` | The revision-stamped 4 KiB page that both the VMXON region and the VMCS are |
| `src/vmx/guest.rs`, `paging.rs` | The built-in test guest's code, data, stack and IDT pages; the page-table walk that checks them |
| `src/vmx/ept/` | EPT: support check, the identity map of the whole guest-physical address space (`MapLayout`: PDs for the memory map, UC 1 GiB pages above) with the guest's data page read-only, write grant and INVEPT, and the memory types that follow the guest's MTRRs, with spare PTs (`mod.rs`); the walk of a GPA through the tables and what the CPU refuses in an entry, for the stop on any other EPT exit (`walk.rs`) |
| `src/vmx/apic.rs` | IA32_APIC_BASE (the Local APIC's register page and mode), and the check that the test guest can read the page through EPT |
| `src/vmx/mtrr/` | The MTRRs: decoding them and the memory type of each address, which the EPT entries copy (`mod.rs`); the MTRR MSRs a CPU has, the values WRMSR refuses, reading them, and the guest's copy (`registers.rs`) |
| `src/vmx/exit_bitmaps.rs` | The MSR and I/O bitmaps: which MSRs and ports exit, and their pages |
| `src/vmx/guest_state.rs` | Guest-state VMCS fields, copied from the host CPU, and where each guest starts |
| `src/vmx/vmcs/mod.rs`, `fields.rs`, `launch.rs` | VMCS lifecycle, field access, controls and host state; every field encoding; the launch stub that returns when the test guest stops, and the in-place launch the firmware goes on from as the guest |
| `src/vmx/vmexit/` | VM-exit stack and entry stub with the VMRESUME path (`mod.rs`); the exit handler, as read, judge, carry out and report (`handler.rs`); the guest's copy of its MTRRs (`guest_mtrrs.rs`); its report lines (`report.rs`), how much of each exit they print (`policy.rs`), and what every stop adds: the guest's state and registers (`dump.rs`) and the last 64 exits (`history.rs`) |
| `src/vmx/exit_decision/` | The pure decision for each exit: shared exit types and the dispatch on the exit reason (`mod.rs`), and one handler per reason; the instructions Aleph0 executes for any guest (CPUID, RDMSR/WRMSR, IN/OUT) and the routing of the guest's MTRR MSRs to its copy and of Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs to Hyper-V are in `emulation.rs`, the test guest's own exits (EPT write, VMCALLs, NMI reinjection) in `scenario.rs` |
| `tests/unit/` | Host unit tests, mirroring `src/` (see [Test](#test)) |
| `tools/ebs-harness/` | The ExitBootServices test harness, an EFI application of its own (see [docs/RESIDENT.md](docs/RESIDENT.md)) |
| `scripts/run.ps1` | Build and boot under QEMU + OVMF (no VMX) |
| `scripts/run-hyperv.ps1`, `scripts/read-serial.ps1` | Hyper-V test VM runner and serial reader (Windows PowerShell) |
| `scripts/linux/` | The Linux target's build (`build.sh`, bash for Linux or WSL), its kernel configuration fragment (`aleph0.config`) and its initramfs's `/init` (see [docs/LINUX_GUEST.md](docs/LINUX_GUEST.md)) |
| `docs/` | Background explanations (see [Documentation](#documentation)) |

## Documentation

Each page explains the mechanism the code implements, with the Intel SDM
references it relies on:

- [SERIAL_LOGGING.md](docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md): the serial logger, a beginner walkthrough
- [PORT_IO.md](docs/PORT_IO.md): `in`/`out` and the I/O port space
- [PAGE_TABLE_WALK.md](docs/PAGE_TABLE_WALK.md): page tables and how Aleph0 walks them
- [HOST_ENVIRONMENT.md](docs/HOST_ENVIRONMENT.md): the page tables, GDT, TSS and IDT that VM exits load, and NMIs in root operation
- [EPT.md](docs/EPT.md): the second translation stage, the identity map and the intentional EPT violation
- [MTRR.md](docs/MTRR.md): memory types, the MTRRs, how EPT entries get them, and the guest's copy of its MTRRs
- [EMULATED_EXITS.md](docs/EMULATED_EXITS.md): CPUID, MSR and port-I/O exits, the bitmaps, passthrough emulation
- [NMI.md](docs/NMI.md): catching NMIs in the guest and reinjecting them
- [CLEAN_STOP.md](docs/CLEAN_STOP.md): stopping the guest, leaving VMX and returning to firmware
- [FIRMWARE_GUEST.md](docs/FIRMWARE_GUEST.md): launching in place, so the firmware itself runs as the guest
- [RESIDENT.md](docs/RESIDENT.md): staying resident after `ExitBootServices`: resident memory, the relocated image copy, the event, the test harness
- [LINUX_GUEST.md](docs/LINUX_GUEST.md): the Linux target, how it is built and staged, and its boot without Aleph0
- [HYPERV_INTERFACE.md](docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md): how the guest sees Hyper-V: the decision to forward its hypercalls and synthetic MSRs, and the runs behind it

`ROADMAP.md`:

```md
# Aleph0 hypervisor roadmap

Aleph0 is an Intel VT-x hypervisor booted as a UEFI application. This roadmap tracks it from the first VM entry to running an operating system as its guest, with EPT memory isolation, multiple vCPUs, and Aleph0 resident after `ExitBootServices`. Each milestone ends in a result that is verified on Hyper-V before the next piece is built. EPT is enabled with an identity map, CPUID, RDMSR/WRMSR, port I/O and HLT exits are emulated, and VM exits run on Aleph0's own page tables, GDT, TSS and IDT. The immediate goal is the first OS boot, in the order issue #15 sets..

## Current state

- [x] Build a `x86_64-unknown-uefi` application with `cargo build`.
- [x] Boot the EFI application with the Hyper-V Gen 2 runner (`scripts/run-hyperv.ps1`); nested virtualization exposes VMX. The runner requires an elevated PowerShell session.
- [x] Check CPUID VMX support and firmware's `IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL` settings.
- [x] Set `CR4.VMXE`, apply the VMX CR0/CR4 fixed bits, allocate a VMXON region, and enter VMX root operation.
- [x] Allocate and load a VMCS; verify a `VMWRITE`/`VMREAD` round trip.
- [x] Read and print current selectors, descriptor-table registers, and FS/GS/TR bases.
- [x] Establish a usable host task register. The tested Hyper-V boot reported a nonzero `TR`; activation checks GDTR, TR, and the decoded TSS base against the prepared values.
- [x] Discover VMX control MSRs, select legal control values, and write/read back the four VMCS control fields.
- [x] Write/read back host selectors, CRs, segment/table bases, SYSENTER state, and `HOST_RSP`/`HOST_RIP`. The Hyper-V run reported host PAT and EFER load controls both false, so those conditional fields were skipped.
- [x] Allocate a dedicated four-page VM-exit stack and compile an inactive entry stub that saves general-purpose registers and calls a non-returning Rust handler. Since section 4 the handler returns 0 to resume the guest, and the stub restores the registers and executes VMRESUME; to stop the guest it returns a stop value, and the stub jumps back into `vmcs::launch`.
- [x] Add a firmware-independent COM1 serial logger and stream it from the Hyper-V VM to the host console and `run\serial.log` (see section 0).
- [x] Replace the `uefi` panic handler with one that needs no firmware, and gate console output by an output phase (see section 0b).

- [x] Launch a minimal guest with `VMLAUNCH` and observe its first VM exit (`VMCALL`, reason 18, marker `0xa1e0` in guest RAX) over serial (see section 3).

- [x] Resume the guest with `VMRESUME` after its first exit and recognise its second `VMCALL` exit (see section 4).

- [x] Stop the guest after its last planned exit, leave VMX operation (`VMCLEAR`, `VMXOFF`, CR0/CR4 restored), restore the firmware's GDTR, IDTR and interrupt flag, and return from the EFI application to firmware (see section 4).

- [x] Catch NMIs that arrive while the guest runs (NMI exiting, virtual NMIs) and reinject them into the guest's own IDT, with NMI-window exiting when the guest blocks NMIs (see section 4).

- [x] Enable EPT with an identity map of all memory, make the guest's data page read-only, and handle the guest's write to it: an intentional EPT violation after which Aleph0 grants write, runs INVEPT and retries the write (see section 5 and [docs/EPT.md](docs/EPT.md)).

- [x] Refactor without changing behaviour: shared register accessors and descriptor decoding, one `vmx_asm!` for the VMX instructions and one `VmxRegion` for the VMXON region and the VMCS, `write_verified` for every checked VMCS write, types for raw values (`SegmentDescriptor`, `ControlCapability`, `EptEntry`, `Eptp`, `InterruptionInfo`, `EptQualification`, `ResumePlan`, `ProtectedPage`), the fixes from the PR #5 review, the `vmexit` module split into stub, handler and report, and a `SAFETY` comment on every `unsafe` block. Host tests, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, and a QEMU boot prints the same lines as before.

- [x] Emulate CPUID, RDMSR, WRMSR and IN/OUT by passthrough: `exit_decision::decide` dispatches on the exit reason, MSR and I/O bitmaps intercept one MSR (`IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE`) and one port (the COM1 scratch register `0x3FF`), and Aleph0 runs them in root operation with CPUID.1:ECX bit 5 (VMX) hidden. On Hyper-V the guest's nine emulated exits printed `emulated exits: cpuid=1 rdmsr=2 wrmsr=2 in=2 out=2.`, the guest saw ECX `0xf7fa3203` where the processor returned `0xf7fa3223`, and `restored=true` (see section 5 and [docs/EMULATED_EXITS.md](docs/EMULATED_EXITS.md)).

- [x] Boot the first-boot Linux target on the Hyper-V test VM without Aleph0 (issue #17), to know what a working boot looks like before #28 boots it under Aleph0. `scripts/linux/build.sh` (Linux or WSL) builds Linux 6.18.58 from `x86_64_defconfig` and the fragment `scripts/linux/aleph0.config`: the EFI stub, the command line built in with `CONFIG_CMDLINE_OVERRIDE` (`console=ttyS0,115200 earlycon=uart8250,io,0x3f8,115200 nokaslr`), an initramfs with a static BusyBox 1.35.0 and `/init`, the 8250 console, `CONFIG_PRINTK_TIME`, Hyper-V guest support on (`CONFIG_HYPERVISOR_GUEST=y`) and the VMBus drivers off (`# CONFIG_HYPERV is not set`). `run-hyperv.ps1` gained `-Kernel` (the image at `\EFI\aleph0\linux.efi`, next to Aleph0), `-WithoutAleph0` (the image as `BOOTX64.EFI`, COM1 streamed) and `-ProcessorCount` (2 by default, 1 with `-InjectNmi`, which refuses other counts). Two runs of `-Kernel run\linux\linux.efi -WithoutAleph0 -ProcessorCount 1` printed the same lines: an empty `Command line:` from the boot manager, then `Kernel command line: console=ttyS0,115200 earlycon=uart8250,io,0x3f8,115200 nokaslr`, `Hypervisor detected: Microsoft Hyper-V`, `aleph0-linux: nproc 1`, `_text` at `ffffffff81000000` as in `System.map`, clocksource `tsc`, `Run /init as init process` at 0.426670 s and 0.428960 s, and `/proc/uptime` 0.63 s and 0.64 s before `aleph0-linux: shell`. Devices in `/proc/iomem`: the IOAPIC at `0xfec00000` and the Local APIC at `0xfee00000` (`PNP0003`), nothing else; no PCI (`PCI: System does not support PCI`) and, with the VMBus drivers off, no VMBus window (#20). The kernel takes its TSC and LAPIC timer frequencies from Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs `0x40000022` and `0x40000023` and writes `0x40000118` (`HV_X64_MSR_TSC_INVARIANT_CONTROL`) at boot, all in the range that gets a #GP under Aleph0 today (#27); the VM has no legacy PIC (`Using NULL legacy PIC`), so IRQ 0 cannot be requested (`Failed to register legacy timer interrupt`). The CPU flags include `xsave xsaveopt xsavec xsaves`, `rdtscp`, `pcid invpcid`, `fsgsbase`, `umip`, `waitpkg`, `smep smap`, `x2apic`, `tsc_deadline_timer` and `vmx ept vpid` (#25). Without the new parameters the runner boots Aleph0 as before: 24 exits, and 26 with `-InjectNmi`, then `SUCCESS`. The full lines are in [docs/LINUX_GUEST.md](docs/LINUX_GUEST.md).

No OS boots as Aleph0's guest yet.

**Next:** the first OS boot (#15): virtualize the running firmware (#21); the Linux target boots without Aleph0 (#17), and EPT maps the whole guest-physical address space (#20). Intercepting the guest's MTRR writes (#14) is done and verified on Hyper-V; staying resident after `ExitBootServices` (#23) is done: the harness exits boot services as Aleph0's guest, overwrites every reclaimable page, and Aleph0 still handles its exits, now that it forwards Hyper-V's hypercalls and synthetic MSRs (#27); hiding Aleph0's pages through EPT comes after the first boot.

## 0. Debug output that works without firmware

`uefi::println!` calls the firmware console, which is unsafe in the VM-exit handler (interrupts off, arbitrary firmware state) and gone after `ExitBootServices`. Serial output drives the UART directly with `in`/`out`, so it works in both. Background and usage: [docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md](docs/SERIAL_LOGGING.md).

- [x] Drive the 16550 UART at COM1 (`0x3F8`) from `src/serial.rs`: 115200 8N1, polled, no interrupts. Probe with loopback before enabling output, and bound every wait so a missing UART cannot hang the hypervisor.
- [x] Provide `serial_print!`/`serial_println!` through `core::fmt` with no allocation, for use in exit context.
- [x] Route bring-up messages through `log!`, which writes each line to both the firmware console and COM1.
- [x] Attach COM1 to `\\.\pipe\aleph0-com1` in `scripts/run-hyperv.ps1` and stream it with `scripts/read-serial.ps1`, which also saves `run\serial.log`. The reader was tested against a local pipe server, not yet against Hyper-V.
- [x] Confirm on Hyper-V: the console prints `Serial output enabled on COM1`, and the PowerShell window and `run\serial.log` show the same bring-up lines as the VM console.

**Checkpoint:** A Hyper-V run produces a `run\serial.log` that matches the VM console. Only then rely on serial as the observation path for the first VM exit.

### 0b. Output in exit context and after `ExitBootServices`

After `ExitBootServices` the OS runs as Aleph0's guest, Aleph0 only runs during VM exits, and serial is its only output. Facts this plan is based on:

- `uefi::println!` (uefi 0.40, `helpers/println.rs`) checks `boot::are_boot_services_active()`. After `ExitBootServices` it silently prints nothing. Before it, the check passes, so a call from the VM-exit handler **would** call the firmware console.
- The `uefi` crate's panic handler (`panic_handler` feature) calls that `println!`, then `boot::stall` and `runtime::reset`: three firmware calls. A panic in the exit handler therefore enters firmware from exit context, and after `ExitBootServices` the panic message is lost.
- The OS will want COM1 too: Linux probes `ttyS0`, including its own loopback test, and Windows may use COM1 for debugging. Unarbitrated sharing loses or interleaves output.
- Under Hyper-V every serial byte is itself a VM exit to Hyper-V, so printing on every guest exit slows the guest dramatically.

Before the first `VMLAUNCH` (section 3):

- [x] Replace the `uefi` panic handler with Aleph0's own and drop the crate's `panic_handler` feature. Always print the panic over serial, print on the console only in ordinary boot-services context, then halt with `cli; hlt`. No `stall`, no `runtime::reset`, no other firmware calls. Done in `src/output.rs`; a recursion guard halts on a nested panic. On Hyper-V a test panic in `main` printed on the console and in `run\serial.log`, and the VM stayed halted instead of resetting.
- [x] Track the output phase in one global (boot services, inside the VM-exit handler, runtime after `ExitBootServices`). `log!` writes to the console only in the boot-services phase and to serial in every phase. `output::Phase`; `vmexit_handler` sets `VmExit` first. On Hyper-V a panic after setting `VmExit` from `main` reached `run\serial.log` only, not the console, and the VM stayed halted. A panic in a real exit is first exercised at `VMLAUNCH`.

Before the firmware runs as the guest (issue #18, ahead of #21 in section 5), since exits become frequent then:

- [x] Make the serial port base a parameter instead of the fixed `COM1`. Send hypervisor output to COM2 (`0x2F8`) and leave COM1 to the guest OS, without interception at first. `serial::init` takes a `SerialPort` (`COM1`, `COM2`) and keeps its base for `write_byte` and the panic handler; a failed loopback test leaves output off, with no fallback to COM1. `scripts/run-hyperv.ps1` attaches COM2 to `\\.\pipe\aleph0-com2` (`run\serial.log`, on the console) and COM1 to `\\.\pipe\aleph0-com1` (`run\guest-serial.log`), with one reader each started before `Start-VM`; `scripts/run.ps1` sends COM1 to the terminal and COM2 to `run\qemu-serial.log`, because OVMF mirrors its console to every serial port and COM2 would show each `log!` line twice. The readers were tested against local pipe servers. On Hyper-V all three runs printed `Serial output enabled on COM2 (0x2f8).`, `run\serial.log` held every line from `Initializing UEFI helpers...` on (174, 186 and 166 lines), and `run\guest-serial.log` stayed empty: the test guest writes nothing to COM1. Under QEMU the terminal showed each line once.
- [x] Add log levels (error, info, trace; trace off by default; no warn level, since nothing would ever filter it) and rate-limit repeated messages. `vmexit::policy` decides how much each exit prints once it knows how the exit ended: a stop or an unreadable field in full (error), the first 16 exits of each basic reason in full (info), then one summary line at each power of two (info), nothing else (trace). The `trace-exits` Cargo feature prints every exit in full; NMIs that arrived in root operation always print. Exits are counted per reason in a fixed array (reasons past 127 and an unreadable one share a last counter), and every stop prints the counts as one histogram line. Host-tested, including that every exit of the test guest's runs still prints in full. On Hyper-V every exit printed in full as before, and the stops printed `exits by reason: 10 (CPUID)=1, 12 (HLT)=1, 18 (VMCALL)=2, 30 (I/O instruction)=4, 31 (RDMSR)=2, 32 (WRMSR)=2, 48 (EPT violation)=1.` (plain), the same with `0 (exception or NMI)=1` and `VMCALL=3` (`-InjectNmi`). The rate limit itself first runs on real VMX with #21.
- [x] Keep an in-memory ring buffer of the last 64 exits (what the handler read, and the event `decide` returned), printed oldest first at every stop and by the panic handler. Every stop also dumps the guest state read back from the VMCS (in the pre-launch format), the 15 general-purpose registers, DR7, PAT and EFER from wherever the controls leave them, and the VMCS fields that explain an exit (pending events, a queued injection, the exit's event and an interrupted delivery with their error codes, guest addresses, controls); a failed VMRESUME prints the same. Host-tested: the ring, the dump's field table, the choice of source for DR7, PAT and EFER, and the formatting. On Hyper-V: the plain run's stop at #13 (`LastMainVmcall`) and the `-InjectNmi` run's at #15 dumped the guest state (`rip=0x7ead408d rsp=0x7ead4000 rflags=0x6 cr0=0x80010033 cr3=0x4401000 cr4=0x2668`, the segments, GDTR/IDTR, SYSENTER), the registers, `dr7=not saved pat=0x7040600070406 (MSR, not switched) efer=0xd00 (MSR, not switched)`, the event, address and control fields (`primary=0xb60065f2 exit=0x36ffb entry=0x13fb exception_bitmap=0xffffffff`), and the 13 and 15 exits oldest first, matching the lines above them (`#13 reason=0 ... info=0x80000202 -> NmiInjected`). With `-Features unexpected-exit-test`, the first real-VMX run of a stop other than the planned one: exit #12 printed `NOT an expected exit (the next main VMCALL should have rax=0xa1e1)`, the same dump and exits 1 to 12 (`#12 ... rax=0xa1e0 -> Unexpected`), then teardown with `firmware CR3 restored=true` and `Returning to firmware with ABORTED.`. After an NMI exit, later exits show VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO `0x202`: the NMI's type and vector with the valid bit clear, which carries no meaning. A failed VMRESUME, which prints the same report, has not happened on real VMX.
- [x] Count exits in per-vCPU statistics for every guest, the way KVM keeps `struct kvm_vcpu_stat` (`vmexit::stats::VcpuStats`: `exits`, one counter per instruction executed for the guest, `halt_exits`, `nmi_injections`, `exception_injections`). The handler counts what it carried out; `decide` no longer counts, so the generic emulation handlers read only the exit. Every stop prints the statistics. The test guest's check moved out of `decide` into bring-up (`guest::expected_stats`, compared after the run, like a KVM selftest), replacing `EmulationCounts` and `EmulationMissing`.

At the `ExitBootServices` milestone (section 5):

- [x] Switch the phase to runtime immediately after `ExitBootServices`. Ideally make the console unreachable from runtime code, so a mistake fails to compile rather than silently printing nothing. Done in issue #23: an `EVT_SIGNAL_EXIT_BOOT_SERVICES` event makes a VMCALL in the guest with `vmx::vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED` in RCX (RAX until #27), and the exit handler resumes the guest in `Phase::Runtime` from then on (`resume_phase`, host-tested). The console stays reachable at compile time; the phase check skips it. On Hyper-V, the harness run printed `VMCALL from Aleph0's ExitBootServices event (rcx=0x416c657068304542): boot services are over; output phase now runtime (serial only)` (section 5, the persistence item).
- [x] Keep the logging code and its state (`serial.rs` statics such as `READY`) in memory the OS will not reclaim. This is part of the persistence item in section 5, not a separate mechanism. Done with it: the code and the statics live in the resident image copy, and Aleph0 kept printing on COM2 after the harness overwrote every reclaimable page.

At multiple vCPUs (section 5):

- [ ] Serialize output per line, not per byte, with a spinlock, and prefix each line with the CPU number (`[cpu2] VM exit: ...`). Never hold the lock across `VMRESUME`. The panic path uses a try-lock and writes anyway if the lock is held, so an NMI or a panic cannot deadlock on it.

When guest exits become frequent (OS guest):

- [ ] Let a guest tool ask for the exit history with a `VMCALL`. Guest VMCALLs also carry Hyper-V hypercalls; since #27 Aleph0's own are told apart by RCX values with reserved hypercall-input bits set (`vmx::vmcall`), so this is one more such value.

At the virtual-device milestone (section 5):

- [ ] Intercept COM1 with I/O bitmaps (exit reason 30). Either hide it (reads return `0xFF`, writes ignored) or emulate a 16550 for the guest and forward its output tagged `[guest]`. See [docs/PORT_IO.md](docs/PORT_IO.md), section 7.

**Checkpoint:** A deliberate panic inside the VM-exit handler prints its message over serial and halts without any firmware call. After `ExitBootServices`, hypervisor lines arrive on COM2 while the guest OS uses COM1 undisturbed.

## 1. Establish a host TSS

- [x] Allocate a long-lived 64-bit TSS and a GDT that preserves the descriptors used by the current CS/SS and other active selectors; append a present 16-byte, 64-bit available-TSS descriptor.
- [x] Load that GDT and use `LTR` with its TSS selector. Keep the GDT and TSS alive while the CPU uses them; do not modify the firmware's GDT in place.
- [x] Re-read `STR`, GDTR, and the TSS base. Confirm `TR` is nonzero and its descriptor resolves to the allocated TSS before copying this state into the VMCS.
- [x] Check firmware interactions on the current boot path: after VMXON, the VMCS self-test, and UEFI calls, GDTR, TR, TSS base, and IDTR still match the activated state.

**Checkpoint:** The reported Hyper-V boot had no failures and printed a nonzero TR selector; activation verified its descriptor's base against the allocated TSS, and the post-VMX check reported the tables preserved. No `VMLAUNCH` yet. Recheck if new firmware call paths are added.

## 2. Prepare a minimal VMCS

- [x] Read `IA32_VMX_BASIC` and check bit 55. Read the true-control MSRs if available, otherwise the ordinary control MSRs, for pin-based, primary processor-based, VM-exit, and VM-entry controls. Print each MSR's low and high 32-bit halves. The Hyper-V boot printed all four values without faulting.
- [x] Derive legal values from those MSRs: the low halves specify bits that must be 1, and the high halves specify bits allowed to be 1. Reject requested features the CPU cannot enable. Write the four controls to the VMCS and read them back. A successful `VMWRITE`/`VMREAD` proves storage, not that VM entry will succeed.
- [x] Add a guest-memory owner (for example, `src/vmx/guest.rs`) that allocates and retains separate guest code and guest stack pages. Start with tiny guest code whose first test instruction is `VMCALL`; keep both pages alive for as long as the CPU stays in VMX operation. `GuestMemory` copies the guest code (since section 4: `mov eax, GUEST_MARKER; vmcall`, a wait loop for an NMI, `inc eax; vmcall`, and an NMI handler) from a `global_asm!` block into a `LOADER_CODE` page (firmware may map `LOADER_DATA` no-execute) and allocates a `LOADER_DATA` stack page and, since section 4, a `LOADER_DATA` guest IDT page with one gate at vector 2. Since section 5 the code page is a two-page `LOADER_CODE` allocation whose second page is the guest's data page, which EPT maps read-only (see [docs/EPT.md](docs/EPT.md)); bring-up keeps all of them allocated (their types cannot free on drop, asserted at compile time in `src/bring_up/mod.rs`). The marker in RAX shows on serial that the guest's own instructions ran. Hyper-V printed `Guest memory allocated: code=0x000000007eb1c000 (10 bytes copied)` (before `inc eax` was added; the guest code is now 73 bytes).
- [x] Decide and verify guest address translation before using those pages. With EPT disabled, guest virtual addresses translate through guest CR3; confirm the code page is executable and the separate stack page is writable under those page tables. Do not assume a UEFI allocation address is automatically usable by the guest. Decided: guest CR3 = host CR3, no EPT. Written: `src/vmx/paging.rs` walks the live 4-level tables (reading them through UEFI's identity mapping), combines R/W and XD over every level, and `GuestMemory::check_mappings` stops bring-up unless the code page has XD clear and the stack page is writable. It also combines U/S over every level and refuses a user code page under CR4.SMEP or a user stack page under CR4.SMAP, since the guest runs in ring 0 with the host's CR4; that check also passed on Hyper-V. Host tests cover 4 KiB/2 MiB/1 GiB leaves, permission combining and missing entries. On Hyper-V both pages were identity-mapped 4 KiB pages, writable, with XD clear (so this firmware does not map `LOADER_DATA` no-execute; `LOADER_CODE` stays as a portable precaution), and host EFER.NXE=1. Step 3 must give the guest EFER.NXE=1 too, or any XD bit in these shared tables becomes a reserved-bit fault.
- [x] Build a known, simple 64-bit guest context: valid CR0/CR3/CR4, segment selectors/bases/limits/access rights, GDTR/IDTR, RIP pointing at the guest code, RSP pointing at the guest stack, RFLAGS bit 1 set, and a VMCS link pointer of all ones. Initialize all other guest fields required by the selected controls and retain their backing memory. Written: `GuestState::from_current` in `src/vmx/guest_state.rs` copies the host's live CR0/CR3/CR4, selectors, GDTR and SYSENTER MSRs (the IDTR is the guest's own IDT since section 4), decodes each segment's limit and access rights from its GDT descriptor (`segment::descriptor_*`, host-tested), sets the accessed bit on code/data segments, makes LDTR unusable, and writes guest PAT/EFER only when the entry controls load them (otherwise the guest keeps the host's EFER, including NXE). It refuses a CS that is not 64-bit code or a TR that is not a busy 64-bit TSS. On Hyper-V both checks passed.
- [x] Add a guest-state writer and read back the fields it writes. This checks VMCS storage only; the CPU's VM-entry checks happen when entry is attempted. `GuestState::write` writes and reads back every field, reporting the first mismatch by encoding; `bring_up::report::guest_state` logs every segment's selector, base, limit and access rights for diagnosing a later exit reason 33. Hyper-V printed `VMCS guest fields written and read back; VM entry not attempted.` followed by `Host GDTR, TR, TSS base and IDTR preserved after VMX/UEFI calls.`
- [x] Write/read back host fields from the current root-mode state: selectors, CRs, FS/GS/TR and GDTR/IDTR bases, SYSENTER MSRs, and the dedicated VM-exit stack top and stub address. Load host PAT/EFER fields only if the selected exit controls require them.
- [x] Complete VM-entry validation of host selectors, CRs, and addresses; write/readback alone does not prove the host state will pass VM-entry checks. The first VMLAUNCH on Hyper-V passed the CPU's own host-state checks (no VM-instruction error 8).
- [x] Document the UEFI memory and address-translation assumptions of the current bring-up. A shared, identity-mapped address space without EPT is a bring-up stage, not guest memory isolation; EPT (section 5) provides that. Documented in [docs/EPT.md](docs/EPT.md): the guest still shares the host's page tables, EPT adds a second, identity-mapped stage built from the UEFI memory map, and that identity map still shows the guest all of Aleph0's memory (section 9 there).

**Checkpoint:** Hyper-V reported successful control, host-state, SYSENTER, and `HOST_RSP`/`HOST_RIP` write/readback. Both host PAT and EFER load controls were false, so those conditional writes were not exercised. Guest memory, its page-table mappings and every guest-state field are also confirmed on Hyper-V. The first `VMLAUNCH` (section 3) then passed the CPU's own control, host-state and guest-state checks.

## 3. Launch and observe one guest exit

- [x] Assemble and link an inactive VM-exit entry stub that saves guest general-purpose registers, prepares the UEFI x64 call frame, and calls a non-returning handler. Do not mistake compilation or `HOST_RIP` readback for a tested exit.
- [x] Replace the spin-only handler with a deliberate first-exit diagnostic: read `VM_EXIT_REASON`, record it through a mechanism that can be observed, and stop safely. Do not assume UEFI printing is safe in the low-level exit handler; there is no `VMRESUME` path yet. `vmexit_handler` reads the exit reason (basic reason plus the VM-entry-failure bit), exit qualification, guest RIP, instruction length and the saved guest RAX-RDX, prints them with `serial_println!`, and halts with `cli; hlt`. It ran for the first time on the first `VMLAUNCH` on Hyper-V, and printed the guest's `VMCALL` exit.
- [x] Before the first launch, finish the "Before the first `VMLAUNCH`" items in section 0b (own panic handler, output phase), so a panic in exit context never calls firmware.
- [x] After guest memory/state readback and the observable exit path are ready, execute `VMLAUNCH` to enter the tiny guest. `VMLAUNCH` enters the guest for the first time; the guest then executes `VMCALL`, which causes the VM exit. `bring_up::run` ends with `vmcs::launch`. On Hyper-V, serial showed `VM exit: reason=18 (VMCALL)`, `instruction length=3`, and guest `rax=0x000000000000a1e0`.
- [x] On instruction failure, distinguish VMfailInvalid, VMfailValid (read `VM_INSTRUCTION_ERROR`), and VM-entry failure reported as a VM exit. Do not treat every return as a successful guest run. `vmcs::launch` returns only on failure and maps CF to `VmFailInvalid`, ZF to `VmFailValid` (decoded by `report_vmcs_error`), and a fall-through with clear flags to `LaunchReturned`, never to success (host-tested). Invalid guest state arrives as an exit with bit 31 set, which the exit handler prints.
- [x] Handle only the expected `VMCALL` at first. Define a controlled stop/observation path; do not blindly `VMRESUME` at the same guest RIP. The handler checks reason 18 plus the guest marker in RAX (`is_expected_first_exit`, renamed `is_expected_vmcall_exit` in section 4; host-tested; since the NMI step: `exit_decision::decide`, host-tested), prints whether this was the expected exit, and halts with `cli; hlt`.

**Checkpoint:** A Hyper-V run confirms that the guest executed and records the expected `VMCALL` exit reason, not merely a successful VMCS write. Reached: serial printed `VM exit: expected first exit: the guest ran and executed VMCALL (marker 0xa1e0 in RAX).`

## 4. Make guest execution repeatable

- [x] Advance guest RIP by the VM-exit instruction length when appropriate, then `VMRESUME` and handle a second known exit. The handler writes GUEST_RIP = RIP + `VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN` and returns (since the NMI step: `exit_decision::decide`, host-tested); the entry stub restores the guest registers and executes `VMRESUME`. The guest runs `inc eax` before its second main `VMCALL`. On Hyper-V, exit #2 showed the same RIP as exit #1 and guest `rax=0x000000000000a1e1`, so the guest resumed past the first `VMCALL`.
- [x] Handle unexpected exits and failed resume paths explicitly. `exit_action` (host-tested; since the NMI step: `exit_decision::decide`, host-tested) resumes only the expected `VMCALL` exits; anything else prints `NOT an expected guest VMCALL exit` (now `NOT an expected exit`) and stops the guest. A failed `VMRESUME` falls through to `vmresume_failed`, which decodes the flags and `VM_INSTRUCTION_ERROR`. Bring-up now stops instead of launching if the host descriptor tables changed.
- [x] Add clean VMCS/VMX shutdown and restore host state before returning control to firmware. A VM exit sets the host GDTR and IDTR limits to 0xFFFF and the TR limit to 0x67, so the return to firmware must reload the firmware's descriptor tables, not only leave VMX operation. `vmx_launch` (`src/vmx/vmcs/launch.rs`) saves the caller's frame before VMLAUNCH; to stop, the exit handler returns a stop value and the exit stub jumps back into that frame, so `vmcs::launch` returns a `GuestStop`. `bring_up::teardown` then loads the firmware's GDTR and IDTR, runs `VMCLEAR` and `VMXOFF`, restores CR0/CR4 and the interrupt flag, and `main` returns to firmware after a UEFI timer event fires. Every failure after VMXON takes the same path. TR stays on Aleph0's TSS, whose pages are never freed. On Hyper-V, serial showed `Teardown: CR4.VMXE=0 firmware GDTR/IDTR restored=true IF=1.`, the timer fired, and the application returned `SUCCESS`.
- [x] Plan for interrupts, exceptions, and firmware calls while in VMX root operation; avoid assuming a UEFI print call is safe inside a low-level exit stub. Exceptions: the exception bitmap is all ones, so a guest fault exits with reason 0 and its vector is printed, instead of running the firmware's handler inside the guest. NMIs: NMI exiting and virtual NMIs are on. `exit_decision::decide` (host-tested) reinjects each NMI through `VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO` (`0x80000202`) into the guest's own IDT (`GuestMemory::idt`, one gate at vector 2), or, while STI, MOV SS or NMI blocking prevents injection, waits for an NMI-window exit. On Hyper-V, `run-hyperv.ps1 -InjectNmi` injected an NMI with `Debug-VM` while the guest waited; serial showed the NMI exit, the guest NMI handler's VMCALL, and `NMIs: 1 reinjected, 1 handled by the guest`. Interrupts: the guest runs with RFLAGS.IF=0 and no interrupt exiting; external-interrupt exiting comes with an OS guest. Still open: an exit that interrupted an event's delivery (IDT-vectoring info) stops the guest instead of re-delivering it, and an NMI-window exit taken while STI blocking still holds would repeat until the guest runs an instruction; the guest runs with IF=0, so it never has STI blocking.

**Checkpoint:** A short guest sequence produces predictable multiple exits and terminates cleanly. Reached on Hyper-V: two VMCALL exits, then teardown and a return to firmware with `SUCCESS`.

## 5. Add isolation and devices incrementally

- [x] Check CPU support for secondary execution controls and EPT; allocate and validate EPT tables before enabling them. Verify allowed guest physical accesses and an intentional EPT-violation exit. `ept::check_support` requires a 4-level walk, WB, 2 MiB pages and INVEPT (host-tested); Hyper-V reported EPT/VPID capabilities `0x00000f0106f34041` and single-context INVEPT. `Ept::build` identity-maps memory up to the highest UEFI memory-map address, rounded up to 1 GiB, with 2 MiB pages, and splits the region holding the guest's data page into 4 KiB pages so that page is read-only (host-tested; since the MTRR item below, a region of mixed memory types gets a PT too). On Hyper-V, before the memory types came from the MTRRs: `identity 0x0..0x80000000 (2 GiB)`, 5 table pages, EPTP `0x7eafc01e`. The guest reads the data page (allowed, RCX = `0xda7a`), writes it, which caused exit 48 at GPA `0x7eb01000` with qualification `0x58a` (write; R=1 W=0 X=0); Aleph0 set W=1, ran INVEPT and resumed at the same RIP, and VMCALL #1 showed RDX = `0x455054`, the retried write. A main VMCALL before the violation would stop the guest (`EptWriteMissing`). The `-InjectNmi` run reinjected an NMI under EPT as before. See [docs/EPT.md](docs/EPT.md).

- [x] EPT memory types from the MTRRs, before an OS guest. With EPT on, the MTRRs no longer apply to guest accesses; the EPT entry's type does. Until now every entry was WB, which would break device memory (Local APIC, IOAPIC, PCI BARs, framebuffer). `mtrr::read` checks CPUID.1:EDX bit 12, then reads `IA32_MTRRCAP`, `IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE`, the fixed-range MTRRs if `IA32_MTRRCAP` reports them and every variable range it counts; `Mtrrs::decode` refuses a reserved type in any MTRR the CPU uses, and `Mtrrs::memory_type` follows the SDM's precedences (host-tested). `Ept::build` maps a 2 MiB region of one type as a 2 MiB page of that type and a region of mixed types through a PT of 4 KiB pages, each with its own type (host-tested, including the fixed ranges of the first MiB). A CPU without MTRRs stays all WB. Bring-up prints the decoded MTRRs and, read back from the PD entries, how each run of 2 MiB regions is mapped. On Hyper-V (issue #16): `MTRRs: enabled, default type UC; fixed ranges enabled; 8 variable ranges, 1 in use.`, `MTRR variable range 0: base=0x000000000000 mask=0x3fff00000000 WB` (the first 4 GiB), `MTRR fixed 0x00000..0xa0000: WB` and `0xa0000..0x100000: UC`; `EPT built: identity 0x0..0x80000000 (2 GiB), 6 table pages, 2 of them PTs` (the first 2 MiB, mixed WB/UC, and the data page's region `0x7ea00000`), every other 2 MiB region WB; EPTP `0x7eada01e`. - [x] Intercept the guest's writes to the MTRR MSRs, before an OS guest (issue #14). A guest WRMSR to an MTRR reached the CPU: the EPT types, copied at bring-up, no longer matched the guest's MTRRs, and since the CPU's MTRRs still set the memory types of Aleph0's own accesses in root operation, the guest could make the hypervisor's memory UC or WP. The MSR bitmap now intercepts every address an MTRR MSR can have (`IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE`, the 11 fixed-range MSRs, the PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK pairs of 32 variable ranges: 76; `IA32_MTRRCAP` is read-only and stays the guest's), and the guest reads and writes a copy of those the CPU has (`vmexit/guest_mtrrs.rs`), as KVM keeps `vcpu->arch.mtrr_state`, and gets #GP for the others, so none reaches the CPU even where `IA32_MTRRCAP` undercounts. `wrmsr` checks the value on its own, as the CPU does (`MtrrCapabilities::check`, KVM's `kvm_mtrr_valid` rules): a reserved type in any type field, or a reserved bit (DEF_TYPE bits 9:8 and 63:12, PHYSBASE bits 11:8, PHYSMASK bits 10:0, both from MAXPHYADDR up), gets the guest a #GP and leaves the copy unchanged, even in an MTRR not in use, which `Mtrrs::decode` alone would accept. Otherwise `MtrrState::write` updates the copy, and when an address changes type, `ept::retype` rewrites the entries that differ: the type bits of a 2 MiB page; a spare PT for a region whose pages come to differ; the PT of a region of one type again back to the spare ones; the protected page's region keeps its PT and access bits. INVEPT follows. `Ept::build` sets aside one spare PT per variable range plus one for the first 2 MiB (9 under Hyper-V), enough for every layout of contiguous masks; a region still left without one is mapped UC as one page, and `retype` takes the regions that need a PT in a second pass, after every PT it gives back is free. The guest's IA32_PAT, which the MSR bitmap passes through and which the VMCS did not switch (`pat=... (MSR, not switched)` above), would likewise have set the memory type of Aleph0's own accesses: `configure_controls` now turns on "save/load IA32_PAT" on VM exit and "load IA32_PAT" on VM entry when the CPU allows all three (`vmcs::pat_switch`, host-tested), which also writes `HOST_IA32_PAT` and `GUEST_IA32_PAT` for the first time on Hyper-V. Memory the UEFI memory map does not call RAM (MMIO, reserved memory, holes) is UC in EPT whatever the MTRRs say (`ept::EptTypes`, `ept::is_ram`): Hyper-V's MTRRs make the first 4 GiB WB, devices included, and the guest's copy can make any range WB; a region only partly RAM always has a PT, so no MTRR write needs a spare one for it. The vCPU statistics count MTRR reads and writes apart (`mtrr_read_exits`, `mtrr_write_exits`), and bring-up stops with `MtrrsChanged` if the CPU's MTRRs read differently after the guest. The test guest moves its last variable range to the 2 MiB at `0x200000` as UC, then 4 KiB, reads the mask back and restores the pair (11 more exits; the EPT violation becomes exit #22, the run 24 exits); the host tests replay that run through `decide`, `MtrrState` and `retype`. On Hyper-V: `Intercepted MTRR addresses (read and write): all 76. The guest reads and writes a copy of the 28 MSRs the CPU has (IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, 11 fixed-range MSRs and 8 variable ranges); the other 48 get #GP.`, `EPT built: identity 0x0..0x80000000 (2 GiB), 15 table pages, 2 of them PTs for 2 MiB regions mapped in 4 KiB pages and 9 spare PTs for the guest's MTRR writes`, `EPT RAM 0x000000000000..0x0000000a0000` and `EPT RAM 0x000000100000..0x000080000000`, UC for everything else. Hyper-V accepts the PAT controls: `host PAT load=true`, and the stop dump read `pat=0x7040600070406 (VMCS)` from `GUEST_IA32_PAT`. Exits #15, #17 and #18 wrote IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASK7 (`0x00003fffffe00800`, `0x00003ffffffff800`, `0x0`), each line ending `the CPU's IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASK7 stays 0x0000000000000000`, and `EPT 0x000000200000..0x000000400000` became `2 MiB pages, UC` (9 spare PTs left), `4 KiB pages (a PT each)` (8 left), then `2 MiB pages, WB` (9 left). The EPT violation was exit #22 and VMCALL #23 read back `rcx=0xda7a rdx=0x455054`; 24 exits with `mtrr_read_exits=3 mtrr_write_exits=7`, `MTRRs after the guest: the CPU's unchanged=true; the guest's copy restored=true.` and `SUCCESS`. With `-InjectNmi`: 26 exits, the NMI as exit #24, `NMIs: 1 reinjected, 1 handled by the guest`, `nmi_injections=1`, `SUCCESS`. The first run of this build stopped at VMCALL #23 instead, with RCX `0x7eabde98` (`DataPageMismatch`): the debug build's exit handler needs 21168 bytes of stack, the VM-exit stack had 16 KiB, and the data page lay right below it, so an exit had overwritten the seed. The exit stack is now 16 pages (64 KiB); after the guest, bring-up prints `VM-exit stack: 21168 of 65536 bytes used.` and stops with `VmExitStackFull` if the stack's lowest word was written, since nothing guards the page below it. The #GP path is host-tested only, like the other #GPs. See [docs/MTRR.md](docs/MTRR.md) section 7.
- [x] Map MMIO beyond the UEFI memory map in EPT (issue #20). - [x] Give Aleph0 its own host page tables, GDT, TSS and IDT (issue #22). - [x] Virtualize the running firmware in place (issue #21). Aleph0 ran a separate test guest, stopped it after its scripted VMCALLs and returned to firmware outside VMX, so nothing after it (boot manager, OS loader) ran as the guest. A default build now launches in place: `vmcs::launch_in_place` writes GUEST_RIP (the instruction after its VMLAUNCH), GUEST_RSP and GUEST_RFLAGS (IF included) in the asm block that runs VMLAUNCH, so the code after it goes on in VMX non-root operation and returns through `bring_up::run` (`GuestRun::Virtualized`, no teardown, no VMXOFF) and `main` to the firmware.
