`scripts/linux/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the first-boot Linux target: a pinned LTS kernel with the EFI stub,
# its command line and a busybox initramfs built in, as one file the firmware
# can start. For Linux or WSL; docs/LINUX_GUEST.md lists the packages it needs.
#
# Writes linux.efi, System.map and the final .config to run/linux/. Sources and
# the build tree go to $ALEPH0_LINUX_WORK (default ~/.cache/aleph0-linux), which
# must be on a Linux filesystem: the kernel tree has file names that differ only
# in case, which a Windows drive under /mnt would merge.
set -euo pipefail

KERNEL_VERSION=6.18.58
KERNEL_SHA256=069b19f9032c4dac8149ae4b6520c35debca0f42a9f6d52ee55ba6ca9b818013
BUSYBOX_VERSION=1.35.0
BUSYBOX_SHA256=6e123e7f3202a8c1e9b1f94d8941580a25135382b99e8d3e34fb858bba311348

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
out=$here/../../run/linux
work=${ALEPH0_LINUX_WORK:-$HOME/.cache/aleph0-linux}
src=$work/linux-$KERNEL_VERSION
build=$work/build-$KERNEL_VERSION
mkdir -p "$work" "$build" "$out"

# fetch URL SHA256 FILE: downloads FILE once, and checks it on every run.
fetch() {
    if [ ! -f "$3" ]; then
        curl -fL --retry 3 -o "$3.part" "$1"
        mv "$3.part" "$3"
    fi
    echo "$2  $3" | sha256sum --check --quiet || { rm -f "$3"; exit 1; }
}

fetch "https://cdn.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/v6.x/linux-$KERNEL_VERSION.tar.xz" "$KERNEL_SHA256" "$src.tar.xz"
fetch "https://busybox.net/downloads/binaries/$BUSYBOX_VERSION-x86_64-linux-musl/busybox" "$BUSYBOX_SHA256" \
    "$work/busybox-$BUSYBOX_VERSION"
if [ ! -d "$src" ]; then
    rm -rf "$src.part" && mkdir "$src.part"
    tar -xf "$src.tar.xz" -C "$src.part" --strip-components=1
    mv "$src.part" "$src"
fi

# The initramfs, as a gen_init_cpio list. /dev/console is a device node in it,
# so the kernel can open a console for /init and the build needs no root.
# init is listed from a copy: the list splits fields on spaces, and a Windows
# checkout's path (/mnt/c/Users/Jane Doe/...) can have one.
cp -p "$here/init" "$work/init"
cat > "$work/initramfs.list" <<EOF
dir /dev 0755 0 0
nod /dev/console 0600 0 0 c 5 1
dir /bin 0755 0 0
dir /proc 0755 0 0
dir /sys 0755 0 0
file /bin/busybox $work/busybox-$BUSYBOX_VERSION 0755 0 0
file /init $work/init 0755 0 0
EOF
echo "CONFIG_INITRAMFS_SOURCE=\"$work/initramfs.list\"" > "$work/initramfs.config"

(cd "$src" && scripts/kconfig/merge_config.sh -O "$build" arch/x86/configs/x86_64_defconfig \
    "$here/aleph0.config" "$work/initramfs.config")
# Kconfig drops a value whose dependencies are unmet, with only a warning.
missing=$(grep -hE '^(CONFIG_|# CONFIG_.* is not set$)' "$here/aleph0.config" "$work/initramfs.config" |
    grep -vxF -f "$build/.config" || true)
if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
    printf 'Not in the final .config:\n%s\n' "$missing" >&2
    exit 1
fi

make -C "$src" O="$build" -j"$(nproc)" bzImage
cp "$build/arch/x86/boot/bzImage" "$out/linux.efi"
cp "$build/System.map" "$build/.config" "$out/"
echo "Linux $KERNEL_VERSION: $(cd "$out" && pwd)/linux.efi"

```

`scripts/linux/init`:

```
#!/bin/busybox sh
# /init of the first-boot Linux target: prints what later issues need to know
# about the VM on the console (ttyS0, COM1), then starts a shell there. Every
# line ends in a newline, since read-serial.ps1 logs whole lines only.
/bin/busybox mount -t proc proc /proc
/bin/busybox --install -s /bin
mount -t sysfs sysfs /sys
mount -t devtmpfs devtmpfs /dev

echo "aleph0-linux: init"
echo "aleph0-linux: nproc $(nproc)"
echo "aleph0-linux: cmdline $(cat /proc/cmdline)"
# The same address as in System.map: nokaslr took effect.
echo "aleph0-linux: $(grep -w _text /proc/kallsyms)"
echo "aleph0-linux: clocksource $(cat /sys/devices/system/clocksource/clocksource0/current_clocksource)"
echo "aleph0-linux: $(grep -m 1 '^flags' /proc/cpuinfo)"
echo "aleph0-linux: iomem"
cat /proc/iomem
echo "aleph0-linux: uptime $(cat /proc/uptime)"
echo "aleph0-linux: shell"
exec setsid cttyhack sh

```

`scripts/read-serial.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Streams one of the test VM's COM ports to this console and to a log in
    run\: by default COM2, Aleph0's output, into run\serial.log.

.DESCRIPTION
    Hyper-V exposes a VM's COM port as a named pipe (configured by
    run-hyperv.ps1 with Set-VMComPort). Hyper-V is the pipe server; this
    script connects as the client and prints each line the hypervisor sends.

    Output written while no client is connected is dropped, so connect as
    soon as the VM starts. run-hyperv.ps1 does that automatically; run this
    script on its own to reattach to a VM that is already running.

    Requires an elevated PowerShell session (the pipe is only open to
    administrators). Reading ends when the VM turns off; Ctrl+C also stops it
    once the next line arrives.

.PARAMETER PipeName
    Pipe name without the \\.\pipe\ prefix. Must match run-hyperv.ps1:
    aleph0-com2 for Aleph0's output (the default), aleph0-com1 for the
    guest's COM1.

.PARAMETER LogName
    File in run\ the lines are saved to: serial.log by default; run-hyperv.ps1
    saves the guest's COM1 to guest-serial.log.

.PARAMETER Quiet
    Save the lines without printing them. run-hyperv.ps1 reads COM1 this way,
    so the console shows Aleph0's lines only.

.PARAMETER TimeoutSeconds
    How long to keep retrying while the VM is starting and the pipe does
    not exist yet.
#>
param(
    [string]$PipeName      = "aleph0-com2",
    [string]$LogName       = "serial.log",
    [switch]$Quiet,
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds   = 30
)

# See run.ps1 for why $ErrorActionPreference is not set to "Stop" globally.

$root    = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot   # this script lives in scripts/
$runDir  = Join-Path $root "run"
$logPath = Join-Path $runDir $LogName
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $runDir | Out-Null

$pipe = [System.IO.Pipes.NamedPipeClientStream]::new(
    ".", $PipeName, [System.IO.Pipes.PipeDirection]::InOut)

# The pipe only exists while the VM is running, so retry until it appears.
# run-hyperv.ps1 waits for this line before it starts the VM.
Write-Host "==> Waiting for \\.\pipe\$PipeName" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
while (-not $pipe.IsConnected) {
    try {
        # Waits up to 1 s for the pipe to appear; throws TimeoutException if
        # not. No sleep after it: the VM may start printing at once.
        $pipe.Connect(1000)
    } catch {
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 20
    }
    if (-not $pipe.IsConnected -and (Get-Date) -gt $deadline) {
        Write-Error "Could not connect to \\.\pipe\$PipeName within $TimeoutSeconds s. Is the VM running with COM1 attached?"
        $pipe.Dispose()
        exit 1
    }
}

Write-Host "==> Connected to \\.\pipe\$PipeName; logging to $logPath" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# One writer for the whole session. Add-Content opened and closed the file
# for every line, slow enough to fall behind a burst of output. AutoFlush
# keeps the file current for the -InjectNmi job, which reads it meanwhile
# (the writer shares the file for reading).
$writer = [System.IO.StreamWriter]::new($logPath, $false, [System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII)
$writer.AutoFlush = $true
$reader = [System.IO.StreamReader]::new($pipe, [System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII)
try {
    # ReadLine returns $null when Hyper-V closes the pipe (VM turned off).
    while ($null -ne ($line = $reader.ReadLine())) {
        if (-not $Quiet) { Write-Host $line }
        $writer.WriteLine($line)
    }
    Write-Host "==> Serial pipe closed (VM stopped)." -ForegroundColor Cyan
} finally {
    $reader.Dispose()
    $writer.Dispose()
    $pipe.Dispose()
}

```

`scripts/run-hyperv.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Builds the hypervisor and boots it in a Hyper-V Gen 2 VM with nested
    virtualization enabled, so VMX is actually exposed to the guest.

    Requires an elevated PowerShell session and the Hyper-V role installed.

.PARAMETER VMName
    Name of the Hyper-V VM to create/reuse.

.PARAMETER MemoryMB
    Static startup memory. Nested virtualization requires Dynamic Memory off.

.PARAMETER Release
    Builds the release profile instead of debug.

.PARAMETER PipeName
    Named pipe COM2, Aleph0's serial output, is attached to (without the
    \\.\pipe\ prefix). Streamed to this console and run\serial.log.

.PARAMETER GuestPipeName
    Named pipe COM1, the guest's serial port, is attached to. Saved to
    run\guest-serial.log without being printed.

.PARAMETER NoSerial
    Do not read the COM ports after starting the VM. Both stay attached, so
    read-serial.ps1 can connect later.

.PARAMETER TestGuest
    Builds the regression mode (Cargo feature test-guest): Aleph0 runs its
    built-in test guest, stops it after its scripted VMCALLs, leaves VMX
    operation and returns to firmware with SUCCESS. Without it, Aleph0
    virtualizes the running firmware in place and returns to it in VMX
    non-root operation.

.PARAMETER InjectNmi
    Gives the VM one vCPU, runs the test guest (-TestGuest), and, as soon as
    serial shows the guest resumed after its first VMCALL, injects an NMI
    with Debug-VM. Tests NMI exiting and reinjection; the result appears on
    serial.

.PARAMETER Features
    Cargo features to build with, comma-separated, for the test-only
    switches in Cargo.toml: host-fault-test (the exit handler faults on
    purpose), host-nmi-test (with -InjectNmi, the NMI arrives while Aleph0
    runs in VMX root operation), unexpected-exit-test (the guest stops at
    main VMCALL #1 as an unexpected exit), ept-misconfig-test (the guest's
    Local APIC read is an EPT misconfiguration, which stops it with a walk
    of the tables), forward-refusal-test (a forwarded WRMSR Hyper-V
    refuses, recovered in root operation), or trace-exits (every VM exit
    printed in full). All but host-fault-test, forward-refusal-test and
    trace-exits turn on test-guest themselves.

.PARAMETER ProcessorCount
    vCPUs to give the VM: 2 by default, 1 with -InjectNmi, which refuses any
    other count.

.PARAMETER Kernel
    A Linux EFI image, such as run\linux\linux.efi from
    scripts/linux/build.sh, to put on the ESP as \EFI\aleph0\linux.efi, next
    to Aleph0.

.PARAMETER WithoutAleph0
    Boots the -Kernel image directly: it becomes \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI in
    Aleph0's place, and Aleph0 is not built. Nothing writes COM2 then, and
    the kernel's console is COM1, so COM1 streams to this console (and
    run\guest-serial.log) instead. With -Harness instead of -Kernel: the
    harness runs on the firmware alone (its without-aleph0 feature), to check
    its steps after ExitBootServices without Aleph0.

.PARAMETER Harness
    Boots the ExitBootServices test harness (tools/ebs-harness) as
    \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI, with Aleph0 next to it as \EFI\BOOT\aleph0.efi.
    The harness starts Aleph0, runs as its guest, exits boot services,
    overwrites every page the OS may reclaim, then makes VM exits and idles
    (docs/RESIDENT.md). Its own lines go to COM1, run\guest-serial.log.

.PARAMETER SetVirtualAddressMap
    With -Harness: the harness also calls SetVirtualAddressMap after
    ExitBootServices (its set-virtual-address-map feature).
#>
param(
    [string]$VMName   = "Aleph0Test",
    [int]$MemoryMB    = 2048,
    [switch]$Release,
    [string]$PipeName = "aleph0-com2",
    [string]$GuestPipeName = "aleph0-com1",
    [switch]$NoSerial,
    [switch]$TestGuest,
    [switch]$InjectNmi,
    [string]$Features = "",
    [ValidateRange(1, 1024)]
    [int]$ProcessorCount = $(if ($InjectNmi) { 1 } else { 2 }),
    [string]$Kernel = "",
    [switch]$WithoutAleph0,
    [switch]$Harness,
    [switch]$SetVirtualAddressMap
)

# See run.ps1 for why $ErrorActionPreference is not set to "Stop" globally.

$espType = '{c12a7328-f81f-11d2-ba4b-00a0c93ec93b}'   # EFI System Partition GPT type

$root         = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot   # this script lives in scripts/
$buildProfile = if ($Release) { "release" } else { "debug" }
$efiSrc       = Join-Path $root "target\x86_64-unknown-uefi\$buildProfile\aleph0hypervisor.efi"
$harnessSrc   = Join-Path $root "target\x86_64-unknown-uefi\$buildProfile\ebs-harness.efi"
$runDir       = Join-Path $root "run"
$vhdPath      = Join-Path $runDir "aleph0-esp.vhdx"

# 0. Preconditions
$isAdmin = ([System.Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]::new(
    [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent())
).IsInRole([System.Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
if (-not $isAdmin) {
    Write-Error "This script must run from an elevated PowerShell session."
    exit 1
}
if (-not (Get-Command Get-VM -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Error "Hyper-V role not installed. Run: Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V -All"
    exit 1
}
# The script turns the VM off hard and replaces its disks, so it must only
# ever touch its own VM. Its disks live in run\: the ESP, and the
# differencing disk Hyper-V makes from it for a checkpoint.
$existingVm = Get-VM -Name $VMName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($existingVm) {
    $foreignDisks = Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName $VMName |
        Where-Object { -not "$($_.Path)".StartsWith("$runDir\", [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) }
    if ($foreignDisks) {
        Write-Error ("VM '$VMName' has disks outside ${runDir}: $(($foreignDisks | ForEach-Object Path) -join ', '). " +
            "Refusing to turn it off and reconfigure it; pass another -VMName.")
        exit 1
    }
}
# The NMI job triggers on a serial line; without the serial stream nothing
# writes serial.log, so the NMI would never be injected.
if ($InjectNmi -and $NoSerial) {
    Write-Error "-InjectNmi needs the serial stream; do not combine it with -NoSerial."
    exit 1
}
# Debug-VM may deliver the NMI to any vCPU, and only the one running Aleph0's
# guest turns it into a VM exit.
if ($InjectNmi -and $ProcessorCount -ne 1) {
    Write-Error "-InjectNmi needs one vCPU; do not combine it with -ProcessorCount $ProcessorCount."
    exit 1
}
if ($Kernel -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Kernel -PathType Leaf)) {
    Write-Error "Kernel image $Kernel not found; scripts/linux/build.sh builds run\linux\linux.efi."
    exit 1
}
if ($WithoutAleph0 -and -not ($Kernel -or $Harness)) {
    Write-Error "-WithoutAleph0 boots the -Kernel image or the harness; pass -Kernel or -Harness."
    exit 1
}
# The NMI job waits for a line only Aleph0 prints.
if ($WithoutAleph0 -and $InjectNmi) {
    Write-Error "-InjectNmi needs Aleph0; do not combine it with -WithoutAleph0."
    exit 1
}
# The harness runs as the guest of the firmware build of Aleph0, which the
# test guest's build is not, and it takes BOOTX64.EFI itself.
if ($Harness -and ($TestGuest -or $InjectNmi -or $Kernel)) {
    Write-Error "-Harness needs the firmware build of Aleph0, or none with -WithoutAleph0; do not combine it with -TestGuest, -InjectNmi or -Kernel."
    exit 1
}
if ($SetVirtualAddressMap -and -not $Harness) {
    Write-Error "-SetVirtualAddressMap is a harness option; pass -Harness."
    exit 1
}

# 1. Build, unless Aleph0 is not on the ESP at all
if (-not $WithoutAleph0) {
    $cargoArgs = @("build")
    if ($Release) { $cargoArgs += "--release" }
    # The NMI job waits for a line only the test guest's VMCALLs print.
    $cargoFeatures = @($Features -split ',' | Where-Object { $_ })
    if ($TestGuest -or $InjectNmi) { $cargoFeatures += "test-guest" }
    if ($cargoFeatures) { $cargoArgs += @("--features", ($cargoFeatures -join ',')) }
    Write-Host "==> cargo $($cargoArgs -join ' ')" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Push-Location $root
    cargo @cargoArgs
    $buildExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    Pop-Location
    if ($buildExit -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "cargo build failed (exit code $buildExit)."
        exit $buildExit
    }
    if (-not (Test-Path $efiSrc)) {
        Write-Error "Compiled binary not found at $efiSrc"
        exit 1
    }
}
if ($Harness) {
    $harnessArgs = @("build", "-p", "ebs-harness")
    if ($Release) { $harnessArgs += "--release" }
    $harnessFeatures = @()
    if ($SetVirtualAddressMap) { $harnessFeatures += "set-virtual-address-map" }
    if ($WithoutAleph0) { $harnessFeatures += "without-aleph0" }
    if ($harnessFeatures) { $harnessArgs += @("--features", ($harnessFeatures -join ',')) }
    Write-Host "==> cargo $($harnessArgs -join ' ')" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Push-Location $root
    cargo @harnessArgs
    $buildExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    Pop-Location
    if ($buildExit -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "cargo build of the harness failed (exit code $buildExit)."
        exit $buildExit
    }
}

try {
    # 2. Stop the VM and detach the old disk so the VHDX can be rebuilt
    $vm = Get-VM -Name $VMName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($vm -and $vm.State -ne 'Off') {
        Write-Host "==> Stopping $VMName" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Stop-VM -Name $VMName -TurnOff -Force -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    if ($vm) {
        Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName $VMName | Remove-VMHardDiskDrive -ErrorAction Stop
    }

    # 3. Rebuild the ESP VHDX from scratch. Simplest way to refresh BOOTX64.EFI:
    #    once the partition carries the ESP GPT type it no longer takes a drive letter.
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -ErrorAction Stop -Path $runDir | Out-Null
    if (Test-Path $vhdPath) {
        Dismount-VHD -Path $vhdPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction Stop $vhdPath
    }

    Write-Host "==> Creating ESP disk $vhdPath" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    New-VHD -Path $vhdPath -SizeBytes 256MB -Dynamic -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null

    $disk = Mount-VHD -Path $vhdPath -Passthru -ErrorAction Stop | Get-Disk
    try {
        Initialize-Disk -Number $disk.Number -PartitionStyle GPT -ErrorAction Stop
        # Formatted as basic data first: Format-Volume needs a drive letter, and an
        # ESP-typed partition will not take one. The type is set afterwards.
        $part = New-Partition -DiskNumber $disk.Number -UseMaximumSize -AssignDriveLetter -ErrorAction Stop
        Format-Volume -DriveLetter $part.DriveLetter -FileSystem FAT32 `
            -NewFileSystemLabel "ESP" -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null

        $bootDir = "$($part.DriveLetter):\EFI\BOOT"
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -ErrorAction Stop -Path $bootDir | Out-Null
        $bootImage = if ($Harness) { $harnessSrc } elseif ($WithoutAleph0) { $Kernel } else { $efiSrc }
        Copy-Item -Force -ErrorAction Stop -LiteralPath $bootImage -Destination (Join-Path $bootDir "BOOTX64.EFI")
        if ($Harness -and -not $WithoutAleph0) {
            # Where the harness loads Aleph0 from.
            Copy-Item -Force -ErrorAction Stop -LiteralPath $efiSrc -Destination (Join-Path $bootDir "aleph0.efi")
        }
        if ($Kernel) {
            $kernelDir = "$($part.DriveLetter):\EFI\aleph0"
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -ErrorAction Stop -Path $kernelDir | Out-Null
            Copy-Item -Force -ErrorAction Stop -LiteralPath $Kernel -Destination (Join-Path $kernelDir "linux.efi")
        }

        $part | Set-Partition -GptType $espType -ErrorAction Stop
    } finally {
        Dismount-VHD -Path $vhdPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }

    # 4. Create or reconfigure the VM
    if (-not $vm) {
        Write-Host "==> Creating VM $VMName" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        New-VM -Name $VMName -Generation 2 -MemoryStartupBytes ($MemoryMB * 1MB) `
            -NoVHD -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
        # No network adapter: nothing here needs one, and it keeps the nested setup simple.
        Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName $VMName | Remove-VMNetworkAdapter -ErrorAction Stop
    }

    Add-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName $VMName -Path $vhdPath -ErrorAction Stop
    # Secure Boot off: the .efi is unsigned. Boot straight off the ESP disk.
    Set-VMFirmware -VMName $VMName -EnableSecureBoot Off -ErrorAction Stop
    Set-VMFirmware -VMName $VMName -FirstBootDevice (Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName $VMName) -ErrorAction Stop
    # Nested virtualization requires static memory.
    Set-VMMemory -VMName $VMName -DynamicMemoryEnabled $false -StartupBytes ($MemoryMB * 1MB) -ErrorAction Stop
    Set-VMProcessor -VMName $VMName -Count $ProcessorCount -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions $true -ErrorAction Stop
    # COM ports -> named pipes. Gen 2 VMs have no COM ports in the UI; this
    # is the only way to attach them. Aleph0 prints on COM2; COM1 is the
    # guest's.
    Set-VMComPort -VMName $VMName -Number 1 -Path "\\.\pipe\$GuestPipeName" -ErrorAction Stop
    Set-VMComPort -VMName $VMName -Number 2 -Path "\\.\pipe\$PipeName" -ErrorAction Stop
} catch {
    Write-Error "Setup failed: $_"
    exit 1
}

# 5. Boot it and open the console (uefi::println writes to ConOut, i.e. the video console)
# A log left over from the previous run must not trigger the NMI job below,
# nor pass for this run's when a reader cannot connect.
$serialLog = Join-Path $runDir "serial.log"
Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue $serialLog, (Join-Path $runDir "guest-serial.log")

# With -InjectNmi, a background job waits until the guest has resumed after
# its first VMCALL (it then sits in its wait loop) and injects one NMI.
# read-serial.ps1 below writes the log the job watches. The job is started
# before Start-VM so its start-up cost cannot delay anything after boot: the
# injection is a race against the guest's wait loop.
$nmiJob = $null
if ($InjectNmi) {
    Write-Host "==> NMI injection armed: waiting for 'resuming the guest' on serial" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $nmiJob = Start-Job -ArgumentList $VMName, $serialLog -ScriptBlock {
        param($vmName, $logPath)
        # Load the module now so the first Debug-VM call is not slowed by
        # module auto-loading.
        Import-Module Hyper-V -ErrorAction Stop
        $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(120)
        while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
            if ((Test-Path $logPath) -and (Select-String -Path $logPath -SimpleMatch 'resuming the guest' -Quiet)) {
                Debug-VM -Name $vmName -InjectNonMaskableInterrupt -Force -ErrorAction Stop
                return "NMI injected into $vmName at $(Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss.fff')."
            }
            Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 200
        }
        return "No 'resuming the guest' line within 120 s; no NMI injected."
    }
}

# 6. Read both COM ports, with the readers waiting before the VM starts:
#    Hyper-V drops serial output written while no client is attached, and
#    Start-VM can return after Aleph0 has already printed its first lines.
#    Each reader runs as a job (in its own process, with this session's
#    elevation) and connects as soon as Start-VM creates its pipe. COM2,
#    Aleph0's output, streams to this console and run\serial.log; COM1, the
#    guest's, goes to run\guest-serial.log only. With -WithoutAleph0 nothing
#    writes COM2, so only COM1 is read, and it streams too. Ctrl+C stops the
#    streaming here; the jobs themselves end when the VM turns off.
function Start-SerialReader([string]$Pipe, [string]$Log, [switch]$Quiet) {
    Start-Job -ArgumentList (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "read-serial.ps1"), $Pipe, $Log, $Quiet.IsPresent -ScriptBlock {
        param($readerScript, $pipeName, $logName, $quiet)
        & $readerScript -PipeName $pipeName -LogName $logName -Quiet:$quiet
    }
}

$serialJob = $null
$guestSerialJob = $null
if (-not $NoSerial) {
    if (-not $WithoutAleph0) {
        $serialJob = Start-SerialReader -Pipe $PipeName -Log "serial.log"
    }
    $guestSerialJob = Start-SerialReader -Pipe $GuestPipeName -Log "guest-serial.log" -Quiet:(-not $WithoutAleph0)
    # A reader's first output is its "Waiting for" line, printed right before
    # it starts connecting.
    $readyDeadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(30)
    foreach ($job in @($serialJob, $guestSerialJob) | Where-Object { $_ }) {
        while ($job.ChildJobs[0].Information.Count -eq 0 -and
               $job.State -in 'NotStarted', 'Running' -and
               (Get-Date) -lt $readyDeadline) {
            Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 50
        }
    }
}

Write-Host "==> Starting $VMName" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Start-VM -Name $VMName
vmconnect.exe localhost $VMName

if ($serialJob) {
    Receive-Job -Job $serialJob -Wait -AutoRemoveJob
}
if ($guestSerialJob) {
    # Only its own status lines, unless -WithoutAleph0: otherwise it saves the
    # guest's lines without printing.
    Receive-Job -Job $guestSerialJob -Wait -AutoRemoveJob
}

if ($nmiJob) {
    Receive-Job -Job $nmiJob -Wait -AutoRemoveJob | ForEach-Object {
        Write-Host "==> $_" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    }
}

```

`scripts/run.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Builds the hypervisor, prepares an ESP disk layout, and starts QEMU with OVMF.

.PARAMETER Release
    Builds the release profile instead of debug.

.PARAMETER Clean
    Removes the esp/ folder before rebuilding it.
#>
param(
    [switch]$Release,
    [switch]$Clean
)

# $ErrorActionPreference is intentionally not set to "Stop": cargo/qemu write
# normal status text to stderr, and under "Stop" that gets treated as a
# terminating error whenever output is redirected or captured. Exit codes are
# checked explicitly after native commands instead.

$root      = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot   # this script lives in scripts/
$profile  = if ($Release) { "release" } else { "debug" }
$target    = "x86_64-unknown-uefi"
$efiSrc    = Join-Path $root "target\$target\$profile\aleph0hypervisor.efi"
$espDir    = Join-Path $root "esp"
$bootDir   = Join-Path $espDir "EFI\BOOT"
$ovmfDir   = Join-Path $root "ovmf"
$ovmfCode  = Join-Path $ovmfDir "OVMF_CODE.fd"
$ovmfVarsTemplate = Join-Path $ovmfDir "OVMF_VARS.fd"
$runDir    = Join-Path $root "run"
$ovmfVars  = Join-Path $runDir "OVMF_VARS.fd"
$serialLog = Join-Path $runDir "qemu-serial.log"

# 1. Build
Write-Host "==> cargo build $(if ($Release) { '--release' })" -ForegroundColor Cyan
if ($Release) {
    cargo build --release
} else {
    cargo build
}
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    Write-Error "cargo build failed (exit code $LASTEXITCODE)."
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

if (-not (Test-Path $efiSrc)) {
    Write-Error "Compiled binary not found at $efiSrc"
    exit 1
}

try {
    # 2. ESP disk layout
    if ($Clean -and (Test-Path $espDir)) {
        Write-Host "==> Cleaning $espDir" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Stop $espDir
    }

    Write-Host "==> Preparing ESP layout in $espDir" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -ErrorAction Stop -Path $bootDir | Out-Null
    Copy-Item -Force -ErrorAction Stop $efiSrc (Join-Path $bootDir "BOOTX64.EFI")

    # 3. OVMF firmware
    if (-not (Test-Path $ovmfCode) -or -not (Test-Path $ovmfVarsTemplate)) {
        Write-Error "OVMF_CODE.fd / OVMF_VARS.fd not found in $ovmfDir. Download them from rust-osdev/ovmf-prebuilt first."
        exit 1
    }

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -ErrorAction Stop -Path $runDir | Out-Null
    if (-not (Test-Path $ovmfVars)) {
        Write-Host "==> Copying writable OVMF_VARS.fd to $runDir" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Copy-Item -Force -ErrorAction Stop $ovmfVarsTemplate $ovmfVars
    }
} catch {
    Write-Error "File preparation failed: $_"
    exit 1
}

# 4. Locate the QEMU executable (may not be in this session's PATH yet)
$qemuExe = Get-Command "qemu-system-x86_64" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($qemuExe) {
    $qemuExe = $qemuExe.Source
} else {
    $fallback = "C:\Program Files\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe"
    if (Test-Path $fallback) {
        $qemuExe = $fallback
    } else {
        Write-Error "qemu-system-x86_64 not found in PATH or at $fallback."
        exit 1
    }
}

# 5. Launch QEMU. The first -serial is COM1, the second COM2. OVMF mirrors
#    its console to every serial port, COM2 included, so COM2 would show each
#    log! line twice: once from Aleph0, once from OVMF's console. COM1 shows
#    the console only, which every log! line reaches once, so the terminal
#    gets COM1. Aleph0's own serial output (COM2) goes to run\qemu-serial.log,
#    not run\serial.log, which a Hyper-V run's reader keeps open while its VM
#    stays on. Nothing reaches VMX under QEMU, so no line is serial-only.
Write-Host "==> Starting QEMU ($qemuExe); COM2 -> $serialLog" -ForegroundColor Cyan
& $qemuExe `
    -drive "if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=$ovmfCode" `
    -drive "if=pflash,format=raw,file=$ovmfVars" `
    -drive "format=raw,file=fat:rw:$espDir" `
    -net none `
    -serial stdio `
    -serial "file:$serialLog" `
    -machine q35

```

`src/bring_up/error.rs`:

```rs
//! Why bring-up stopped, and how that gets printed.

use uefi::Status;
use uefi::boot::MemoryType;

use crate::vmx;
use crate::vmx::apic::LocalApicError;
use crate::vmx::context_tables::{GdtError, TssError};
use crate::vmx::ept::EptError;
use crate::vmx::exit_bitmaps::ExitBitmapsError;
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::ExitReason;
use crate::vmx::guest::GuestMemoryError;
use crate::vmx::guest_state::GuestStateError;
use crate::vmx::host::HostError;
use crate::vmx::mtrr::MtrrError;
use crate::vmx::vmcs::VmcsError;
use crate::vmx::vmexit::{VcpuStats, VmExitStackError};
use crate::vmx::vmxon::VmxOnError;

use super::teardown::TeardownError;

/// Why bring-up stopped. Each step returns one of these, so the sequence
/// reads top to bottom with `?` and [`report_error`] prints the outcome.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BringUpError {
    Tss(TssError),
    Gdt(GdtError),
    VmExitStack(VmExitStackError),
    GuestMemory(GuestMemoryError),
    ExitBitmaps(ExitBitmapsError),
    VmxNotSupportedByCpu,
    VmxDisabledByFirmware,
    /// An MTRR MSR holds a value the CPU would refuse, or the MTRRs hold
    /// something Aleph0 cannot copy into EPT. Before VMXON.
    Mtrr(MtrrError),
    /// The CPU lacks EPT support Aleph0 needs, or building the EPT tables
    /// failed. Both happen before VMXON.
    Ept(EptError),
    /// The test guest could not read the Local APIC's registers in xAPIC
    /// mode: its page tables or EPT do not map their page to itself, EPT
    /// with UC. Before VMXON.
    LocalApic(LocalApicError),
    /// Building the page tables, GDT, TSS or IDT that VMX root operation
    /// runs on failed. Before VMXON.
    Host(HostError),
    VmxOn(VmxOnError),
    /// A VMCS step failed; `operation` names the step for the report.
    /// `instruction_error` is the VM-instruction error number of a
    /// VmFailValid, read when the error was created: after teardown it can
    /// no longer be read.
    Vmcs {
        operation: &'static str,
        error: VmcsError,
        instruction_error: Option<u32>,
    },
    /// Building or writing the guest state failed. For a VMCS failure,
    /// `instruction_error` is captured as for [`BringUpError::Vmcs`].
    GuestState {
        error: GuestStateError,
        instruction_error: Option<u32>,
    },
    /// GDTR, TR, the TSS base or IDTR of the context tables changed between
    /// activation and the launch. The VMCS guest fields were copied from the
    /// activated tables, so the guest would start on stale ones.
    ContextTablesChanged,
    /// The UEFI memory map, which the resident allocations are checked
    /// against, could not be read. Before the launch.
    ResidentMemoryMapUnavailable,
    /// The resident allocation at `address` lies in memory the OS may reuse
    /// after `ExitBootServices`: its memory-map region has type
    /// `memory_type`, or no region holds it (`None`). Before the launch.
    NotResident {
        address: u64,
        memory_type: Option<MemoryType>,
    },
    /// `count` resident allocations came after `vmx::page`'s list was full,
    /// so they could not be checked. Before the launch.
    ResidentAllocationsUnlisted(usize),
    /// `vmx::page` listed no resident allocation, not even the image copy,
    /// so the check would have checked nothing. Before the launch.
    NoResidentAllocations,
    /// The `ExitBootServices` event could not be created. Before the launch.
    ExitBootServicesEvent(Status),
    /// The guest stopped at exit `number`, which the exit handler did not
    /// resume: it does not handle that exit, or it is an expected VMCALL the
    /// handler could not step past. Its lines on serial say which.
    UnexpectedExit {
        number: u64,
        reason: ExitReason,
    },
    /// The CPU's MTRRs read differently after the guest than before: a
    /// guest write reached them instead of the guest's copy.
    MtrrsChanged,
    /// The exit handler wrote the lowest word of the VM-exit stack: it used
    /// all of it and may have run on into the memory below, which nothing
    /// guards.
    VmExitStackFull,
    /// The guest finished, but its exit statistics differ from what the
    /// test guest does (`guest::expected_stats`): an emulated exit is
    /// missing or came twice.
    UnexpectedExitStats(VcpuStats),
    /// VMRESUME failed after an exit the handler resumed.
    ResumeFailed {
        error: VmcsError,
        instruction_error: Option<u32>,
    },
    /// Leaving VMX operation failed. Returned only when nothing failed
    /// before teardown; otherwise that earlier error is returned and this
    /// one was printed when it happened.
    Teardown(TeardownError),
}

impl From<LocalApicError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: LocalApicError) -> Self {
        Self::LocalApic(error)
    }
}

impl From<TssError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: TssError) -> Self {
        Self::Tss(error)
    }
}

impl From<GdtError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: GdtError) -> Self {
        Self::Gdt(error)
    }
}

impl From<VmExitStackError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: VmExitStackError) -> Self {
        Self::VmExitStack(error)
    }
}

impl From<GuestMemoryError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: GuestMemoryError) -> Self {
        Self::GuestMemory(error)
    }
}

impl From<ExitBitmapsError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: ExitBitmapsError) -> Self {
        Self::ExitBitmaps(error)
    }
}

impl From<MtrrError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: MtrrError) -> Self {
        Self::Mtrr(error)
    }
}

impl From<EptError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: EptError) -> Self {
        Self::Ept(error)
    }
}

impl From<HostError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: HostError) -> Self {
        Self::Host(error)
    }
}

impl From<VmxOnError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: VmxOnError) -> Self {
        Self::VmxOn(error)
    }
}

/// Converts a guest-state failure, for use with `map_err`. Reads the
/// VM-instruction error number now, while the VMCS is still current.
pub(super) fn guest_state_error(error: GuestStateError) -> BringUpError {
    let instruction_error = match error {
        // SAFETY: a VmFailValid came from a VMX instruction in VMX operation,
        // and the VMCS is not cleared until teardown, after this runs.
        GuestStateError::Vmcs { error, .. } => unsafe { vmx::vmcs::instruction_error_for(error) },
        _ => None,
    };
    BringUpError::GuestState {
        error,
        instruction_error,
    }
}

impl From<TeardownError> for BringUpError {
    fn from(error: TeardownError) -> Self {
        Self::Teardown(error)
    }
}

/// Tags a VMCS failure with the step it came from, for use with `map_err`.
/// Reads the VM-instruction error number now, while the VMCS is still
/// current.
pub(super) fn vmcs_step(operation: &'static str) -> impl FnOnce(VmcsError) -> BringUpError {
    move |error| BringUpError::Vmcs {
        operation,
        error,
        // SAFETY: a VmFailValid came from a VMX instruction in VMX
        // operation, and the VMCS is not cleared until teardown, after this
        // runs.
        instruction_error: unsafe { vmx::vmcs::instruction_error_for(error) },
    }
}

/// Prints why bring-up stopped.
pub fn report_error(error: BringUpError) {
    match error {
        BringUpError::Tss(error) => log!("Context TSS allocation failed: {error:?}"),
        // Only this variant comes after LGDT/LTR; every other GdtError is
        // returned before the CPU's tables are touched.
        BringUpError::Gdt(GdtError::ActivationVerificationFailed) => {
            log!("Context GDT/TSS activation failed verification; the CPU may already use the new tables.")
        }
        BringUpError::Gdt(error) => log!("Context GDT/TSS setup failed: {error:?}; GDTR/TR unchanged."),
        BringUpError::VmExitStack(error) => log!("VM-exit stack allocation failed: {error:?}"),
        BringUpError::GuestMemory(GuestMemoryError::NotIdentityMapped {
            virtual_address,
            physical,
        }) => log!(
            "Guest memory setup failed: page {virtual_address:#018x} is mapped at {physical:#018x}, not identity-mapped."
        ),
        BringUpError::GuestMemory(error) => log!("Guest memory setup failed: {error:?}"),
        BringUpError::ExitBitmaps(error) => log!("Exit bitmap allocation failed: {error:?}"),
        BringUpError::VmxNotSupportedByCpu => log!("VMX not supported by this CPU."),
        BringUpError::VmxDisabledByFirmware => log!("VMX supported by CPU but disabled by firmware."),
        BringUpError::Mtrr(error) => log!("MTRR setup failed: {error}."),
        BringUpError::Ept(EptError::RangeTooLarge { end, limit }) => log!(
            "EPT setup failed: the memory map reaches {end:#x}, past {limit:#x}, the end of the guest-physical address space (MAXPHYADDR, at most the 48 bits a 4-level EPT walk translates)."
        ),
        BringUpError::Ept(error) => log!("EPT setup failed: {error:?}"),
        BringUpError::LocalApic(LocalApicError::GuestMapping { address, translation }) => log!(
            "The page tables the guest shares do not map the Local APIC's registers at {address:#x} to themselves: {translation:?}."
        ),
        BringUpError::LocalApic(LocalApicError::EptMapping { address, end }) => {
            log!("EPT does not map the Local APIC's registers at {address:#x} to themselves, UC: {end}.")
        }
        BringUpError::Host(error) => log!("Host environment setup failed: {error:?}"),
        BringUpError::VmxOn(error) => log!("VMXON failed: {error:?}"),
        BringUpError::Vmcs {
            operation,
            error,
            instruction_error,
        } => report_vmcs_error(operation, error, instruction_error),
        BringUpError::GuestState {
            error:
                GuestStateError::Vmcs {
                    field,
                    error: VmcsError::ReadbackMismatch { written, read, .. },
                },
            ..
        } => log!("Guest-state field {field:#06x} read back {read:#x}, but {written:#x} was written."),
        BringUpError::GuestState {
            error: GuestStateError::Vmcs { field, error },
            instruction_error,
        } => {
            log!("Guest-state field {field:#06x} failed:");
            report_vmcs_error("guest-state write", error, instruction_error);
        }
        BringUpError::GuestState { error, .. } => log!("Guest state invalid: {error:x?}"),
        BringUpError::ContextTablesChanged => {
            log!("Context descriptor tables changed after VMX/UEFI calls; the guest was not launched.")
        }
        BringUpError::ResidentMemoryMapUnavailable => {
            log!(
                "The UEFI memory map is unavailable, so the resident allocations went unchecked; the guest was not launched."
            )
        }
        BringUpError::NotResident {
            address,
            memory_type: Some(memory_type),
        } => log!(
            "The resident allocation at {address:#018x} is {memory_type:?}, which the OS may reuse after ExitBootServices; the guest was not launched."
        ),
        BringUpError::NotResident {
            address,
            memory_type: None,
        } => log!("The resident allocation at {address:#018x} is in no memory-map region; the guest was not launched."),
        BringUpError::ResidentAllocationsUnlisted(count) => log!(
            "{count} resident allocation(s) came after the list was full and went unchecked; the guest was not launched."
        ),
        BringUpError::NoResidentAllocations => {
            log!("No resident allocation was listed, not even the image copy; the guest was not launched.")
        }
        BringUpError::ExitBootServicesEvent(status) => {
            log!("The ExitBootServices event could not be created: {status:?}; the firmware was not launched.")
        }
        BringUpError::UnexpectedExit { number, reason } => log!(
            "Guest stopped at VM exit #{number}: reason={} ({}){}; Aleph0 did not resume the guest.",
            reason.basic,
            vmx::exit_decision::exit_reason_name(reason.basic),
            if reason.entry_failure { " [VM entry failed]" } else { "" },
        ),
        BringUpError::MtrrsChanged => {
            log!("The CPU's MTRRs changed while the guest ran: a guest write reached them, not its copy.")
        }
        BringUpError::VmExitStackFull => log!(
            "The exit handler used all {} bytes of the VM-exit stack and may have overwritten the memory below it.",
            vmx::vmexit::VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE,
        ),
        BringUpError::UnexpectedExitStats(stats) => log!(
            "Guest finished, but its exit statistics were {stats}; expected {}.",
            vmx::guest::expected_stats(&stats),
        ),
        BringUpError::ResumeFailed {
            error,
            instruction_error,
        } => report_vmcs_error("resume", error, instruction_error),
        BringUpError::Teardown(error) => log!("Leaving VMX operation failed: {error:?}."),
    }
}

/// Prints a VMCS failure with the VM-instruction error number captured when
/// it happened. Reads nothing from the VMCS: by now it may be cleared.
fn report_vmcs_error(operation: &str, error: VmcsError, instruction_error: Option<u32>) {
    match (error, instruction_error) {
        (VmcsError::VmFailValid, Some(code)) => {
            let name = vmx::vmcs::vm_instruction_error_name(code);
            log!("VMCS {operation} failed: {name} ({code})");
        }
        (VmcsError::VmFailValid, None) => {
            log!("VMCS {operation} failed: VmFailValid, error number unreadable");
        }
        (VmcsError::ReadbackMismatch { field, written, read }, _) => {
            log!("VMCS {operation} failed: field {field:#06x} read back {read:#x}, but {written:#x} was written.");
        }
        _ => log!("VMCS {operation} failed: {error:?}"),
    }
}

```

`src/bring_up/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! The bring-up sequence: everything `main` does between setting up output
//! and returning to firmware.
//!
//! The steps, in order:
//!
//! 1. Load a copy of the firmware's GDT with a TSS appended
//!    ([`activate_context_tables`]); the guest state copies TR, and VM entry
//!    refuses an unusable guest TR. The firmware's GDTR is recorded first,
//!    and put back on every return path once this step has succeeded: by
//!    `run` if a failure comes before VMXON, by step 7 after it.
//! 2. Allocate the VM-exit stack and the guest's pages, and check how the
//!    page tables map the guest pages.
//! 3. Detect VMX, read its capability MSRs and check EPT support
//!    ([`check_vmx_support`]), read the MTRRs, then build the EPT identity
//!    map with their memory types and the guest's data page read-only, with
//!    spare PTs for the guest's MTRR writes. Allocate the MSR and I/O
//!    bitmaps, which intercept every MTRR MSR, and give the exit handler the
//!    guest's copy of the MTRRs. Build what Aleph0 runs on after a VM exit
//!    ([`HostEnvironment`]): page tables mapping the same range, a GDT, a
//!    TSS with interrupt stacks, an IDT.
//! 4. Enter VMX root operation and create the VMCS.
//! 5. Check in the UEFI memory map that every resident allocation, the
//!    image copy included, lies in memory the OS keeps after
//!    `ExitBootServices` ([`check_resident_memory`]). Fill in the VMCS:
//!    controls, EPT pointer, exit bitmaps, host state, guest state
//!    ([`prepare_vmcs`]). Then check that none of this disturbed the host's
//!    descriptor tables, and stop if it did.
//! 6. Launch the guest with VMLAUNCH: the one `GuestKind::SELECTED` names.
//!    - The test guest ([`run_test_guest`]): `vmx::vmcs::launch` returns
//!      once the guest has stopped: after its last planned exit, or at an
//!      exit or failure the exit handler in `vmx::vmexit` does not handle.
//!      The host state the guest reaches through passthrough emulation
//!      ([`PassthroughState`]) is read before and after, and printed, and
//!      so are the CPU's MTRRs, which the guest must never reach.
//!    - The firmware ([`virtualize_firmware`]): the `ExitBootServices`
//!      event is created first (`resident::watch_exit_boot_services`), then
//!      `vmx::vmcs::launch_in_place` returns in VMX non-root operation, as
//!      the guest. `run` then returns to `main`, and `main` to the firmware,
//!      which keeps running virtualized. Step 7 does not run; a stop of the
//!      firmware halts in the exit handler.
//! 7. Leave VMX operation and restore the firmware's state
//!    ([`teardown::teardown`]). Runs whatever happened after VMXON
//!    succeeded (creating the VMCS, steps 5 and 6), except a firmware that
//!    now runs as the guest, so firmware gets the CPU back outside VMX
//!    operation unless VMXOFF itself fails. If VMXON or an earlier step
//!    failed there is nothing to leave, and only the firmware's GDTR needs
//!    loading again.
//!
//! Each step returns either what the CPU will keep using or a
//! [`BringUpError`]; `?` stops at the first failure and [`report_error`]
//! prints it. Before VMXON that failure goes straight back to `main` (with
//! the firmware's GDTR loaded again); after VMXON it still goes through
//! teardown first. Lines that only print state live in [`report`], so this
//! file reads as the sequence itself.

mod error;
mod report;
mod teardown;

pub use error::{BringUpError, report_error};

use uefi::boot::{self, MemoryType};
use uefi::mem::memory_map::MemoryMap;

use crate::resident::{self, memory};
use crate::vmx;
use crate::vmx::VmxCapabilities;
use crate::vmx::apic::{self, ApicBase, IA32_APIC_BASE, LapicMode};
use crate::vmx::context_tables::{GdtError, GdtRegion, TssRegion};
use crate::vmx::ept::{self, Ept, EptSupport, TypeTables};
use crate::vmx::exit_bitmaps::ExitBitmaps;
use crate::vmx::guest::{GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT, GuestMemory};
use crate::vmx::guest_state::{GuestEntry, GuestState};
use crate::vmx::host::{FirmwareSelectors, HostEnvironment};
use crate::vmx::msr::{IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE, VmcsControlMsrs};
use crate::vmx::mtrr::{MtrrError, MtrrRegisters, MtrrState};
use crate::vmx::page;
use crate::vmx::segment::DescriptorTable;
use crate::vmx::vmcs::{DesiredControls, GuestKind, GuestStop, VmcsRegion};
use crate::vmx::vmexit::{VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE, VmExitStack};
use crate::vmx::vmxon::VmxOperation;

use error::{guest_state_error, vmcs_step};
use teardown::FirmwareState;

/// How bring-up ended when everything went to plan.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum GuestRun {
    /// The test guest finished after `exits` VM exits, all of them handled,
    /// and VMX operation is left.
    Finished { exits: u64 },
    /// The firmware runs as the guest: the code that receives this runs in
    /// VMX non-root operation, and returns to the firmware virtualized.
    Virtualized,
}

/// Host state the guest reaches through passthrough emulation: real
/// hardware, not a copy. The guest saves and restores it, so it reads the
/// same before and after the guest's run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct PassthroughState {
    kernel_gs_base: u64,
    com1_scratch: u8,
}

impl PassthroughState {
    /// Reads the current values.
    fn read() -> Self {
        Self {
            // SAFETY: IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE exists on every 64-bit CPU, and
            // reading it has no side effect.
            kernel_gs_base: unsafe { vmx::msr::rdmsr(IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE) },
            // SAFETY: the COM1 scratch register, a byte with no effect on
            // the UART; reading it has no side effect. Aleph0 prints on
            // COM2, so this does not disturb its output.
            com1_scratch: unsafe { crate::port::inb(GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT) },
        }
    }
}

/// The GDT copy and TSS that bring-up and the test guest run on, plus the
/// descriptor-table state recorded right after they were activated, and the
/// firmware's GDTR from before. VMX root operation runs on
/// [`HostEnvironment`] instead.
struct ContextTables {
    _tss: TssRegion,
    _gdt: GdtRegion,
    gdtr: DescriptorTable,
    tr: u16,
    tss_base: u64,
    /// IDTR after activation. Activation does not touch the IDT, so this is
    /// also the firmware's IDTR.
    idtr: DescriptorTable,
    /// GDTR before activation. Teardown loads it again.
    firmware_gdtr: DescriptorTable,
}

// The CPU uses these pages while `run` is in progress, and some of them after
// it returns: the TSS through TR, and the VMXON region and VMCS if VMXOFF
// failed. Freeing them on drop would hand memory the CPU still uses back to
// UEFI, so none of them may implement `Drop`; this turns adding a `Drop` impl
// (or a field that needs dropping) into a compile error.
const _: () = assert!(
    !core::mem::needs_drop::<HostEnvironment>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<TssRegion>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<GdtRegion>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<VmExitStack>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<GuestMemory>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<Ept>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<TypeTables>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<ExitBitmaps>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<VmxOperation>()
        && !core::mem::needs_drop::<VmcsRegion>()
);

/// Activates the host tables, enters VMX operation, prepares the VMCS,
/// launches the guest, and, for the test guest, leaves VMX operation again.
///
/// Returns once the test guest has stopped, once the firmware runs as the
/// guest ([`GuestRun::Virtualized`], in VMX non-root operation), or at the
/// first failure. Once the host tables are active, every other return path
/// puts the firmware's GDTR back. If VMXON succeeded, it also puts back the
/// IDTR and interrupt flag and leaves VMX operation. The one exception is a
/// failing VMXOFF: the CPU then stays in VMX root operation with CR4.VMXE
/// set, and teardown prints that. The firmware guest keeps Aleph0's GDT
/// copy, TSS and CR4.VMXE.
///
/// Every region allocated here (TSS, GDT, VM-exit stack, guest pages, EPT
/// tables, host environment, exit bitmaps, VMXON region, VMCS) stays allocated, even after this
/// returns. None of these types implement `Drop`, so their pages are never
/// returned to UEFI. TR keeps pointing at the TSS (see `teardown`). All of
/// them are resident (`vmx::page`), so after a return to the firmware the
/// OS loses them too.
pub fn run() -> Result<GuestRun, BringUpError> {
    let context_tables = activate_context_tables()?;

    // Independent of VMX, so this runs and prints even under QEMU/TCG.
    report::segment_state();

    let entry = match enter_vmx(&context_tables) {
        Ok(entry) => entry,
        Err(error) => {
            // Nothing to leave yet, but the CPU still runs on Aleph0's GDT,
            // which firmware never knew about. IF is still 1 and the phase
            // is still boot services, so this needs no ordering care.
            // SAFETY: the firmware's own GDT, read before activation. Boot
            // services are still running, so it is still live.
            unsafe { vmx::segment::load_gdtr(&context_tables.firmware_gdtr) };
            return Err(error);
        }
    };
    let VmxEntry {
        vmexit_stack,
        guest,
        ept,
        host,
        bitmaps,
        controls,
        firmware,
        vmx_operation,
    } = entry;

    // From here on every path goes through teardown before returning.
    // SAFETY: VMXON succeeded in `enter_vmx`, so this CPU is in VMX root
    // operation; outside it the VMCS instructions would raise #UD.
    let vmcs = unsafe { VmcsRegion::create_current() }.map_err(vmcs_step("creation"));
    let result = match &vmcs {
        Ok(_) => launch_guest(&controls, &vmexit_stack, &guest, &ept, &host, &bitmaps, &context_tables),
        Err(error) => Err(*error),
    };
    // This already runs as the guest: the firmware gets the CPU back
    // virtualized, with no teardown and no VMXOFF.
    if let Ok(GuestRun::Virtualized) = result {
        return result;
    }
    // SAFETY: `vmx_operation` is this CPU's and `vmcs` its only VMCS; the
    // guest is not running (launch returned, or never happened); `firmware`
    // was read from the live tables before activation.
    let left = unsafe { teardown::teardown(vmx_operation, vmcs.as_ref().ok(), &firmware) };

    // A failure before teardown explains more than one during it; a
    // teardown failure was printed when it happened.
    match (result, left) {
        (Err(error), _) => Err(error),
        (Ok(_), Err(error)) => Err(error.into()),
        (Ok(run), Ok(())) => Ok(run),
    }
}

/// What exists once VMXON has succeeded, for the rest of [`run`].
struct VmxEntry {
    vmexit_stack: VmExitStack,
    guest: GuestMemory,
    ept: Ept,
    host: HostEnvironment,
    bitmaps: ExitBitmaps,
    controls: VmcsControlMsrs,
    firmware: FirmwareState,
    vmx_operation: VmxOperation,
}

/// Steps 2 to 4 up to the VMCS: allocates the VM-exit stack and the guest's
/// pages, checks VMX and EPT support, reads the MTRRs, builds the EPT
/// tables, the exit bitmaps and the host environment, and enters VMX root
/// operation. A failure here leaves the CPU outside VMX operation, so `run`
/// only has to put the firmware's GDTR back.
fn enter_vmx(context_tables: &ContextTables) -> Result<VmxEntry, BringUpError> {
    let vmexit_stack = VmExitStack::allocate()?;
    log!(
        "VM-exit stack allocated: top={:#018x} size={VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE}.",
        vmexit_stack.top()
    );

    // shortcut: the firmware guest gets the test guest's pages too, since
    // `Ept::build` protects their data page, and they are resident so that no
    // OS writes it; drop them once EPT protects a list of pages (hiding
    // Aleph0's pages, ROADMAP section 5).
    let guest = GuestMemory::allocate()?;
    log!(
        "Guest memory allocated: code={:#018x} ({} bytes copied) stack top={:#018x}.",
        guest.code_base(),
        guest.code_len(),
        guest.stack_top(),
    );
    log!(
        "Guest IDT at {:#018x} (limit {:#06x}): vector 2 -> NMI handler at {:#018x}.",
        guest.idt().base,
        guest.idt().limit,
        guest.nmi_handler(),
    );
    // SAFETY: boot services are still active.
    let mappings = unsafe { guest.check_mappings() }?;
    report::guest_mappings(&guest, &mappings);

    let (controls, ept_support) = check_vmx_support()?;

    // The guest's MTRRs start as the CPU's.
    let mtrrs = MtrrState::new(vmx::mtrr::read()?)?;
    let capabilities = mtrrs.registers().capabilities();
    report::mtrrs(mtrrs.mtrrs());
    // SAFETY: boot services are still active, and UEFI identity-maps
    // memory, which also makes the data page's address its GPA.
    let (ept, types) = unsafe {
        Ept::build(
            guest.data_page(),
            ept_support,
            mtrrs.mtrrs(),
            ept::spare_pts(capabilities),
        )
    }?;
    report::ept(&ept, &types, guest.data_page());
    let _local_apic = check_local_apic(&ept, &types, ept_support)?;
    // Test only: the guest's read of the Local APIC then meets a PDPT entry
    // the CPU refuses, so the run shows the EPT misconfiguration stop and
    // its walk on real VMX.
    #[cfg(feature = "ept-misconfig-test")]
    if let Some(registers) = _local_apic {
        // SAFETY: before VMLAUNCH: the CPU has never walked the tables.
        unsafe { types.misconfigure(registers) };
        log!(
            "ept-misconfig-test: the PDPT entry of GiB {:#x} is now W without R.",
            registers >> 30
        );
    }

    let bitmaps = ExitBitmaps::allocate()?;
    report::exit_bitmaps(&bitmaps, capabilities);
    vmx::vmexit::publish_guest_mtrrs(mtrrs, types);
    let hyperv = vmx::hyperv::Detection::read();
    report::hyperv(&hyperv);
    vmx::hyperv::publish(hyperv.offers_interface());

    // Every address the UEFI memory map reaches, which holds the image,
    // every allocation (the EPT tables included) and the firmware stack:
    // not the device space above it, which EPT maps for the guest only.
    // SAFETY: boot services are still active, and UEFI identity-maps memory.
    let host = unsafe { HostEnvironment::build(ept.memory_map_end(), FirmwareSelectors::read()) }?;
    report::host_environment(&host, vmx::cr::read_cr3());

    // Recorded before VMXON: once the guest runs, its VM exits clear IF, and
    // teardown turns interrupts back on only if firmware had them on.
    let firmware = FirmwareState {
        cr3: vmx::cr::read_cr3(),
        gdtr: context_tables.firmware_gdtr,
        idtr: context_tables.idtr,
        interrupts_enabled: teardown::interrupts_enabled(),
    };
    // SAFETY: `check_vmx_support` confirmed VMX support and enablement, and
    // nothing has entered VMX operation yet.
    let vmx_operation = unsafe { vmx::vmxon::enter_vmx_root_operation() }?;
    log!("Entered VMX root operation.");

    Ok(VmxEntry {
        vmexit_stack,
        guest,
        ept,
        host,
        bitmaps,
        controls,
        firmware,
        vmx_operation,
    })
}

/// Builds a GDT that adds a TSS descriptor to a copy of the firmware's GDT,
/// loads it with LTR, and records the resulting state for later checks.
fn activate_context_tables() -> Result<ContextTables, BringUpError> {
    // Before anything is loaded, so teardown can give firmware its own GDT
    // back.
    let firmware_gdtr = vmx::segment::read_gdtr();

    let tss = TssRegion::allocate()?;
    log!("Context TSS allocated at {:#018x}; TR not loaded yet.", tss.base());

    // SAFETY: the active GDTR is the firmware's, live and readable through
    // its limit, and nothing changes it while it is copied.
    let mut gdt = unsafe { GdtRegion::copy_active() }?;
    log!("Context GDT copied at {:#018x}.", gdt.base());

    let selector = gdt.append_tss_descriptor(&tss)?;

    // `activate` checks the TSS descriptor and the GDTR before loading them.
    // SAFETY: `ContextTables` keeps the GDT and TSS pages, which are never
    // freed; the copy keeps the firmware's descriptors, so the active
    // selectors stay usable; the firmware IDT is live; and this is the only
    // activation.
    unsafe { gdt.activate(&tss) }?;
    let prepared = gdt.prepared_gdtr().ok_or(GdtError::GdtrPreparationFailed)?;
    log!(
        "Context GDT and TSS activated and verified: base={:#018x} limit={:#06x} tr_selector={selector:#06x}.",
        prepared.base,
        prepared.limit,
    );

    Ok(ContextTables {
        gdtr: prepared,
        tr: selector,
        tss_base: tss.base(),
        idtr: vmx::segment::read_idtr(),
        firmware_gdtr,
        _tss: tss,
        _gdt: gdt,
    })
}

/// Checks that the test guest can read the Local APIC's version register,
/// and returns where it reads it. In xAPIC mode both the page tables the
/// guest shares and EPT must map the register page, device memory above the
/// UEFI memory map, to itself, EPT with UC. In any other mode there is no
/// register page: the guest skips its read, and this returns `None`.
fn check_local_apic(ept: &Ept, types: &TypeTables, support: EptSupport) -> Result<Option<u64>, BringUpError> {
    // SAFETY: IA32_APIC_BASE exists on every CPU with a Local APIC, which
    // every x86-64 CPU has, and reading it has no side effects.
    let apic_base = ApicBase(unsafe { vmx::msr::rdmsr(IA32_APIC_BASE) });
    if apic_base.mode() != LapicMode::Xapic {
        report::local_apic_skipped(apic_base);
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let registers = apic_base.address(support.rules.physical_address_bits);
    // SAFETY: boot services are still active, so the firmware's tables are
    // identity-mapped.
    let translation = unsafe { vmx::paging::walk_current(registers) };
    let walk = types.walk(ept.eptp(), registers);
    report::local_apic(apic_base, registers, walk.end);
    apic::check_registers(registers, translation, walk.end)?;
    Ok(Some(registers))
}

/// Detects VMX, reads the capability MSRs the VMCS controls are chosen from,
/// and checks that the CPU supports the EPT Aleph0 builds. Returns the MSRs
/// and what the CPU's EPT offers.
fn check_vmx_support() -> Result<(VmcsControlMsrs, EptSupport), BringUpError> {
    match vmx::detect() {
        VmxCapabilities::Supported => {
            log!("VMX supported and enabled by firmware.");
        }
        VmxCapabilities::NotSupportedByCpu => return Err(BringUpError::VmxNotSupportedByCpu),
        VmxCapabilities::DisabledByFirmware => return Err(BringUpError::VmxDisabledByFirmware),
    }

    // SAFETY: `detect` just confirmed VMX support.
    let controls = unsafe { vmx::msr::read_vmcs_control_msrs() };
    report::vmx_capabilities(&controls);

    let support = ept::check_support(
        controls.secondary,
        controls.ept_vpid_cap,
        vmx::cpuid::physical_address_bits(),
    )?;
    report::ept_support(support);
    Ok((controls, support))
}

/// Checks the resident memory, prepares the current VMCS for the guest
/// `GuestKind::SELECTED` names, checks the host tables, and launches the
/// guest. Returns once the test guest has stopped, or in VMX non-root
/// operation once the firmware runs as the guest.
fn launch_guest(
    controls: &VmcsControlMsrs,
    vmexit_stack: &VmExitStack,
    guest: &GuestMemory,
    ept: &Ept,
    host: &HostEnvironment,
    bitmaps: &ExitBitmaps,
    context_tables: &ContextTables,
) -> Result<GuestRun, BringUpError> {
    let kind = GuestKind::SELECTED;
    let entry = match kind {
        GuestKind::BuiltInTest => GuestEntry::At {
            rip: guest.code_base(),
            rsp: guest.stack_top(),
            idtr: guest.idt(),
        },
        GuestKind::Firmware => GuestEntry::InPlace {
            idtr: context_tables.idtr,
        },
    };
    check_resident_memory()?;
    prepare_vmcs(controls, vmexit_stack, ept, host, bitmaps, kind, entry)?;
    check_context_tables_preserved(context_tables)?;

    match kind {
        GuestKind::BuiltInTest => run_test_guest(vmexit_stack),
        GuestKind::Firmware => virtualize_firmware(),
    }
}

/// Checks, in the UEFI memory map, that every resident allocation
/// (`vmx::page`) lies in memory the OS keeps after `ExitBootServices`, and
/// prints each one's type. A `LOADER_*` or `BOOT_SERVICES_*` page here would
/// be reused by the OS while Aleph0 still needs it.
fn check_resident_memory() -> Result<(), BringUpError> {
    let map = boot::memory_map(MemoryType::LOADER_DATA).map_err(|_| BringUpError::ResidentMemoryMapUnavailable)?;
    let mut pages = 0;
    for allocation in page::resident_allocations() {
        let regions = map
            .entries()
            .map(|region| (region.phys_start, region.page_count, region.ty));
        let memory_type = resident::memory_type_at(regions, allocation.address);
        report::resident_allocation(allocation, memory_type);
        if memory_type.is_none_or(memory::is_reclaimable) {
            return Err(BringUpError::NotResident {
                address: allocation.address,
                memory_type,
            });
        }
        pages += allocation.pages;
    }
    // The image copy is always listed: an empty list means listing broke,
    // and the loop above checked nothing.
    if pages == 0 {
        return Err(BringUpError::NoResidentAllocations);
    }
    match page::unlisted_resident_allocations() {
        0 => {
            log!("Resident memory checked: {pages} pages, all kept by the OS after ExitBootServices.");
            Ok(())
        }
        unlisted => Err(BringUpError::ResidentAllocationsUnlisted(unlisted)),
    }
}

/// Creates the `ExitBootServices` event, then launches the firmware in
/// place: from VMLAUNCH on, this code is the guest. Returns
/// [`GuestRun::Virtualized`] in VMX non-root operation, or the launch's
/// failure in root operation, with the event closed again.
fn virtualize_firmware() -> Result<GuestRun, BringUpError> {
    // Before VMLAUNCH: once the firmware is the guest, every firmware call
    // can exit, and one Aleph0 does not handle stops it.
    let event =
        resident::watch_exit_boot_services().map_err(|error| BringUpError::ExitBootServicesEvent(error.status()))?;
    log!("ExitBootServices event created: its VMCALL will tell Aleph0 when boot services end.");
    log!("Launching the firmware in place with VMLAUNCH; its VM exits are reported on serial only.");
    // SAFETY: `prepare_vmcs` wrote the controls, the host state
    // (HOST_RSP/HOST_RIP at the live exit stack and handler) and the guest
    // state of this context (`GuestEntry::InPlace`); the exit stack, EPT
    // tables, host environment and exit bitmaps are never freed, and the
    // handler halts at a stop of the firmware (`GuestKind::Firmware`).
    match unsafe { vmx::vmcs::launch_in_place() } {
        Ok(()) => Ok(GuestRun::Virtualized),
        Err(stop) => {
            // Outside VMX operation its VMCALL would raise #UD inside
            // ExitBootServices.
            if let Err(error) = boot::close_event(event) {
                log!("ExitBootServices event not closed: {:?}.", error.status());
            }
            guest_result(stop)
        }
    }
}

/// Launches the test guest and checks its run once it has stopped: the
/// exit stack, the host state it reaches through passthrough emulation,
/// the CPU's MTRRs, and its exit statistics.
fn run_test_guest(vmexit_stack: &VmExitStack) -> Result<GuestRun, BringUpError> {
    log!("Launching the guest with VMLAUNCH; its VM exits are reported on serial only.");
    let before = PassthroughState::read();
    let mtrrs_before = vmx::mtrr::read();
    // SAFETY: `prepare_vmcs` wrote the controls, the host state
    // (HOST_RSP/HOST_RIP at the live exit stack and handler) and the guest
    // state; the exit stack, guest pages, EPT tables, host environment and
    // exit bitmaps are never freed.
    let stop = unsafe { vmx::vmcs::launch() };
    // SAFETY: the guest has stopped, so no exit handler runs on the stack.
    let stack_used = unsafe { vmexit_stack.used() };
    log!("VM-exit stack: {stack_used} of {VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE} bytes used.");
    report::passthrough_state(before, PassthroughState::read());
    let mtrrs_after = vmx::mtrr::read();
    // The guest has stopped, so no exit handler writes its MTRRs any more.
    let guest_mtrrs = vmx::vmexit::guest_mtrr_registers();
    report::mtrrs_after_guest(&mtrrs_before, &mtrrs_after, guest_mtrrs.as_ref());
    // Before the guest's own result: an overflow corrupts whatever lies below
    // the stack, and the guest's stop may only be its consequence.
    if stack_used == VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE {
        return Err(BringUpError::VmExitStackFull);
    }
    let run = guest_result(stop)?;
    // The guest has stopped, so no exit handler is counting any more.
    let stats = vmx::vmexit::vcpu_stats();
    if stats != vmx::guest::expected_stats(&stats) {
        return Err(BringUpError::UnexpectedExitStats(stats));
    }
    check_mtrrs_untouched(&mtrrs_before, &mtrrs_after)?;
    Ok(run)
}

/// Checks that the CPU's MTRRs read the same after the guest as before
/// (`before`, `after`): its MTRR writes went to its copy, never to the MSRs
/// that set the memory types of Aleph0's own accesses.
fn check_mtrrs_untouched(
    before: &Result<MtrrRegisters, MtrrError>,
    after: &Result<MtrrRegisters, MtrrError>,
) -> Result<(), BringUpError> {
    match (before, after) {
        (Ok(before), Ok(after)) if before == after => Ok(()),
        (Err(error), _) | (_, Err(error)) => Err(BringUpError::Mtrr(*error)),
        (Ok(_), Ok(_)) => Err(BringUpError::MtrrsChanged),
    }
}

/// Fills in the current VMCS: controls for a `kind` guest, EPT pointer, exit
/// bitmaps, host state, and guest state starting at `entry`. VM entry is not
/// attempted.
fn prepare_vmcs(
    controls: &VmcsControlMsrs,
    vmexit_stack: &VmExitStack,
    ept: &Ept,
    host: &HostEnvironment,
    bitmaps: &ExitBitmaps,
    kind: GuestKind,
    entry: GuestEntry,
) -> Result<(), BringUpError> {
    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current.
    unsafe { vmx::vmcs::self_test() }.map_err(vmcs_step("self-test"))?;
    log!("VMCS self-test passed: VMREAD returned what VMWRITE stored.");

    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current.
    unsafe { vmx::vmcs::configure_controls(controls, DesiredControls::minimal_64_bit_guest(kind)) }
        .map_err(vmcs_step("control setup"))?;
    log!("VMCS controls for the {kind:?} guest written and read back successfully.");

    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current. The EPT tables are never freed.
    unsafe { vmx::vmcs::set_ept_pointer(ept.eptp()) }.map_err(vmcs_step("EPT pointer setup"))?;
    log!(
        "VMCS EPT pointer {:#018x} (WB, 4-level) written and read back.",
        ept.eptp().raw()
    );

    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current. The bitmap pages are never freed.
    unsafe { bitmaps.write_to_vmcs() }.map_err(vmcs_step("exit bitmap setup"))?;
    log!("VMCS MSR and I/O bitmap addresses written and read back.");

    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current. The host environment's pages are never freed.
    unsafe { vmx::vmcs::configure_host_state(&host.vmcs_tables()) }.map_err(vmcs_step("host-state setup"))?;
    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current.
    let exit_controls = unsafe { vmx::vmcs::vmread(vmx::vmcs::fields::VM_EXIT_CONTROLS) }
        .map_err(vmcs_step("exit-control readback"))?;
    log!(
        "VMCS host fields written and read back; host PAT load={} EFER load={}; VM entry not attempted.",
        exit_controls & vmx::vmcs::fields::VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_PAT != 0,
        exit_controls & vmx::vmcs::fields::VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_EFER != 0,
    );

    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current. The exit stack and the handler stay in place for as long as
    // the guest can exit.
    unsafe { vmx::vmcs::configure_host_entry(vmexit_stack.top(), vmx::vmexit::entry_address()) }
        .map_err(vmcs_step("host entry address setup"))?;
    log!("VMCS HOST_RSP/HOST_RIP written and read back; VM entry not attempted.");

    // After the controls: they decide whether guest PAT/EFER fields exist.
    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current. The controls are written, and the host GDT is live and stable.
    let guest_state = unsafe { GuestState::from_current(entry) }.map_err(guest_state_error)?;
    // SAFETY: VMX root operation with the VMCS `run` created and made
    // current.
    unsafe { guest_state.write() }.map_err(guest_state_error)?;
    report::guest_state(&guest_state, entry);

    Ok(())
}

/// Turns the way the guest stopped into bring-up's result.
fn guest_result(stop: GuestStop) -> Result<GuestRun, BringUpError> {
    match stop {
        GuestStop::Finished { exits } => Ok(GuestRun::Finished { exits }),
        GuestStop::Unexpected { number, reason } => Err(BringUpError::UnexpectedExit { number, reason }),
        GuestStop::LaunchFailed {
            error,
            instruction_error,
        } => Err(BringUpError::Vmcs {
            operation: "launch",
            error,
            instruction_error,
        }),
        GuestStop::ResumeFailed {
            error,
            instruction_error,
        } => Err(BringUpError::ResumeFailed {
            error,
            instruction_error,
        }),
    }
}

/// Confirms that VMXON, the VMCS work, and UEFI calls left the context
/// GDTR, TR, TSS base, and IDTR as they were after activation. If anything
/// changed, stops before the launch: the guest-state fields in the VMCS
/// were copied from the activated tables.
fn check_context_tables_preserved(expected: &ContextTables) -> Result<(), BringUpError> {
    let gdtr = vmx::segment::read_gdtr();
    let tr = vmx::segment::read_tr();
    let idtr = vmx::segment::read_idtr();
    let same_gdtr = gdtr == expected.gdtr;
    let same_idtr = idtr == expected.idtr;
    let same_tss_base = same_gdtr && tr == expected.tr && {
        // SAFETY: `gdtr` is Aleph0's own GDT (`same_gdtr`), live and never
        // freed.
        unsafe { vmx::segment::segment_base_from_gdt(&gdtr, tr) == expected.tss_base }
    };

    if same_gdtr && same_idtr && same_tss_base {
        log!("Context GDTR, TR, TSS base and IDTR preserved after VMX/UEFI calls.");
        Ok(())
    } else {
        log!("WARNING: Context descriptor state changed after VMX/UEFI calls.");
        log!(
            "Expected GDTR={:?} TR={:#06x} TSS={:#018x} IDTR={:?}",
            expected.gdtr,
            expected.tr,
            expected.tss_base,
            expected.idtr,
        );
        log!("Actual GDTR={gdtr:?} TR={tr:#06x} IDTR={idtr:?} TSS base matches={same_tss_base}");
        Err(BringUpError::ContextTablesChanged)
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Bring-up lines that only print state. Kept apart from the sequence in
//! `mod.rs`, so that file reads as the steps themselves.
//!
//! Nothing here changes CPU state or can fail.

use uefi::boot::MemoryType;

use super::PassthroughState;
use crate::vmx;
use crate::vmx::apic::{ApicBase, LAPIC_VERSION};

/// Prints the segmentation state of the context tables, which the guest
/// state copies and the host GDT keeps the selectors of.
///
/// TR is the one to watch: VM entry rejects an unusable guest TR.
pub(super) fn segment_state() {
    // SAFETY: the context GDT is live (activated by bring-up, never freed), and
    // UEFI runs in long mode.
    let state = unsafe { vmx::segment::read_all() };

    log!(
        "segments: cs={:#06x} ss={:#06x} ds={:#06x} es={:#06x} fs={:#06x} gs={:#06x} tr={:#06x}",
        state.cs,
        state.ss,
        state.ds,
        state.es,
        state.fs,
        state.gs,
        state.tr,
    );
    log!(
        "bases:    fs={:#018x} gs={:#018x} tr={:#018x}",
        state.fs_base,
        state.gs_base,
        state.tr_base,
    );
    log!(
        "gdtr:     base={:#018x} limit={:#06x}",
        state.gdtr.base,
        state.gdtr.limit,
    );
    log!(
        "idtr:     base={:#018x} limit={:#06x}",
        state.idtr.base,
        state.idtr.limit,
    );

    if state.tr == 0 {
        log!("WARNING: TR is 0; VM entry would reject this host state.");
    }
}

/// Prints the VMX capability MSRs: IA32_VMX_BASIC; for each of the four
/// control fields and the secondary controls, which bits must be 1 (low
/// half) and may be 1 (high half); and IA32_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP.
pub(super) fn vmx_capabilities(controls: &VmcsControlMsrs) {
    log!(
        "VMX BASIC={:#018x}; true controls={}",
        controls.basic,
        controls.basic & vmx::msr::VMX_BASIC_TRUE_CONTROLS != 0,
    );
    for (name, capability) in [
        ("pin", controls.pinbased),
        ("primary", controls.primary),
        ("exit", controls.exit),
        ("entry", controls.entry),
    ] {
        log!(
            "VMX {name}: required={:#010x} allowed={:#010x}",
            capability.required(),
            capability.allowed(),
        );
    }
    log!(
        "VMX secondary: required={:#010x} allowed={:#010x}; EPT/VPID capabilities={:#018x}",
        controls.secondary.required(),
        controls.secondary.allowed(),
        controls.ept_vpid_cap,
    );
}

/// Prints the MTRRs [`vmx::mtrr::read`] decoded: whether they are on, the
/// default type, each variable range in use, and the types the fixed ranges
/// give the first MiB.
pub(super) fn mtrrs(mtrrs: &Mtrrs) {
    log!("MTRRs: {mtrrs}.");
    let Mtrrs::Enabled(enabled) = mtrrs else {
        return;
    };
    for range in enabled.variable_ranges() {
        log!("MTRR {range}");
    }
    if enabled.fixed_enabled() {
        for run in mtrrs.runs(vmx::mtrr::FIXED_END, vmx::page::PAGE_SIZE as u64) {
            log!("MTRR fixed {:#07x}..{:#07x}: {}", run.start, run.end, run.type_name());
        }
    }
}

/// Prints what the CPU's EPT offers: what Aleph0 requires of it, and what
/// the map may use.
pub(super) fn ept_support(support: EptSupport) {
    log!(
        "EPT supported: 4-level walk, WB, 2 MiB pages, INVEPT {}; 1 GiB pages={}; MAXPHYADDR {} bits.",
        support.invept.name(),
        support.rules.huge_pages,
        support.rules.physical_address_bits,

}

/// Prints the EPT identity map [`Ept::build`] made, and how its entries
/// (`types`) map each run of it: read back from the entries, so the lines
/// show what the CPU walks.
pub(super) fn ept(ept: &Ept, types: &TypeTables, data_page: u64) {
    let layout = ept.layout();
    log!(
        "EPT built: identity 0x0..{:#x} ({} GiB), {} table pages: {} PDPT(s); {} PD(s), for 0x0..{:#x}, with {} PTs for 2 MiB regions mapped in 4 KiB pages and {} spare PTs for the guest's MTRR writes; {} GiB above as 1 GiB pages; data page {data_page:#018x} read-only (R=1 W=0 X=0).",
        ept.end(),
        ept.end() >> 30,
        ept.table_pages(),
        layout.pdpts(),
        layout.pd_gibs(),
        layout.pd_end(),
        ept.split_regions(),
        ept.spare_pts(),
        layout.huge_gibs(),
    );
    let ram = types.ram().ranges();
    log!(
        "EPT memory types: the MTRRs' for the {} RAM range(s) of the UEFI memory map, UC for everything else (MMIO, reserved memory, holes).",
        ram.len()
    );
    for &(start, end) in ram {
        log!("EPT RAM {start:#014x}..{end:#014x}");
    }
    for run in types.region_runs(0, ept.end()) {
        log!("EPT {:#014x}..{:#014x}: {}", run.start, run.end, run.mapping);
    }
}

/// Prints IA32_APIC_BASE and how EPT maps the Local APIC's register page at
```
