`src/vmx/ept/walk.rs`:

```rs
//! Reading the EPT tables back the way the CPU walks them: what it refuses
//! in an entry ([`check_entry`]), and the path of one GPA from the EPTP down
//! ([`walk`]).
//!
//! An EPT misconfiguration (exit reason 49) is an entry the CPU refuses to
//! use at all; an EPT violation (reason 48) an access the entries do not
//! allow, or a GPA nothing maps. Aleph0's map allows every access but one
//! (`Ept::build`), so either exit means the map is wrong, and the exit
//! handler prints the walk: every entry on the GPA's path, what the CPU
//! refuses in it, and how the walk ended. KVM prints the same hierarchy for
//! a reserved-bit fault on its own EPT entries (`get_mmio_spte`: "reserved
//! bits set on MMU-present spte ... hierarchy"), from the same rules
//! (`__reset_rsvds_bits_mask_ep` and `is_rsvd_spte`).
//!
//! Both are pure. [`walk`] reads entries through a function the caller
//! gives it, which returns `None` for an address outside the tables, so a
//! corrupt table pointer is reported, never followed.

use core::fmt;

use super::level::{Level, Pd, Pdpt, Pml4, Pt};
use super::{
    ADDRESS_MASK, EPT_EXECUTE, EPT_READ, EPT_RWX, EPT_WRITE, EntryRules, Eptp, LARGE_PAGE, MEMORY_TYPE_BITS,
    MEMORY_TYPE_SHIFT, WALK_ADDRESS_BITS, leaf_memory_type,
};
use crate::vmx::mtrr::MemoryType;

/// A table level of the walk, from the root down.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WalkLevel {
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

impl WalkLevel {
    /// The level's name: "PML4", "PDPT", "PD" or "PT".
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Pml4 => Pml4::NAME,
            Self::Pdpt => Pdpt::NAME,
            Self::Pd => Pd::NAME,
            Self::Pt => Pt::NAME,
        }
    }

    /// Index of `gpa`'s entry in a table of this level.
    pub fn index(self, gpa: u64) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Pml4 => Pml4::index(gpa),
            Self::Pdpt => Pdpt::index(gpa),
            Self::Pd => Pd::index(gpa),
            Self::Pt => Pt::index(gpa),
        }
    }

    /// The level of the table an entry here points to; `None` for a PT,
    /// whose entries always map a page.
    fn below(self) -> Option<Self> {
        match self {
            Self::Pml4 => Some(Self::Pdpt),
            Self::Pdpt => Some(Self::Pd),
            Self::Pd => Some(Self::Pt),
            Self::Pt => None,
        }
    }

    /// Whether the entry `raw` at this level maps a page itself: every PT
    /// entry, and a PDPT or PD entry with bit 7 set. A PML4 entry never
    /// does: bit 7 is reserved there.
    fn is_leaf(self, raw: u64) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Pml4 => false,
            Self::Pdpt | Self::Pd => raw & LARGE_PAGE != 0,
            Self::Pt => true,
        }
    }

    /// Bytes a page this level's entry maps: 4 KiB at a PT, 2 MiB at a PD,
    /// 1 GiB at a PDPT.
    fn page_size(self) -> u64 {
        let shift = match self {
            Self::Pml4 => Pml4::SHIFT,
            Self::Pdpt => Pdpt::SHIFT,
            Self::Pd => Pd::SHIFT,
            Self::Pt => Pt::SHIFT,
        };
        1 << shift
    }
}

/// Bits `low..=high` set, as KVM's `rsvd_bits`.
const fn bits(low: u32, high: u32) -> u64 {
    (u64::MAX >> (63 - high)) & (u64::MAX << low)
}

/// The bits an entry at `level` must keep 0: one that points to a table,
/// or with `leaf` one that maps a page. These are KVM's EPT
/// `rsvd_bits_mask` (`__reset_rsvds_bits_mask_ep`), from the formats in the
/// Intel SDM (Vol. 3C, "EPT Translation Mechanism").
fn reserved_bits(level: WalkLevel, leaf: bool, rules: EntryRules) -> u64 {
    // Address bits from MAXPHYADDR up to 51, at every level.
    let address = match rules.physical_address_bits {
        bits_used @ 0..=51 => bits(u32::from(bits_used), 51),
        _ => 0,
    };
    address
        | match (level, leaf) {
            // No memory type, no IPAT and no page size in a PML4 entry.
            (WalkLevel::Pml4, _) => bits(3, 7),
            // No memory type and no IPAT in an entry pointing to a table.
            (WalkLevel::Pdpt | WalkLevel::Pd, false) => bits(3, 6),
            // A 1 GiB page's address bits below its alignment, and the page
            // size bit itself on a CPU without 1 GiB pages.
            (WalkLevel::Pdpt, true) => bits(12, 29) | if rules.huge_pages { 0 } else { LARGE_PAGE },
            // A 2 MiB page's address bits below its alignment. 2 MiB pages
            // themselves are allowed: `check_support` requires them.
            (WalkLevel::Pd, true) => bits(12, 20),
            (WalkLevel::Pt, _) => 0,
        }
}

/// An access an entry's bits 2:0 may not allow (KVM's `bad_mt_xwr` for its
/// XWR part).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BadAccess {
    /// W = 1 with R = 0: 010b or 110b.
    WriteWithoutRead,
    /// X = 1 with R = W = 0, 100b, on a CPU without execute-only pages
    /// ([`EntryRules::execute_only`]).
    ExecuteOnly,
}

/// What the CPU refuses in one EPT entry ([`check_entry`]): any of it is an
/// EPT misconfiguration once a walk reaches the entry (Intel SDM Vol. 3C,
/// "EPT Misconfigurations").
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct EntryFaults {
    /// The bits set that the entry's level reserves.
    pub reserved_bits: u64,
    /// An access bits 2:0 may not allow.
    pub bad_access: Option<BadAccess>,
    /// A page's memory type (bits 5:3) when it is a reserved value: 2, 3 or
    /// 7.
    pub reserved_memory_type: Option<u8>,
}

impl EntryFaults {
    /// Whether the CPU uses the entry as it is.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        *self == Self::default()
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for EntryFaults {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return f.write_str("ok");
        }
        let mut separator = "";
        if self.reserved_bits != 0 {
            write!(f, "reserved bits {:#x} set", self.reserved_bits)?;
            separator = "; ";
        }
        if let Some(access) = self.bad_access {
            let what = match access {
                BadAccess::WriteWithoutRead => "write without read",
                BadAccess::ExecuteOnly => "execute-only, which this CPU does not allow",
            };
            write!(f, "{separator}{what}")?;
            separator = "; ";
        }
        if let Some(memory_type) = self.reserved_memory_type {
            write!(f, "{separator}reserved memory type {memory_type}")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// What the CPU refuses in `raw`, an entry at `level`, on a CPU with
/// `rules`: KVM's `is_rsvd_spte`. Nothing for an entry with R = W = X = 0:
/// that one is not present, and a walk reaching it is an EPT violation, not
/// a misconfiguration. (Mode-based execute control, which would make bit 10
/// an execute bit too, is off.)
pub fn check_entry(raw: u64, level: WalkLevel, rules: EntryRules) -> EntryFaults {
    let access = raw & EPT_RWX;
    if access == 0 {
        return EntryFaults::default();
    }
    let leaf = level.is_leaf(raw);
    let bad_access = if access & EPT_WRITE != 0 && access & EPT_READ == 0 {
        Some(BadAccess::WriteWithoutRead)
    } else if access == EPT_EXECUTE && !rules.execute_only {
        Some(BadAccess::ExecuteOnly)
    } else {
        None
    };
    // Only a page has a memory type; in an entry pointing to a table the
    // same bits are reserved ones.
    let memory_type = ((raw >> MEMORY_TYPE_SHIFT) & MEMORY_TYPE_BITS) as u8;
    EntryFaults {
        reserved_bits: raw & reserved_bits(level, leaf, rules),
        bad_access,
        reserved_memory_type: (leaf && MemoryType::from_raw(memory_type).is_none()).then_some(memory_type),
    }
}

/// One entry a [`walk`] read.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WalkedEntry {
    pub level: WalkLevel,
    /// Its index in its table.
    pub index: usize,
    /// Its physical address.
    pub address: u64,
    pub raw: u64,
    /// What the CPU refuses in it.
    pub faults: EntryFaults,
}

/// How a [`walk`] ended.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WalkEnd {
    /// A page of `size` bytes maps the GPA to `hpa`, allowing `access`
    /// (R, W, X in bits 2:0), of `memory_type`.
    Mapped {
        hpa: u64,
        size: u64,
        access: u64,
        memory_type: MemoryType,
    },
    /// The last entry has R = W = X = 0: nothing maps the GPA.
    NotPresent,
    /// The last entry is one the CPU refuses: an EPT misconfiguration.
    Misconfigured,
    /// The last entry points to `table` (or the EPTP does, with no entry
    /// read), which is not one of the tables: not followed.
    OutsideTables { table: u64 },
    /// The GPA has a bit set above the 48 a 4-level walk translates, which
    /// a CPU whose MAXPHYADDR is larger lets the guest use: nothing maps
    /// it, and no entry is read.
    BeyondWalk,
}

impl fmt::Display for WalkEnd {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match *self {
            Self::Mapped {
                hpa,
                size,
                access,
                memory_type,
            } => {
                let size = match size {
                    0x1000 => "4 KiB",
                    0x20_0000 => "2 MiB",
                    _ => "1 GiB",
                };
                write!(
                    f,
                    "mapped to HPA {hpa:#x} by a {size} page, {}, R={} W={} X={}",
                    memory_type.name(),
                    access & EPT_READ,
                    (access & EPT_WRITE) >> 1,
                    (access & EPT_EXECUTE) >> 2,
                )
            }
            Self::NotPresent => f.write_str("not present: nothing maps the GPA"),
            Self::Misconfigured => f.write_str("the CPU refuses the last entry: an EPT misconfiguration"),
            Self::OutsideTables { table } => {
                write!(f, "points to {table:#x}, none of Aleph0's EPT tables: not followed")
            }
            Self::BeyondWalk => f.write_str("beyond the 48 bits a 4-level walk translates: nothing maps the GPA"),
        }
    }
}

/// The path of one GPA through the tables ([`walk`]).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct EptWalk {
    pub gpa: u64,
    entries: [Option<WalkedEntry>; 4],
    pub end: WalkEnd,
}

impl EptWalk {
    /// The entries the walk read, from the PML4 down.
    pub fn entries(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &WalkedEntry> {
        self.entries.iter().flatten()
    }
}

/// Walks `gpa` through the tables `eptp` names, as the CPU does: one entry
/// per level from the PML4 down, until one maps a page, is not present, or
/// is one the CPU refuses by `rules` ([`check_entry`]). `read` returns the
/// 8-byte entry at a physical address, or `None` for an address outside
/// the tables, where the walk stops instead of reading on.
pub fn walk(eptp: Eptp, gpa: u64, rules: EntryRules, read: impl Fn(u64) -> Option<u64>) -> EptWalk {
    let mut entries = [None; 4];
    // The levels index bits 47:12 only: walked, such a GPA would alias one
    // 2^48 lower.
    if gpa >> WALK_ADDRESS_BITS != 0 {
        return EptWalk {
            gpa,
            entries,
            end: WalkEnd::BeyondWalk,
        };
    }
    let mut table = eptp.pml4();
    let mut level = WalkLevel::Pml4;
    for slot in &mut entries {
        let index = level.index(gpa);
        let address = table + (index * size_of::<u64>()) as u64;
        let Some(raw) = read(address) else {
            return EptWalk {
                gpa,
                entries,
                end: WalkEnd::OutsideTables { table },
            };
        };
        let faults = check_entry(raw, level, rules);
        *slot = Some(WalkedEntry {
            level,
            index,
            address,
            raw,
            faults,
        });
        let end = if raw & EPT_RWX == 0 {
            Some(WalkEnd::NotPresent)
        } else if !faults.is_empty() {
            Some(WalkEnd::Misconfigured)
        } else if level.is_leaf(raw) {
            let size = level.page_size();
            // `check_entry` found no reserved type, so there is one; a page
            // without one would be a misconfiguration all the same.
            Some(
                leaf_memory_type(raw).map_or(WalkEnd::Misconfigured, |memory_type| WalkEnd::Mapped {
                    hpa: (raw & ADDRESS_MASK & !(size - 1)) | (gpa & (size - 1)),
                    size,
                    access: raw & EPT_RWX,
                    memory_type,
                }),
            )
        } else {
            None
        };
        if let Some(end) = end {
            return EptWalk { gpa, entries, end };
        }
        table = raw & ADDRESS_MASK;
        level = level.below().expect("a PT entry always maps a page");
    }
    unreachable!("a PT entry always ends the walk")
}

`src/vmx/exit_bitmaps.rs`:

```rs
//! The MSR bitmap and the two I/O bitmaps: which guest RDMSR/WRMSR and
//! IN/OUT exit to Aleph0.
//!
//! With "use MSR bitmaps" (primary control bit 28) RDMSR/WRMSR exit only for
//! MSRs whose bit is set, and with "use I/O bitmaps" (bit 25) IN/OUT exit
//! only for ports whose bit is set. Everything else reaches the hardware
//! directly. That is a correct passthrough even for MSRs whose guest value
//! is a VMCS field: while the guest runs, the CPU holds the guest's value.
//! It keeps the guest's value away from Aleph0 only where VM exit loads the
//! host's back: IA32_PAT when the CPU allows the controls that switch it
//! (`vmcs::configure_controls`), but not IA32_EFER yet, whose bits other
//! than LME and LMA stay as the guest wrote them.
//!
//! ```text
//! MSR bitmap, one 4 KiB page (Intel SDM Vol. 3C, "MSR-Bitmap Address"):
//! offset 0x000  read,  MSR 0x00000000..=0x00001FFF
//! offset 0x400  read,  MSR 0xC0000000..=0xC0001FFF
//! offset 0x800  write, MSR 0x00000000..=0x00001FFF
//! offset 0xC00  write, MSR 0xC0000000..=0xC0001FFF
//! RDMSR/WRMSR of any other MSR always exits.
//!
//! I/O bitmaps, one bit per port:
//! A (one page): ports 0x0000..=0x7FFF    B (one page): ports 0x8000..=0xFFFF
//! An access to several ports exits if any of their bits is set.
//! ```

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::guest::GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT;
use super::msr::{
    IA32_BNDCFGS, IA32_DEBUGCTL, IA32_EFER, IA32_FS_BASE, IA32_GS_BASE, IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE, IA32_PAT,
    IA32_PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL, IA32_SYSENTER_CS, IA32_SYSENTER_EIP, IA32_SYSENTER_ESP,
};
use super::mtrr;
use super::page::{PAGE_SIZE, allocate_zeroed_page};
use super::vmcs::fields::{IO_BITMAP_A, IO_BITMAP_B, MSR_BITMAP};
use super::vmcs::{self, VmcsError};

/// MSRs whose RDMSR and WRMSR exit to Aleph0, which passes them through: it
/// runs a real RDMSR/WRMSR in root operation, which reaches the CPU's own
/// MSR, so none may be in [`VMCS_HELD_MSRS`] (checked at compile time
/// below).
///
/// The MTRR MSRs exit too ([`ExitBitmaps::allocate`]), but are never
/// passed through: the guest reads and writes a copy of them
/// (`vmexit::guest_mtrrs`), since the CPU's still set the memory types of
/// Aleph0's own accesses. Every address an MTRR can have exits
/// ([`mtrr::every_msr_address`]), not only those the CPU has, so the guest
/// gets #GP for the others from Aleph0 rather than from whatever the CPU
/// holds there.
pub const INTERCEPTED_MSRS: [u32; 1] = [IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE];

/// Ports whose IN and OUT exit to Aleph0.
pub const INTERCEPTED_PORTS: [u16; 1] = [GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT];

/// MSRs whose guest value is a VMCS guest-state field. In root operation a
/// real RDMSR/WRMSR reaches the host's value, not the guest's, so an
/// emulated access to one would read or overwrite the wrong value.
const VMCS_HELD_MSRS: [u32; 10] = [
    IA32_DEBUGCTL,
    IA32_SYSENTER_CS,
    IA32_SYSENTER_ESP,
    IA32_SYSENTER_EIP,
    IA32_PAT,
    IA32_PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL,
    IA32_BNDCFGS,
    IA32_EFER,
    IA32_FS_BASE,
    IA32_GS_BASE,
];

// Every intercepted MSR has a bitmap bit, and none is held in the VMCS.
const _: () = {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < INTERCEPTED_MSRS.len() {
        assert!(msr_bit(INTERCEPTED_MSRS[i], MsrAccess::Read).is_some());
        let mut j = 0;
        while j < VMCS_HELD_MSRS.len() {
            assert!(
                INTERCEPTED_MSRS[i] != VMCS_HELD_MSRS[j],
                "an intercepted MSR is held in the VMCS"
            );
            j += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
};

/// Which half of the MSR bitmap: RDMSR or WRMSR.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MsrAccess {
    Read,
    Write,
}

/// Where `msr`'s bit for `access` is in the MSR bitmap: (byte offset in the
/// page, bit in that byte). `None` for MSRs outside the two ranges the
/// bitmap covers, whose RDMSR and WRMSR always exit.
pub const fn msr_bit(msr: u32, access: MsrAccess) -> Option<(usize, u8)> {
    let (read_offset, index) = match msr {
        0..=0x1FFF => (0x000, msr),
        0xC000_0000..=0xC000_1FFF => (0x400, msr - 0xC000_0000),
        _ => return None,
    };
    let offset = match access {
        MsrAccess::Read => read_offset,
        MsrAccess::Write => read_offset + 0x800,
    };
    Some((offset + index as usize / 8, (index % 8) as u8))
}

/// Which I/O bitmap page a port is in.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum IoBitmap {
    /// Ports 0x0000–0x7FFF.
    A,
    /// Ports 0x8000–0xFFFF.
    B,
}

/// Where `port`'s bit is: (page, byte offset in it, bit in that byte).
pub const fn io_bit(port: u16) -> (IoBitmap, usize, u8) {
    let page = if port < 0x8000 { IoBitmap::A } else { IoBitmap::B };
    let index = (port & 0x7FFF) as usize;
    (page, index / 8, (port % 8) as u8)
}

/// Sets the bits of [`INTERCEPTED_MSRS`] and of every address an MTRR MSR
/// can have (read and write), and of [`INTERCEPTED_PORTS`], in zeroed
/// bitmap pages.
fn fill(msr: &mut [u8], io_a: &mut [u8], io_b: &mut [u8]) {
    for intercepted in INTERCEPTED_MSRS.into_iter().chain(mtrr::every_msr_address()) {
        for access in [MsrAccess::Read, MsrAccess::Write] {
            // Always `Some`: checked at compile time above, and every MTRR
            // MSR is below 0x300.
            if let Some((offset, bit)) = msr_bit(intercepted, access) {
                msr[offset] |= 1 << bit;
            }
        }
    }
    for port in INTERCEPTED_PORTS {
        let (page, offset, bit) = io_bit(port);
        let page = match page {
            IoBitmap::A => &mut *io_a,
            IoBitmap::B => &mut *io_b,
        };
        page[offset] |= 1 << bit;
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ExitBitmapsError {
    /// UEFI could not provide a bitmap page.
    AllocationFailed,
}

/// The three bitmap pages. Never freed: the CPU reads them on every guest
/// RDMSR, WRMSR, IN and OUT for as long as the VMCS points at them.
pub struct ExitBitmaps {
    msr: NonNull<u8>,
    io_a: NonNull<u8>,
    io_b: NonNull<u8>,
}

impl ExitBitmaps {
    /// Allocates three zeroed pages and sets the intercepted bits: those of
    /// [`INTERCEPTED_MSRS`], of every address an MTRR MSR can have, and of
    /// [`INTERCEPTED_PORTS`].
    pub fn allocate() -> Result<Self, ExitBitmapsError> {
        let page = || allocate_zeroed_page(ExitBitmapsError::AllocationFailed);
        let bitmaps = Self {
            msr: page()?,
            io_a: page()?,
            io_b: page()?,
        };
        // SAFETY: three separate fresh allocations of one zeroed page each,
        // which nothing else refers to while these slices live.
        let (msr, io_a, io_b) = unsafe {
            (
                core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(bitmaps.msr.as_ptr(), PAGE_SIZE),
                core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(bitmaps.io_a.as_ptr(), PAGE_SIZE),
                core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(bitmaps.io_b.as_ptr(), PAGE_SIZE),
            )
        };
        fill(msr, io_a, io_b);
        Ok(bitmaps)
    }

    /// Physical address of the MSR bitmap. UEFI identity-maps memory, so it
    /// is the page's address.
    pub fn msr_address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.msr.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// Physical address of I/O bitmap A.
    pub fn io_a_address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.io_a.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// Physical address of I/O bitmap B.
    pub fn io_b_address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.io_b.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// Writes the three addresses to the current VMCS and reads them back.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// VMX root operation with a current VMCS. The pages must stay allocated
    /// for as long as that VMCS can be entered (they are never freed).
    pub unsafe fn write_to_vmcs(&self) -> Result<(), VmcsError> {
        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX root operation with a current
        // VMCS; the pages are never freed.
        unsafe {
            vmcs::write_verified(MSR_BITMAP, self.msr_address())?;
            vmcs::write_verified(IO_BITMAP_A, self.io_a_address())?;
            vmcs::write_verified(IO_BITMAP_B, self.io_b_address())?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[path = "../../tests/unit/vmx/exit_bitmaps.rs"]
mod tests;

`src/vmx/exit_decision/emulation.rs`:

```rs
//! Instructions Aleph0 executes for the guest: passthrough emulation.
//!
//! Some guest instructions always exit (CPUID). Others exit because the
//! exit bitmaps ask for it (RDMSR/WRMSR through the MSR bitmap, IN/OUT through
//! the I/O bitmaps, both in `vmx::exit_bitmaps`). A handler here decides
//! what to execute. `vmexit::handler` then runs the real
//! instruction in root operation, writes the result into the guest's
//! registers and moves RIP past the instruction, so the guest sees what the
//! hardware says, except where a policy here changes it
//! ([`cpuid_policy`]).
//!
//! The guest's MTRRs are the exception to passthrough. The CPU's still set
//! the memory types of Aleph0's own accesses in root operation, so the
//! guest's RDMSR and WRMSR of them reach a copy instead
//! (`vmexit::guest_mtrrs`), and a value WRMSR would refuse gets the #GP it
//! would get on bare metal. So does an MTRR address the CPU has no MSR at,
//! which the MSR bitmap intercepts too.
//!
//! Hyper-V's hypercalls and synthetic MSRs are passed through one level
//! further: Aleph0 makes the same access in root operation, and L0 Hyper-V
//! answers it (`vmx::hyperv`), or refuses it with the exception the guest
//! then gets.
//!
//! HLT is decided here too, but never executed: Aleph0 resumes past it (see
//! [`hlt`]).
//!
//! These handlers hold for any guest, so they read only the exit itself, never
//! the test guest's `ExitState`. What they did is counted afterwards, in
//! `vmexit::stats`.

use core::arch::x86_64::CpuidResult;

use super::{ExitEvent, ExitInfo};
use crate::vmx::exit_bitmaps::{INTERCEPTED_MSRS, MsrAccess, msr_bit};
use crate::vmx::hyperv;
use crate::vmx::mtrr::{self, MtrrCapabilities, MtrrMsr};

/// An instruction the exit handler executes for the guest.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Emulation {
    /// CPUID with EAX = `leaf`, ECX = `subleaf`.
    Cpuid { leaf: u32, subleaf: u32 },
    /// RDMSR of `msr`, an intercepted MSR.
    Rdmsr { msr: u32 },
    /// WRMSR of `value` (EDX:EAX) to `msr`, an intercepted MSR. `value` is
    /// canonical, so the real WRMSR cannot fault.
    Wrmsr { msr: u32, value: u64 },
    /// RDMSR of `msr`, one of the guest's MTRRs: from its copy, never the
    /// CPU's.
    MtrrRead { msr: MtrrMsr },
    /// WRMSR of `value` to `msr`, one of the guest's MTRRs: into its copy,
    /// never the CPU's, and EPT takes the types it gives. `value` is one
    /// WRMSR would take.
    MtrrWrite { msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64 },
    /// IN of `size` from `port`.
    In { port: u16, size: IoSize },
    /// OUT of `value` (`size` wide) to `port`.
    Out { port: u16, size: IoSize, value: u32 },
    /// VMCALL with the hypercall input value `input` in RCX: made again in
    /// root operation with the guest's RCX, RDX and R8, for Hyper-V.
    Hypercall { input: u64 },
    /// RDMSR of `msr`, one of Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs: from Hyper-V.
    SyntheticRead { msr: u32 },
    /// WRMSR of `value` to `msr`, one of Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs: to
    /// Hyper-V, which checks the value.
    SyntheticWrite { msr: u32, value: u64 },
}

/// CPUID.1:ECX bit 5: VMX.
const CPUID_1_ECX_VMX: u32 = 1 << 5;

/// What the guest sees for CPUID `leaf`, given what the processor returned
/// in root operation.
///
/// Everything passes through except CPUID.1:ECX.VMX. A guest that saw it
/// would try VMXON, which always exits (reason 27), and Aleph0 does not
/// emulate VMX. Left as the processor says:
/// - ECX bit 31 (hypervisor present) and the leaves from 0x40000000, which
///   under Hyper-V describe Hyper-V: the guest keeps Hyper-V's interface,
///   and Aleph0 forwards it (docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md);
/// - values that depend on CR4 and XCR0 (CPUID.1:ECX.OSXSAVE, leaf 0xD),
///   which are right for the guest only while it shares the host's.
pub fn cpuid_policy(leaf: u32, raw: CpuidResult) -> CpuidResult {
    match leaf {
        1 => CpuidResult {
            ecx: raw.ecx & !CPUID_1_ECX_VMX,
            ..raw
        },
        _ => raw,
    }
}

/// CPUID (exit reason 10), which always exits: execute it with the guest's
/// EAX (leaf) and ECX (subleaf).
pub(super) fn cpuid(exit: &ExitInfo) -> ExitEvent {
    ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Cpuid {
        leaf: exit.guest_rax as u32,
        subleaf: exit.guest_rcx as u32,
    })
}

/// HLT (exit reason 12): resume past it without halting. A halted vCPU
/// waits for an interrupt, and the guest's interrupts are delivered when it
/// next runs anyway, so going on at once is a correct, if busy, wait. The
/// HLT activity state would avoid one exit per idle loop round, but needs
/// IA32_VMX_MISC bit 6 and a rule for NMI exits taken in that state.
pub(super) fn hlt() -> ExitEvent {
    ExitEvent::Halted
}

/// Whether `value` is a canonical 48-bit address: bits 63:47 all equal.
/// With 5-level paging (CR4.LA57) it would be bits 63:56; Aleph0's guest
/// shares the host's CR4, which UEFI leaves without LA57.
pub fn is_canonical_48(value: u64) -> bool {
    ((value as i64) << 16 >> 16) as u64 == value
}

/// What an RDMSR or WRMSR of an MSR gets.
enum MsrRoute {
    /// In [`INTERCEPTED_MSRS`]: pass it through.
    Intercepted,
    /// One of the guest's MTRRs: read or write its copy.
    Mtrr(MtrrMsr),
    /// An address an MTRR has on some CPU, but not on this one (a variable
    /// range past IA32_MTRRCAP's count, the fixed ranges without
    /// IA32_MTRRCAP.FIX, any of them without MTRRs). The bitmap intercepts
    /// these too, and the guest gets the #GP a CPU without the MSR gives.
    AbsentMtrr,
    /// One of Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs ([`hyperv::SYNTHETIC_MSRS`]), with
    /// Hyper-V's interface present: forward it.
    Synthetic,
    /// Outside both MSR-bitmap ranges, so it exits whatever the bitmap
    /// says, and not forwarded. Aleph0 does not know it exists, and a real
    /// RDMSR/WRMSR of a missing MSR would #GP in the host, so the guest gets
    /// the #GP.
    OutOfRange,
    /// In range but its bit is clear, so it should never have exited: the
    /// bitmap is broken. Stop.
    NotIntercepted,
}

/// Which [`MsrRoute`] `msr` takes, for a guest whose MTRR MSRs are `mtrr`,
/// with Hyper-V's interface (`hyperv`) or without.
fn route(msr: u32, mtrr: MtrrCapabilities, hyperv: bool) -> MsrRoute {
    if msr_bit(msr, MsrAccess::Read).is_none() {
        if hyperv && hyperv::SYNTHETIC_MSRS.contains(&msr) {
            MsrRoute::Synthetic
        } else {
            MsrRoute::OutOfRange
        }
    } else if INTERCEPTED_MSRS.contains(&msr) {
        MsrRoute::Intercepted
    } else if let Some(msr) = mtrr.msr(msr) {
        MsrRoute::Mtrr(msr)
    } else if mtrr::is_msr_address(msr) {
        MsrRoute::AbsentMtrr
    } else {
        MsrRoute::NotIntercepted
    }
}

/// RDMSR (exit reason 31) of the MSR in ECX.
pub(super) fn rdmsr(exit: &ExitInfo) -> ExitEvent {
    let msr = exit.guest_rcx as u32;
    match route(msr, exit.mtrr, exit.hyperv) {
        MsrRoute::Intercepted => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr }),
        MsrRoute::Mtrr(msr) => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::MtrrRead { msr }),
        MsrRoute::Synthetic => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::SyntheticRead { msr }),
        MsrRoute::AbsentMtrr | MsrRoute::OutOfRange => ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
        MsrRoute::NotIntercepted => ExitEvent::Unexpected,
    }
}

/// The value a WRMSR exit writes: EDX:EAX. Like WRMSR itself, it ignores
/// the upper halves of RDX and RAX.
pub fn wrmsr_value(exit: &ExitInfo) -> u64 {
    (exit.guest_rdx << 32) | (exit.guest_rax & 0xFFFF_FFFF)
}

/// WRMSR (exit reason 32) of EDX:EAX to the MSR in ECX.
pub(super) fn wrmsr(exit: &ExitInfo) -> ExitEvent {
    let msr = exit.guest_rcx as u32;
    let value = wrmsr_value(exit);
    match route(msr, exit.mtrr, exit.hyperv) {
        // Every intercepted MSR holds an address (only IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE
        // today). A real WRMSR of a non-canonical one would #GP in the host,
        // in exit context, so the guest gets that #GP instead.
        MsrRoute::Intercepted if !is_canonical_48(value) => ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
        MsrRoute::Intercepted => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Wrmsr { msr, value }),
        // Checked on its own, as the CPU does: a reserved type or bit gets
        // the #GP even in an MTRR not in use, and the copy stays as it was.
        MsrRoute::Mtrr(msr) => match exit.mtrr.check(msr, value) {
            Ok(()) => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::MtrrWrite { msr, value }),
            Err(_) => ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
        },
        MsrRoute::Synthetic => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::SyntheticWrite { msr, value }),
        MsrRoute::AbsentMtrr | MsrRoute::OutOfRange => ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
        MsrRoute::NotIntercepted => ExitEvent::Unexpected,
    }
}

/// How many bytes an IN or OUT moves.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum IoSize {
    Byte,
    Word,
    Dword,
}

impl IoSize {
    /// Bytes moved: 1, 2 or 4.
    pub fn bytes(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Self::Byte => 1,
            Self::Word => 2,
            Self::Dword => 4,
        }
    }

    /// The bits of RAX the access uses: AL, AX or EAX.
    fn mask(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::Byte => 0xFF,
            Self::Word => 0xFFFF,
            Self::Dword => 0xFFFF_FFFF,
        }
    }
}

/// An I/O instruction's exit qualification (Intel SDM Vol. 3C, "Exit
/// Qualification for I/O Instructions"):
///
/// ```text
/// bits 2:0   size − 1: 0 = 1 byte, 1 = 2 bytes, 3 = 4 bytes
/// bit  3     direction: 1 = IN, 0 = OUT
/// bit  4     string instruction (INS/OUTS)
/// bit  5     REP prefix
/// bit  6     operand: 1 = immediate port, 0 = DX
/// bits 31:16 port
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IoQualification(pub u64);

impl IoQualification {
    /// The access size, or `None` for the encodings the SDM leaves unused.
    pub fn size(self) -> Option<IoSize> {
        match self.0 & 0b111 {
            0 => Some(IoSize::Byte),
            1 => Some(IoSize::Word),
            3 => Some(IoSize::Dword),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Whether it is IN (bit 3); OUT otherwise.
    pub fn is_in(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & (1 << 3) != 0
    }

    /// Whether it is INS or OUTS (bit 4).
    pub fn is_string(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & (1 << 4) != 0
    }

    /// Whether it has a REP prefix (bit 5).
    pub fn is_rep(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & (1 << 5) != 0
    }

    /// The port (bits 31:16).
    pub fn port(self) -> u16 {
        (self.0 >> 16) as u16
    }
}

/// RAX after an IN of `size` that read `value`. A 1- or 2-byte IN writes
/// only AL or AX and keeps the rest of RAX. A 4-byte IN writes EAX, which
/// zero-extends into RAX like every 32-bit register write in 64-bit mode.
pub fn merge_in(rax: u64, size: IoSize, value: u32) -> u64 {
    match size {
        IoSize::Dword => u64::from(value),
        _ => (rax & !size.mask()) | (u64::from(value) & size.mask()),
    }
}

/// The value an OUT of `size` sends: AL, AX or EAX.
pub fn out_value(rax: u64, size: IoSize) -> u32 {
    (rax & size.mask()) as u32
}

/// IN or OUT (exit reason 30), for a port the I/O bitmaps intercept: passed
/// through with the port and size from the exit qualification. Not checked
/// against INTERCEPTED_PORTS: an access to several ports exits if any of
/// them is intercepted (`in ax, dx` at 0x3FE covers 0x3FF), and passing
/// that access through is what the guest would have done anyway. String
/// and REP forms, which read or write guest memory, stop the guest.
pub(super) fn io(exit: &ExitInfo) -> ExitEvent {
    let io = IoQualification(exit.qualification);
    let Some(size) = io.size() else {
        return ExitEvent::Unexpected;
    };
    if io.is_string() || io.is_rep() {
        return ExitEvent::Unexpected;
    }
    let port = io.port();
    if io.is_in() {
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::In { port, size })
    } else {
        let value = out_value(exit.guest_rax, size);
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Out { port, size, value })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../../tests/unit/vmx/exit_decision/emulation.rs"]
mod tests;

```

`src/vmx/exit_decision/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! What the VM-exit handler does with each exit: pure decisions, one
//! handler per exit reason.
//!
//! The handler reads the exit's VMCS fields into an [`ExitInfo`], calls
//! [`decide`] with the [`ExitState`] kept between exits, and applies the
//! [`ExitAction`] of the returned [`ExitEvent`]. Nothing here touches the
//! CPU, so every case is a host unit test.
//!
//! [`decide`] first checks what holds for every exit (a failed VM entry, an
//! interrupted event delivery), then dispatches on the exit reason to a
//! handler, the way KVM's `kvm_vmx_exit_handlers[]` does, but as a `match`
//! instead of a table of function pointers, so the handled reasons are listed
//! in one place:
//!
//! - `emulation.rs`: instructions Aleph0 executes for any guest (CPUID,
//!   RDMSR, WRMSR, IN, OUT), RDMSR and WRMSR of the guest's MTRRs, which
//!   reach a copy of them instead, and of Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs, which
//!   are forwarded to Hyper-V, and HLT, which it skips. Each handler reads
//!   the exit alone: `fn(&ExitInfo) -> ExitEvent`. MWAIT and MONITOR, which
//!   get #UD, need no handler of their own.
//! - `scenario.rs`: exits that depend on what came before:
//!   `fn(ExitState, &ExitInfo) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState)`. NMI reinjection,
//!   for every guest, and the test guest's own exits: its EPT write and its
//!   VMCALLs. Any other EPT violation stops the guest as
//!   [`ExitEvent::EptViolation`].
//! - An EPT misconfiguration stops the guest as
//!   [`ExitEvent::EptMisconfig`]. Aleph0 makes no misconfigured entry on
//!   purpose (KVM does, for MMIO, and emulates the access in
//!   `handle_ept_misconfig`), so one means the map is broken.
//!
//! The guest's kind (`GuestKind`) decides the VMCALLs and the test guest's
//! own exits. The firmware has no scripted end: its VMCALLs are Aleph0's
//! own (`vmx::vmcall`) or else Hyper-V hypercalls, forwarded to Hyper-V
//! (`firmware_vmcall`), and every EPT violation stops it, so it never
//! finishes and runs until an exit Aleph0 does not handle.
//!
//! An exit reason without a handler stops the guest. Nothing here counts
//! exits: `vmexit::stats` does, for every guest, from what the handler
//! carried out.

mod emulation;
mod scenario;

use crate::vmx::mtrr::MtrrCapabilities;
use crate::vmx::vmcall;
use crate::vmx::vmcs::GuestKind;

pub use emulation::{Emulation, IoSize, cpuid_policy, is_canonical_48, merge_in, wrmsr_value};
pub use scenario::{PLANNED_MAIN_VMCALLS, expected_main_rax};

/// VM-exit reason, split into the fields of the VM_EXIT_REASON VMCS field.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ExitReason {
    /// Bits 15:0: which event caused the exit (Intel SDM Vol. 3D, Appendix C).
    pub basic: u16,
    /// Bit 31: VM entry itself failed. The guest never ran; `basic` says
    /// why (33 = invalid guest state, 34 = MSR loading, 41 = machine check).
    pub entry_failure: bool,
}

impl ExitReason {
    pub fn from_raw(raw: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            basic: raw as u16,
            entry_failure: raw & (1 << 31) != 0,
        }
    }
}

/// Human-readable name for a basic exit reason. Only the reasons this
/// hypervisor is likely to meet early on are spelled out.
pub fn exit_reason_name(basic: u16) -> &'static str {
    match basic {
        0 => "exception or NMI",
        1 => "external interrupt",
        2 => "triple fault",
        3 => "INIT signal",
        7 => "interrupt window",
        8 => "NMI window",
        9 => "task switch",
        10 => "CPUID",
        12 => "HLT",
        18 => "VMCALL",
        28 => "control-register access",
        30 => "I/O instruction",
        31 => "RDMSR",
        32 => "WRMSR",
        33 => "VM-entry failure: invalid guest state",
        34 => "VM-entry failure: MSR loading",
        36 => "MWAIT",
        39 => "MONITOR",
        41 => "VM-entry failure: machine-check event",
        48 => "EPT violation",
        49 => "EPT misconfiguration",
        UNREADABLE_REASON => "VM_EXIT_REASON unreadable",
        _ => "unnamed exit reason",
    }
}

/// Reason the handler reports when VM_EXIT_REASON itself could not be read.
/// Basic exit reasons stop far below 0xFFFF, so it never names a real exit.
pub const UNREADABLE_REASON: u16 = 0xFFFF;

/// Basic exit reason of an exception or NMI exit.
pub const EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI: u16 = 0;
/// Basic exit reason of an NMI-window exit.
pub const EXIT_REASON_NMI_WINDOW: u16 = 8;
/// Basic exit reason of CPUID, which always exits.
pub const EXIT_REASON_CPUID: u16 = 10;
/// Basic exit reason of HLT, with HLT exiting on.
pub const EXIT_REASON_HLT: u16 = 12;
/// Basic exit reason of a VMCALL exit.
pub const EXIT_REASON_VMCALL: u16 = 18;
/// Basic exit reason of IN/OUT (and INS/OUTS) to a port the I/O bitmaps
/// intercept.
pub const EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION: u16 = 30;
/// Basic exit reason of RDMSR, which exits for MSRs the MSR bitmap
/// intercepts or does not cover.
pub const EXIT_REASON_RDMSR: u16 = 31;
/// Basic exit reason of WRMSR, which exits for the same MSRs as RDMSR.
pub const EXIT_REASON_WRMSR: u16 = 32;
/// Basic exit reason of MWAIT, with MWAIT exiting on (Hyper-V forces it).
pub const EXIT_REASON_MWAIT: u16 = 36;
/// Basic exit reason of MONITOR, with MONITOR exiting on (Hyper-V forces it).
pub const EXIT_REASON_MONITOR: u16 = 39;
/// Basic exit reason of an EPT violation: an access the EPT entries do not
/// allow.
pub const EXIT_REASON_EPT_VIOLATION: u16 = 48;
/// Basic exit reason of an EPT misconfiguration: an EPT entry the CPU
/// cannot use at all (for example W = 1 with R = 0). It stops the guest
/// ([`ExitEvent::EptMisconfig`]).
pub const EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG: u16 = 49;

// Exit qualification bits of an EPT violation (Intel SDM Vol. 3C, "Exit
// Qualification for EPT Violations").
/// Bit 0: the access was a read.
pub const EPT_ACCESS_READ: u64 = 1 << 0;
/// Bit 1: the access was a write.
pub const EPT_ACCESS_WRITE: u64 = 1 << 1;
/// Bit 2: the access was an instruction fetch.
pub const EPT_ACCESS_FETCH: u64 = 1 << 2;
/// Bit 3: the EPT entries allowed reads of the page.
pub const EPT_PAGE_READABLE: u64 = 1 << 3;
/// Bit 4: the EPT entries allowed writes.
pub const EPT_PAGE_WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
/// Bit 5: the EPT entries allowed execution.
pub const EPT_PAGE_EXECUTABLE: u64 = 1 << 5;
/// Bit 7: GUEST_LINEAR_ADDRESS is valid.
pub const EPT_LINEAR_VALID: u64 = 1 << 7;
/// Bit 8 (with bit 7): the access was to the linear address the guest
/// used, not to one of the guest's own page tables during the walk.
pub const EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS: u64 = 1 << 8;
/// Bit 12: the violation happened during an IRET that ended NMI blocking.
/// Resuming would then need NMI blocking set again by hand, which Aleph0
/// does not do, so such a violation is never handled.
pub const EPT_NMI_UNBLOCKING_IRET: u64 = 1 << 12;

/// An EPT violation's exit qualification (EXIT_QUALIFICATION), decoded with
/// the bits above.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct EptQualification(pub u64);

impl EptQualification {
    /// Whether the access was a write.
    pub fn is_write(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & EPT_ACCESS_WRITE != 0
    }

    /// The kind of access, for the report. Only one is named; a write wins,
    /// since that is the access Aleph0 handles.
    pub fn access_name(self) -> &'static str {
        if self.is_write() {
            "write"
        } else if self.0 & EPT_ACCESS_FETCH != 0 {
            "instruction fetch"
        } else if self.0 & EPT_ACCESS_READ != 0 {
            "read"
        } else {
            "no access bit set"
        }
    }

    /// What the EPT entries allowed for the page, from bits 5:3, as
    /// `(R, W, X)` with 1 for allowed.
    pub fn permissions(self) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
        (
            u8::from(self.0 & EPT_PAGE_READABLE != 0),
            u8::from(self.0 & EPT_PAGE_WRITABLE != 0),
            u8::from(self.0 & EPT_PAGE_EXECUTABLE != 0),
        )
    }

    /// Whether GUEST_LINEAR_ADDRESS is valid (bit 7).
    pub fn linear_valid(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & EPT_LINEAR_VALID != 0
    }

    /// The EPT violation Aleph0 handles: a write to a page EPT maps readable
    /// but not writable, through the linear address the guest used.
    pub fn is_protected_write(self) -> bool {
        let required = EPT_ACCESS_WRITE | EPT_PAGE_READABLE | EPT_LINEAR_VALID | EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS;
        let refused = EPT_PAGE_WRITABLE | EPT_NMI_UNBLOCKING_IRET;
        self.0 & required == required && self.0 & refused == 0
    }
}

/// IDT vector of NMI.
pub const NMI_VECTOR: u8 = 2;

/// An interruption-information value: VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO,
/// IDT_VECTORING_INFO and VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO share the layout.
///
/// ```text
///  31    30  13  12           11          10   8  7      0
/// ┌─────┬──────┬────────────┬────────────┬───────┬────────┐
/// │valid│ res. │NMI unblock.│ error code │ type  │ vector │
/// │     │      │ (exit only)│   valid    │       │        │
/// └─────┴──────┴────────────┴────────────┴───────┴────────┘
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InterruptionInfo(pub u32);

impl InterruptionInfo {
    /// Bit 31: the field is valid.
    pub const VALID: u32 = 1 << 31;
    /// Interruption type 2 (bits 10:8): NMI.
    const TYPE_NMI: u32 = 2;
    /// Interruption type 3 (bits 10:8): hardware exception.
    const TYPE_HARDWARE_EXCEPTION: u32 = 3;
    /// Bit 11: deliver an error code (VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE).
    const DELIVER_ERROR_CODE: u32 = 1 << 11;
    /// IDT vector of #UD.
    const UD_VECTOR: u32 = 6;
    /// IDT vector of #GP.
    const GP_VECTOR: u32 = 13;

    /// The VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO value that injects an NMI at the next
    /// VM entry: valid, type NMI, vector 2. The CPU clears the field after
    /// each successful entry, so it injects once.
    pub const NMI: Self = Self(Self::VALID | (Self::TYPE_NMI << 8) | NMI_VECTOR as u32);

    /// The VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO value that injects #GP with an error
    /// code at the next VM entry, delivered before the faulting instruction
    /// runs again.
    pub const GENERAL_PROTECTION: Self =
        Self(Self::VALID | (Self::TYPE_HARDWARE_EXCEPTION << 8) | Self::DELIVER_ERROR_CODE | Self::GP_VECTOR);

    /// The VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO value that injects #UD, which has no
    /// error code, at the next VM entry.
    pub const INVALID_OPCODE: Self = Self(Self::VALID | (Self::TYPE_HARDWARE_EXCEPTION << 8) | Self::UD_VECTOR);

    /// Whether the field describes an event at all (bit 31).
    pub fn is_valid(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & Self::VALID != 0
    }

    /// Whether this describes an NMI: valid, type 2, vector 2. Bit 12 (NMI
    /// unblocking due to IRET) is ignored.
    pub fn is_nmi(self) -> bool {
        self.is_valid() && (self.0 >> 8) & 0b111 == Self::TYPE_NMI && self.vector() == Some(NMI_VECTOR)
    }

    /// Whether VM entry also delivers VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE (bit 11).
    pub fn delivers_error_code(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & Self::DELIVER_ERROR_CODE != 0
    }

    /// The vector (bits 7:0), if the field is valid.
    pub fn vector(self) -> Option<u8> {
        self.is_valid().then_some(self.0 as u8)
    }

    /// The interruption type (bits 10:8).
    const fn event_type(self) -> u32 {
        (self.0 >> 8) & 0b111
    }

    /// Whether VM entry charges an instruction length for this event:
    /// software interrupt (type 4), privileged software exception (5) and
    /// software exception (6). The CPU then needs VM_ENTRY_INSTRUCTION_LEN to
    /// land RIP past the INT/INT3/INTO it delivers.
    pub fn needs_instruction_len(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.event_type(), 4..=6)
    }

    /// This field re-armed for VM entry from IDT_VECTORING_INFO: the valid
    /// bit and the event kept, bits 30:12 cleared. Bit 12 (NMI unblocking
    /// due to IRET) is an exit-only bit, undefined at entry, and bits 30:13
    /// are reserved there.
    pub fn for_reentry(self) -> Self {
        Self(self.0 & !0x7FFF_F000)
    }
}

/// An event the VM exit interrupted mid-delivery, to re-deliver at the next
/// VM entry (from IDT_VECTORING_INFO; Intel SDM Vol. 3C, "Information for VM
/// Exits During Event Delivery" and "Event Injection").
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Redelivery {
    /// VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO: the interrupted event, re-armed for entry.
    pub info: InterruptionInfo,
    /// VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE, when the event carries one (bit 11).
    pub error_code: Option<u32>,
    /// VM_ENTRY_INSTRUCTION_LEN, for a software interrupt or exception.
    pub instruction_len: Option<u32>,
}

/// What the handler read about the current exit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ExitInfo {
    pub reason: ExitReason,
    /// VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO.
    pub interruption_info: InterruptionInfo,
    /// The guest's RAX, RCX and RDX. CPUID reads its leaf from EAX and its
    /// subleaf from ECX. RDMSR and WRMSR read the MSR from ECX, and WRMSR its
    /// value from EDX:EAX. OUT reads its value from AL, AX or EAX. At main
    /// VMCALL #1, ECX and EDX hold what the guest read from its data page
    /// before and after its write.
    pub guest_rax: u64,
    pub guest_rcx: u64,
    pub guest_rdx: u64,
    /// GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE.
    pub interruptibility: u32,
    /// IDT_VECTORING_INFO: when valid (bit 31), the exit interrupted the
    /// delivery of this event through the guest IDT, and it is re-delivered.
    pub idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo,
    /// IDT_VECTORING_ERROR_CODE, meaningful when `idt_vectoring` is valid and
    /// delivers an error code.
    pub idt_vectoring_error_code: u32,
    /// EXIT_QUALIFICATION. Its layout depends on the reason; [`decide`]
    /// reads it for EPT violations ([`EptQualification`]) and I/O
    /// instructions (`emulation::IoQualification`) only. `read_exit` keeps
    /// the real value whenever the VMCS field is readable, and uses 0 only
    /// when it is unreadable on an exit `decide` does not judge by it. A
    /// handler that reads it for another reason (CR access, reason 28, for
    /// example) must add that reason to `judged_by_qualification` in
    /// `vmexit/handler.rs`.
    pub qualification: u64,
    /// GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS, read for EPT exits only; 0 otherwise.
    pub guest_physical: u64,
    /// GPA of the page EPT maps read-only (`ept::protected_page`), 0 if none.
    pub protected_page: u64,
    /// The guest's MTRR MSRs: which exist, and which values WRMSR refuses
    /// (`vmexit::guest_mtrrs`). [`MtrrCapabilities::NONE`] until bring-up
    /// publishes them, and on a CPU without MTRRs.
    pub mtrr: MtrrCapabilities,
    /// Whether bring-up found Hyper-V's interface (`hyperv::offered`): its
    /// hypercalls and synthetic MSRs are forwarded to it.
    pub hyperv: bool,
    /// The guest's CPL, SS.DPL (Intel SDM Vol. 3C, "Checks on Guest Segment
    /// Registers": SS.DPL is the CPL), read for VMCALL exits only; 0
    /// otherwise, which [`decide`] never looks at.
    pub guest_cpl: u8,
}

/// The CPL from the guest's SS access rights (GUEST_SS_ACCESS_RIGHTS): its
/// DPL, bits 6:5.
pub fn cpl_from_ss(access_rights: u64) -> u8 {
    (access_rights >> 5) as u8 & 0b11
}

impl ExitInfo {
    /// The event this exit interrupted mid-delivery, to re-deliver at the
    /// next VM entry, or `None` when the exit interrupted no delivery.
    /// `instruction_len` is VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN, needed only for a
    /// software interrupt or exception; `None` when it was unreadable.
    pub fn redelivery(&self, instruction_len: Option<u32>) -> Option<Redelivery> {
        if !self.idt_vectoring.is_valid() {
            return None;
        }
        let info = self.idt_vectoring.for_reentry();
        Some(Redelivery {
            info,
            error_code: info.delivers_error_code().then_some(self.idt_vectoring_error_code),
            instruction_len: info.needs_instruction_len().then_some(instruction_len).flatten(),
        })
    }
}

/// What the handler remembers between exits: the NMI waiting for the guest,
/// and how far the test guest's scenario has got.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct ExitState {
    /// Main VMCALLs handled so far.
    pub main_vmcalls: u32,
    /// An NMI arrived while the guest blocked NMIs and is not injected yet.
    pub nmi_pending: bool,
    /// VMCALLs from the guest's NMI handler: reinjected NMIs that arrived.
    pub nmis_handled: u32,
    /// EPT violations on the protected page after which write was granted.
    pub ept_writes_granted: u32,
}

impl ExitState {
    /// The state once an NMI that arrived while Aleph0 ran in root operation
    /// (`arrived`) is folded in: pending for the guest, like an NMI the guest
    /// could not take yet. The exit's own handler then decides with it, so
    /// an NMI-window exit injects it, and every other exit keeps it waiting
    /// for the window ([`ResumePlan::keeping_pending_nmi`]).
    ///
    /// At most one NMI waits, as on real hardware: an NMI arriving while one
    /// is pending is the same pending NMI.
    pub fn with_host_nmi(self, arrived: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            nmi_pending: self.nmi_pending || arrived,
            ..self
        }
    }
}

/// What an exit turned out to be.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ExitEvent {
    /// A main VMCALL before the last one.
    MainVmcall,
    /// The last planned main VMCALL.
    LastMainVmcall,
    /// The guest's NMI handler reporting that a reinjected NMI arrived.
    GuestNmiHandler,
    /// An NMI the guest can take now: inject it.
    NmiInjected,
    /// An NMI while the guest cannot take an NMI yet (STI, MOV SS or NMI
    /// blocking): wait for the NMI window.
    NmiDeferred,
    /// The NMI window opened: inject the pending NMI.
    NmiWindowInjected,
    /// The guest wrote its protected data page: grant write and retry the
    /// write.
    EptWriteGranted,
    /// A main VMCALL arrived before any EPT violation: the write to the data
    /// page went through, so EPT did not protect it.
    EptWriteMissing,
    /// Main VMCALL #1 after the granted write, but ECX/EDX do not hold what
    /// the guest should have read from its data page: the seed before its
    /// write, its own value after it.
    DataPageMismatch,
    /// An EPT violation other than the guest's first write to its
    /// protected data page. The map allows every other access to every GPA
    /// up to MAXPHYADDR, so the map itself is wrong: stop, and show the walk
    /// of the GPA.
    EptViolation,
    /// An EPT misconfiguration: an entry on the GPA's path is one the CPU
    /// refuses. `Ept::build` makes none, so stop, and show the walk.
    EptMisconfig,
    /// An instruction Aleph0 executes for the guest, then resumes past it.
    Emulated(Emulation),
    /// RDMSR or WRMSR the guest gets a #GP for: an MSR outside the MSR
    /// bitmap that is not forwarded to Hyper-V, an MTRR address the CPU has
    /// no MSR at, a non-canonical value for an intercepted MSR, or a value
    /// its MTRRs would refuse.
    GuestGeneralProtection,
    /// HLT: resume past it at once. The guest's next instruction runs as if
    /// an interrupt had woken it.
    Halted,
    /// An instruction the guest gets #UD for, as on hardware without what
    /// it asks for: MWAIT or MONITOR (the guest's CPUID.1:ECX bit 3 is clear
    /// under Hyper-V, and `cpuid_policy` passes it through), or a VMCALL
    /// that is neither Aleph0's own nor one Hyper-V takes: without Hyper-V's
    /// interface, or from CPL > 0, which Hyper-V refuses with #UD too.
    GuestInvalidOpcode,
    /// Aleph0's `ExitBootServices` event ran in the guest
    /// ([`vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED`]): resume past its VMCALL, from now
    /// on in the runtime output phase.
    BootServicesEnded,
    /// A VMCALL that only tests the exit ([`vmcall::TEST`]): resume past it.
    TestVmcall,
    /// Anything else.
    Unexpected,
}

/// How the handler prepares the VMCS (and EPT) before resuming the guest.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ResumePlan {
    /// Move GUEST_RIP past the exiting instruction, which also ends blocking
    /// by STI and by MOV SS ([`after_skipped_instruction`]).
    pub advance_rip: bool,
    /// Write [`InterruptionInfo::NMI`] to VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO.
    pub inject_nmi: bool,
    /// Turn NMI-window exiting on (`Some(true)`) or off (`Some(false)`), or
    /// leave it (`None`).
    pub nmi_window: Option<bool>,
    /// Make the protected page writable in EPT
    /// (`ept::ProtectedPage::grant_write`).
    pub grant_write: bool,
    /// Execute this instruction for the guest and put its result in the
    /// guest's registers, before RIP moves past it.
    pub emulate: Option<Emulation>,
    /// Write this exception to VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO, with error code 0
    /// when it delivers one. RIP stays on the faulting instruction.
    pub inject_exception: Option<InterruptionInfo>,
    /// Re-deliver an event the exit interrupted mid-delivery, by writing its
    /// VM-entry fields. Never set together with `advance_rip`, `inject_nmi`
    /// or `inject_exception`: only one event is injected per entry
    /// ([`ResumePlan::redelivering`]).
    pub redeliver: Option<Redelivery>,
}

impl ResumePlan {
    /// Go on after the exiting instruction (a VMCALL).
    pub const PAST_INSTRUCTION: Self = Self {
        advance_rip: true,
        inject_nmi: false,
        nmi_window: None,
        grant_write: false,
        emulate: None,
        inject_exception: None,
        redeliver: None,
    };
    /// Inject an NMI, delivered before the instruction the guest was about
    /// to run. Injecting always turns NMI-window exiting off: it may have
    /// been on for an earlier NMI the new one replaces, and turning it off
    /// when it was already off is harmless.
    pub const INJECT_NMI: Self = Self {
        advance_rip: false,
        inject_nmi: true,
        nmi_window: Some(false),
        grant_write: false,
        emulate: None,
        inject_exception: None,
        redeliver: None,
    };
    /// Go on where the guest was, with NMI-window exiting on, so the next
    /// exit comes as soon as the guest can take an NMI.
    pub const WAIT_FOR_NMI_WINDOW: Self = Self {
        advance_rip: false,
        inject_nmi: false,
        nmi_window: Some(true),
        grant_write: false,
        emulate: None,
        inject_exception: None,
        redeliver: None,
    };
    /// Make the protected page writable; RIP stays on the faulting write, so
    /// it runs again.
    pub const RETRY_AFTER_GRANT: Self = Self {
        advance_rip: false,
        inject_nmi: false,
        nmi_window: None,
        grant_write: true,
        emulate: None,
        inject_exception: None,
        redeliver: None,
    };
    /// Inject #GP(0); RIP stays on the faulting instruction, as for any
    /// fault.
    pub const INJECT_GP: Self = Self {
        advance_rip: false,
        inject_nmi: false,
        nmi_window: None,
        grant_write: false,
        emulate: None,
        inject_exception: Some(InterruptionInfo::GENERAL_PROTECTION),
        redeliver: None,
    };
    /// Inject #UD; RIP stays on the faulting instruction.
    pub const INJECT_UD: Self = Self {
        inject_exception: Some(InterruptionInfo::INVALID_OPCODE),
        ..Self::INJECT_GP
    };
}

impl ResumePlan {
    /// This plan, with NMI-window exiting turned on if an NMI is still
    /// pending after the exit (`next`). Without that, an NMI folded in by
    /// [`ExitState::with_host_nmi`] at an exit that does not handle NMIs
    /// would wait until some unrelated exit came along. Plans that inject an
    /// NMI leave nothing pending, so they keep turning the window off.
    pub fn keeping_pending_nmi(self, next: ExitState) -> Self {
        if next.nmi_pending {
            Self {
                nmi_window: Some(true),
                ..self
            }
        } else {
            self
        }
    }

    /// This plan once Hyper-V refused its forwarded access with `exception`:
    /// RIP stays on the guest's instruction, which gets the exception, as it
    /// would without Aleph0. The rest of the plan (NMI window, the emulation
    /// it tried, for the counts) is kept.
    pub fn refused_with(self, exception: InterruptionInfo) -> Self {
        Self {
            advance_rip: false,
            inject_exception: Some(exception),
            ..self
        }
    }

    /// This plan with `redelivery` added, or `None` when it cannot be added
    /// and the guest must stop.
    ///
    /// Only one event is injected per VM entry, so a plan that advances RIP
    /// or injects an NMI or an exception of its own cannot also re-deliver
    /// one: stop (no double-fault synthesis yet). A software interrupt or
    /// exception also needs VM_ENTRY_INSTRUCTION_LEN, so an unreadable length
    /// stops too.
    pub fn redelivering(self, redelivery: Redelivery) -> Option<Self> {
        if self.advance_rip || self.inject_nmi || self.inject_exception.is_some() {
            return None;
        }
        if redelivery.info.needs_instruction_len() && redelivery.instruction_len.is_none() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Self {
            redeliver: Some(redelivery),
            ..self
        })
    }
}

/// GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE after Aleph0 skips the instruction the guest
/// exited on: blocking by STI and by MOV SS cleared, the rest kept.
///
/// Both last until the end of the instruction after STI or MOV SS. When
/// that instruction is the one skipped, the CPU never ends them, so the
/// handler must, as KVM does whenever it skips an instruction. Example: an
/// idle loop's `sti; hlt` exits on the HLT with interruptibility 0x1.
/// Resumed past it with bit 0 still set, the guest would keep interrupts
/// blocked through one more instruction it never asked to protect.
pub fn after_skipped_instruction(interruptibility: u32) -> u32 {
    interruptibility & !(scenario::BLOCKING_BY_STI | scenario::BLOCKING_BY_MOV_SS)
}

/// What the handler does after an exit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ExitAction {
    /// Return to the guest, after preparing it as the plan says.
    Resume(ResumePlan),
    /// The last planned exit arrived as expected; stop.
    Finished,
    /// Not an exit this hypervisor handles; stop without resuming.
    Unexpected,
}

impl ExitEvent {
    /// The action for this event.
    pub fn action(self) -> ExitAction {
        match self {
            Self::MainVmcall | Self::GuestNmiHandler => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION),
            Self::NmiInjected | Self::NmiWindowInjected => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::INJECT_NMI),
            Self::NmiDeferred => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::WAIT_FOR_NMI_WINDOW),
            Self::EptWriteGranted => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::RETRY_AFTER_GRANT),
            Self::Emulated(emulation) => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan {
                emulate: Some(emulation),
                ..ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION
            }),
            Self::GuestGeneralProtection => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::INJECT_GP),
            Self::Halted | Self::BootServicesEnded | Self::TestVmcall => {
                ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION)
            }
            Self::GuestInvalidOpcode => ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::INJECT_UD),
            Self::LastMainVmcall => ExitAction::Finished,
            Self::EptWriteMissing
            | Self::DataPageMismatch
            | Self::EptViolation
            | Self::EptMisconfig
            | Self::Unexpected => ExitAction::Unexpected,
        }
    }
}

/// Decides what `exit` of a `guest` is, given what happened before
/// (`state`), and returns the event with the state for the next exit.
///
/// A VM-entry failure is never handled, whatever the reason. Every other
/// exit goes to the handler for its reason. An exit that interrupted an
/// event's delivery (`exit.idt_vectoring` valid) is still judged by its
/// reason; the handler re-delivers the event with the plan's `redeliver`
/// (built by [`ExitInfo::redelivery`] and [`ResumePlan::redelivering`]).
pub fn decide(guest: GuestKind, state: ExitState, exit: ExitInfo) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState) {
    if exit.reason.entry_failure {
        return (ExitEvent::Unexpected, state);
    }
    let test_guest = guest == GuestKind::BuiltInTest;
    match exit.reason.basic {
        EXIT_REASON_CPUID => (emulation::cpuid(&exit), state),
        EXIT_REASON_RDMSR => (emulation::rdmsr(&exit), state),
        EXIT_REASON_WRMSR => (emulation::wrmsr(&exit), state),
        EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION => (emulation::io(&exit), state),
        EXIT_REASON_HLT => (emulation::hlt(), state),
        EXIT_REASON_MWAIT | EXIT_REASON_MONITOR => (ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode, state),
        EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI => scenario::exception_or_nmi(state, &exit),
        EXIT_REASON_NMI_WINDOW => scenario::nmi_window(state, &exit),
        EXIT_REASON_EPT_VIOLATION if test_guest => scenario::ept_violation(state, &exit),
        EXIT_REASON_EPT_VIOLATION => (ExitEvent::EptViolation, state),
        EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG => (ExitEvent::EptMisconfig, state),
        EXIT_REASON_VMCALL if test_guest => scenario::vmcall(state, &exit),
        EXIT_REASON_VMCALL => (firmware_vmcall(&exit), state),
        _ => (ExitEvent::Unexpected, state),
    }
}

/// A VMCALL of the firmware, or of the OS after it:
///
/// | CPL | RCX | Event |
/// |---|---|---|
/// | > 0 | anything | #UD, as Hyper-V gives (and KVM's emulation of it) |
/// | 0 | one of Aleph0's own (`vmx::vmcall`) | handled here |
/// | 0 | anything else, with Hyper-V's interface | a hypercall, forwarded |
/// | 0 | anything else, without it | #UD, as on hardware without a hypervisor |
///
/// Aleph0's own values have reserved hypercall-input bits set, so no
/// hypercall Hyper-V would take is mistaken for one.
fn firmware_vmcall(exit: &ExitInfo) -> ExitEvent {
    if exit.guest_cpl != 0 {
        return ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode;
    }
    match exit.guest_rcx {
        vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED => ExitEvent::BootServicesEnded,
        vmcall::TEST => ExitEvent::TestVmcall,
        // shortcut: forwards the x64 register convention only; a guest
        // calling from 32-bit mode passes its input in EDX:EAX and would
        // need translating, once a 32-bit guest exists.
        input if exit.hyperv => ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Hypercall { input }),
        _ => ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode,
    }
}

mod tests;

`src/vmx/exit_decision/scenario.rs`:

```rs
//! The test guest's own exits: its write to the EPT-protected data page,
//! its main VMCALLs, and NMI reinjection. `decide` sends only the test
//! guest's VMCALLs and EPT violations here; NMI reinjection serves every
//! guest, the firmware too.
//!
//! The guest (`guest.rs`) writes its read-only data page, makes two main
//! VMCALLs, with `GUEST_MARKER` and then `GUEST_MARKER + 1` in RAX, and
//! waits between them for an NMI:
//!
//! ```text
//! (before these: the guest's emulated exits; see emulation.rs)
//! EPT violation  ──▶ a write to the protected data page: make it writable,
//!                    resume at the same RIP so the write is retried
//! main VMCALL #1 ──▶ resume past it (only after the EPT violation, and only
//!                    if ECX/EDX hold the data page's seed and new value)
//! NMI exit       ──▶ guest can take the NMI:  inject it at the next entry
//!                    guest cannot yet (STI, MOV SS or NMI blocking):
//!                                             turn on NMI-window exiting,
//! NMI-window exit──▶                          inject when the window opens
//! VMCALL with GUEST_NMI_MARKER (the guest's NMI handler) ──▶ resume past it
//! main VMCALL #2 ──▶ finished
//! ```
//!
//! Whether every emulated exit came is not decided here: bring-up checks the
//! exit statistics once the guest has finished (`guest::expected_stats`).

use super::{EptQualification, ExitEvent, ExitInfo, ExitState};
use crate::vmx::guest::{GUEST_DATA_SEED, GUEST_EPT_VALUE, GUEST_MARKER, GUEST_NMI_MARKER};

/// How many main VMCALLs the guest makes; the last one ends the run.
pub const PLANNED_MAIN_VMCALLS: u32 = 2;

/// Guest interruptibility bit 0: blocking by STI. The Intel SDM (Vol. 3C,
/// checks on guest non-register state) says: "A processor may require bit 0
/// (blocking by STI) to be 0 if the valid bit is 1 and the interruption type
/// is NMI." So an NMI is injected only when this bit is clear too.
pub(super) const BLOCKING_BY_STI: u32 = 1 << 0;
/// Guest interruptibility bit 1: blocking by MOV SS. VM entry refuses to
/// inject an NMI while it is set.
pub(super) const BLOCKING_BY_MOV_SS: u32 = 1 << 1;
/// Guest interruptibility bit 3: blocking by NMI. With virtual NMIs this is
/// an injected NMI the guest has not ended with IRET yet; VM entry refuses
/// to inject another while it is set.
pub(super) const BLOCKING_BY_NMI: u32 = 1 << 3;
/// Any of the blocking bits that may stop an NMI injection. The handler
/// injects only when none is set, and otherwise waits for the NMI window
/// instead of injecting blindly.
const NMI_INJECTION_BLOCKED: u32 = BLOCKING_BY_STI | BLOCKING_BY_MOV_SS | BLOCKING_BY_NMI;

/// Whether, at main VMCALL #1, ECX holds the seed the guest read from its
/// data page and EDX the value it wrote and read back. Compared as 32-bit
/// values: the guest loads both with 32-bit moves.
fn data_page_read_back(exit: &ExitInfo) -> bool {
    exit.guest_rcx as u32 == GUEST_DATA_SEED && exit.guest_rdx as u32 == GUEST_EPT_VALUE
}

/// The guest's RAX at its next main VMCALL: the marker, plus one for each
/// main VMCALL already handled (the guest runs `inc eax` before #2).
///
/// The test-only `unexpected-exit-test` Cargo feature expects one more than
/// the guest loads, so main VMCALL #1 is unexpected: a stop other than the
/// planned one, on purpose, to show its report on real VMX.
pub fn expected_main_rax(state: ExitState) -> u64 {
    u64::from(GUEST_MARKER) + u64::from(state.main_vmcalls) + u64::from(cfg!(feature = "unexpected-exit-test"))
}

/// `state` after an NMI is injected: nothing pending. Several NMIs never
/// queue: a new NMI while one is pending replaces it, as on real hardware,
/// where at most one NMI waits.
fn injected(state: ExitState) -> ExitState {
    ExitState {
        nmi_pending: false,
        ..state
    }
}

/// Exception or NMI (exit reason 0). Only an NMI is handled: reinjected now,
/// or once the guest's NMI window opens. Any exception stops the guest.
pub(super) fn exception_or_nmi(state: ExitState, exit: &ExitInfo) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState) {
    if !exit.interruption_info.is_nmi() {
        return (ExitEvent::Unexpected, state);
    }
    if exit.interruptibility & NMI_INJECTION_BLOCKED == 0 {
        (ExitEvent::NmiInjected, injected(state))
    } else {
        (
            ExitEvent::NmiDeferred,
            ExitState {
                nmi_pending: true,
                ..state
            },
        )
    }
}

/// NMI window (exit reason 8): inject the pending NMI.
pub(super) fn nmi_window(state: ExitState, exit: &ExitInfo) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState) {
    if !state.nmi_pending {
        return (ExitEvent::Unexpected, state);
    }
    // Per the SDM, NMI-window exits never occur under MOV SS blocking, but
    // the processor may still report one under STI blocking. Injecting then
    // would fail the VM entry, so keep waiting. (MOV SS stays in the mask;
    // it is harmless.)
    if exit.interruptibility & NMI_INJECTION_BLOCKED != 0 {
        (ExitEvent::NmiDeferred, state)
    } else {
        (ExitEvent::NmiWindowInjected, injected(state))
    }
}

/// EPT violation (exit reason 48). Exactly one is handled: the guest's
/// write to its protected data page, which must come before the first main
/// VMCALL. Any other is [`ExitEvent::EptViolation`].
pub(super) fn ept_violation(state: ExitState, exit: &ExitInfo) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState) {
    let protected_write = exit.protected_page != 0
        && exit.guest_physical & !0xFFF == exit.protected_page
        && EptQualification(exit.qualification).is_protected_write();
    if protected_write && state.ept_writes_granted == 0 {
        (
            ExitEvent::EptWriteGranted,
            ExitState {
                ept_writes_granted: 1,
                ..state
            },
        )
    } else {
        (ExitEvent::EptViolation, state)
    }
}

/// VMCALL (exit reason 18): the guest's NMI handler, or its next main
/// VMCALL. Main VMCALL #1 must come after the EPT violation and show the
/// data page read back as planned.
pub(super) fn vmcall(state: ExitState, exit: &ExitInfo) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState) {
    if exit.guest_rax == u64::from(GUEST_NMI_MARKER) {
        // Saturates: any guest code can make this VMCALL, any number of times.
        return (
            ExitEvent::GuestNmiHandler,
            ExitState {
                nmis_handled: state.nmis_handled.saturating_add(1),
                ..state
            },
        );
    }
    if exit.guest_rax != expected_main_rax(state) {
        return (ExitEvent::Unexpected, state);
    }
    if state.ept_writes_granted == 0 {
        return (ExitEvent::EptWriteMissing, state);
    }
    if state.main_vmcalls == 0 && !data_page_read_back(exit) {
        return (ExitEvent::DataPageMismatch, state);
    }
    let next = ExitState {
        main_vmcalls: state.main_vmcalls + 1,
        ..state
    };
    if next.main_vmcalls < PLANNED_MAIN_VMCALLS {
        (ExitEvent::MainVmcall, next)
    } else {
        (ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall, next)
    }
}
