`src/vmx/guest.rs`:

```rs
//! Guest memory: a code page with a data page right after it, one stack
//! page and one IDT page.
//!
//! The guest's instructions are assembled into the `.efi` image between
//! `guest_code_start` and `guest_code_end`, then copied into a page of their
//! own, so the guest never executes from host code pages. The copy only
//! works because the code is position-independent: no absolute addresses,
//! only relative jumps and RIP-relative addressing.
//!
//! The data page is the one EPT maps read-only (`vmx::ept`). It is allocated
//! together with the code page, so the guest finds it at a fixed distance
//! from its own code (`lea rdi, [rip + guest_code_start]`, plus one page)
//! without being told an address. The guest reads it (allowed), writes it
//! (an EPT violation, after which Aleph0 makes it writable and the write is
//! retried), and reads it back.
//!
//! Before that, the guest runs the instructions Aleph0 emulates (CPUID,
//! RDMSR/WRMSR of IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE, IN/OUT of the COM1 scratch register)
//! and checks each result itself. A wrong one ends in `ud2` with
//! [`GUEST_EMULATION_FAIL_MARKER`] in EAX. MSRs and ports it writes are real
//! hardware, so it saves each one first and restores it afterwards. Then it
//! moves its last variable MTRR to [`GUEST_MTRR_BASE`] and back, which
//! reaches only Aleph0's copy of its MTRRs and the EPT memory types. Then it
//! reads the Local APIC's version register, device memory above RAM that
//! EPT maps UC (`vmx::apic`), which must not exit and must hold a version an
//! integrated APIC has; outside xAPIC mode there is no register page, and it
//! skips the read. Then it runs one `hlt` with IF = 0, with that register
//! (or IA32_APIC_BASE's low half) in EAX for the exit's report: only Aleph0
//! moving RIP past it lets the guest go on.
//!
//! Guest RIP is [`GuestMemory::code_base`], guest RSP
//! [`GuestMemory::stack_top`], and guest IDTR [`GuestMemory::idt`];
//! `GuestState::write` (in `guest_state`) writes them to the VMCS.
//! [`GuestMemory::check_mappings`] confirms that the current page tables,
//! which the guest shares, map the code page executable, the stack and data
//! pages writable, and the IDT page readable for the ring-0 guest.
//!
//! The guest has its own IDT because Aleph0 reinjects NMIs into it: the
//! firmware's IDT would run the firmware's default NMI handler, which
//! dead-loops. Only vector 2 (NMI) is present. Every exception exits to
//! Aleph0 before it reaches the IDT (exception bitmap all ones), and the
//! guest runs with IF = 0, so no other vector is ever delivered through it.

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::apic::{APIC_BASE_MODE, APIC_BASE_XAPIC, IA32_APIC_BASE, INTEGRATED_APIC_VERSIONS, LAPIC_VERSION};
use super::cpuid::ADDRESS_SIZES;
use super::cr::{self, read_cr4};
use super::ept::SIZE_2M;
use super::exit_decision::NMI_VECTOR;
use super::msr::IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE;
use super::mtrr::{self, IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0, IA32_MTRRCAP, PHYSMASK_VALID};
use super::page::{PAGE_SIZE, RESIDENT_CODE, allocate_zeroed_page, allocate_zeroed_pages_of_type};
use super::paging::{self, Mapping, WalkError};
use super::segment::{self, DescriptorTable, GATE_SIZE};
use super::vmexit::VcpuStats;

/// Value the guest loads into EAX before its first main VMCALL.
///
/// The VM-exit handler prints the guest's RAX, so seeing this value on
/// serial shows the guest's own instructions ran, not just that an exit
/// happened. `mov eax` zero-extends, so RAX reads back as this value. The
/// guest adds one before its second main VMCALL, so that exit shows
/// `GUEST_MARKER + 1`.
pub const GUEST_MARKER: u32 = 0xA1E0;

/// Value the guest's NMI handler loads into EAX before its VMCALL: "NMI" in
/// ASCII. The main code's RAX is only ever `GUEST_MARKER` or
/// `GUEST_MARKER + 1`, so the exit handler can tell the VMCALLs apart.
pub const GUEST_NMI_MARKER: u32 = 0x004E_4D49;

/// Rounds of the guest's wait loop (test, pause, decrement) before it gives
/// up waiting for an NMI. PAUSE takes a different number of cycles on each
/// CPU, and its speed varied threefold between Hyper-V runs: 0x20000000
/// rounds once took about 65 s, these 0x04000000 at most about 2.5 s. The
/// `-InjectNmi` NMI arrived after 15.5 and 18.8 million rounds, under a
/// third of this.
pub const GUEST_WAIT_ITERATIONS: u32 = 0x0400_0000;

/// Value Aleph0 writes at the start of the guest data page before launch.
/// The guest reads it into ECX, so seeing it at main VMCALL #1 shows the
/// read went through EPT.
pub const GUEST_DATA_SEED: u32 = 0xDA7A;

/// Value the guest writes to its data page: "EPT" in ASCII. The write is the
/// intentional EPT violation; the guest reads the page back into EDX, so
/// seeing it at main VMCALL #1 shows the retried write landed.
pub const GUEST_EPT_VALUE: u32 = 0x0045_5054;

/// The I/O port the guest reads and writes through Aleph0: the COM1 scratch
/// register (base + 7), a byte with no effect on the UART. COM1 is the
/// guest's; Aleph0 prints on COM2.
pub const GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT: u16 = crate::serial::SerialPort::COM1.base() + 7;

/// Value the guest writes to IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE through Aleph0 and reads
/// back: canonical (bits 63:47 equal), so WRMSR accepts it. The guest puts
/// the original back afterwards.
pub const GUEST_MSR_VALUE: u64 = 0x0000_7A1E_0000_0000;

/// Byte the guest writes to [`GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT`] through Aleph0 and reads
/// back. The guest puts the original back afterwards.
pub const GUEST_IO_VALUE: u8 = 0xA5;

/// Where the guest moves its last variable MTRR, making it UC: the 2 MiB
/// region at 2 MiB. Every identity map reaches it (it spans at least 1 GiB),
/// and UEFI allocates far above it, so nothing the guest runs on is there.
/// With the range's mask for 2 MiB, EPT maps the region as one UC page;
/// with its mask for 4 KiB, only the first page is UC, so the region takes
/// a spare PT.
pub const GUEST_MTRR_BASE: u64 = SIZE_2M;

/// Value the guest loads into EAX before `ud2` when an emulated instruction
/// returned the wrong value, or the Local APIC reads as no integrated APIC. The #UD exit (vector 6) stops the guest,
/// and this marker in RAX on serial says why; its RIP says which check.
pub const GUEST_EMULATION_FAIL_MARKER: u32 = 0xFA11;

/// The exit statistics a finished run of the guest must end with, given the
/// run's own (`actual`): two CPUIDs (leaf 1 and the address sizes), two
/// RDMSRs and two WRMSRs of IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE, three RDMSRs and seven
/// WRMSRs of its last variable MTRR, two INs and two OUTs of the COM1
/// scratch register, one HLT, no exception injected, and nothing forwarded
/// to Hyper-V: its VMCALLs are its script's. Bring-up compares
/// the two once the guest has finished. The number of exits and of NMIs
/// injected depend on whether an NMI arrived during the run, so they are
/// taken from `actual`.
pub fn expected_stats(actual: &VcpuStats) -> VcpuStats {
    VcpuStats {
        cpuid_exits: 2,
        msr_read_exits: 2,
        msr_write_exits: 2,
        mtrr_read_exits: 3,
        mtrr_write_exits: 7,
        io_in_exits: 2,
        io_out_exits: 2,
        halt_exits: 1,
        exception_injections: 0,
        hypercall_exits: 0,
        synthetic_read_exits: 0,
        synthetic_write_exits: 0,
        ..*actual
    }
}

core::arch::global_asm!(
    r#"
    .globl guest_code_start
    .globl guest_nmi_handler
    .globl guest_code_end
guest_code_start:
    // CPUID always exits; Aleph0 executes it and hides VMX (CPUID.1:ECX
    // bit 5), so a guest never tries VMXON.
    mov eax, 1
    xor ecx, ecx
    cpuid
    bt ecx, 5
    jc guest_emulation_failed
    // IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE exits through the MSR bitmap; Aleph0 runs the
    // real RDMSR/WRMSR. Save it, write GUEST_MSR_VALUE, read it back,
    // restore it.
    mov ecx, {kernel_gs_base}
    rdmsr
    mov esi, eax
    mov edi, edx
    mov eax, {msr_low}
    mov edx, {msr_high}
    wrmsr
    xor eax, eax
    xor edx, edx
    rdmsr
    cmp eax, {msr_low}
    jne guest_emulation_failed
    cmp edx, {msr_high}
    jne guest_emulation_failed
    mov eax, esi
    mov edx, edi
    wrmsr
    // The COM1 scratch register exits through the I/O bitmap; Aleph0 runs
    // the real IN/OUT. Save it, write GUEST_IO_VALUE, read it back, restore
    // it.
    mov dx, {scratch_port}
    in al, dx
    mov sil, al
    mov al, {io_value}
    out dx, al
    xor eax, eax
    in al, dx
    cmp al, {io_value}
    jne guest_emulation_failed
    mov al, sil
    out dx, al
    // The MTRRs exit through the MSR bitmap; Aleph0 keeps a copy for the
    // guest and never writes the CPU's. A PHYSMASK holds the address bits
    // below MAXPHYADDR (CPUID.80000008H:EAX[7:0]): R10 = those bits.
    mov eax, {address_sizes}
    cpuid
    mov ecx, eax
    mov r10d, 1
    shl r10, cl
    dec r10
    // IA32_MTRRCAP is not intercepted: AL is the number of variable ranges.
    // Take the last one, ECX = its PHYSBASE, and save its pair in R8D:R9D
    // and R11D:R12D.
    mov ecx, {mtrrcap}
    rdmsr
    movzx ecx, al
    lea ecx, [rcx + rcx + {physbase0} - 2]
    rdmsr
    mov r8d, eax
    mov r9d, edx
    inc ecx
    rdmsr
    mov r11d, eax
    mov r12d, edx
    // Turn the range off before moving it, as an OS does, then give it
    // GUEST_MTRR_BASE and type UC. EDX stays 0 for both writes.
    xor eax, eax
    xor edx, edx
    wrmsr
    dec ecx
    mov eax, {mtrr_base_uc}
    wrmsr
    // Turn it on for 2 MiB: EPT maps the region as one UC page.
    inc ecx
    mov r13, r10
    and r13, -{two_mib}
    or r13, {physmask_valid}
    mov eax, r13d
    mov rdx, r13
    shr rdx, 32
    wrmsr
    // The copy reads back what was written.
    xor eax, eax
    xor edx, edx
    rdmsr
    shl rdx, 32
    or rax, rdx
    cmp rax, r13
    jne guest_emulation_failed
    // Only 4 KiB: the region's pages now differ, so it takes a spare PT.
    mov r13, r10
    and r13, -{page_size}
    or r13, {physmask_valid}
    mov eax, r13d
    mov rdx, r13
    shr rdx, 32
    wrmsr
    // Put the pair back: off, base, mask. The region is one WB page again,
    // and its PT goes back to the spare ones.
    xor eax, eax
    xor edx, edx
    wrmsr
    dec ecx
    mov eax, r8d
    mov edx, r9d
    wrmsr
    inc ecx
    mov eax, r11d
    mov edx, r12d
    wrmsr
    // The Local APIC: in xAPIC mode, which IA32_APIC_BASE (passed through by
    // the MSR bitmap) says, its registers are a page of MMIO at the base
    // address (bits MAXPHYADDR-1:12, R10 still masking the first). EPT maps
    // that page UC, outside RAM, so the read of the version register must
    // not exit, and must give an integrated APIC's version. In any other
    // mode there is no page to read: EAX keeps the MSR's low half.
    mov ecx, {apic_base_msr}
    rdmsr
    mov ecx, eax
    and ecx, {apic_mode_bits}
    cmp ecx, {xapic_mode}
    jne guest_local_apic_done
    shl rdx, 32
    or rax, rdx
    and rax, r10
    and rax, -{page_size}
    mov eax, dword ptr [rax + {lapic_version}]
    cmp al, {apic_version_min}
    jb guest_emulation_failed
    cmp al, {apic_version_max}
    ja guest_emulation_failed
guest_local_apic_done:
    // HLT exits (HLT exiting is on), with the version register in EAX. IF =
    // 0, so no interrupt could ever end the halt: the guest goes on only
    // because Aleph0 resumes past it.
    hlt
    // No NMI handled yet. General-purpose registers are not VMCS fields, so
    // without this EBX would hold whatever the host had at VMLAUNCH.
    xor ebx, ebx
    // The data page follows the code page. RIP-relative, so this still
    // finds it after the code is copied.
    lea rdi, [rip + guest_code_start]
    add rdi, 0x1000
    // Read: EPT allows it, ECX = GUEST_DATA_SEED.
    mov ecx, dword ptr [rdi]
    // Write: EPT maps the page read-only, so this exits (EPT violation).
    // Aleph0 makes the page writable and resumes at this same instruction,
    // which then succeeds.
    mov dword ptr [rdi], {ept_value}
    // Read back: EDX = GUEST_EPT_VALUE.
    mov edx, dword ptr [rdi]
    mov eax, {marker}
    vmcall
    // Main VMCALL #1 is done and Aleph0 advanced RIP past it. Wait for an
    // NMI: the handler below sets EBX. Give up after a fixed number of
    // rounds, so a run without an NMI still ends.
    mov ecx, {iterations}
guest_wait:
    test ebx, ebx
    jnz guest_wait_done
    pause
    dec ecx
    jnz guest_wait
guest_wait_done:
    // Main VMCALL #2: RAX one higher shows the code after VMCALL #1 ran,
    // and EBX says whether an NMI was handled.
    inc eax
    vmcall
    // Aleph0 stops the guest at main VMCALL #2. If it ever resumed it, UD2
    // turns that into an exception exit instead of running into the handler.
    ud2
guest_nmi_handler:
    // Vector 2 of the guest IDT. Tell Aleph0 the reinjected NMI arrived,
    // keeping the main code's RAX intact.
    push rax
    mov eax, {nmi_marker}
    vmcall
    pop rax
    mov ebx, 1
    // IRETQ restores RIP, CS, RFLAGS, RSP and SS only, so EBX stays set for
    // the wait loop. With virtual NMIs on, it also ends the guest's NMI
    // blocking.
    iretq
guest_emulation_failed:
    // An emulated instruction or the Local APIC gave the wrong value: stop
    // with a marker in RAX, which the #UD exit prints.
    mov eax, {fail_marker}
    ud2
guest_code_end:
"#,
    marker = const GUEST_MARKER,
    iterations = const GUEST_WAIT_ITERATIONS,
    nmi_marker = const GUEST_NMI_MARKER,
    ept_value = const GUEST_EPT_VALUE,
    fail_marker = const GUEST_EMULATION_FAIL_MARKER,
    kernel_gs_base = const IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE,
    msr_low = const GUEST_MSR_VALUE as u32,
    msr_high = const (GUEST_MSR_VALUE >> 32) as u32,
    scratch_port = const GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT,
    io_value = const GUEST_IO_VALUE,
    address_sizes = const ADDRESS_SIZES,
    mtrrcap = const IA32_MTRRCAP,
    physbase0 = const IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0,
    mtrr_base_uc = const GUEST_MTRR_BASE | mtrr::MemoryType::Uncacheable as u64,
    two_mib = const SIZE_2M,
    page_size = const PAGE_SIZE,
    physmask_valid = const PHYSMASK_VALID,
    apic_base_msr = const IA32_APIC_BASE,
    apic_mode_bits = const APIC_BASE_MODE,
    xapic_mode = const APIC_BASE_XAPIC,
    lapic_version = const LAPIC_VERSION,
    apic_version_min = const *INTEGRATED_APIC_VERSIONS.start(),
    apic_version_max = const *INTEGRATED_APIC_VERSIONS.end(),
);

unsafe extern "C" {
    static guest_code_start: u8;
    static guest_nmi_handler: u8;
    static guest_code_end: u8;
}

/// The guest's instruction bytes, as assembled into the image.
fn guest_code() -> &'static [u8] {
    let start = &raw const guest_code_start;
    let end = &raw const guest_code_end;
    // SAFETY: both labels come from the one asm block above, start before
    // end, so the range is the assembled code: initialised, in the image for
    // as long as it runs, and never written.
    unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(start, end.offset_from(start) as usize) }
}

/// Offset of `guest_nmi_handler` from the start of the guest code, which is
/// also its offset in the code page after the copy.
fn nmi_handler_offset() -> usize {
    let start = &raw const guest_code_start;
    let handler = &raw const guest_nmi_handler;
    // SAFETY: both labels come from the one asm block above, so they point
    // into the same object, start before handler.
    unsafe { handler.offset_from(start) as usize }
}

/// Byte offset of the NMI gate (vector 2) in the guest IDT.
const NMI_GATE_OFFSET: usize = NMI_VECTOR as usize * GATE_SIZE;
/// GUEST_IDTR limit: three gates, vectors 0 to 2. Only vector 2 is present.
const GUEST_IDT_LIMIT: u16 = (3 * GATE_SIZE - 1) as u16;
// The NMI gate must lie inside the IDT limit, or the guest would #GP on an NMI.
const _: () = assert!(NMI_GATE_OFFSET + GATE_SIZE - 1 <= GUEST_IDT_LIMIT as usize);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GuestMemoryError {
    /// The assembled guest code does not fit in one page.
    CodeTooLarge,
    /// Failed to allocate the guest code and data pages.
    CodeAllocationFailed,
    /// Failed to allocate the guest stack page.
    StackAllocationFailed,
    /// Failed to allocate the guest IDT page.
    IdtAllocationFailed,
    /// The page-table walk for the code page failed.
    CodeNotMapped(WalkError),
    /// The page-table walk for the stack page failed.
    StackNotMapped(WalkError),
    /// The page-table walk for the IDT page failed.
    IdtNotMapped(WalkError),
    /// The page-table walk for the data page failed.
    DataNotMapped(WalkError),
    /// The code page is mapped with XD set at some level.
    CodeNotExecutable,
    /// The code page is a user page and CR4.SMEP is set, so the ring-0
    /// guest could not execute it.
    CodeBlockedBySmep,
    /// The stack page is read-only at some level.
    StackNotWritable,
    /// The stack page is a user page and CR4.SMAP is set, so the ring-0
    /// guest (RFLAGS.AC = 0) could not push to it.
    StackBlockedBySmap,
    /// The IDT page is a user page and CR4.SMAP is set, so the CPU could
    /// not read the NMI gate while delivering an NMI to the guest.
    IdtBlockedBySmap,
    /// The data page is read-only at some level of the guest's page
    /// tables. The guest's write would then be a page fault, not the EPT
    /// violation the test needs.
    DataNotWritable,
    /// The data page is a user page and CR4.SMAP is set, so the ring-0
    /// guest's accesses to it would fault before reaching EPT.
    DataBlockedBySmap,
    /// The page tables map a guest page somewhere other than itself. Guest
    /// RIP, RSP and IDTR are these virtual addresses, and the EPT identity
    /// map and its protected GPA assume virtual = guest-physical = physical.
    NotIdentityMapped { virtual_address: u64, physical: u64 },
}

/// Checks that `mapping`, the page-table walk of `virtual_address`, maps it
/// to the same physical address.
fn check_identity(virtual_address: u64, mapping: &Mapping) -> Result<(), GuestMemoryError> {
    if mapping.physical != virtual_address {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::NotIdentityMapped {
            virtual_address,
            physical: mapping.physical,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Checks that a ring-0 guest running with `cr4` can execute from `code`
/// and write to `stack`.
///
/// Assumes the guest gets this same CR4 and RFLAGS.AC = 0, as planned for
/// the guest state.
fn check_permissions(code: &Mapping, stack: &Mapping, cr4: u64) -> Result<(), GuestMemoryError> {
    if code.execute_disable {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::CodeNotExecutable);
    }
    if code.user && cr4 & cr::CR4_SMEP != 0 {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::CodeBlockedBySmep);
    }
    if !stack.writable {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::StackNotWritable);
    }
    if stack.user && cr4 & cr::CR4_SMAP != 0 {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::StackBlockedBySmap);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Checks that the CPU can read the guest IDT while delivering an NMI to the
/// ring-0 guest. Delivery reads the IDT as an implicit supervisor access,
/// which CR4.SMAP blocks on a user page whatever RFLAGS.AC says. The CPU
/// never writes the IDT, so a read-only page is fine.
fn check_idt_permissions(idt: &Mapping, cr4: u64) -> Result<(), GuestMemoryError> {
    if idt.user && cr4 & cr::CR4_SMAP != 0 {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::IdtBlockedBySmap);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Checks that the ring-0 guest can read and write the data page through
/// the page tables it shares with the host, so its write reaches EPT
/// instead of causing a page fault first.
fn check_data_permissions(data: &Mapping, cr4: u64) -> Result<(), GuestMemoryError> {
    if !data.writable {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::DataNotWritable);
    }
    if data.user && cr4 & cr::CR4_SMAP != 0 {
        return Err(GuestMemoryError::DataBlockedBySmap);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// How the current page tables map the four guest pages.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GuestMappings {
    pub code: Mapping,
    pub stack: Mapping,
    pub idt: Mapping,
    pub data: Mapping,
}

/// Owns the guest code and data, stack and IDT pages. Never freed: the
/// guest may run from them for as long as the CPU stays in VMX operation.
pub struct GuestMemory {
    /// Two pages: the code, then the data page.
    code: NonNull<u8>,
    stack: NonNull<u8>,
    idt: NonNull<u8>,
}

impl GuestMemory {
    /// Allocate the pages, copy the guest code into the code page, write the
    /// seed into the data page, and write the NMI gate into the IDT page.
    ///
    /// The code and data pages are one two-page [`RESIDENT_CODE`]
    /// allocation: a code type because firmware may map data types
    /// no-execute, and one allocation because the guest finds the data page
    /// right after its code. The stack and IDT pages are resident data. All
    /// four are resident although the test guest never runs after
    /// `ExitBootServices`: EPT keeps the data page read-only for the firmware
    /// guest too, so an OS reusing it would stop at an EPT violation. The
    /// gate uses the current CS selector, which the guest state copies.
    pub fn allocate() -> Result<Self, GuestMemoryError> {
        let code_bytes = guest_code();
        if code_bytes.len() > PAGE_SIZE {
            return Err(GuestMemoryError::CodeTooLarge);
        }

        let code = allocate_zeroed_pages_of_type(2, RESIDENT_CODE, GuestMemoryError::CodeAllocationFailed)?;
        let stack = allocate_zeroed_page(GuestMemoryError::StackAllocationFailed)?;
        let idt = allocate_zeroed_page(GuestMemoryError::IdtAllocationFailed)?;

        // SAFETY: `code` is a fresh two-page allocation, and the code is at
        // most one page (checked above).
        unsafe { core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code_bytes.as_ptr(), code.as_ptr(), code_bytes.len()) };
        let memory = Self { code, stack, idt };
        // SAFETY: the data page is the second page of the fresh `code`
        // allocation, 4 KiB-aligned, so a u32 at its start is in bounds and
        // aligned.
        unsafe { (memory.data_page() as *mut u32).write_volatile(GUEST_DATA_SEED) };

        // IST 0: the guest takes its NMI on the stack it is running on.
        let gate = segment::interrupt_gate(memory.nmi_handler(), segment::read_cs(), 0);
        // SAFETY: `idt` is a fresh page, and the gate ends within the IDT
        // limit (asserted at compile time), far inside it.
        unsafe { core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(gate.as_ptr(), idt.as_ptr().add(NMI_GATE_OFFSET), GATE_SIZE) };
        Ok(memory)
    }

    /// Address of the first guest instruction, for GUEST_RIP.
    pub fn code_base(&self) -> u64 {
        self.code.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// Number of guest code bytes copied into the code page.
    pub fn code_len(&self) -> usize {
        guest_code().len()
    }

    /// Address of the guest's NMI handler in the code page: the target of
    /// the vector 2 gate.
    pub fn nmi_handler(&self) -> u64 {
        self.code_base() + nmi_handler_offset() as u64
    }

    /// Address of the data page, right after the code page. Under the
    /// identity mappings it is also the page's guest-physical address, the
    /// one EPT maps read-only.
    pub fn data_page(&self) -> u64 {
        self.code_base() + PAGE_SIZE as u64
    }

    /// Top of the downward-growing guest stack, for GUEST_RSP.
    pub fn stack_top(&self) -> u64 {
        // SAFETY: the stack is one page, so this is one past its end, which
        // `add` allows.
        let top = unsafe { self.stack.as_ptr().add(PAGE_SIZE) } as usize;
        assert_eq!(top % 16, 0);
        top as u64
    }

    /// The guest's own IDT, for GUEST_IDTR: vectors 0 to 2, only vector 2
    /// (NMI) present.
    pub fn idt(&self) -> DescriptorTable {
        DescriptorTable {
            base: self.idt.as_ptr() as u64,
            limit: GUEST_IDT_LIMIT,
        }
    }

    /// Walks the current page tables for the four pages and checks that
    /// each is identity-mapped ([`check_identity`]), the code page
    /// executable, the stack and data pages writable, and the IDT page
    /// readable by the CPU on the ring-0 guest's behalf.
    ///
    /// The guest will use these same tables (guest CR3 = host CR3); EPT
    /// translates their result a second time.
    /// Each page is 4 KiB-aligned, so one walk covers the whole page: a page
    /// can never straddle two mappings.
    ///
    /// Requiring XD clear is stricter than needed when EFER.NXE = 0, but then
    /// a set XD bit is reserved and would fault anyway. The guest runs in
    /// ring 0, so a user page is also refused where CR4.SMEP (code) or
    /// CR4.SMAP (stack, IDT) would block it; see [`check_permissions`] and
    /// [`check_idt_permissions`].
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Boot services must still be active; see [`paging::walk_current`].
    pub unsafe fn check_mappings(&self) -> Result<GuestMappings, GuestMemoryError> {
        let stack_base = self.stack.as_ptr() as u64;
        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees boot services are active, which is
        // what `walk_current` needs.
        let walk = |address| unsafe { paging::walk_current(address) };
        let code = walk(self.code_base()).map_err(GuestMemoryError::CodeNotMapped)?;
        let stack = walk(stack_base).map_err(GuestMemoryError::StackNotMapped)?;
        let idt = walk(self.idt().base).map_err(GuestMemoryError::IdtNotMapped)?;
        let data = walk(self.data_page()).map_err(GuestMemoryError::DataNotMapped)?;
        for (virtual_address, mapping) in [
            (self.code_base(), &code),
            (stack_base, &stack),
            (self.idt().base, &idt),
            (self.data_page(), &data),
        ] {
            check_identity(virtual_address, mapping)?;
        }

        let cr4 = read_cr4();
        check_permissions(&code, &stack, cr4)?;
        check_idt_permissions(&idt, cr4)?;
        check_data_permissions(&data, cr4)?;
        Ok(GuestMappings { code, stack, idt, data })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../tests/unit/vmx/guest.rs"]
mod tests;

```

`src/vmx/guest_state.rs`:

```rs
//! Guest state for the first VM entry.
//!
//! On VMLAUNCH the CPU loads the guest's registers from the VMCS guest-state
//! fields, checks them, and starts executing at GUEST_RIP. Every register the
//! guest will have must therefore be written here first.
//!
//! The simplest valid 64-bit state is a copy of what the host CPU is running
//! with right now, since that state demonstrably works. Only RIP, RSP,
//! RFLAGS and IDTR depend on the guest ([`GuestEntry`]):
//!
//! | Guest field                  | Value                                     |
//! |------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
//! | RIP, RSP                     | test guest: its code page and stack top; firmware: the instruction after VMLAUNCH and the stack it runs on |
//! | RFLAGS                       | test guest: `0x2`, only the always-1 bit (IF = 0, AC = 0); firmware: the running RFLAGS, IF included |
//! | CR0, CR3, CR4                | the host's (same page tables, same modes) |
//! | CS, SS, DS, ES, FS, GS, TR   | the host's selectors, decoded from the GDT |
//! | LDTR                         | unusable (UEFI does not use an LDT)       |
//! | GDTR                         | the host's table                          |
//! | IDTR                         | test guest: its own IDT (`GuestMemory::idt`); firmware: the firmware's |
//! | SYSENTER MSRs                | the host's                                |
//! | DR7, IA32_DEBUGCTL           | `0x400` (reset value), `0`                |
//! | PAT, EFER                    | the host's, only if the entry controls load them |
//! | VMCS link pointer            | all ones: no shadow VMCS                  |
//! | activity, interruptibility, pending debug exceptions | `0`: running, nothing blocked |
//!
//! Without the "load IA32_EFER" entry control, the guest keeps the CPU's
//! current EFER, with LMA/LME set from the "IA-32e mode guest" control. So
//! the guest gets the host's EFER.NXE either way, which the shared page
//! tables need (see [`super::paging`]).
//!
//! The guest shares the host's GDT, TSS and page tables. The test guest has
//! an IDT of its own for NMIs; the firmware keeps its own IDT, and stays on
//! Aleph0's GDT copy with its TSS, since VM entry needs a busy TSS in TR and
//! Hyper-V's firmware never loads one. That is a bring-up stage, not
//! isolation.
//!
//! [`GuestState::write`] reads every field back after writing it. As with
//! the host fields, that proves storage only: the CPU checks the state when
//! VMLAUNCH runs, and reports a bad guest state as exit reason 33.
//! [`check_segments`] catches the two mistakes most likely to cause that.
//!
//! After a VM exit the same fields hold the guest's state as the CPU saved
//! it. [`GuestState::read`] reads them back, and every stop prints them with
//! [`GuestState::report`], in the format bring-up prints before VMLAUNCH.

use core::fmt;

use super::cr;
use super::msr;
use super::segment::{self, ACCESS_RIGHTS_UNUSABLE, DescriptorTable, SegmentDescriptor};
use super::vmcs::{self, VmcsError, fields};

/// RFLAGS bit 1 is reserved and must be 1; every other bit is 0.
const INITIAL_RFLAGS: u64 = 0x2;
/// DR7 after reset: only the reserved bit 10 set, no breakpoints.
const INITIAL_DR7: u64 = 0x400;
/// No shadow VMCS. Zero would be read as a pointer and fail VM entry.
const VMCS_LINK_POINTER_NONE: u64 = !0;

/// Access-rights type bit 0: "accessed". VM entry requires it in every
/// usable code/data segment. The CPU normally sets it in the descriptor when
/// the segment is loaded, but that is not guaranteed in a copied GDT.
const TYPE_ACCESSED: u32 = 1 << 0;
/// Access-rights bit 4 (S): 1 = code or data segment, 0 = system segment
/// (TSS, LDT, gates).
const CODE_OR_DATA: u32 = 1 << 4;
/// Access-rights bit 13 (L): 64-bit code segment.
const LONG_MODE: u32 = 1 << 13;
/// Access-rights bits 4:0: S and the 4-bit type, which together say what
/// kind of descriptor it is.
const KIND_MASK: u32 = 0x1F;
/// Access-rights bits 4:0 of a busy 64-bit TSS: S = 0, type 0xB. LTR marks
/// the TSS busy, and VM entry into a 64-bit guest requires that type.
const BUSY_TSS_64: u32 = 0xB;

/// One segment register as the VMCS stores it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GuestSegment {
    pub selector: u16,
    pub base: u64,
    /// In bytes, already scaled by the granularity bit.
    pub limit: u32,
    /// VMCS format; see [`SegmentDescriptor::access_rights`].
    pub access_rights: u32,
}

impl GuestSegment {
    /// A register holding a null selector: unusable, so VM entry ignores
    /// its limit and access rights. FS and GS still pass their MSR base.
    fn unusable(selector: u16, base: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            selector,
            base,
            limit: 0,
            access_rights: ACCESS_RIGHTS_UNUSABLE,
        }
    }

    /// A usable register loaded from its 8-byte descriptor, with `base`
    /// supplied by the caller (it lives in different places per register).
    fn from_descriptor(selector: u16, descriptor: SegmentDescriptor, base: u64) -> Self {
        let mut access_rights = descriptor.access_rights();
        if access_rights & CODE_OR_DATA != 0 {
            access_rights |= TYPE_ACCESSED;
        }
        Self {
            selector,
            base,
            limit: descriptor.limit(),
            access_rights,
        }
    }

    fn is_usable(&self) -> bool {
        self.access_rights & ACCESS_RIGHTS_UNUSABLE == 0
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for GuestSegment {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "selector={:#06x} base={:#018x} limit={:#010x} access={:#07x}",
            self.selector, self.base, self.limit, self.access_rights,
        )
    }
}

/// The four VMCS fields of one segment register.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct SegmentFields {
    selector: u32,
    base: u32,
    limit: u32,
    access_rights: u32,
}

/// The fields of ES, CS, SS, DS, FS, GS, LDTR and TR, in the order
/// [`GuestState::segments`] lists the registers. [`GuestState::write`] and
/// [`GuestState::read`] both walk this table, so they cannot disagree.
const SEGMENT_FIELDS: [SegmentFields; 8] = {
    use fields::*;
    [
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_ES_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_ES_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_ES_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_ES_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_CS_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_CS_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_CS_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_CS_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_SS_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_SS_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_SS_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_SS_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_DS_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_DS_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_DS_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_DS_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_FS_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_FS_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_FS_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_FS_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_GS_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_GS_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_GS_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_GS_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_LDTR_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_LDTR_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_LDTR_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_LDTR_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
        SegmentFields {
            selector: GUEST_TR_SELECTOR,
            base: GUEST_TR_BASE,
            limit: GUEST_TR_LIMIT,
            access_rights: GUEST_TR_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
        },
    ]
};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GuestStateError {
    /// The selector names the LDT or lies past the GDT limit.
    BadSelector { selector: u16 },
    /// CS is unusable or not a 64-bit code segment (L = 0), so the guest
    /// could not run 64-bit code at GUEST_RIP.
    CsNot64Bit { access_rights: u32 },
    /// TR is unusable or not a busy 64-bit TSS.
    TrNotBusyTss { access_rights: u32 },
    /// Writing `field` failed: VMWRITE or VMREAD failed, or it read back a
    /// different value than was written ([`VmcsError::ReadbackMismatch`]).
    Vmcs { field: u32, error: VmcsError },
}

/// Where the guest starts: the part of its state that is not a copy of the
/// running CPU's.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GuestEntry {
    /// At `rip` on the stack `rsp`, with interrupts off (RFLAGS `0x2`) and the
    /// IDT `idtr`: the built-in test guest.
    At { rip: u64, rsp: u64, idtr: DescriptorTable },
    /// In place: the code after VMLAUNCH goes on as the guest, on the stack
    /// it runs on, with the RFLAGS it has there, and the IDT `idtr`, the
    /// firmware's. Only VMLAUNCH knows that RIP, RSP and RFLAGS, so
    /// `vmcs::launch_in_place` writes them; until then the fields hold
    /// placeholders: 0, 0 and `0x2`.
    InPlace { idtr: DescriptorTable },
}

impl GuestEntry {
    /// GUEST_RIP, GUEST_RSP and GUEST_RFLAGS to write before VMLAUNCH.
    fn registers(self) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
        match self {
            Self::At { rip, rsp, .. } => (rip, rsp, INITIAL_RFLAGS),
            Self::InPlace { .. } => (0, 0, INITIAL_RFLAGS),
        }
    }

    /// GUEST_IDTR.
    fn idtr(self) -> DescriptorTable {
        match self {
            Self::At { idtr, .. } | Self::InPlace { idtr } => idtr,
        }
    }
}

/// The complete guest state, captured from the host and ready to write.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct GuestState {
    pub rip: u64,
    pub rsp: u64,
    pub rflags: u64,
    pub cr0: u64,
    pub cr3: u64,
    pub cr4: u64,
    pub es: GuestSegment,
    pub cs: GuestSegment,
    pub ss: GuestSegment,
    pub ds: GuestSegment,
    pub fs: GuestSegment,
    pub gs: GuestSegment,
    pub ldtr: GuestSegment,
    pub tr: GuestSegment,
    pub gdtr: DescriptorTable,
    pub idtr: DescriptorTable,
    pub sysenter_cs: u64,
    pub sysenter_esp: u64,
    pub sysenter_eip: u64,
    /// `Some` only when the VM-entry controls load guest PAT.
    pub pat: Option<u64>,
    /// `Some` only when the VM-entry controls load guest EFER.
    pub efer: Option<u64>,
}

impl GuestState {
    /// Captures the host's current state, with the guest's own RIP, RSP,
    /// RFLAGS and IDTR from `entry`, and checks CS and TR.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// VMX operation must be active with the controls already written to the
    /// current VMCS (they decide whether PAT and EFER are needed). The host
    /// GDT must be live and stable.
    pub unsafe fn from_current(entry: GuestEntry) -> Result<Self, GuestStateError> {
        let (rip, rsp, rflags) = entry.registers();
        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees a live, stable host GDT, and UEFI
        // runs in long mode.
        let host = unsafe { segment::read_all() };
        let gdt = &host.gdtr;
        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX operation with a current VMCS.
        let entry_controls =
            unsafe { vmcs::vmread(fields::VM_ENTRY_CONTROLS) }.map_err(|error| GuestStateError::Vmcs {
                field: fields::VM_ENTRY_CONTROLS,
                error,
            })?;

        // SAFETY: `gdt` is the live host GDT (the caller's obligation). The
        // SYSENTER MSRs exist on every x86_64 CPU; PAT and EFER are read only
        // when the entry controls load them, which the CPU allows only if it
        // has them.
        let state = unsafe {
            Self {
                rip,
                rsp,
                rflags,
                cr0: cr::read_cr0(),
                cr3: cr::read_cr3(),
                cr4: cr::read_cr4(),
                es: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.es, None)?,
                cs: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.cs, None)?,
                ss: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.ss, None)?,
                ds: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.ds, None)?,
                fs: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.fs, Some(host.fs_base))?,
                gs: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.gs, Some(host.gs_base))?,
                ldtr: GuestSegment::unusable(0, 0),
                tr: segment_from_gdt(gdt, host.tr, Some(host.tr_base))?,
                gdtr: host.gdtr,
                idtr: entry.idtr(),
                sysenter_cs: u64::from(msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_SYSENTER_CS) as u32),
                sysenter_esp: msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_SYSENTER_ESP),
                sysenter_eip: msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_SYSENTER_EIP),
                pat: (entry_controls & fields::VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_PAT != 0).then(|| msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_PAT)),
                efer: (entry_controls & fields::VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_EFER != 0).then(|| msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_EFER)),
            }
        };

        check_segments(&state.cs, &state.tr)?;
        Ok(state)
    }

    /// The segment registers, in [`SEGMENT_FIELDS`] order.
    fn segments(&self) -> [GuestSegment; 8] {
        [self.es, self.cs, self.ss, self.ds, self.fs, self.gs, self.ldtr, self.tr]
    }

    /// Writes every guest-state field to the current VMCS and reads each one
    /// back. Does not launch.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// VMX operation must be active and a VMCS current on this CPU.
    pub unsafe fn write(&self) -> Result<(), GuestStateError> {
        use fields::*;

        let other_fields = [
            (GUEST_RIP, self.rip),
            (GUEST_RSP, self.rsp),
            (GUEST_RFLAGS, self.rflags),
            (GUEST_CR0, self.cr0),
            (GUEST_CR3, self.cr3),
            (GUEST_CR4, self.cr4),
            (GUEST_GDTR_BASE, self.gdtr.base),
            (GUEST_GDTR_LIMIT, self.gdtr.limit.into()),
            (GUEST_IDTR_BASE, self.idtr.base),
            (GUEST_IDTR_LIMIT, self.idtr.limit.into()),
            (GUEST_IA32_SYSENTER_CS, self.sysenter_cs),
            (GUEST_IA32_SYSENTER_ESP, self.sysenter_esp),
            (GUEST_IA32_SYSENTER_EIP, self.sysenter_eip),
            (GUEST_DR7, INITIAL_DR7),
            (GUEST_IA32_DEBUGCTL, 0),
            (VMCS_LINK_POINTER, VMCS_LINK_POINTER_NONE),
            (GUEST_ACTIVITY_STATE, 0),
            (GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE, 0),
            (GUEST_PENDING_DEBUG_EXCEPTIONS, 0),
        ];

        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX operation with a current VMCS.
        unsafe {
            for (segment, fields) in self.segments().into_iter().zip(SEGMENT_FIELDS) {
                write_field(fields.selector, segment.selector.into())?;
                write_field(fields.base, segment.base)?;
                write_field(fields.limit, segment.limit.into())?;
                write_field(fields.access_rights, segment.access_rights.into())?;
            }
            for (field, value) in other_fields {
                write_field(field, value)?;
            }
            if let Some(pat) = self.pat {
                write_field(GUEST_IA32_PAT, pat)?;
            }
            if let Some(efer) = self.efer {
                write_field(GUEST_IA32_EFER, efer)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads the state back from the current VMCS: the fields
    /// [`write`](Self::write) writes that this type holds. After a VM exit
    /// they are the guest's state as the CPU saved it. PAT and EFER are read
    /// when the entry controls load them, as [`from_current`](Self::from_current)
    /// decides.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// VMX operation must be active and a VMCS current on this CPU.
    pub unsafe fn read() -> Result<Self, GuestStateError> {
        use fields::*;

        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX operation with a current VMCS.
        unsafe {
            let mut segments = [GuestSegment::unusable(0, 0); 8];
            for (segment, fields) in segments.iter_mut().zip(SEGMENT_FIELDS) {
                *segment = GuestSegment {
                    selector: read_field(fields.selector)? as u16,
                    base: read_field(fields.base)?,
                    limit: read_field(fields.limit)? as u32,
                    access_rights: read_field(fields.access_rights)? as u32,
                };
            }
            let [es, cs, ss, ds, fs, gs, ldtr, tr] = segments;
            let entry_controls = read_field(VM_ENTRY_CONTROLS)?;
            Ok(Self {
                rip: read_field(GUEST_RIP)?,
                rsp: read_field(GUEST_RSP)?,
                rflags: read_field(GUEST_RFLAGS)?,
                cr0: read_field(GUEST_CR0)?,
                cr3: read_field(GUEST_CR3)?,
                cr4: read_field(GUEST_CR4)?,
                es,
                cs,
                ss,
                ds,
                fs,
                gs,
                ldtr,
                tr,
                gdtr: DescriptorTable {
                    base: read_field(GUEST_GDTR_BASE)?,
                    limit: read_field(GUEST_GDTR_LIMIT)? as u16,
                },
                idtr: DescriptorTable {
                    base: read_field(GUEST_IDTR_BASE)?,
                    limit: read_field(GUEST_IDTR_LIMIT)? as u16,
                },
                sysenter_cs: read_field(GUEST_IA32_SYSENTER_CS)?,
                sysenter_esp: read_field(GUEST_IA32_SYSENTER_ESP)?,
                sysenter_eip: read_field(GUEST_IA32_SYSENTER_EIP)?,
                pat: match entry_controls & VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_PAT {
                    0 => None,
                    _ => Some(read_field(GUEST_IA32_PAT)?),
                },
                efer: match entry_controls & VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_EFER {
                    0 => None,
                    _ => Some(read_field(GUEST_IA32_EFER)?),
                },
            })
        }
    }

    /// Prints the state, a few lines each starting with `prefix`: before
    /// VMLAUNCH what bring-up wrote, at a stop what the CPU saved. The same
    /// format both times, so the two can be compared line by line.
    pub fn report(&self, prefix: fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
        log!(
            "{prefix} rip={:#018x} rsp={:#018x} rflags={:#x} cr0={:#x} cr3={:#x} cr4={:#x}",
            self.rip,
            self.rsp,
            self.rflags,
            self.cr0,
            self.cr3,
            self.cr4,
        );
        for (name, segment) in [
            ("cs", self.cs),
            ("ss", self.ss),
            ("ds", self.ds),
            ("es", self.es),
            ("fs", self.fs),
            ("gs", self.gs),
            ("tr", self.tr),
            ("ldtr", self.ldtr),
        ] {
            log!("{prefix} {name:<4} {segment}");
        }
        log!(
            "{prefix} gdtr={:#018x}/{:#06x} idtr={:#018x}/{:#06x}; PAT load={} EFER load={}",
            self.gdtr.base,
            self.gdtr.limit,
            self.idtr.base,
            self.idtr.limit,
            self.pat.is_some(),
            self.efer.is_some(),
        );
        log!(
            "{prefix} sysenter cs={:#x} esp={:#018x} eip={:#018x}",
            self.sysenter_cs,
            self.sysenter_esp,
            self.sysenter_eip,
        );
    }
}

/// Builds the guest copy of one host segment register.
///
/// `base` overrides the descriptor's base: FS and GS keep theirs in MSRs,
/// and TR's is 64 bits wide in a 16-byte descriptor.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `gdt` must describe a live, readable GDT through its limit.
unsafe fn segment_from_gdt(
    gdt: &DescriptorTable,
    selector: u16,
    base: Option<u64>,
) -> Result<GuestSegment, GuestStateError> {
    // Selectors 0-3 all name the null descriptor (the low 2 bits are RPL).
    if selector & !segment::SELECTOR_RPL == 0 {
        return Ok(GuestSegment::unusable(selector, base.unwrap_or(0)));
    }
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `gdt` is live and readable.
    let descriptor =
        unsafe { segment::read_descriptor(gdt, selector) }.ok_or(GuestStateError::BadSelector { selector })?;
    let base = base.unwrap_or_else(|| descriptor.base());
    Ok(GuestSegment::from_descriptor(selector, descriptor, base))
}

/// Checks the two segments whose mistakes would otherwise only show up as an
/// unexplained "invalid guest state" exit: CS must be 64-bit code, and TR a
/// busy 64-bit TSS.
fn check_segments(cs: &GuestSegment, tr: &GuestSegment) -> Result<(), GuestStateError> {
    if !cs.is_usable() || cs.access_rights & LONG_MODE == 0 {
        return Err(GuestStateError::CsNot64Bit {
            access_rights: cs.access_rights,
        });
    }
    if !tr.is_usable() || tr.access_rights & KIND_MASK != BUSY_TSS_64 {
        return Err(GuestStateError::TrNotBusyTss {
            access_rights: tr.access_rights,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Reads one field.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// VMX operation must be active and a VMCS current on this CPU.
unsafe fn read_field(field: u32) -> Result<u64, GuestStateError> {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX operation with a current VMCS.
    unsafe { vmcs::vmread(field) }.map_err(|error| GuestStateError::Vmcs { field, error })
}

/// Writes one field and verifies it by reading it back.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// VMX operation must be active and a VMCS current on this CPU.
unsafe fn write_field(field: u32, value: u64) -> Result<(), GuestStateError> {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX operation with a current VMCS.
    unsafe { vmcs::write_verified(field, value) }.map_err(|error| GuestStateError::Vmcs { field, error })
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../tests/unit/vmx/guest_state.rs"]
mod tests;

`src/vmx/host/gdt.rs`:

```rs
//! Aleph0's own GDT for VMX root operation.
//!
//! A VM exit loads GDTR from HOST_GDTR_BASE and the selectors from the host
//! selector fields. The CPU then reads this GDT whenever it reloads a
//! segment register from it: IRETQ out of the host NMI handler reloads CS
//! and SS, and so does any interrupt return.
//!
//! The descriptors sit at the *firmware's* selector indices. On Hyper-V the
//! firmware runs with CS = 0x28 and SS = DS = ES = FS = GS = 0x08, so:
//!
//! ```text
//! index  selector  descriptor
//!   0     0x00     null
//!   1     0x08     data: flat, read/write
//!   2-4            null (unused)
//!   5     0x28     code: 64-bit, execute/read
//!   6-7   0x30     TSS (16 bytes: two slots)
//! ```
//!
//! Teardown loads the firmware's GDTR again but cannot reload CS without a
//! far return. With the same selectors in both tables, the selectors the CPU
//! keeps after a VM exit name the firmware's own code and data descriptors
//! once the firmware's GDT is back, so a later interrupt return in firmware
//! finds what it expects. The TSS takes the first free slot above them.

use super::HostError;
use crate::vmx::context_tables::{TSS_SIZE, tss_descriptor};
use crate::vmx::page::PAGE_SIZE;
use crate::vmx::segment::{self, SELECTOR_RPL_TI};
use crate::vmx::vmcs::HostSelectors;

/// A flat 64-bit code descriptor: base 0, limit 0xFFFFF in 4 KiB units
/// (G = 1), L = 1 and D = 0 (64-bit), present, DPL 0, type 0xB
/// (execute/read, accessed).
pub const CODE_64: u64 = 0x00AF_9B00_0000_FFFF;
/// A flat data descriptor: base 0, limit 0xFFFFF in 4 KiB units (G = 1),
/// D/B = 1, present, DPL 0, type 0x3 (read/write, accessed).
///
/// Both descriptors have the accessed bit set already, so the CPU never
/// writes the GDT to set it.
pub const DATA: u64 = 0x00CF_9300_0000_FFFF;

/// Bytes per GDT slot.
const SLOT_SIZE: usize = 8;
/// Slots in the one page the GDT lives in.
pub const SLOTS: usize = PAGE_SIZE / SLOT_SIZE;

/// The selectors the firmware runs with, which the host GDT keeps.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FirmwareSelectors {
    pub cs: u16,
    pub ss: u16,
    pub ds: u16,
    pub es: u16,
    pub fs: u16,
    pub gs: u16,
}

impl FirmwareSelectors {
    /// The selectors in the segment registers right now.
    pub fn read() -> Self {
        Self {
            cs: segment::read_cs(),
            ss: segment::read_ss(),
            ds: segment::read_ds(),
            es: segment::read_es(),
            fs: segment::read_fs(),
            gs: segment::read_gs(),
        }
    }

    /// The data selectors, in the order the VMCS host fields list them.
    fn data(self) -> [u16; 5] {
        [self.ss, self.ds, self.es, self.fs, self.gs]
    }
}

/// Why the host GDT cannot keep the firmware's selectors.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GdtLayoutError {
    /// CS is null. VM entry refuses a null host CS.
    NullCode,
    /// `selector` has RPL or TI set. VM entry requires both clear in every
    /// host selector.
    NotRing0Gdt { selector: u16 },
    /// A data selector names CS's slot, which cannot hold both descriptors.
    DataInCodeSlot { selector: u16 },
    /// The descriptors and the TSS do not fit in one page.
    TooLarge,
}

/// Where the descriptors go: the selectors the VMCS host fields take, and
/// the GDT limit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GdtLayout {
    pub selectors: HostSelectors,
    /// GDTR limit: the last byte of the TSS descriptor. A VM exit sets the
    /// limit to 0xFFFF regardless; this is for the report and the tests.
    pub limit: u16,
}

/// The slot `selector` names: its index, bits 15:3.
fn slot(selector: u16) -> usize {
    usize::from(selector >> 3)
}

/// Lays out a GDT that keeps `firmware`'s selectors: the code descriptor at
/// CS's slot, a data descriptor at the slot of every non-null data selector,
/// and the TSS in the two slots after the highest of them.
pub fn layout(firmware: FirmwareSelectors) -> Result<GdtLayout, GdtLayoutError> {
    let all = [firmware.cs].into_iter().chain(firmware.data());
    if let Some(selector) = all.clone().find(|selector| selector & SELECTOR_RPL_TI != 0) {
        return Err(GdtLayoutError::NotRing0Gdt { selector });
    }
    if slot(firmware.cs) == 0 {
        return Err(GdtLayoutError::NullCode);
    }
    if let Some(selector) = firmware
        .data()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|&data| slot(data) == slot(firmware.cs))
    {
        return Err(GdtLayoutError::DataInCodeSlot { selector });
    }

    let tss_slot = all.map(slot).max().unwrap_or(0) + 1;
    if tss_slot + 2 > SLOTS {
        return Err(GdtLayoutError::TooLarge);
    }
    let tr = (tss_slot * SLOT_SIZE) as u16;
    Ok(GdtLayout {
        selectors: HostSelectors {
            cs: firmware.cs,
            ss: firmware.ss,
            ds: firmware.ds,
            es: firmware.es,
            fs: firmware.fs,
            gs: firmware.gs,
            tr,
        },
        limit: tr + 2 * SLOT_SIZE as u16 - 1,
    })
}

/// Writes the GDT `layout` describes into `gdt` (one page of [`SLOTS`]
/// slots), with a TSS descriptor for the TSS at `tss_base`. Every slot the
/// layout does not use is null.
pub fn encode(layout: &GdtLayout, tss_base: u64, gdt: &mut [u64; SLOTS]) {
    let selectors = layout.selectors;
    gdt.fill(0);
    for data in [selectors.ss, selectors.ds, selectors.es, selectors.fs, selectors.gs] {
        if slot(data) != 0 {
            gdt[slot(data)] = DATA;
        }
    }
    gdt[slot(selectors.cs)] = CODE_64;

    let tss = tss_descriptor(tss_base, (TSS_SIZE - 1) as u32);
    let (low, high) = tss.split_at(SLOT_SIZE);
    gdt[slot(selectors.tr)] = u64::from_le_bytes(low.try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
    gdt[slot(selectors.tr) + 1] = u64::from_le_bytes(high.try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
}

impl From<GdtLayoutError> for HostError {
    fn from(error: GdtLayoutError) -> Self {
        Self::Gdt(error)
    }
}

`src/vmx/host/handlers.rs`:

```rs
//! What the host IDT's gates run: an NMI handler that hands the NMI to the
//! guest, and a fault handler that prints and halts, except for the #UD or
//! #GP Hyper-V raises at an instruction Aleph0 forwards for the guest
//! (`hyperv::recovery`), which it resumes at the forwarder's recovery point.
//!
//! Both run in VMX root operation with the guest's VMCS current: the CPU
//! loads this IDT only on a VM exit, and teardown loads the firmware's IDT
//! again before it leaves VMX operation. Like the exit handler, they use no
//! firmware and no allocation, and print with `serial_println!`, whose
//! driver keeps no lock that an interrupted print could hold.
//!
//! # NMIs
//!
//! An NMI that arrives in root operation belongs to the guest: it would
//! have caused an NMI exit had the guest been running. The handler cannot
//! inject it, since injecting depends on the exit being handled. Instead:
//!
//! 1. It sets [`NMI_PENDING`], which the exit handler folds into its exit
//!    state at the next exit (`ExitState::with_host_nmi`).
//! 2. It turns NMI-window exiting on, so the guest exits as soon as it can
//!    take an NMI, even if no other exit comes first. That exit injects the
//!    NMI the way an NMI deferred by the guest is injected.
//!
//! Step 2 covers an NMI arriving after the exit handler's last look at
//! `NMI_PENDING` and before VMRESUME: nothing writes the primary controls
//! after that look, so the NMI-window bit stays on.
//!
//! NMIs that arrive while the guest stops or teardown starts are counted but
//! never reach a guest.
//!
//! After an NMI-caused VM exit, the CPU blocks NMIs until the next IRET or
//! VM entry (Intel SDM Vol. 3C, "Architectural State Before a VM Exit").
//! The exit handler never runs IRET, so the next VMRESUME unblocks them; an
//! NMI that arrives in between is held by the CPU and causes an NMI exit
//! right after the entry. A guest that stops at such an exit leaves NMIs
//! blocked until firmware's next interrupt handler runs IRET, as before.

use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, Ordering};

use super::idt::{exception_name, has_error_code};
use crate::vmx::cr::read_cr2;
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::NMI_VECTOR;
use crate::vmx::hyperv;
use crate::vmx::vmcs;

/// Bytes per fault stub: each starts on a 16-byte boundary and fits in it.
const STUB_SIZE: u64 = 16;

/// Set by the host NMI handler, cleared by [`take_pending_nmi`].
static NMI_PENDING: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
/// NMIs taken in VMX root operation since bring-up, for the report.
static NMIS_TAKEN: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

// AT&T syntax, so `$` marks immediates: the vector is an assembler symbol,
// which Intel syntax would read as a memory operand.
//
// `host_vector_stubs`: 256 stubs, one per vector, each at
// `host_vector_stubs + 16 * vector`. A stub makes every frame alike (a 0
// where the CPU pushes no error code, then the vector) and jumps to the
// common part. The error-code list matches `idt::has_error_code`; a host
// test checks every stub's bytes against it. The largest stub is 12 bytes:
// `push $0` (2), `push $vector` (5 from vector 128 on), `jmp` (5).
//
// `host_exception_common`: passes a pointer to the frame to
// `host_exception_handler` (Microsoft x64 ABI: first argument in RCX,
// RSP 16-byte aligned at the call, 32 bytes of shadow space), keeping the
// frame's address in RBP, which the handler preserves. The handler returns
// only for a fault it recovers from, with the frame's RIP moved to the
// recovery point: then it drops the vector and error code and returns with
// IRETQ. Nothing else is restored: the forwarders resume with the registers
// the ABI lets a call change, possibly changed, which they allow for.
//
// `host_nmi_entry`: saves the registers the ABI lets a callee change (RAX,
// RCX, RDX, R8-R11; no vector registers, the target is soft-float, see
// `vmx::vmexit`), calls `host_nmi_handler` on an aligned stack, restores
// them, and returns with IRETQ, which also restores RFLAGS (DF included).
core::arch::global_asm!(
    r#"
    .text
    .balign 16
    .globl host_vector_stubs
host_vector_stubs:
    .set host_vector, 0
    .rept 256
    .balign 16
    .if !((host_vector == 8) || ((host_vector >= 10) && (host_vector <= 14)) || (host_vector == 17) || (host_vector == 21) || (host_vector == 29) || (host_vector == 30))
    pushq $0
    .endif
    pushq $host_vector
    jmp host_exception_common
    .set host_vector, host_vector + 1
    .endr

host_exception_common:
    pushq %rbp
    movq %rsp, %rbp
    leaq 8(%rbp), %rcx
    andq $-16, %rsp
    subq $32, %rsp
    cld
    call host_exception_handler
    movq %rbp, %rsp
    popq %rbp
    addq $16, %rsp
    iretq

    .balign 16
    .globl host_nmi_entry
host_nmi_entry:
    pushq %rax
    pushq %rcx
    pushq %rdx
    pushq %r8
    pushq %r9
    pushq %r10
    pushq %r11
    pushq %rbp
    movq %rsp, %rbp
    andq $-16, %rsp
    subq $32, %rsp
    cld
    call host_nmi_handler
    movq %rbp, %rsp
    popq %rbp
    popq %r11
    popq %r10
    popq %r9
    popq %r8
    popq %rdx
    popq %rcx
    popq %rax
    iretq
"#,
    options(att_syntax)
);

unsafe extern "C" {
    static host_vector_stubs: u8;
    fn host_nmi_entry();
}

/// The handler the host IDT's gate for `vector` points to: the NMI entry
/// for vector 2, the vector's fault stub for every other.
pub fn handler_address(vector: u8) -> u64 {
    if vector == NMI_VECTOR {
        host_nmi_entry as *const () as u64
    } else {
        (&raw const host_vector_stubs) as u64 + u64::from(vector) * STUB_SIZE
    }
}

/// The frame `host_exception_common` passes: what the stub pushed, then
/// what the CPU pushed, lowest address first.
#[repr(C)]
struct ExceptionFrame {
    vector: u64,
    /// The CPU's error code, or the stub's 0 for a vector without one.
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
    rsp: u64,
    ss: u64,
}

/// Called by the fault stubs: prints where Aleph0 faulted and halts this
/// CPU for good. A fault in root operation is a bug in Aleph0, and the
/// state it broke is unknown, so nothing is retried. The one exception is
/// Hyper-V refusing an instruction Aleph0 forwards for the guest: that
/// fault moves the frame's RIP to the forwarder's recovery point and
/// returns, and `host_exception_common` resumes there.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
extern "efiapi" fn host_exception_handler(frame: *mut ExceptionFrame) {
    // SAFETY: `host_exception_common` passes the address of the frame on
    // its stack, which stays put until it returns with IRETQ, and nothing
    // else touches it meanwhile.
    let frame = unsafe { &mut *frame };
    let vector = frame.vector as u8;
    if let Some(resume) = hyperv::recovery(frame.rip, vector) {
        frame.rip = resume;
        return;
    }
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} HOST EXCEPTION in VMX root operation: vector {vector} ({}).",
        exception_name(vector)
    );
    if has_error_code(vector) {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} HOST EXCEPTION: error code {:#x}.", frame.error_code);
    }
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} HOST EXCEPTION: rip={:#018x} cs={:#06x} rflags={:#x} rsp={:#018x} ss={:#06x} cr2={:#018x}.",
        frame.rip,
        frame.cs,
        frame.rflags,
        frame.rsp,
        frame.ss,
        read_cr2(),
    );
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} HOST EXCEPTION: halting this CPU.");
    crate::output::halt_forever()
}

/// Called by `host_nmi_entry`: marks the NMI pending for the guest and asks
/// for an exit as soon as the guest can take it (see the module docs).
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
extern "efiapi" fn host_nmi_handler() {
    NMIS_TAKEN.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    NMI_PENDING.store(true, Ordering::Release);
    // SAFETY: this IDT is live only between a VM exit and teardown, so the
    // CPU is in VMX root operation with the guest's VMCS current. Bring-up
    // checked that the CPU allows NMI-window exiting. A failure leaves the
    // NMI pending; the exit handler turns the window on again before it
    // resumes the guest.
    let _ = unsafe { vmcs::set_nmi_window_exiting(true) };
}

/// Whether an NMI arrived in root operation since the last
/// [`take_pending_nmi`], and clears that.
pub fn take_pending_nmi() -> bool {
    NMI_PENDING.swap(false, Ordering::Acquire)
}

/// Whether an NMI arrived in root operation that the exit handler has not
/// taken yet.
pub fn nmi_pending() -> bool {
    NMI_PENDING.load(Ordering::Acquire)
}

/// How many NMIs arrived in root operation so far.
pub fn nmis_taken() -> u32 {
    NMIS_TAKEN.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// The assembled fault stubs, for the host test that checks them.
#[cfg(test)]
fn stubs() -> &'static [u8] {
    // SAFETY: the 256 stubs are 16 bytes each, back to back from the label,
    // in the image's text for as long as it runs, and never written.
    unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(&raw const host_vector_stubs, super::idt::VECTORS * STUB_SIZE as usize) }
}

/// Faults on purpose in root operation, to show the host fault handler at
/// work: a read of a non-canonical address raises #GP(0).
#[cfg(feature = "host-fault-test")]
pub fn fault_on_purpose() {
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{} host-fault-test: reading a non-canonical address in VMX root operation.",
        crate::TAG
    );
    // SAFETY: none: this faults by design. The #GP goes to the host fault
    // handler, which prints it and halts, so nothing runs after it.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov {value}, qword ptr [{address}]",
            address = in(reg) 0x8000_0000_0000_0000u64,
            value = out(reg) _,
            options(nostack, readonly),
        );
    }
}

`src/vmx/host/idt.rs`:

```rs
//! Aleph0's own IDT for VMX root operation: what the CPU runs when an
//! exception or NMI arrives while Aleph0 itself runs.
//!
//! Until now HOST_IDTR_BASE was the firmware's IDT, so a fault in the exit
//! handler ran a firmware handler from exit context, and an NMI ran the
//! firmware's NMI handler, which dead-loops. This IDT has all 256 gates
//! (one page: 256 × 16 bytes), each to an Aleph0 handler (`handlers.rs`):
//!
//! | Vectors | Handler | Stack |
//! |---|---|---|
//! | 2 (NMI) | marks the NMI pending for the guest, returns | IST1 |
//! | 8 (#DF) | prints and halts | IST2 |
//! | 18 (#MC) | prints and halts | IST3 |
//! | every other | prints and halts | the current one |
//!
//! NMI, #DF and #MC get stacks of their own because they can arrive when the
//! current stack is unusable: an NMI at any instruction, #DF after a fault
//! while delivering a fault (a stack overflow, for example), #MC at any time.
//! Maskable interrupts never arrive: a VM exit loads RFLAGS as 0x2 (IF = 0),
//! and Aleph0 never sets IF in root operation. Their gates exist so a stray
//! `int n` is printed instead of hitting a missing gate.

use crate::vmx::exit_decision::NMI_VECTOR;
use crate::vmx::segment::{GATE_SIZE, interrupt_gate};

/// Gates in the IDT: one per vector.
pub const VECTORS: usize = 256;
/// IDT vector of #DF (double fault).
pub const DOUBLE_FAULT_VECTOR: u8 = 8;
/// IDT vector of #MC (machine check).
pub const MACHINE_CHECK_VECTOR: u8 = 18;

/// The interrupt stacks the host TSS provides, by IST number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum InterruptStack {
    Nmi = 1,
    DoubleFault = 2,
    MachineCheck = 3,
}

impl InterruptStack {
    /// Every interrupt stack, in IST order.
    pub const ALL: [Self; 3] = [Self::Nmi, Self::DoubleFault, Self::MachineCheck];

    /// The IST number a gate names: 1-7.
    pub fn ist(self) -> u8 {
        self as u8
    }

    /// Name for the report.
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Nmi => "NMI",
            Self::DoubleFault => "#DF",
            Self::MachineCheck => "#MC",
        }
    }
}

/// The stack `vector` is delivered on: its own for NMI, #DF and #MC, the
/// current one (`None`) for every other vector.
pub fn interrupt_stack(vector: u8) -> Option<InterruptStack> {
    match vector {
        NMI_VECTOR => Some(InterruptStack::Nmi),
        DOUBLE_FAULT_VECTOR => Some(InterruptStack::DoubleFault),
        MACHINE_CHECK_VECTOR => Some(InterruptStack::MachineCheck),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Whether the CPU pushes an error code when it delivers exception
/// `vector`: #DF, #TS, #NP, #SS, #GP, #PF, #AC, #CP, #VC and #SX (Intel SDM
/// Vol. 3A, "Exception and Interrupt Reference"). The handler stubs push a 0
/// for every other vector, so all frames look alike; their assembly lists
/// the same vectors.
pub fn has_error_code(vector: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(vector, 8 | 10..=14 | 17 | 21 | 29 | 30)
}

/// The mnemonic of exception `vector`, for the report.
pub fn exception_name(vector: u8) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "#DE divide error",
        1 => "#DB debug",
        NMI_VECTOR => "NMI",
        3 => "#BP breakpoint",
        4 => "#OF overflow",
        5 => "#BR bound range",
        6 => "#UD invalid opcode",
        7 => "#NM device not available",
        DOUBLE_FAULT_VECTOR => "#DF double fault",
        10 => "#TS invalid TSS",
        11 => "#NP segment not present",
        12 => "#SS stack fault",
        13 => "#GP general protection",
        14 => "#PF page fault",
        16 => "#MF x87 floating point",
        17 => "#AC alignment check",
        MACHINE_CHECK_VECTOR => "#MC machine check",
        19 => "#XM SIMD floating point",
        20 => "#VE virtualization exception",
        21 => "#CP control protection",
        28 => "#HV hypervisor injection",
        29 => "#VC VMM communication",
        30 => "#SX security",
        // 9 was the 386's coprocessor segment overrun; the rest never had a use.
        9 | 15 | 22..=27 | 31 => "reserved exception",
        _ => "interrupt",
    }
}

/// Fills `idt` with a gate for every vector: to `handler(vector)`, through
/// code segment `selector`, on the stack [`interrupt_stack`] picks.
pub fn fill(idt: &mut [[u8; GATE_SIZE]; VECTORS], selector: u16, handler: impl Fn(u8) -> u64) {
    for (vector, gate) in (0..=u8::MAX).zip(idt.iter_mut()) {
        let ist = interrupt_stack(vector).map_or(0, InterruptStack::ist);
        *gate = interrupt_gate(handler(vector), selector, ist);
    }
}

`src/vmx/host/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! What Aleph0 runs on in VMX root operation: its own page tables, GDT,
//! TSS and IDT, with interrupt stacks and handlers.
//!
//! A VM exit loads HOST_CR3, HOST_GDTR_BASE, HOST_IDTR_BASE, HOST_TR_BASE
//! and the host selectors from the VMCS. Until now they were the firmware's
//! (a copy of its GDT, in the TSS's case), so the exit handler depended on
//! firmware memory the OS may reuse after `ExitBootServices`, and an NMI or
//! fault in root operation ran a firmware handler. [`HostEnvironment`]
//! replaces all of them:
//!
//! | VMCS field | Built by | Contents |
//! |---|---|---|
//! | HOST_CR3 | `page_tables.rs` | identity map of everything the UEFI memory map reaches |
//! | HOST_GDTR_BASE, selectors | `gdt.rs` | code, data and TSS, at the firmware's selector indices |
//! | HOST_TR_BASE | `context_tables::Tss` | IST1-3: the NMI, #DF and #MC stacks |
//! | HOST_IDTR_BASE | `idt.rs`, `handlers.rs` | 256 gates: NMI to the guest, faults printed |
//!
//! The firmware context does not use any of them: bring-up and the test
//! guest keep the firmware's page tables and IDT and the GDT copy from
//! `context_tables.rs`. Only VM exits switch to these, and teardown switches
//! back (`bring_up::teardown`).
//!
//! The pages come from `page.rs` like every other allocation; moving them to
//! memory the OS keeps is a later step.

mod gdt;
mod handlers;
mod idt;
mod page_tables;

pub use gdt::{FirmwareSelectors, GdtLayoutError};
pub use handlers::{nmi_pending, nmis_taken, take_pending_nmi};
pub use idt::InterruptStack;
pub use page_tables::{HostPageTables, HostPagingError, PageSize};

#[cfg(feature = "host-fault-test")]
pub use handlers::fault_on_purpose;

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::context_tables::{TssError, TssRegion};
use super::cpuid;
use super::cr::read_cr4;
use super::page::{PAGE_SIZE, allocate_zeroed_page, allocate_zeroed_pages};
use super::segment::GATE_SIZE;
use super::vmcs::{HostSelectors, HostTables};

/// Pages per interrupt stack. The fault handler formats with `core::fmt`,
/// which needs more than the few hundred bytes the NMI handler does.
pub const INTERRUPT_STACK_PAGES: usize = 2;

/// Why the host environment could not be built.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HostError {
    Paging(HostPagingError),
    Gdt(GdtLayoutError),
    Tss(TssError),
    /// UEFI could not provide the GDT, IDT or interrupt-stack pages.
    AllocationFailed,
}

impl From<HostPagingError> for HostError {
    fn from(error: HostPagingError) -> Self {
        Self::Paging(error)
    }
}

impl From<TssError> for HostError {
    fn from(error: TssError) -> Self {
        Self::Tss(error)
    }
}

/// Aleph0's root-operation environment. Its pages are never freed: every VM
/// exit loads them.
pub struct HostEnvironment {
    page_tables: HostPageTables,
    gdt: NonNull<u8>,
    gdt_limit: u16,
    selectors: HostSelectors,
    tss: TssRegion,
    idt: NonNull<u8>,
    /// Top of each interrupt stack, in [`InterruptStack::ALL`] order.
    interrupt_stacks: [u64; InterruptStack::ALL.len()],
}

impl HostEnvironment {
    /// Builds the page tables (an identity map of `[0, map_end)`), the
    /// interrupt stacks, the TSS, the GDT that keeps `firmware`'s selectors,
    /// and the IDT.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Boot services must still be active, and physical memory must be
    /// identity-mapped (as UEFI does), since the tables are written through
    /// their physical addresses.
    pub unsafe fn build(map_end: u64, firmware: FirmwareSelectors) -> Result<Self, HostError> {
        page_tables::check_paging_mode(read_cr4())?;
        let layout = gdt::layout(firmware)?;
        let page_size = PageSize::for_cpu(cpuid::has_1g_pages());
        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees boot services and identity mapping.
        let page_tables = unsafe { HostPageTables::build(map_end, page_size) }?;

        let mut interrupt_stacks = [0; InterruptStack::ALL.len()];
        let mut ist = [0; 7];
        for (stack, top) in InterruptStack::ALL.into_iter().zip(&mut interrupt_stacks) {
            let base = allocate_zeroed_pages(INTERRUPT_STACK_PAGES, HostError::AllocationFailed)?;
            // The CPU aligns RSP down to 16 bytes before it pushes on an IST
            // stack; a page-aligned top already is.
            *top = base.as_ptr() as u64 + (INTERRUPT_STACK_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE) as u64;
            ist[usize::from(stack.ist()) - 1] = *top;
        }
        let tss = TssRegion::allocate_with_interrupt_stacks(ist)?;

        let gdt = allocate_zeroed_page(HostError::AllocationFailed)?;
        // SAFETY: `gdt` is a fresh page, 8-byte aligned, holding exactly
        // `SLOTS` u64s, which nothing else refers to yet.
        gdt::encode(&layout, tss.base(), unsafe {
            &mut *gdt.cast::<[u64; gdt::SLOTS]>().as_ptr()
        });

        let idt = allocate_zeroed_page(HostError::AllocationFailed)?;
        const _: () = assert!(idt::VECTORS * GATE_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE);
        // SAFETY: `idt` is a fresh page, exactly `VECTORS` gates long, which
        // nothing else refers to yet.
        let gates = unsafe { &mut *idt.cast::<[[u8; GATE_SIZE]; idt::VECTORS]>().as_ptr() };
        idt::fill(gates, layout.selectors.cs, handlers::handler_address);

        Ok(Self {
            page_tables,
            gdt,
            gdt_limit: layout.limit,
            selectors: layout.selectors,
            tss,
            idt,
            interrupt_stacks,
        })
    }

    /// The VMCS host fields that come from this environment.
    pub fn vmcs_tables(&self) -> HostTables {
        HostTables {
            cr3: self.page_tables.cr3(),
            gdtr_base: self.gdt_base(),
            idtr_base: self.idt_base(),
            tr_base: self.tss.base(),
            selectors: self.selectors,
        }
    }

    pub fn page_tables(&self) -> &HostPageTables {
        &self.page_tables
    }

    pub fn gdt_base(&self) -> u64 {
        self.gdt.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// The GDT limit: through the TSS descriptor.
    pub fn gdt_limit(&self) -> u16 {
        self.gdt_limit
    }

    pub fn selectors(&self) -> HostSelectors {
        self.selectors
    }

    pub fn tss_base(&self) -> u64 {
        self.tss.base()
    }

    pub fn idt_base(&self) -> u64 {
        self.idt.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// The top of `stack`, as the TSS holds it.
    pub fn interrupt_stack_top(&self, stack: InterruptStack) -> u64 {
        self.interrupt_stacks[usize::from(stack.ist()) - 1]
    }
}
