`src/vmx/host/page_tables.rs`:

```rs
//! Aleph0's own page tables: the identity map VM exits load through
//! HOST_CR3.
//!
//! Until now HOST_CR3 was the firmware's CR3, so the exit handler ran on
//! page tables in `BOOT_SERVICES_DATA`, which the OS may reuse after
//! `ExitBootServices`. These tables belong to Aleph0 and map every address
//! the UEFI memory map reaches, identity (linear = physical), as the
//! firmware's do: the image, every allocation, and the firmware stack that
//! `vmx_return_to_launcher` returns to.
//!
//! The shape is the one `docs/PAGE_TABLE_WALK.md` describes: one PML4 entry
//! (the map ends below 512 GiB), one PDPT, and below it either 1 GiB pages
//! or one PD of 2 MiB pages per GiB:
//!
//! ```text
//! 1 GiB pages:  PML4[0] ─▶ PDPT[0..gibs] = 1 GiB pages               2 table pages
//! 2 MiB pages:  PML4[0] ─▶ PDPT[0..gibs] ─▶ PD[0..512] = 2 MiB pages  2 + gibs table pages
//! ```
//!
//! Every entry is present, writable and supervisor, with XD clear: the host
//! does not switch IA32_EFER on VM exit, so the tables must work whether or
//! not EFER.NXE is set. The memory-type bits (PWT, PCD, PAT) are 0, which
//! selects PAT entry 0, WB by default; the MTRRs then give device memory
//! its type, as they do for the firmware. Accessed and dirty are set from
//! the start, so the CPU never writes the tables.

use crate::vmx::cr::CR4_LA57;
use crate::vmx::ept::level::{Level, Pd, Pdpt, Pml4, TableLevel};
use crate::vmx::ept::{PDPT_SPAN, SIZE_1G};
use crate::vmx::page::{PAGE_SIZE, allocate_zeroed_pages};
use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// Entry bit 0 (P): the entry is used.
const PRESENT: u64 = 1 << 0;
/// Entry bit 1 (R/W): writes allowed.
const WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
/// Entry bit 5 (A): the CPU has used the entry. Set in advance.
const ACCESSED: u64 = 1 << 5;
/// Leaf bit 6 (D): the CPU has written the page. Set in advance.
const DIRTY: u64 = 1 << 6;
/// PDPT or PD entry bit 7 (PS): maps a 1 GiB or 2 MiB page directly.
const LARGE_PAGE: u64 = 1 << 7;
/// Bits 51:12: the physical address in an entry.
const ADDRESS_MASK: u64 = 0x000F_FFFF_FFFF_F000;

/// Entries per table: 4096 bytes / 8 bytes per entry.
const ENTRIES: usize = 512;

/// The size of the pages the map is made of.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageSize {
    /// PDPT entries map 1 GiB each: no PDs at all.
    Huge1G,
    /// PDPT entries point to PDs whose entries map 2 MiB each.
    Large2M,
}

impl PageSize {
    /// 1 GiB pages when the CPU has them ([`crate::vmx::cpuid::has_1g_pages`]),
    /// 2 MiB pages otherwise. Every 64-bit CPU has 2 MiB pages.
    pub fn for_cpu(has_1g_pages: bool) -> Self {
        if has_1g_pages { Self::Huge1G } else { Self::Large2M }
    }

    /// Name for the report.
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Huge1G => "1 GiB pages",
            Self::Large2M => "2 MiB pages",
        }
    }
}

/// Why the host page tables could not be built.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HostPagingError {
    /// CR4.LA57 is set: the CPU walks 5 levels, and these tables have 4.
    /// HOST_CR4 is the running CR4, so the host would walk 5 levels too.
    FiveLevelPaging,
    /// The map would end at `end`: not a whole number of GiB above 0, or
    /// past what one PDPT reaches (512 GiB).
    InvalidEnd { end: u64 },
    /// UEFI could not provide the table pages.
    AllocationFailed,
}

/// Refuses 5-level paging: with CR4.LA57 set, CR3 would have to point to a
/// PML5.
pub fn check_paging_mode(cr4: u64) -> Result<(), HostPagingError> {
    if cr4 & CR4_LA57 != 0 {
        return Err(HostPagingError::FiveLevelPaging);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// How many GiB a map ending at `end` covers. `end` comes from
/// `ept::memory_map_end`, so it is a whole number of GiB, and the map has
/// one PDPT, so it reaches 512 GiB at most; anything else is refused rather
/// than rounded.
fn gibs(end: u64) -> Result<usize, HostPagingError> {
    if end == 0 || !end.is_multiple_of(SIZE_1G) || end > PDPT_SPAN {
        return Err(HostPagingError::InvalidEnd { end });
    }
    Ok((end / SIZE_1G) as usize)
}

/// Pages the tables of a map of `gibs` GiB take: the PML4, the PDPT, and
/// with 2 MiB pages one PD per GiB.
pub fn table_pages(gibs: usize, page_size: PageSize) -> usize {
    match page_size {
        PageSize::Huge1G => 2,
        PageSize::Large2M => 2 + gibs,
    }
}

/// One entry of a level-`L` table. `repr(transparent)`, so a table page is
/// 512 of these back to back.
///
/// As with `ept::EptEntry`, the level decides the constructors: every level
/// above PT may point to a table ([`table`](Self::table)); a PDPT entry may
/// map 1 GiB ([`huge_page`](Self::huge_page)) and a PD entry 2 MiB
/// ([`large_page`](Self::large_page)). The map has no 4 KiB pages.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct HostEntry<L: Level> {
    raw: u64,
    level: PhantomData<L>,
}

impl<L: Level> HostEntry<L> {
    const fn from_raw(raw: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            raw,
            level: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<L: TableLevel> HostEntry<L> {
    /// An entry pointing to the level-`L::Next` table at `address`.
    pub fn table(address: u64) -> Self {
        Self::from_raw((address & ADDRESS_MASK) | PRESENT | WRITABLE | ACCESSED)
    }
}

/// The bits of a leaf entry for the large page at `address`.
fn large_page_bits(address: u64) -> u64 {
    (address & ADDRESS_MASK) | PRESENT | WRITABLE | ACCESSED | DIRTY | LARGE_PAGE
}

impl HostEntry<Pdpt> {
    /// An entry mapping the 1 GiB page at `address`, which must be 1 GiB
    /// aligned.
    pub fn huge_page(address: u64) -> Self {
        Self::from_raw(large_page_bits(address))
    }
}

impl HostEntry<Pd> {
    /// An entry mapping the 2 MiB page at `address`, which must be 2 MiB
    /// aligned.
    pub fn large_page(address: u64) -> Self {
        Self::from_raw(large_page_bits(address))
    }
}

/// The tables of a map, as slices, with the physical address of the PDPT
/// and of the first PD. Under UEFI's identity mapping a table's physical
/// address is its virtual one; on the host tests these are made-up numbers.
struct Tables<'a> {
    pml4: &'a mut [HostEntry<Pml4>],
    pdpt: &'a mut [HostEntry<Pdpt>],
    /// With 2 MiB pages, one PD per GiB, back to back; empty otherwise.
    pds: &'a mut [HostEntry<Pd>],
    pdpt_address: u64,
    pds_address: u64,
}

/// Fills `tables` with an identity map of the first `gibs` GiB in
/// `page_size` pages. `tables.pds` holds `gibs` PDs for 2 MiB pages, and
/// none for 1 GiB pages.
fn fill_identity_map(tables: Tables<'_>, gibs: usize, page_size: PageSize) {
    tables.pml4[0] = HostEntry::table(tables.pdpt_address);
    for (gib, entry) in tables.pdpt[..gibs].iter_mut().enumerate() {
        let address = gib as u64 * SIZE_1G;
        *entry = match page_size {
            PageSize::Huge1G => HostEntry::huge_page(address),
            PageSize::Large2M => HostEntry::table(tables.pds_address + (gib * PAGE_SIZE) as u64),
        };
    }
    // The PDs are back to back, so PD entry number `i` across all of them
    // maps i * 2 MiB.
    for (i, entry) in tables.pds.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *entry = HostEntry::large_page(i as u64 * (SIZE_1G / ENTRIES as u64));
    }
}

/// Aleph0's host page tables. Never freed: every VM exit loads them, and
/// the code that runs after the guest stops uses them until teardown loads
/// the firmware's CR3 again.
pub struct HostPageTables {
    pml4: u64,
    end: u64,
    page_size: PageSize,
    table_pages: usize,
}

impl HostPageTables {
    /// Builds an identity map of `[0, end)` in `page_size` pages.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Boot services must still be active, and physical memory must be
    /// identity-mapped (as UEFI does), since the tables are filled through
    /// their physical addresses.
    pub unsafe fn build(end: u64, page_size: PageSize) -> Result<Self, HostPagingError> {
        let gibs = gibs(end)?;
        let pd_pages = table_pages(gibs, page_size) - 2;
        let pml4 = allocate_zeroed_pages(1, HostPagingError::AllocationFailed)?.as_ptr() as u64;
        let pdpt = allocate_zeroed_pages(1, HostPagingError::AllocationFailed)?.as_ptr() as u64;
        // No allocation at all when there are no PDs: UEFI refuses 0 pages.
        let pds = match pd_pages {
            0 => 0,
            pages => allocate_zeroed_pages(pages, HostPagingError::AllocationFailed)?.as_ptr() as u64,
        };

        /// The `pages` table pages at `address` as one slice of entries.
        ///
        /// # Safety
        ///
        /// `address` is a page-aligned allocation of `pages` zeroed pages
        /// (or `pages` is 0), and nothing else refers to it while the slice
        /// lives.
        unsafe fn table<'a, L: Level>(address: u64, pages: usize) -> &'a mut [HostEntry<L>] {
            if pages == 0 {
                return &mut [];
            }
            // SAFETY: the caller guarantees the memory is ours and as long as
            // the slice; an all-zero entry is a valid (not present) entry.
            unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(address as *mut HostEntry<L>, pages * ENTRIES) }
        }
        // SAFETY: each allocation above is page-aligned, zeroed and as long
        // as its slice, and nothing else refers to it yet.
        let tables = unsafe {
            Tables {
                pml4: table(pml4, 1),
                pdpt: table(pdpt, 1),
                pds: table(pds, pd_pages),
                pdpt_address: pdpt,
                pds_address: pds,
            }
        };
        fill_identity_map(tables, gibs, page_size);

        Ok(Self {
            pml4,
            end,
            page_size,
            table_pages: table_pages(gibs, page_size),
        })
    }

    /// The value for HOST_CR3: the PML4's address, with PWT, PCD and (when
    /// CR4.PCIDE is set) the PCID all 0.
    pub fn cr3(&self) -> u64 {
        self.pml4
    }

    /// End of the map: linear addresses `[0, end)` are mapped to themselves.
    pub fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    /// The size of the pages the map uses.
    pub fn page_size(&self) -> PageSize {
        self.page_size
    }

    /// Pages holding the tables.
    pub fn table_pages(&self) -> usize {
        self.table_pages
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../../tests/unit/vmx/host/page_tables.rs"]
mod tests;

```

`src/vmx/hyperv.rs`:

```rs
//! Hyper-V's interface to its guests, which Aleph0's guest keeps
//! (docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md): Aleph0 repeats each hypercall and each
//! synthetic-MSR access in root operation, so L0 Hyper-V serves it as an
//! access of Aleph0's own virtual processor, the one the guest ran on before
//! Aleph0 started.
//!
//! ```text
//! guest (L2)                    Aleph0 (L1, root)                 Hyper-V (L0)
//! VMCALL, RCX/RDX/R8 ─exit 18─▶ forward_hypercall: same RCX/RDX/R8,
//!                               VMCALL ──────────────────────────▶ serves it
//!        RAX, RCX, RDX, R8 ◀──── into the guest's frame, RIP past ◀ RAX = status
//! RDMSR 0x40000020 ─exit 31───▶ forward_rdmsr: RDMSR ────────────▶ answers
//!        EDX:EAX ◀────────────── into the guest's frame ◀──────────
//! ```
//!
//! EPT is an identity map, so every GPA a hypercall names (its input and
//! output pages in RDX and R8) means the same page to Hyper-V. The pages
//! Hyper-V overlays at GPAs the guest picked (the hypercall page, the
//! reference TSC page, the SynIC's message and event pages) sit in Aleph0's
//! address space, which the guest sees through the same map.
//!
//! Hyper-V refuses some of what it is asked: a hypercall before the guest
//! enabled the hypercall page gets #UD, a value an MSR does not take #GP.
//! (An MSR Hyper-V does not define at all, in its block or not, reads 0 and
//! ignores writes: `forward-refusal-test` showed it.) Aleph0 cannot know all
//! of that up front, so the forwarders let the CPU tell: the host fault
//! handler resumes each forwarding instruction's #UD or #GP at its recovery
//! point ([`recovery`]), and the guest gets the same exception at its own
//! instruction, as it would without Aleph0.
//!
//! Fast hypercalls also pass data in XMM0-XMM5. Aleph0 never touches vector
//! state (soft-float target, see `vmx::vmexit`), so those stay the guest's
//! across the forward.

use core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid, CpuidResult};
use core::ops::RangeInclusive;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

/// CPUID.1:ECX bit 31: a hypervisor is present, and leaves 0x40000000 and up
/// describe it.
const HYPERVISOR_PRESENT: u32 = 1 << 31;
/// CPUID leaf whose EAX is the highest hypervisor leaf and EBX:ECX:EDX the
/// vendor ("Microsoft Hv").
pub const VENDOR_LEAF: u32 = 0x4000_0000;
/// CPUID leaf whose EAX names the interface the hypervisor implements.
pub const INTERFACE_LEAF: u32 = 0x4000_0001;
/// CPUID.40000001H:EAX of the Microsoft hypervisor interface, "Hv#1". The
/// TLFS says to check this, not the vendor: other hypervisors (KVM, QEMU)
/// offer the same interface under their own vendor.
pub const INTERFACE_SIGNATURE: u32 = u32::from_le_bytes(*b"Hv#1");

/// Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs, all at `0x4000_0000 + n` (TLFS appendix): the
/// partition's (guest OS ID, hypercall page, reference counter and TSC
/// page, frequencies), the virtual processor's (VP index, APIC assist,
/// SynIC, synthetic timers), and past `0x400000FF` the crash MSRs
/// (`0x40000100`-`0x40000105`), TSC invariant control (`0x40000118`, which
/// Linux writes) and the nested SynIC's (`0x40001080` and up). None is in
/// the MSR bitmap's ranges, so each RDMSR and WRMSR of them exits. One
/// Hyper-V does not define reads 0 and ignores writes, as it does for the
/// guest without Aleph0, so a wide range forwards nothing the guest could
/// not already reach.
pub const SYNTHETIC_MSRS: RangeInclusive<u32> = 0x4000_0000..=0x4000_FFFF;

/// Whether CPUID says the Microsoft hypervisor interface is offered: the
/// hypervisor-present bit in `leaf1_ecx`, a highest hypervisor leaf
/// (`max_leaf`, CPUID.40000000H:EAX) that includes the interface leaf, and
/// "Hv#1" there (`interface`, CPUID.40000001H:EAX).
///
/// Without the present bit, leaves 0x40000000 and up are not a hypervisor's:
/// Intel answers an out-of-range leaf with the highest basic leaf's data.
pub fn offers_interface(leaf1_ecx: u32, max_leaf: u32, interface: u32) -> bool {
    leaf1_ecx & HYPERVISOR_PRESENT != 0 && max_leaf >= INTERFACE_LEAF && interface == INTERFACE_SIGNATURE
}

/// What CPUID says about Hyper-V's interface, for bring-up's report.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Detection {
    /// CPUID.1:ECX.
    pub leaf1_ecx: u32,
    /// CPUID.40000000H: the highest hypervisor leaf and the vendor.
    pub vendor: CpuidResult,
    /// CPUID.40000001H:EAX.
    pub interface: u32,
}

impl Detection {
    /// Reads the three leaves. Under Hyper-V, root operation sees what the
    /// guest sees, since `cpuid_policy` passes these leaves through.
    pub fn read() -> Self {
        Self {
            leaf1_ecx: __cpuid(1).ecx,
            vendor: __cpuid(VENDOR_LEAF),
            interface: __cpuid(INTERFACE_LEAF).eax,
        }
    }

    /// Whether the interface is offered ([`offers_interface`]).
    pub fn offers_interface(&self) -> bool {
        offers_interface(self.leaf1_ecx, self.vendor.eax, self.interface)
    }

    /// The vendor's 12 bytes, EBX then ECX then EDX, as CPUID returns them.
    pub fn vendor_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 12] {
        let mut bytes = [0; 12];
        bytes[0..4].copy_from_slice(&self.vendor.ebx.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&self.vendor.ecx.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[8..12].copy_from_slice(&self.vendor.edx.to_le_bytes());
        bytes
    }
}

/// Whether bring-up found Hyper-V's interface; the exit handler reads it at
/// every exit. False until [`publish`] runs.
static OFFERED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Records, before VMLAUNCH, whether Hyper-V's interface is offered.
pub fn publish(offered: bool) {
    OFFERED.store(offered, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// What [`publish`] recorded.
pub fn offered() -> bool {
    OFFERED.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// The call code of a hypercall input value: bits 15:0 of RCX.
///
/// ```text
///  63:60  59:48        47:44  43:32      31      30:27  26:17        16    15:0
/// ┌─────┬────────────┬──────┬──────────┬───────┬──────┬────────────┬─────┬───────────┐
/// │ res │ rep start  │ res  │ rep count│ nested│ res  │ var. header│ fast│ call code │
/// └─────┴────────────┴──────┴──────────┴───────┴──────┴────────────┴─────┴───────────┘
/// ```
pub fn call_code(input: u64) -> u16 {
    input as u16
}

/// The registers a hypercall reads and writes (TLFS, "Hypercall Inputs" for
/// x64): RCX the input value, RDX and R8 the input and output GPAs (or, for
/// a fast hypercall, its input data, and RDX:R8 its output), RAX the result
/// value. Hyper-V may also update RCX, the rep start index, when it
/// continues a rep hypercall.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct HypercallRegisters {
    pub rcx: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub rax: u64,
}

// `hyperv_forward_hypercall` reads and writes the fields at these offsets.
const _: () = {
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(HypercallRegisters, rcx) == 0);
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(HypercallRegisters, rdx) == 8);
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(HypercallRegisters, r8) == 16);
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(HypercallRegisters, rax) == 24);
};

/// Hyper-V refused a forwarded instruction with the exception its
/// forwarder recovers from: #UD for VMCALL, #GP for RDMSR and WRMSR.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Refused;

/// IDT vectors the forwarders recover from.
const INVALID_OPCODE: u8 = 6;
const GENERAL_PROTECTION: u8 = 13;

// The forwarders, Microsoft x64 ABI (`efiapi`), each returning 0 when the
// instruction ran and 1 when Hyper-V raised the exception [`recovery`] names
// for it. The host fault handler resumes that exception at the `_refused`
// label, with RSP and RFLAGS as at the instruction and every register the
// ABI lets a callee change possibly changed.
//
// hyperv_forward_hypercall(registers = RCX): loads RCX, RDX and R8 from
// `registers`, keeping the pointer on the stack, since Hyper-V may write
// RCX (and RDX, R8 for a fast hypercall's output), and stores all four back.
//
// hyperv_forward_rdmsr(msr = ECX, value = RDX): stores EDX:EAX at `value`.
//
// hyperv_forward_wrmsr(msr = ECX, value = RDX): writes RDX as EDX:EAX.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    r#"
    .globl hyperv_forward_hypercall
    .globl hyperv_hypercall_instruction
    .globl hyperv_hypercall_refused
hyperv_forward_hypercall:
    push rcx
    mov rax, rcx
    mov rcx, [rax]
    mov rdx, [rax + 8]
    mov r8, [rax + 16]
hyperv_hypercall_instruction:
    vmcall
    pop r9
    mov [r9], rcx
    mov [r9 + 8], rdx
    mov [r9 + 16], r8
    mov [r9 + 24], rax
    xor eax, eax
    ret
hyperv_hypercall_refused:
    pop r9
    mov eax, 1
    ret

    .globl hyperv_forward_rdmsr
    .globl hyperv_rdmsr_instruction
    .globl hyperv_rdmsr_refused
hyperv_forward_rdmsr:
    mov r8, rdx
hyperv_rdmsr_instruction:
    rdmsr
    shl rdx, 32
    or rax, rdx
    mov [r8], rax
    xor eax, eax
    ret
hyperv_rdmsr_refused:
    mov eax, 1
    ret

    .globl hyperv_forward_wrmsr
    .globl hyperv_wrmsr_instruction
    .globl hyperv_wrmsr_refused
hyperv_forward_wrmsr:
    mov eax, edx
    shr rdx, 32
hyperv_wrmsr_instruction:
    wrmsr
    xor eax, eax
    ret
hyperv_wrmsr_refused:
    mov eax, 1
    ret
"#
);

unsafe extern "efiapi" {
    fn hyperv_forward_hypercall(registers: *mut HypercallRegisters) -> u64;
    fn hyperv_forward_rdmsr(msr: u32, value: *mut u64) -> u64;
    fn hyperv_forward_wrmsr(msr: u32, value: u64) -> u64;
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    static hyperv_hypercall_instruction: u8;
    static hyperv_hypercall_refused: u8;
    static hyperv_rdmsr_instruction: u8;
    static hyperv_rdmsr_refused: u8;
    static hyperv_wrmsr_instruction: u8;
    static hyperv_wrmsr_refused: u8;
}

/// Where the host fault handler resumes after exception `vector` at `rip`:
/// the forwarder's `_refused` label, when `rip` is a forwarding instruction
/// and `vector` the exception Hyper-V refuses it with. `None` for any other
/// fault, which stays a bug in Aleph0.
pub fn recovery(rip: u64, vector: u8) -> Option<u64> {
    let points = [
        (
            &raw const hyperv_hypercall_instruction,
            INVALID_OPCODE,
            &raw const hyperv_hypercall_refused,
        ),
        (
            &raw const hyperv_rdmsr_instruction,
            GENERAL_PROTECTION,
            &raw const hyperv_rdmsr_refused,
        ),
        (
            &raw const hyperv_wrmsr_instruction,
            GENERAL_PROTECTION,
            &raw const hyperv_wrmsr_refused,
        ),
    ];
    points
        .into_iter()
        .find(|&(at, refused_with, _)| at as u64 == rip && refused_with == vector)
        .map(|(_, _, resume)| resume as u64)
}

/// The guest's hypercall in `registers`, made again in root operation:
/// Hyper-V's results replace them.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// VMX root operation under Hyper-V, at CPL 0, with the guest stopped at its
/// VMCALL exit and the host IDT loaded, whose #UD gate recovers through
/// [`recovery`]. The hypercall acts on Aleph0's virtual processor and on the
/// guest pages the GPAs name, as the guest asked.
pub unsafe fn forward_hypercall(registers: &mut HypercallRegisters) -> Result<(), Refused> {
    // SAFETY: the caller's guarantees; the forwarder reads and writes only
    // `registers` and its own stack.
    match unsafe { hyperv_forward_hypercall(registers) } {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(Refused),
    }
}

/// RDMSR of the synthetic MSR `msr`, in root operation.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for [`forward_hypercall`], for the guest's RDMSR exit and the #GP
/// gate.
pub unsafe fn forward_rdmsr(msr: u32) -> Result<u64, Refused> {
    let mut value = 0;
    // SAFETY: the caller's guarantees; the forwarder writes only `value`.
    match unsafe { hyperv_forward_rdmsr(msr, &mut value) } {
        0 => Ok(value),
        _ => Err(Refused),
    }
}

/// WRMSR of `value` to the synthetic MSR `msr`, in root operation. It acts
/// on Aleph0's virtual processor, as the guest's would have.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for [`forward_rdmsr`], for the guest's WRMSR exit.
pub unsafe fn forward_wrmsr(msr: u32, value: u64) -> Result<(), Refused> {
    // SAFETY: the caller's guarantees.
    match unsafe { hyperv_forward_wrmsr(msr, value) } {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(Refused),
    }
}

/// Once, at the first exit under Hyper-V, forwards an access Hyper-V takes
/// and one that faults, and prints what came back:
/// - RDMSR and WRMSR of 0 to `0x4000FFFF`, which Hyper-V does not define:
///   it reads 0 and ignores the write (seen on Hyper-V), no #GP;
/// - WRMSR of a non-canonical value to IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE, which raises
///   #GP whoever runs it: `Err(Refused)` means the host fault handler
///   resumed the forwarder at its recovery point.
#[cfg(feature = "forward-refusal-test")]
pub fn refuse_on_purpose() {
    static DONE: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
    if !offered() || DONE.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    const UNDEFINED: u32 = 0x4000_FFFF;
    const KERNEL_GS_BASE: u32 = crate::vmx::msr::IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE;
    const NON_CANONICAL: u64 = 0x8000_0000_0000_0000;
    // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation under Hyper-V at CPL 0, with
    // the host IDT loaded; the guest is stopped at this exit. Hyper-V does not
    // define 0x4000FFFF, and the non-canonical WRMSR faults before it writes.
    let (read, write, refused) = unsafe {
        (
            forward_rdmsr(UNDEFINED),
            forward_wrmsr(UNDEFINED, 0),
            forward_wrmsr(KERNEL_GS_BASE, NON_CANONICAL),
        )
    };
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{} forward-refusal-test: RDMSR {UNDEFINED:#x} -> {read:x?}, WRMSR {UNDEFINED:#x} <- 0 -> {write:?}; WRMSR {KERNEL_GS_BASE:#x} <- {NON_CANONICAL:#x} -> {refused:?}; Aleph0 still runs.",
        crate::TAG
    );
}

`src/vmx/instruction.rs`:

```rs
//! Outcome reporting shared by every VMX instruction.
//!
//! VMX instructions do not raise exceptions on ordinary failure; they report
//! through RFLAGS instead. Each module's error type converts from
//! [`VmxFail`], so callers can use `?` straight after [`check_rflags`].

/// How a VMX instruction failed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VmxFail {
    /// CF=1: failed with no current VMCS to record why (VMfailInvalid).
    Invalid,
    /// ZF=1: failed and stored a reason in the current VMCS's
    /// VM-instruction error field (VMfailValid).
    Valid,
}

/// Decodes the RFLAGS value a VMX instruction leaves behind.
///
/// All flags clear on success, CF set for VMfailInvalid, ZF set for
/// VMfailValid. Call this right after the `asm!` block instead of repeating
/// the bit tests.
pub fn check_rflags(rflags: u64) -> Result<(), VmxFail> {
    /// RFLAGS.CF, bit 0.
    const CF: u64 = 1 << 0;
    /// RFLAGS.ZF, bit 6.
    const ZF: u64 = 1 << 6;

    if rflags & CF != 0 {
        Err(VmxFail::Invalid)
    } else if rflags & ZF != 0 {
        Err(VmxFail::Valid)
    } else {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Runs one VMX instruction and decodes its outcome from RFLAGS.
///
/// Expands to the instruction, then `pushfq; pop` into a fresh register,
/// then [`check_rflags`], and evaluates to `Result<(), VmxFail>`. Operands
/// follow the template as in `asm!`, without a trailing comma. Use it
/// inside an `unsafe` block whose `SAFETY` comment covers the instruction.
///
/// VMREAD and VMWRITE do not use it: they have an output, or operands whose
/// width needs spelling out, so they stay explicit `asm!` blocks.
macro_rules! vmx_asm {
    ($template:literal $(, $($operands:tt)+)?) => {{
        let rflags: u64;
        ::core::arch::asm!($template, "pushfq", "pop {rflags}", $($($operands)+,)? rflags = lateout(reg) rflags);
        $crate::vmx::instruction::check_rflags(rflags)
    }};
}
pub(crate) use vmx_asm;

#[path = "../../tests/unit/vmx/instruction.rs"]
mod tests;

`src/vmx/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! VMX (Intel VT-x) support detection.
//!
//! Checking whether the CPU can enter VMX operation takes two checks,
//! which [`detect`] combines into the single entry point the rest of the
//! hypervisor calls:
//!
//! 1. [`cpuid::is_vmx_supported`] — CPUID.1:ECX.VMX\[bit 5\] is set.
//! 2. [`msr::feature_control_vmx_enabled`] — IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL MSR
//!    (0x3A) has the lock bit set and the "VMX outside SMX" bit set.
//!
//! The CPUID check must run before the MSR check: IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL is
//! only guaranteed to exist on CPUs that support VMX or SMX, so reading it
//! on a CPU that doesn't (per CPUID) risks a #GP with no exception handler
//! installed yet.

pub mod apic;
pub mod context_tables;
pub mod cpuid;
pub mod cr;
pub mod ept;
pub mod exit_bitmaps;
pub mod exit_decision;
pub mod guest;
pub mod guest_state;
pub mod host;
pub mod hyperv;
pub mod instruction;
pub mod msr;
pub mod mtrr;
pub mod page;
pub mod paging;
pub mod region;
pub mod segment;
pub mod vmcall;
pub mod vmcs;
pub mod vmexit;
pub mod vmxon;

/// Overall VMX support/readiness state for the current CPU.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VmxCapabilities {
    /// CPUID reports VMX and IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL allows entering VMX operation.
    Supported,
    /// CPUID does not report the VMX feature bit.
    NotSupportedByCpu,
    /// CPUID reports VMX, but IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL disables it (e.g. locked
    /// by BIOS/firmware with the VMX-outside-SMX bit clear).
    DisabledByFirmware,
}

/// Runs the full VMX support/enablement check.
///
/// Checks CPUID first; the MSR check only runs if CPUID confirms VMX
/// support, since IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL isn't guaranteed to exist otherwise.
/// That order is what makes this safe to call on any CPU.
pub fn detect() -> VmxCapabilities {
    if !cpuid::is_vmx_supported() {
        return VmxCapabilities::NotSupportedByCpu;
    }

    // SAFETY: CPUID reports VMX, so IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL exists.
    if unsafe { msr::feature_control_vmx_enabled() } {
        VmxCapabilities::Supported
    } else {
        VmxCapabilities::DisabledByFirmware
    }
}

`src/vmx/msr.rs`:

```rs
//! Model-specific registers (MSRs): their addresses, the bits this
//! hypervisor reads in them, and RDMSR and WRMSR.
use core::arch::asm;

use super::vmcs::fields::{CPU_BASED_ACTIVATE_SECONDARY_CONTROLS, SECONDARY_ENABLE_EPT, SECONDARY_ENABLE_VPID};

/// MSR address of IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL.
pub const IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL: u32 = 0x3A;

/// Bit 0: lock bit. Once set, the MSR is read-only until reset.
pub const LOCK_BIT: u64 = 1 << 0;

/// Bit 2: enable VMX outside SMX operation.
pub const VMX_OUTSIDE_SMX_BIT: u64 = 1 << 2;

/// SYSENTER's host code selector, stack pointer, and entry address.
pub const IA32_SYSENTER_CS: u32 = 0x174;
pub const IA32_SYSENTER_ESP: u32 = 0x175;
pub const IA32_SYSENTER_EIP: u32 = 0x176;

/// Page attribute table and extended feature enable register.
pub const IA32_PAT: u32 = 0x277;
pub const IA32_EFER: u32 = 0xC000_0080;

/// IA32_EFER bit 11 (NXE): no-execute enable. While clear, the XD bit in a
/// page-table entry is reserved, not a permission.
pub const EFER_NXE: u64 = 1 << 11;

/// MSRs holding the FS and GS segment bases. Unlike the selectors, these are
/// live in long mode: operating systems use FS/GS for per-thread and per-CPU
/// data.
pub const IA32_FS_BASE: u32 = 0xC000_0100;
pub const IA32_GS_BASE: u32 = 0xC000_0101;
/// IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE: the GS base SWAPGS exchanges with IA32_GS_BASE.
/// VM entry and exit do not switch it, so while the guest runs it holds the
/// guest's value, and Aleph0 (which never runs SWAPGS) does not use it.
pub const IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE: u32 = 0xC000_0102;
/// MSRs whose guest value is a VMCS guest-state field (loaded at VM entry,
/// saved at VM exit when the controls say so). Listed for
/// `exit_bitmaps::VMCS_HELD_MSRS`; Aleph0 does not read or write them.
pub const IA32_DEBUGCTL: u32 = 0x1D9;
pub const IA32_PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL: u32 = 0x38F;
pub const IA32_BNDCFGS: u32 = 0xD90;

/// Reads IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The CPU must support VMX or SMX (CPUID), or the MSR may not exist and the
/// read raises #GP.
pub unsafe fn read_feature_control() -> u64 {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX or SMX support, so the MSR exists;
    // reading it has no side effects.
    unsafe { rdmsr(IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL) }
}

/// Returns whether VMX is enabled for operation outside SMX.
///
/// The IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL MSR must be locked and the
/// VMX-outside-SMX bit (bit 2) must be set.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for [`read_feature_control`]: the CPU must support VMX or SMX.
pub unsafe fn feature_control_vmx_enabled() -> bool {
    // SAFETY: the caller's obligation, as for `read_feature_control`.
    let value = unsafe { read_feature_control() };

    let locked = value & LOCK_BIT != 0;
    let vmx_enabled = value & VMX_OUTSIDE_SMX_BIT != 0;

    locked && vmx_enabled
}

/// IA32_VMX_BASIC. Bits 0..=30: VMCS revision identifier (bit 31 is always 0).
/// Bit 55: see [`VMX_BASIC_TRUE_CONTROLS`].
pub const IA32_VMX_BASIC: u32 = 0x480;
/// IA32_VMX_BASIC bit 55: the `IA32_VMX_TRUE_*_CTLS` MSRs exist and should
/// be preferred over the non-TRUE variants when configuring the VMCS.
pub const VMX_BASIC_TRUE_CONTROLS: u64 = 1 << 55;

pub const IA32_VMX_PINBASED_CTLS: u32 = 0x481;
pub const IA32_VMX_PROCBASED_CTLS: u32 = 0x482;
pub const IA32_VMX_EXIT_CTLS: u32 = 0x483;
pub const IA32_VMX_ENTRY_CTLS: u32 = 0x484;
pub const IA32_VMX_TRUE_PINBASED_CTLS: u32 = 0x48D;
pub const IA32_VMX_TRUE_PROCBASED_CTLS: u32 = 0x48E;
pub const IA32_VMX_TRUE_EXIT_CTLS: u32 = 0x48F;
pub const IA32_VMX_TRUE_ENTRY_CTLS: u32 = 0x490;

/// Secondary processor-based controls: same layout as the other control
/// MSRs. It has no "true" variant. Exists only if the primary controls allow
/// bit 31 (activate secondary controls).
pub const IA32_VMX_PROCBASED_CTLS2: u32 = 0x48B;
/// What EPT and VPID support: page-walk lengths, memory types, page sizes,
/// INVEPT types. Exists only if the secondary controls allow EPT or VPID.
pub const IA32_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP: u32 = 0x48C;

/// One raw VMX control capability MSR, for one 32-bit control field.
///
/// The low 32 bits require control bits to be 1; the high 32 bits allow
/// control bits to be 1. At the same bit position: (low, high) = (0, 0)
/// means must be 0, (0, 1) means either value, and (1, 1) means must be 1.
/// (1, 0) is inconsistent.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ControlCapability(pub u64);

/// A control value the CPU does not allow: a requested bit outside the
/// allowed half, or a capability whose required bits are not allowed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UnsupportedControl;

impl ControlCapability {
    /// Bits that must be 1 (the low half).
    pub fn required(self) -> u32 {
        self.0 as u32
    }

    /// Bits that may be 1 (the high half).
    pub fn allowed(self) -> u32 {
        (self.0 >> 32) as u32
    }

    /// Whether every bit of `bits` may be 1.
    pub fn allows(self, bits: u32) -> bool {
        self.allowed() & bits == bits
    }

    /// The control value for `desired`: its bits plus the required ones.
    /// Rejects an inconsistent capability or a requested bit the CPU
    /// cannot enable.
    pub fn choose(self, desired: u32) -> Result<u32, UnsupportedControl> {
        if !self.allows(self.required()) || !self.allows(desired) {
            return Err(UnsupportedControl);
        }
        // Add mandatory bits without changing any other requested bits.
        Ok(desired | self.required())
    }
}

/// Raw VMX capability MSRs, not the values currently in the VMCS.
/// `basic` and `ept_vpid_cap` have their own layouts; the rest are
/// [`ControlCapability`] pairs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct VmcsControlMsrs {
    pub basic: u64,
    pub pinbased: ControlCapability,
    pub primary: ControlCapability,
    pub exit: ControlCapability,
    pub entry: ControlCapability,
    /// IA32_VMX_PROCBASED_CTLS2, or 0 when the CPU has no secondary
    /// controls. 0 allows no bit, so every secondary request is refused.
    pub secondary: ControlCapability,
    /// IA32_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP, or 0 when the CPU supports neither EPT nor
    /// VPID.
    pub ept_vpid_cap: u64,
}

/// Read IA32_VMX_BASIC and the four control MSRs, selecting the true variants
/// when [`VMX_BASIC_TRUE_CONTROLS`] reports them, plus the secondary controls
/// and the EPT/VPID capabilities where they exist. This does not write VMCS
/// fields.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must first confirm CPU support for VMX before reading VMX MSRs.
pub unsafe fn read_vmcs_control_msrs() -> VmcsControlMsrs {
    // SAFETY: the caller confirmed VMX support, so IA32_VMX_BASIC and the
    // control MSRs exist; the optional ones are read only when the MSR
    // before them says they exist.
    unsafe {
        let basic = rdmsr(IA32_VMX_BASIC);
        let use_true_controls = basic & VMX_BASIC_TRUE_CONTROLS != 0;
        let (pin_id, primary_id, exit_id, entry_id) = if use_true_controls {
            (
                IA32_VMX_TRUE_PINBASED_CTLS,
                IA32_VMX_TRUE_PROCBASED_CTLS,
                IA32_VMX_TRUE_EXIT_CTLS,
                IA32_VMX_TRUE_ENTRY_CTLS,
            )
        } else {
            (
                IA32_VMX_PINBASED_CTLS,
                IA32_VMX_PROCBASED_CTLS,
                IA32_VMX_EXIT_CTLS,
                IA32_VMX_ENTRY_CTLS,
            )
        };
        let pinbased = ControlCapability(rdmsr(pin_id));
        let primary = ControlCapability(rdmsr(primary_id));
        let exit = ControlCapability(rdmsr(exit_id));
        let entry = ControlCapability(rdmsr(entry_id));
        // Reading an MSR the CPU does not have raises #GP, so each one is
        // read only when the MSR before it says it exists.
        let secondary = ControlCapability(if primary.allows(CPU_BASED_ACTIVATE_SECONDARY_CONTROLS) {
            rdmsr(IA32_VMX_PROCBASED_CTLS2)
        } else {
            0
        });
        let ept_vpid_cap = if secondary.allows(SECONDARY_ENABLE_EPT) || secondary.allows(SECONDARY_ENABLE_VPID) {
            rdmsr(IA32_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP)
        } else {
            0
        };

        VmcsControlMsrs {
            basic,
            pinbased,
            primary,
            exit,
            entry,
            secondary,
            ept_vpid_cap,
        }
    }
}

/// Bits that must be 1 in CR0 while in VMX operation.
pub const IA32_VMX_CR0_FIXED0: u32 = 0x486;
/// Bits that may be 1 in CR0 while in VMX operation (a 0 here means "must be 0").
pub const IA32_VMX_CR0_FIXED1: u32 = 0x487;
/// Bits that must be 1 in CR4 while in VMX operation.
pub const IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED0: u32 = 0x488;
/// Bits that may be 1 in CR4 while in VMX operation (a 0 here means "must be 0").
pub const IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED1: u32 = 0x489;

/// Reads an arbitrary MSR.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `msr` must exist on this CPU, or RDMSR raises #GP. A few MSRs change
/// state when read; reading one of those must be what the caller wants.
pub unsafe fn rdmsr(msr: u32) -> u64 {
    let (low, high): (u32, u32);

    // SAFETY: RDMSR only reads the MSR; the caller guarantees it exists
    // and that reading it is harmless.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "rdmsr",
            in("ecx") msr,
            out("eax") low,
            out("edx") high,
            options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags),
        );
    }

    ((high as u64) << 32) | low as u64
}

/// Writes an arbitrary MSR.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `msr` must exist on this CPU and accept `value`, or WRMSR raises #GP.
/// The new value changes how the CPU behaves, so it must be one the code
/// running afterwards (Aleph0, firmware) can live with.
pub unsafe fn wrmsr(msr: u32, value: u64) {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees the MSR exists, accepts the value, and
    // that the change is harmless here.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "wrmsr",
            in("ecx") msr,
            in("eax") value as u32,
            in("edx") (value >> 32) as u32,
            options(nostack, preserves_flags),
        );
    }
}

`src/vmx/mtrr/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! Memory type range registers (MTRRs): the memory type firmware gives each
//! range of physical memory.
//!
//! The memory type decides how the CPU caches an access: write-back for RAM,
//! uncacheable for device registers, write-combining for a framebuffer.
//! Without EPT the CPU takes it from the MTRRs, combined with the PAT type
//! the page tables select. With EPT on, the MTRRs no longer apply to guest
//! accesses: the EPT leaf entry's type takes their place. So `ept.rs` puts
//! the type read here into each entry, and the guest gets the types it would
//! get without Aleph0. The longer walkthrough is in `docs/MTRR.md`.
//!
//! The registers (Intel SDM Vol. 3A, "Memory Type Range Registers"):
//!
//! - IA32_MTRRCAP: how many variable ranges exist, and whether the fixed
//!   ones do.
//! - IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: the type of memory no range covers, and the enable
//!   bits.
//! - 11 fixed-range MSRs: the first MiB, eight ranges per MSR (of 64, 16 or
//!   4 KiB), one type byte per range.
//! - Variable ranges: IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASEn / IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASKn pairs. An
//!   address is in range n when `address & mask == base & mask`.
//!
//! This file decodes their values into memory types; `registers.rs` reads
//! the MSRs and knows which values WRMSR refuses.

use core::fmt;

use super::page::PAGE_SIZE;

mod registers;

pub use registers::{MtrrCapabilities, MtrrMsr, MtrrRegisters, MtrrState, every_msr_address, is_msr_address, read};

/// IA32_MTRRCAP: bits 7:0 count the variable ranges, bit 8 says the fixed
/// ranges exist.
pub const IA32_MTRRCAP: u32 = 0xFE;
const CAP_VARIABLE_COUNT: u64 = 0xFF;
const CAP_FIXED: u64 = 1 << 8;

/// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: bits 7:0 the default type, bit 10 (FE) enables the
/// fixed ranges, bit 11 (E) enables the MTRRs.
pub const IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: u32 = 0x2FF;
const DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE: u64 = 1 << 10;
const DEF_TYPE_ENABLE: u64 = 1 << 11;

/// IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0. Variable range n has its PHYSBASE at
/// `0x200 + 2n` and its PHYSMASK right after.
pub const IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0: u32 = 0x200;
/// PHYSMASK bit 11: the range is in use.
pub const PHYSMASK_VALID: u64 = 1 << 11;
/// Bits 7:0 of IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE and of a PHYSBASE: a memory type.
const TYPE_BITS: u64 = 0xFF;
/// Bits 51:12 of a PHYSBASE or PHYSMASK: the address part. Bits above the
/// CPU's physical-address width are reserved, so they read as 0 and need no
/// masking of their own.
const ADDRESS_BITS: u64 = 0x000F_FFFF_FFFF_F000;

/// How many variable ranges Aleph0 keeps. CPUs have 8 or 10; IA32_MTRRCAP
/// could report up to 255, which [`Mtrrs::decode`] refuses rather than
/// dropping ranges.
pub const MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES: usize = 32;

/// Number of fixed-range MSRs.
pub const FIXED_MSRS: usize = 11;

// The fixed-range MSRs, each named after the first address it covers.
/// 0x00000..0x80000 in eight 64 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX64K_00000: u32 = 0x250;
/// 0x80000..0xA0000 in eight 16 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX16K_80000: u32 = 0x258;
/// 0xA0000..0xC0000 in eight 16 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX16K_A0000: u32 = 0x259;
/// 0xC0000..0xC8000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_C0000: u32 = 0x268;
/// 0xC8000..0xD0000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_C8000: u32 = 0x269;
/// 0xD0000..0xD8000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_D0000: u32 = 0x26A;
/// 0xD8000..0xE0000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_D8000: u32 = 0x26B;
/// 0xE0000..0xE8000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_E0000: u32 = 0x26C;
/// 0xE8000..0xF0000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_E8000: u32 = 0x26D;
/// 0xF0000..0xF8000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_F0000: u32 = 0x26E;
/// 0xF8000..0x100000 in eight 4 KiB ranges.
pub const IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_F8000: u32 = 0x26F;

/// The fixed-range MSRs in address order: each one's address, the start of
/// its first range and the size of each of its eight ranges. Byte n of the
/// MSR is the type of range n.
pub const FIXED_RANGES: [(u32, u64, u64); FIXED_MSRS] = [
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX64K_00000, 0x0_0000, 0x1_0000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX16K_80000, 0x8_0000, 0x4000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX16K_A0000, 0xA_0000, 0x4000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_C0000, 0xC_0000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_C8000, 0xC_8000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_D0000, 0xD_0000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_D8000, 0xD_8000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_E0000, 0xE_0000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_E8000, 0xE_8000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_F0000, 0xF_0000, 0x1000),
    (IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_F8000, 0xF_8000, 0x1000),
];

/// Where the fixed ranges end: they cover the first MiB.
pub const FIXED_END: u64 = 0x10_0000;

/// A memory type, as the MTRRs, the PAT and EPT entries encode it. The
/// values not listed (2, 3, 7 and up) are reserved: in an MTRR they are a
/// firmware bug, in an EPT entry an EPT misconfiguration. `repr(u8)`: the
/// discriminants are the hardware encodings, which [`raw`](Self::raw) returns.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum MemoryType {
    /// UC: every access goes to memory or the device, in program order.
    /// Device registers (MMIO) need it.
    Uncacheable = 0,
    /// WC: not cached, but writes are combined into bursts. Framebuffers.
    WriteCombining = 1,
    /// WT: reads cached, writes go straight through to memory.
    WriteThrough = 4,
    /// WP: reads cached, writes go to memory without updating the cache.
    WriteProtected = 5,
    /// WB: fully cached. Ordinary RAM.
    WriteBack = 6,
}

impl MemoryType {
    /// The type encoded as `value`, or `None` for a reserved value.
    pub fn from_raw(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        match value {
            0 => Some(Self::Uncacheable),
            1 => Some(Self::WriteCombining),
            4 => Some(Self::WriteThrough),
            5 => Some(Self::WriteProtected),
            6 => Some(Self::WriteBack),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The encoding: the value the MTRRs and EPT entries hold.
    pub fn raw(self) -> u64 {
        self as u64
    }

    /// The SDM's abbreviation.
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Uncacheable => "UC",
            Self::WriteCombining => "WC",
            Self::WriteThrough => "WT",
            Self::WriteProtected => "WP",
            Self::WriteBack => "WB",
        }
    }

    /// The type of an address that two variable ranges of types `self` and
    /// `other` both cover (SDM, "MTRR Precedences"): the same type stays,
    /// UC wins over anything, and WT wins over WB. Any other overlap is
    /// undefined; UC is the one choice that cannot hand a device stale data.
    fn overlap(self, other: Self) -> Self {
        match (self, other) {
            _ if self == other => self,
            (Self::WriteThrough, Self::WriteBack) | (Self::WriteBack, Self::WriteThrough) => Self::WriteThrough,
            _ => Self::Uncacheable,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrError {
    /// A type field of MSR `msr` holds the reserved memory type `value`.
    ReservedType { msr: u32, value: u8 },
    /// MSR `msr` has the reserved bits `bits` set.
    ReservedBits { msr: u32, bits: u64 },
    /// IA32_MTRRCAP reports `count` variable ranges, more than
    /// [`MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES`].
    TooManyVariableRanges { count: usize },
}

impl fmt::Display for MtrrError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match *self {
            Self::ReservedType { msr, value } => write!(f, "the reserved memory type {value} in MSR {msr:#x}"),
            Self::ReservedBits { msr, bits } => write!(f, "reserved bits {bits:#x} set in MSR {msr:#x}"),
            Self::TooManyVariableRanges { count } => write!(
                f,
                "IA32_MTRRCAP reports {count} variable ranges, more than the {MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES} Aleph0 keeps"
            ),
        }
    }
}

/// A variable range in use (its PHYSMASK valid bit set), decoded.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VariableRange {
    /// Its number n: the MSRs are IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASEn and PHYSMASKn.
    pub number: usize,
    /// PHYSBASE bits 51:12.
    pub base: u64,
    /// PHYSMASK bits 51:12: which address bits must equal the base's.
    pub mask: u64,
    pub memory_type: MemoryType,
}

impl VariableRange {
    /// Fills the unused slots of [`EnabledMtrrs::variable`].
    const UNUSED: Self = Self {
        number: 0,
        base: 0,
        mask: 0,
        memory_type: MemoryType::Uncacheable,
    };

    /// Whether `address` is in the range.
    fn covers(&self, address: u64) -> bool {
        address & self.mask == self.base & self.mask
    }

    /// Whether the range may cover some pages of the `size`-byte block at
    /// `base` and not others. The block's pages differ only in the address
    /// bits below `size`. If the mask tests none of those, the range covers
    /// the whole block or none of it; if it tests some, it covers part of
    /// the block, as long as the bits above match.
    fn may_split(&self, base: u64, size: u64) -> bool {
        let inside = (size - 1) & ADDRESS_BITS;
        let above = self.mask & !inside;
        self.mask & inside != 0 && base & above == self.base & above
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for VariableRange {
    /// `variable range 0: base=0x000000000000 mask=0x3fff00000000 WB`.
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "variable range {}: base={:#014x} mask={:#014x} {}",
            self.number,
            self.base,
            self.mask,
            self.memory_type.name()
        )
    }
}

/// The MTRRs of this CPU, decoded and checked: every type in use is a valid
/// memory type, so looking one up cannot fail.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[expect(
    clippy::large_enum_variant,
    reason = "built once at bring-up and passed by reference; the crate has no allocator to box it"
)]
pub enum Mtrrs {
    /// The CPU has no MTRRs at all (CPUID). Every address is WB, so caching
    /// is up to the PAT alone, as it was for Aleph0's EPT before MTRRs were
    /// read.
    Unsupported,
    /// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.E is clear: all memory is UC, whatever the other
    /// MTRRs hold.
    Disabled,
    /// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.E is set: the default type and the ranges apply.
    Enabled(EnabledMtrrs),
}

/// MTRRs that are on: the default type and the ranges that override it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct EnabledMtrrs {
    default_type: MemoryType,
    /// The type of each fixed range, per MSR in [`FIXED_RANGES`] order, or
    /// `None` when the fixed ranges are missing or disabled.
    fixed: Option<[[MemoryType; 8]; FIXED_MSRS]>,
    /// How many variable ranges the CPU has, used or not.
    variable_count: usize,
    /// The ranges in use, first `in_use` entries.
    variable: [VariableRange; MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES],
    in_use: usize,
}

impl Mtrrs {
    /// Decodes the MSR values: `def_type` is IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, `fixed` the
    /// fixed-range MSRs in [`FIXED_RANGES`] order (`None` when IA32_MTRRCAP
    /// says they do not exist), and `variable` the (PHYSBASE, PHYSMASK) pair
    /// of every variable range, in order.
    ///
    /// Only what the CPU uses is checked: nothing while the MTRRs are
    /// disabled, the fixed ranges only when enabled, and only the variable
    /// ranges in use.
    pub fn decode(def_type: u64, fixed: Option<[u64; FIXED_MSRS]>, variable: &[(u64, u64)]) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        if variable.len() > MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES {
            return Err(MtrrError::TooManyVariableRanges { count: variable.len() });
        }
        if def_type & DEF_TYPE_ENABLE == 0 {
            return Ok(Self::Disabled);
        }
        let mut mtrrs = EnabledMtrrs {
            default_type: decode_type(IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, def_type)?,
            fixed: None,
            variable_count: variable.len(),
            variable: [VariableRange::UNUSED; MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES],
            in_use: 0,
        };

        if def_type & DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE != 0
            && let Some(fixed) = fixed
        {
            let mut types = [[MemoryType::Uncacheable; 8]; FIXED_MSRS];
            for ((value, &(msr, ..)), types) in fixed.iter().zip(&FIXED_RANGES).zip(&mut types) {
                for (byte, memory_type) in value.to_le_bytes().into_iter().zip(types) {
                    *memory_type = decode_type(msr, byte.into())?;
                }
            }
            mtrrs.fixed = Some(types);
        }

        for (number, &(base, mask)) in variable.iter().enumerate() {
            if mask & PHYSMASK_VALID == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            mtrrs.variable[mtrrs.in_use] = VariableRange {
                number,
                base: base & ADDRESS_BITS,
                mask: mask & ADDRESS_BITS,
                memory_type: decode_type(IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * number as u32, base)?,
            };
            mtrrs.in_use += 1;
        }
        Ok(Self::Enabled(mtrrs))
    }

    /// The memory type of the 4 KiB page at `address` (SDM, "MTRR
    /// Precedences"): WB without MTRRs, UC while they are disabled, and
    /// otherwise what [`EnabledMtrrs`] gives it.
    pub fn memory_type(&self, address: u64) -> MemoryType {
        match self {
            Self::Unsupported => MemoryType::WriteBack,
            Self::Disabled => MemoryType::Uncacheable,
            Self::Enabled(mtrrs) => mtrrs.memory_type(address),
        }
    }

    /// The memory type of the whole `size`-byte block at `base`, or `None`
    /// when its 4 KiB pages do not all have the same type. `size` is a power
    /// of two of at least 4 KiB, and `base` a multiple of it.
    pub fn block_type(&self, base: u64, size: u64) -> Option<MemoryType> {
        debug_assert!(size.is_power_of_two() && size >= PAGE_SIZE as u64 && base.is_multiple_of(size));
        match self {
            Self::Unsupported | Self::Disabled => Some(self.memory_type(base)),
            Self::Enabled(mtrrs) => mtrrs.block_type(base, size),
        }
    }

    /// `[0, end)` cut into blocks of `size` bytes, with consecutive blocks of
    /// the same [`block_type`](Self::block_type) merged into one run. `end`
    /// is a multiple of `size`. Each block's type is looked up once.
    pub fn runs(&self, end: u64, size: u64) -> impl Iterator<Item = TypeRun> + '_ {
        debug_assert!(end.is_multiple_of(size));
        let mut blocks = (0..end)
            .step_by(size as usize)
            .map(move |start| (start, self.block_type(start, size)))
            .peekable();
        core::iter::from_fn(move || {
            let (start, memory_type) = blocks.next()?;
            let mut run_end = start + size;
            while let Some((next, _)) = blocks.next_if(|&(_, next_type)| next_type == memory_type) {
                run_end = next + size;
            }
            Some(TypeRun {
                start,
                end: run_end,
                memory_type,
            })
        })
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Mtrrs {
    /// Whether the MTRRs are on and, when they are, the default type and
    /// how many ranges apply: `enabled, default type UC; fixed ranges
    /// enabled; 8 variable ranges, 1 in use`.
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Unsupported => f.write_str("not supported (CPUID); all memory is treated as WB"),
            Self::Disabled => f.write_str("disabled (IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.E=0); all memory is UC"),
            Self::Enabled(enabled) => write!(
                f,
                "enabled, default type {}; fixed ranges {}; {} variable ranges, {} in use",
                enabled.default_type().name(),
                if enabled.fixed_enabled() { "enabled" } else { "disabled" },
                enabled.variable_count(),
                enabled.variable_ranges().len(),
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl EnabledMtrrs {
    /// The type of memory no range covers.
    pub fn default_type(&self) -> MemoryType {
        self.default_type
    }

    /// Whether the fixed ranges exist and are enabled.
    pub fn fixed_enabled(&self) -> bool {
        self.fixed.is_some()
    }

    /// How many variable ranges the CPU has, used or not.
    pub fn variable_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.variable_count
    }

    /// The variable ranges in use.
    pub fn variable_ranges(&self) -> &[VariableRange] {
        &self.variable[..self.in_use]
    }

    /// The memory type of the 4 KiB page at `address`: below 1 MiB the fixed
    /// range's type, when they are enabled; otherwise the type of the
    /// variable ranges covering it, or the default type if none does.
    fn memory_type(&self, address: u64) -> MemoryType {
        if let Some(memory_type) = self.fixed_type(address) {
            return memory_type;
        }
        self.variable_ranges()
            .iter()
            .filter(|range| range.covers(address))
            .map(|range| range.memory_type)
            .reduce(MemoryType::overlap)
            .unwrap_or(self.default_type)
    }

    /// See [`Mtrrs::block_type`].
    ///
    /// The type is the same for every page unless the fixed ranges reach
    /// into the block or a variable range covers only part of it. Only then
    /// are the pages looked at one by one, so a map of all memory stays
    /// cheap to build.
    fn block_type(&self, base: u64, size: u64) -> Option<MemoryType> {
        let fixed_inside = self.fixed.is_some() && base < FIXED_END;
        let split = self.variable_ranges().iter().any(|range| range.may_split(base, size));
        let first = self.memory_type(base);
        if !fixed_inside && !split {
            return Some(first);
        }
        (base..base + size)
            .step_by(PAGE_SIZE)
            .all(|page| self.memory_type(page) == first)
            .then_some(first)
    }

    /// The type of the fixed range holding `address`, or `None` when the
    /// fixed ranges are off or `address` is past the first MiB.
    fn fixed_type(&self, address: u64) -> Option<MemoryType> {
        let fixed = self.fixed.as_ref()?;
        FIXED_RANGES.iter().zip(fixed).find_map(|(&(_, start, size), types)| {
            let offset = address.checked_sub(start)?;
            types.get((offset / size) as usize).copied()
        })
    }
}

/// Consecutive blocks of one memory type: see [`Mtrrs::runs`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TypeRun {
    pub start: u64,
    pub end: u64,
    /// `None` when the pages of each block differ in type.
    pub memory_type: Option<MemoryType>,
}

impl TypeRun {
    /// The run's type for a report: its name, or "mixed" for blocks whose
    /// pages differ.
    pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        self.memory_type.map_or("mixed (4 KiB pages)", MemoryType::name)
    }
}

/// The memory type in bits 7:0 of `value`, read from MSR `msr`.
fn decode_type(msr: u32, value: u64) -> Result<MemoryType, MtrrError> {
    let raw = (value & TYPE_BITS) as u8;
    MemoryType::from_raw(raw).ok_or(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr, value: raw })
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../../tests/unit/vmx/mtrr.rs"]
pub(crate) mod tests;

`src/vmx/mtrr/registers.rs`:

```rs
//! The MTRR MSRs as RDMSR and WRMSR see them: which ones a CPU has, which
//! values WRMSR refuses, and reading them.
//!
//! `mod.rs` decodes MTRR values into memory types. This file is about the
//! MSRs themselves (Intel SDM Vol. 3A, "Memory Type Range Registers"):
//!
//! - Which exist ([`MtrrCapabilities`]): IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, the 11
//!   fixed-range MSRs when IA32_MTRRCAP bit 8 is set, and a PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK
//!   pair for each variable range IA32_MTRRCAP counts. IA32_MTRRCAP itself
//!   is read-only, and not counted among them.
//! - Which values WRMSR refuses with #GP ([`MtrrCapabilities::check`]): a
//!   reserved memory type in a type field, or a reserved bit set. The CPU
//!   checks the value on its own, whether or not that MTRR is in use, which
//!   makes this stricter than [`Mtrrs::decode`]. KVM's `kvm_mtrr_valid`
//!   applies the same rules.
//!
//! ```text
//! MSR                  bits that may be set (any other bit is reserved)
//! IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE   7:0 default type, 10 FE, 11 E
//! fixed-range MSRs     all 64: eight type bytes
//! IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASEn  7:0 type, MAXPHYADDR-1:12 base
//! IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASKn  11 valid, MAXPHYADDR-1:12 mask
//! ```
//!
//! - Their values ([`MtrrRegisters`]), each one a value the CPU would
//!   accept, and the same values decoded ([`MtrrState`]), which is what the
//!   guest's copy of its MTRRs is (`vmexit::guest_mtrrs`).

use core::fmt;

use super::{
    ADDRESS_BITS, CAP_FIXED, CAP_VARIABLE_COUNT, DEF_TYPE_ENABLE, DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE, FIXED_MSRS, FIXED_RANGES,
    IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0, IA32_MTRRCAP, MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES, MtrrError, Mtrrs, PHYSMASK_VALID,
    TYPE_BITS, decode_type,
};
use crate::vmx::cpuid;
use crate::vmx::msr::rdmsr;

/// The widest physical address a PHYSBASE or PHYSMASK holds: its address
/// part is bits 51:12.
const MAX_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;

/// Just past the PHYSMASK of variable range [`MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES`] - 1:
/// 0x240.
const VARIABLE_END: u32 = IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES as u32;

/// Every address an MTRR MSR has on some CPU, whether or not this one has
/// it: IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, the fixed-range MSRs, and PHYSBASEn and
/// PHYSMASKn of the first [`MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES`] variable ranges
/// (0x200..0x240).
///
/// The MSR bitmap intercepts all of them (`exit_bitmaps`), and the guest
/// gets #GP for those the CPU lacks ([`MtrrCapabilities::msr`] is `None`),
/// as it would on bare metal. So whether the guest reaches a real MTRR
/// never depends on IA32_MTRRCAP counting every one the CPU has.
pub fn every_msr_address() -> impl Iterator<Item = u32> {
    core::iter::once(IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE)
        .chain(FIXED_RANGES.iter().map(|&(msr, ..)| msr))
        .chain(IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0..VARIABLE_END)
}

/// Whether `address` is one of [`every_msr_address`].
pub fn is_msr_address(address: u32) -> bool {
    address == IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE
        || FIXED_RANGES.iter().any(|&(msr, ..)| msr == address)
        || (IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0..VARIABLE_END).contains(&address)
}

/// What IA32_MTRRCAP and CPUID say about the MTRR MSRs: which of them
/// exist, and which bits of a PHYSBASE or PHYSMASK are reserved.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrCapabilities {
    /// CPUID.1:EDX bit 12: the CPU has MTRRs at all.
    supported: bool,
    /// IA32_MTRRCAP bit 8: the fixed-range MSRs exist.
    fixed: bool,
    /// IA32_MTRRCAP bits 7:0: how many variable ranges, at most
    /// [`MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES`].
    variable_count: u8,
    /// MAXPHYADDR. Bits of a PHYSBASE or PHYSMASK from this one up are
    /// reserved.
    physical_address_bits: u8,
}

impl MtrrCapabilities {
    /// A CPU without MTRRs (CPUID.1:EDX bit 12 clear): no MTRR MSR exists.
    pub const NONE: Self = Self {
        supported: false,
        fixed: false,
        variable_count: 0,
        physical_address_bits: 0,
    };

    /// The MTRR MSRs of a CPU whose IA32_MTRRCAP is `mtrrcap` and whose
    /// physical addresses have `physical_address_bits` bits (MAXPHYADDR).
    /// Refuses more variable ranges than [`MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES`] rather than
    /// dropping some.
    pub fn new(mtrrcap: u64, physical_address_bits: u8) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        let count = (mtrrcap & CAP_VARIABLE_COUNT) as usize;
        if count > MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES {
            return Err(MtrrError::TooManyVariableRanges { count });
        }
        Ok(Self {
            supported: true,
            fixed: mtrrcap & CAP_FIXED != 0,
            variable_count: count as u8,
            physical_address_bits: physical_address_bits.min(MAX_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS),
        })
    }

    /// How many variable ranges the CPU has.
    pub fn variable_count(self) -> usize {
        self.variable_count.into()
    }

    /// Whether the fixed-range MSRs exist.
    pub fn fixed(self) -> bool {
        self.supported && self.fixed
    }

    /// The MTRR MSR at `address`, or `None` when the CPU has no MTRR there.
    pub fn msr(self, address: u32) -> Option<MtrrMsr> {
        if !self.supported {
            return None;
        }
        if address == IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE {
            return Some(MtrrMsr(Kind::DefType));
        }
        if let Some(index) = FIXED_RANGES.iter().position(|&(msr, ..)| msr == address) {
            return self.fixed.then_some(MtrrMsr(Kind::Fixed(index as u8)));
        }
        let offset = address.checked_sub(IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0)?;
        let number = u8::try_from(offset / 2)
            .ok()
            .filter(|&number| number < self.variable_count)?;
        Some(MtrrMsr(if offset % 2 == 0 {
            Kind::PhysBase(number)
        } else {
            Kind::PhysMask(number)
        }))
    }

    /// Every MTRR MSR the CPU has: IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE, the fixed-range MSRs
    /// in [`FIXED_RANGES`] order, then IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASEn and PHYSMASKn of
    /// each variable range. None without MTRRs.
    pub fn msrs(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = MtrrMsr> {
        let def_type = self.supported.then_some(MtrrMsr(Kind::DefType));
        let fixed = (0..FIXED_MSRS as u8)
            .filter(move |_| self.supported && self.fixed)
            .map(|index| MtrrMsr(Kind::Fixed(index)));
        let variable = (0..self.variable_count)
            .flat_map(|number| [MtrrMsr(Kind::PhysBase(number)), MtrrMsr(Kind::PhysMask(number))]);
        def_type.into_iter().chain(fixed).chain(variable)
    }

    /// Checks `value` as WRMSR to `msr` does: `Ok` if the CPU would take it,
    /// otherwise what it would refuse with #GP. A reserved bit set (see the
    /// module docs), or a reserved memory type in a type field. The CPU
    /// checks every type field, used or not: a variable range's type even
    /// while its valid bit is clear, the fixed ranges' while they are off.
    pub fn check(self, msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64) -> Result<(), MtrrError> {
        let address = msr.address();
        // What may be set, and how many type bytes there are, from bit 0.
        let (allowed, type_bytes) = match msr.0 {
            Kind::DefType => (TYPE_BITS | DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE | DEF_TYPE_ENABLE, 1),
            Kind::Fixed(_) => (u64::MAX, 8),
            Kind::PhysBase(_) => (TYPE_BITS | self.address_bits(), 1),
            Kind::PhysMask(_) => (PHYSMASK_VALID | self.address_bits(), 0),
        };
        let reserved = value & !allowed;
        if reserved != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedBits {
                msr: address,
                bits: reserved,
            });
        }
        for byte in value.to_le_bytes().into_iter().take(type_bytes) {
            decode_type(address, byte.into())?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The address bits of a PHYSBASE or PHYSMASK the CPU implements: bits
    /// MAXPHYADDR-1:12.
    fn address_bits(self) -> u64 {
        ADDRESS_BITS & ((1 << self.physical_address_bits) - 1)
    }
}

/// One MTRR MSR. Only [`MtrrCapabilities`] makes them, so its fixed-range
/// index or variable range number is always one the CPU has.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrMsr(Kind);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Kind {
    /// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.
    DefType,
    /// The fixed-range MSR at this index of [`FIXED_RANGES`].
    Fixed(u8),
    /// IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASEn of variable range n.
    PhysBase(u8),
    /// IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASKn of variable range n.
    PhysMask(u8),
}

impl MtrrMsr {
    /// The MSR's address, as RDMSR and WRMSR take it in ECX.
    pub fn address(self) -> u32 {
        match self.0 {
            Kind::DefType => IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE,
            Kind::Fixed(index) => FIXED_RANGES[usize::from(index)].0,
            Kind::PhysBase(number) => IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * u32::from(number),
            Kind::PhysMask(number) => IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * u32::from(number) + 1,
        }
    }

    /// Whether it is one of the fixed-range MSRs.
    pub fn is_fixed(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.0, Kind::Fixed(_))
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for MtrrMsr {
    /// The SDM's name: `IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE`, `IA32_MTRR_FIX16K_A0000`,
    /// `IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASK7`.
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self.0 {
            Kind::DefType => f.write_str("IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE"),
            Kind::Fixed(index) => {
                let (_, start, size) = FIXED_RANGES[usize::from(index)];
                write!(f, "IA32_MTRR_FIX{}K_{start:05X}", size / 1024)
            }
            Kind::PhysBase(number) => write!(f, "IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE{number}"),
            Kind::PhysMask(number) => write!(f, "IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASK{number}"),
        }
    }
}

/// The values of every MTRR MSR a CPU has ([`MtrrCapabilities::msrs`]),
/// each one a value the CPU would accept ([`MtrrCapabilities::check`]).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisters {
    capabilities: MtrrCapabilities,
    def_type: u64,
    /// In [`FIXED_RANGES`] order; 0 when the fixed ranges do not exist.
    fixed: [u64; FIXED_MSRS],
    /// (PHYSBASEn, PHYSMASKn) of variable range n; 0 past the CPU's count.
    variable: [(u64, u64); MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES],
}

impl MtrrRegisters {
    /// The value of each MSR `capabilities` lists, as `read` returns it.
    /// Refuses a value the CPU would not accept: no CPU holds one, since
    /// WRMSR refuses them, so it can only come from a broken VMM below
    /// Aleph0.
    pub fn read_with(capabilities: MtrrCapabilities, mut read: impl FnMut(MtrrMsr) -> u64) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        let mut registers = Self {
            capabilities,
            def_type: 0,
            fixed: [0; FIXED_MSRS],
            variable: [(0, 0); MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES],
        };
        for msr in capabilities.msrs() {
            let value = read(msr);
            capabilities.check(msr, value)?;
            *registers.value_mut(msr) = value;
        }
        Ok(registers)
    }

    /// Which MSRs there are.
    pub fn capabilities(&self) -> MtrrCapabilities {
        self.capabilities
    }

    /// The value of `msr`, as RDMSR returns it.
    pub fn get(&self, msr: MtrrMsr) -> u64 {
        match msr.0 {
            Kind::DefType => self.def_type,
            Kind::Fixed(index) => self.fixed[usize::from(index)],
            Kind::PhysBase(number) => self.variable[usize::from(number)].0,
            Kind::PhysMask(number) => self.variable[usize::from(number)].1,
        }
    }

    /// Writes `value` to `msr` as WRMSR does: a value the CPU would refuse
    /// ([`MtrrCapabilities::check`]) is refused, and every value stays as
    /// it was.
    pub fn write(&mut self, msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64) -> Result<(), MtrrError> {
        self.capabilities.check(msr, value)?;
        *self.value_mut(msr) = value;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The memory types the values give ([`Mtrrs::decode`]).
    /// [`Mtrrs::Unsupported`] without MTRRs.
    pub fn decode(&self) -> Result<Mtrrs, MtrrError> {
        if !self.capabilities.supported {
            return Ok(Mtrrs::Unsupported);
        }
        Mtrrs::decode(
            self.def_type,
            self.capabilities.fixed.then_some(self.fixed),
            &self.variable[..self.capabilities.variable_count()],
        )
    }

    /// Where `msr`'s value is kept.
    fn value_mut(&mut self, msr: MtrrMsr) -> &mut u64 {
        match msr.0 {
            Kind::DefType => &mut self.def_type,
            Kind::Fixed(index) => &mut self.fixed[usize::from(index)],
            Kind::PhysBase(number) => &mut self.variable[usize::from(number)].0,
            Kind::PhysMask(number) => &mut self.variable[usize::from(number)].1,
        }
    }
}

/// MTRRs both as their MSRs hold them and decoded, kept in step: what the
/// guest's copy of its MTRRs is. KVM keeps the same per vCPU
/// (`kvm_mtrr`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrState {
    registers: MtrrRegisters,
    /// `registers`, decoded.
    mtrrs: Mtrrs,
}

impl MtrrState {
    /// `registers` with their decoding.
    pub fn new(registers: MtrrRegisters) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        let mtrrs = registers.decode()?;
        Ok(Self { registers, mtrrs })
    }

    /// The MSRs' values.
    pub fn registers(&self) -> &MtrrRegisters {
        &self.registers
    }

    /// The memory types they give.
    pub fn mtrrs(&self) -> &Mtrrs {
        &self.mtrrs
    }

    /// Writes `value` to `msr` as WRMSR does, and returns whether the
    /// memory type of any address changed.
    ///
    /// A value the CPU would refuse is refused, and everything stays as it
    /// was: the #GP the guest gets for it is all that happens, as on bare
    /// metal. That holds while the MTRRs are disabled too, when nothing
    /// decodes them: an OS clears IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.E, writes the ranges,
    /// then sets E again, and a bad range must fault at its own WRMSR, not
    /// at the one that sets E. Writes while E is clear change no type, so
    /// only the write that sets E again returns `true`.
    ///
    /// A value WRMSR takes always decodes, every type field being valid;
    /// should one not, it is refused all the same.
    pub fn write(&mut self, msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64) -> Result<bool, MtrrError> {
        let old = self.registers.get(msr);
        self.registers.write(msr, value)?;
        match self.registers.decode() {
            Ok(mtrrs) => {
                let changed = mtrrs != self.mtrrs;
                self.mtrrs = mtrrs;
                Ok(changed)
            }
            Err(error) => {
                *self.registers.value_mut(msr) = old;
                Err(error)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Reads this CPU's MTRR MSRs: none when CPUID says it has no MTRRs, since
/// reading one would then raise #GP.
pub fn read() -> Result<MtrrRegisters, MtrrError> {
    let capabilities = if cpuid::has_mtrr() {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports MTRRs, so IA32_MTRRCAP exists. Reading it
        // has no side effects.
        MtrrCapabilities::new(unsafe { rdmsr(IA32_MTRRCAP) }, cpuid::physical_address_bits())?
    } else {
        MtrrCapabilities::NONE
    };
    // SAFETY: `capabilities` lists only the MTRR MSRs CPUID and
    // IA32_MTRRCAP say exist. Reading them has no side effects.
    MtrrRegisters::read_with(capabilities, |msr| unsafe { rdmsr(msr.address()) })
}

mod tests;

```rs
//! Page allocation, and the memory types that keep Aleph0's pages after
//! `ExitBootServices`.
//!
//! After `ExitBootServices` the OS may reuse every page of a type
//! `resident::memory::is_reclaimable` names (`LOADER_*`, `BOOT_SERVICES_*`,
//! conventional memory, ...). Aleph0 runs at every VM exit for as long as
//! the guest does, so everything it keeps comes from here as a resident
//! type: [`allocate_zeroed_pages`] gives [`RESIDENT_DATA`], and the image
//! copy (`resident::ResidentImage`) and the test guest's code ask for
//! [`RESIDENT_CODE`]. Each resident allocation is listed
//! ([`resident_allocations`]), so bring-up can check every one of them in
//! the memory map before the launch.

use core::ptr::NonNull;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use uefi::boot::{self, AllocateType, MemoryType};

pub const PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;

/// The type of every page Aleph0 keeps after `ExitBootServices`. The UEFI
/// spec has the OS preserve runtime-services memory, and an OS leaves it out
/// of its free memory. docs/RESIDENT.md says why this and not `RESERVED`.
pub const RESIDENT_DATA: MemoryType = MemoryType::RUNTIME_SERVICES_DATA;

/// The type of Aleph0's image copy: its code runs from these pages, also in
/// the guest on the firmware's page tables (the `ExitBootServices` event),
/// and firmware with DXE memory protection commonly maps the data types,
/// `RESERVED` and [`RESIDENT_DATA`] included, no-execute.
pub const RESIDENT_CODE: MemoryType = MemoryType::RUNTIME_SERVICES_CODE;

/// One resident allocation: `pages` pages from `address`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Allocation {
    pub address: u64,
    pub pages: usize,
}

/// How many resident allocations [`resident_allocations`] can list.
/// Bring-up makes 27 on the Hyper-V test VM.
const LISTED_ALLOCATIONS: usize = 64;

/// Address and page count of each resident allocation, oldest first. Only
/// bring-up allocates, on one CPU; the atomics just avoid `static mut`.
static ALLOCATIONS: [[AtomicU64; 2]; LISTED_ALLOCATIONS] =
    [const { [AtomicU64::new(0), AtomicU64::new(0)] }; LISTED_ALLOCATIONS];
/// Resident allocations so far, listed or not.
static ALLOCATION_COUNT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

/// Lists `allocation` if it has a resident type, or counts it as unlisted
/// once the list is full.
fn record(allocation: Allocation, memory_type: MemoryType) {
    if memory_type != RESIDENT_DATA && memory_type != RESIDENT_CODE {
        return;
    }
    let index = ALLOCATION_COUNT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    if let Some([address, pages]) = ALLOCATIONS.get(index) {
        address.store(allocation.address, Ordering::Relaxed);
        pages.store(allocation.pages as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

/// Every resident allocation so far, oldest first, up to the first
/// [`LISTED_ALLOCATIONS`].
pub fn resident_allocations() -> impl Iterator<Item = Allocation> {
    let listed = ALLOCATION_COUNT.load(Ordering::Relaxed).min(LISTED_ALLOCATIONS);
    ALLOCATIONS[..listed].iter().map(|[address, pages]| Allocation {
        address: address.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        pages: pages.load(Ordering::Relaxed) as usize,
    })
}

/// Resident allocations made after the list was full, which
/// [`resident_allocations`] leaves out.
pub fn unlisted_resident_allocations() -> usize {
    ALLOCATION_COUNT
        .load(Ordering::Relaxed)
        .saturating_sub(LISTED_ALLOCATIONS)
}

/// Allocate and zero one resident page, preserving the caller's allocation
/// error type.
pub fn allocate_zeroed_page<E>(allocation_error: E) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, E> {
    allocate_zeroed_pages(1, allocation_error)
}

/// Allocate and zero `count` contiguous resident pages ([`RESIDENT_DATA`]),
/// preserving the caller's allocation error type.
pub fn allocate_zeroed_pages<E>(count: usize, allocation_error: E) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, E> {
    allocate_zeroed_pages_of_type(count, RESIDENT_DATA, allocation_error)
}

/// Like [`allocate_zeroed_pages`], with an explicit UEFI memory type. The
/// allocation is listed if the type is [`RESIDENT_DATA`] or
/// [`RESIDENT_CODE`].
///
/// The type can decide the page's permissions: firmware with DXE memory
/// protection commonly maps the data types no-execute and leaves the code
/// types executable.
pub fn allocate_zeroed_pages_of_type<E>(
    count: usize,
    memory_type: MemoryType,
    allocation_error: E,
) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, E> {
    let pages = boot::allocate_pages(AllocateType::AnyPages, memory_type, count).map_err(|_| allocation_error)?;

    assert_eq!(
        pages.as_ptr() as usize % PAGE_SIZE,
        0,
        "UEFI returned an unaligned page"
    );
    // SAFETY: `allocate_pages` returned `count` pages at `pages`, which
    // nothing else uses yet.
    unsafe { pages.write_bytes(0, count * PAGE_SIZE) };
    record(
        Allocation {
            address: pages.as_ptr() as u64,
            pages: count,
        },
        memory_type,
    );
    Ok(pages)
}
