`src/vmx/vmexit/dump.rs`:

```rs
//! What every stop prints about the guest after its exit's lines, so a stop
//! nobody planned for can be read without another run:
//!
//! 1. its state as the CPU saved it at the exit ([`GuestState::read`]), in
//!    the format bring-up printed before VMLAUNCH;
//! 2. its 15 general-purpose registers, from the frame the entry stub saved;
//! 3. its DR7, PAT and EFER, from wherever the controls leave them
//!    ([`saved_registers`]);
//! 4. the VMCS fields that explain an exit ([`DUMP_LINES`]): pending events,
//!    an injection Aleph0 queued, the exit's event, the guest addresses, and
//!    the controls.
//!
//! Every value comes from a VMREAD or an MSR read in exit context. A field
//! that cannot be read is printed as unreadable, and the dump goes on.

use core::fmt;

use super::{RegisterFrame, read_field};
use crate::vmx::guest_state::GuestState;
use crate::vmx::msr::{self, IA32_EFER, IA32_PAT};
use crate::vmx::vmcs::VmcsError;
use crate::vmx::vmcs::fields::{
    EXCEPTION_BITMAP, GUEST_ACTIVITY_STATE, GUEST_DR7, GUEST_IA32_EFER, GUEST_IA32_PAT, GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE,
    GUEST_LINEAR_ADDRESS, GUEST_PENDING_DEBUG_EXCEPTIONS, GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS, IDT_VECTORING_ERROR_CODE,
    IDT_VECTORING_INFO, PIN_BASED_VM_EXEC_CONTROL, PRIMARY_VM_EXEC_CONTROL, SECONDARY_VM_EXEC_CONTROL,
    VM_ENTRY_CONTROLS, VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE, VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO, VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_EFER,
    VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_PAT, VM_EXIT_CONTROLS, VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_ERROR_CODE, VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO,
    VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_EFER, VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_PAT, VM_EXIT_SAVE_DEBUG_CONTROLS, VM_EXIT_SAVE_IA32_EFER,
    VM_EXIT_SAVE_IA32_PAT,
};

/// One line of the dump: a label and the VMCS fields it shows, by name.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct DumpLine {
    pub label: &'static str,
    pub fields: &'static [(&'static str, u32)],
}

/// The VMCS fields the dump prints besides the guest state, one line each.
pub const DUMP_LINES: [DumpLine; 5] = [
    DumpLine {
        label: "guest events",
        fields: &[
            ("interruptibility", GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE),
            ("activity", GUEST_ACTIVITY_STATE),
            ("pending_debug", GUEST_PENDING_DEBUG_EXCEPTIONS),
        ],
    },
    DumpLine {
        label: "queued injection",
        fields: &[
            ("info", VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO),
            ("error_code", VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE),
        ],
    },
    DumpLine {
        label: "exit event",
        fields: &[
            ("info", VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO),
            ("error_code", VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_ERROR_CODE),
            ("idt_vectoring", IDT_VECTORING_INFO),
            ("idt_vectoring_error_code", IDT_VECTORING_ERROR_CODE),
        ],
    },
    DumpLine {
        label: "addresses",
        fields: &[
            ("guest_linear", GUEST_LINEAR_ADDRESS),
            ("guest_physical", GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS),
        ],
    },
    DumpLine {
        label: "controls",
        fields: &[
            ("pin", PIN_BASED_VM_EXEC_CONTROL),
            ("primary", PRIMARY_VM_EXEC_CONTROL),
            ("secondary", SECONDARY_VM_EXEC_CONTROL),
            ("exit", VM_EXIT_CONTROLS),
            ("entry", VM_ENTRY_CONTROLS),
            ("exception_bitmap", EXCEPTION_BITMAP),
        ],
    },
];

/// Fields on the longest [`DumpLine`].
const MAX_FIELDS: usize = 6;

/// A VMCS value for the dump: hexadecimal, or why it could not be read.
pub struct Value(pub Result<u64, VmcsError>);

impl fmt::Display for Value {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self.0 {
            Ok(value) => write!(f, "{value:#x}"),
            Err(error) => write!(f, "unreadable ({error:?})"),
        }
    }
}

/// A [`DumpLine`] with the values read for its fields, as printed:
/// `label: name=0x.. name=0x..`. A value missing from `values` prints as
/// unreadable.
pub struct DumpValues<'a> {
    pub line: &'a DumpLine,
    pub values: &'a [Result<u64, VmcsError>],
}

impl fmt::Display for DumpValues<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.line.label)?;
        f.write_str(":")?;
        for (index, &(name, _)) in self.line.fields.iter().enumerate() {
            let value = self.values.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(Err(VmcsError::VmFailInvalid));
            write!(f, " {name}={}", Value(value))?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Where the guest's value of a register that VM exits may save can be
/// found after the exit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Source {
    /// In this VMCS guest field: the exit controls saved it there.
    Vmcs(u32),
    /// In this MSR: neither entry nor exit switches it, so the CPU still
    /// holds the guest's value.
    Msr(u32),
    /// Nowhere: the exit loaded a value of its own without saving the
    /// guest's.
    NotSaved,
}

/// Where the guest's DR7, PAT and EFER are after an exit, from the VM-entry
/// controls (`entry`) and VM-exit controls (`exit`). Every exit sets DR7 to
/// 0x400, so the guest's DR7 is only in the VMCS, under "save debug
/// controls". PAT and EFER are in the VMCS under their save controls, still
/// in the MSR when no control loads them on entry or exit, and lost
/// otherwise.
pub fn saved_registers(entry: u64, exit: u64) -> [(&'static str, Source); 3] {
    let msr_source = |save: u64, field: u32, entry_load: u64, exit_load: u64, msr: u32| {
        if exit & save != 0 {
            Source::Vmcs(field)
        } else if entry & entry_load == 0 && exit & exit_load == 0 {
            Source::Msr(msr)
        } else {
            Source::NotSaved
        }
    };
    [
        (
            "dr7",
            if exit & VM_EXIT_SAVE_DEBUG_CONTROLS != 0 {
                Source::Vmcs(GUEST_DR7)
            } else {
                Source::NotSaved
            },
        ),
        (
            "pat",
            msr_source(
                VM_EXIT_SAVE_IA32_PAT,
                GUEST_IA32_PAT,
                VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_PAT,
                VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_PAT,
                IA32_PAT,
            ),
        ),
        (
            "efer",
            msr_source(
                VM_EXIT_SAVE_IA32_EFER,
                GUEST_IA32_EFER,
                VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_EFER,
                VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_EFER,
                IA32_EFER,
            ),
        ),
    ]
}

/// Prints the dump for the stop at exit `number`, with the guest's
/// general-purpose registers from `frame`.
pub(super) fn report_guest(number: u64, frame: &RegisterFrame) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS
    // current.
    match unsafe { GuestState::read() } {
        Ok(state) => state.report(format_args!("VM exit #{number}: guest")),
        Err(error) => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest state unreadable ({error:?})"),
    }
    report_registers(number, frame);
    report_saved_registers(number);
    for line in &DUMP_LINES {
        let mut values = [Err(VmcsError::VmFailInvalid); MAX_FIELDS];
        for (value, &(_, field)) in values.iter_mut().zip(line.fields) {
            *value = read_field(field);
        }
        let values = &values[..line.fields.len()];
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: {}", DumpValues { line, values });
    }
}

/// Prints the 15 general-purpose registers in `frame`, four to a line.
fn report_registers(number: u64, frame: &RegisterFrame) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    let RegisterFrame {
        rax,
        rbx,
        rcx,
        rdx,
        rsi,
        rdi,
        rbp,
        r8,
        r9,
        r10,
        r11,
        r12,
        r13,
        r14,
        r15,
    } = *frame;
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest rax={rax:#018x} rbx={rbx:#018x} rcx={rcx:#018x} rdx={rdx:#018x}"
    );
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest rsi={rsi:#018x} rdi={rdi:#018x} rbp={rbp:#018x} r8={r8:#018x}"
    );
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest r9={r9:#018x} r10={r10:#018x} r11={r11:#018x} r12={r12:#018x}"
    );
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest r13={r13:#018x} r14={r14:#018x} r15={r15:#018x}");
}

/// Prints the guest's DR7, PAT and EFER from wherever [`saved_registers`]
/// finds them.
fn report_saved_registers(number: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    let (Ok(entry), Ok(exit)) = (read_field(VM_ENTRY_CONTROLS), read_field(VM_EXIT_CONTROLS)) else {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest dr7/pat/efer: controls unreadable");
        return;
    };
    crate::serial_print!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest");
    for (name, source) in saved_registers(entry, exit) {
        match source {
            Source::Vmcs(field) => crate::serial_print!(" {name}={} (VMCS)", Value(read_field(field))),
            Source::Msr(msr) => {
                // SAFETY: IA32_PAT and IA32_EFER exist on every 64-bit CPU,
                // and reading them has no side effects.
                let value = unsafe { msr::rdmsr(msr) };
                crate::serial_print!(" {name}={value:#x} (MSR, not switched)");
            }
            Source::NotSaved => crate::serial_print!(" {name}=not saved"),
        }
    }
    crate::serial_println!();
}
```

`src/vmx/vmexit/guest_mtrrs.rs`:

```rs
//! The guest's MTRRs: the copy its RDMSR and WRMSR of an MTRR MSR reach
//! instead of the CPU's, and the EPT memory types that follow it.
//!
//! With EPT on, the MTRRs no longer set the memory types of guest accesses:
//! the EPT entries do (`docs/MTRR.md`). They still set those of Aleph0's own
//! accesses in root operation, so a guest that wrote them could make
//! Aleph0's code, data or stacks UC or WP. So the guest never writes them.
//! The MSR bitmap intercepts every MTRR MSR (`exit_bitmaps`), RDMSR reads
//! this copy, and WRMSR writes it, after which EPT takes the types the copy
//! gives (`ept::TypeTables`). KVM keeps the same per vCPU
//! (`vcpu->arch.mtrr_state`).
//!
//! Like the statistics (`stats.rs`), this is exit-handler state. Bring-up
//! publishes it before VMLAUNCH, starting as the CPU's own MTRRs; from then
//! on only the exit handler touches it, until the guest has stopped.

use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::fmt;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

use crate::vmx::ept::{InveptType, Retyped, TypeTables};
use crate::vmx::instruction::VmxFail;
use crate::vmx::mtrr::{MtrrCapabilities, MtrrError, MtrrMsr, MtrrRegisters, MtrrState, Mtrrs};

/// The guest's MTRRs, and the EPT tables whose memory types follow them.
struct GuestMtrrs {
    state: MtrrState,
    types: TypeTables,
}

struct Cell {
    guest: UnsafeCell<Option<GuestMtrrs>>,
    /// Set while [`with`] lends out `guest`, so that a call from inside its
    /// closure is refused instead of making a second `&mut` to it.
    in_use: AtomicBool,
}

// SAFETY: Aleph0 runs one vCPU on one CPU. Bring-up writes the cell
// ([`publish`]) before the guest runs; then only the exit handler uses it,
// with interrupts off, and the host NMI handler never touches it; bring-up
// reads it again once the guest has stopped. Nobody keeps a reference past
// the call that made it, and `in_use` refuses a call made while one is
// lent out ([`with`]).
unsafe impl Sync for Cell {}

static GUEST_MTRRS: Cell = Cell {
    guest: UnsafeCell::new(None),
    in_use: AtomicBool::new(false),
};

/// Gives the exit handler the guest's MTRRs, starting as `state` (the
/// CPU's), and `types`, the EPT tables whose memory types follow them. For
/// bring-up, before VMLAUNCH. `types` comes from the one `Ept::build`, so
/// there is only ever one guest to publish.
pub fn publish(state: MtrrState, types: TypeTables) {
    // SAFETY: no exit handler runs before VMLAUNCH, and bring-up holds no
    // reference from `with` here (see `Cell`).
    unsafe { *GUEST_MTRRS.guest.get() = Some(GuestMtrrs { state, types }) };
}

/// Why [`with`] could not lend out the guest's MTRRs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Unavailable {
    /// Before [`publish`].
    NotPublished,
    /// A call from inside another `with`'s closure.
    InUse,
}

/// Calls `f` with the guest's MTRRs. Refused before [`publish`], and from
/// inside another call's `f`, which would otherwise hold a second `&mut` to
/// them.
fn with<R>(f: impl FnOnce(&mut GuestMtrrs) -> R) -> Result<R, Unavailable> {
    if GUEST_MTRRS.in_use.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        return Err(Unavailable::InUse);
    }
    // SAFETY: bring-up and the exit handler never run at the same time,
    // `in_use` makes this the only reference, and it does not outlive `f`
    // (see `Cell`).
    let result = unsafe { (*GUEST_MTRRS.guest.get()).as_mut().map(f) };
    GUEST_MTRRS.in_use.store(false, Ordering::Release);
    result.ok_or(Unavailable::NotPublished)
}

/// The guest's MTRR MSRs, for `decide`: [`MtrrCapabilities::NONE`] before
/// [`publish`], so none of them is routed to the copy.
pub(super) fn capabilities() -> MtrrCapabilities {
    with(|guest| guest.state.registers().capabilities()).unwrap_or(MtrrCapabilities::NONE)
}

/// The guest's MTRR MSRs as they stand, or `None` before [`publish`]. For
/// bring-up, once the guest has stopped.
pub fn registers() -> Option<MtrrRegisters> {
    with(|guest| guest.state.registers().clone()).ok()
}

/// What RDMSR of `msr` returns the guest: its copy's value.
pub(super) fn read(msr: MtrrMsr) -> Result<u64, MtrrAccessFailure> {
    with(|guest| guest.state.registers().get(msr)).map_err(MtrrAccessFailure::from)
}

/// What a guest WRMSR of an MTRR came to.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) struct MtrrWrite {
    /// What changed in EPT, or `None` when every address keeps the type it
    /// had, so EPT was left alone.
    pub(super) retyped: Option<Retyped>,
    /// The INVEPT run once EPT changed.
    pub(super) invept: Option<InveptType>,
}

/// Why an access to the guest's MTRRs failed. None of these should happen:
/// `decide` routes an MSR to the copy only once it is published, and checks
/// a written value first.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum MtrrAccessFailure {
    /// Bring-up never published the guest's MTRRs.
    NotPublished,
    /// Reached again from inside an access to them.
    InUse,
    /// The copy refused the value.
    Refused(MtrrError),
    /// INVEPT failed after EPT took the new types.
    Invept(VmxFail),
}

impl From<Unavailable> for MtrrAccessFailure {
    fn from(unavailable: Unavailable) -> Self {
        match unavailable {
            Unavailable::NotPublished => Self::NotPublished,
            Unavailable::InUse => Self::InUse,
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for MtrrAccessFailure {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::NotPublished => f.write_str("the guest's MTRRs were never set up"),
            Self::InUse => f.write_str("the guest's MTRRs were reached again while already in use"),
            Self::Refused(error) => write!(f, "the guest's MTRRs refused the write ({error})"),
            Self::Invept(error) => write!(f, "EPT took the guest's MTRR types, but INVEPT failed ({error:?})"),
        }
    }
}

/// WRMSR of `value` to the guest's `msr`: into its copy, never the CPU's.
/// If that changes the type of any address, EPT takes the new types, and
/// INVEPT drops the translations made with the old ones.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest stopped at an exit.
pub(super) unsafe fn write(msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64) -> Result<MtrrWrite, MtrrAccessFailure> {
    with(|guest| {
        let changed = guest.state.write(msr, value).map_err(MtrrAccessFailure::Refused)?;
        if !changed {
            return Ok(MtrrWrite {
                retyped: None,
                invept: None,
            });
        }
        // SAFETY: the caller guarantees exit context, and `types` came from
        // `Ept::build`, whose tables are never freed.
        let retyped = unsafe { guest.types.apply(guest.state.mtrrs()) }.map_err(MtrrAccessFailure::Invept)?;
        Ok(MtrrWrite {
            retyped: Some(retyped),
            invept: retyped.changed().then(|| guest.types.invept()),
        })
    })
    .unwrap_or_else(|unavailable| Err(unavailable.into()))
}

/// Calls `f` with the memory types the guest's MTRRs give and the EPT
/// tables that carry them, for the exit handler's report. `None` before
/// [`publish`].
pub(super) fn inspect<R>(f: impl FnOnce(&Mtrrs, &TypeTables) -> R) -> Option<R> {
    with(|guest| f(guest.state.mtrrs(), &guest.types)).ok()
}
```

`src/vmx/vmexit/handler.rs`:

```rs
//! The VM-exit handler the entry stub calls: read the exit, judge it, carry
//! it out, report it.
//!
//! [`vmexit_handler`] runs four steps:
//!
//! 1. [`read_exit`] reads the exit's VMCS fields and the guest registers.
//!    It prints nothing.
//! 2. [`judge`] folds in an NMI that arrived while Aleph0 ran (`vmx::host`)
//!    and passes the exit to `exit_decision::decide` with the state kept
//!    between exits.
//! 3. [`carry_out`] executes an emulated instruction and prepares the VMCS as
//!    the event's `ResumePlan` says, or stops the guest. It prints nothing
//!    either: a step that fails says why in its [`ResumeFailure`].
//! 4. `report.rs` prints the exit and its [`Outcome`], once everything about
//!    the exit is known, in as much detail as the print policy gives it
//!    (`policy.rs`): whole for a stop and for the first exits of each reason,
//!    rate-limited after that.

use core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid_count, CpuidResult};
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};

use core::fmt;

use super::guest_mtrrs::{self, MtrrAccessFailure, MtrrWrite};
use super::history::{self, ExitRecord};
use super::policy::{self, COUNTERS, MAX_LEVEL, exit_detail};
use super::report::{ExitReport, after_stop, report_exit, report_stop};
use super::stats::{self, VcpuStats};
use super::{RegisterFrame, read_field};
use crate::output::Phase;
use crate::port;
use crate::vmx::ept::{self, InveptType, ProtectedPage};
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::{
    EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG, EXIT_REASON_EPT_VIOLATION, EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION, EXIT_REASON_VMCALL, Emulation,
    ExitAction, ExitEvent, ExitInfo, ExitReason, ExitState, InterruptionInfo, IoSize, Redelivery, ResumePlan,
    UNREADABLE_REASON, after_skipped_instruction, cpl_from_ss, cpuid_policy, decide, is_canonical_48, merge_in,
};
use crate::vmx::host;
use crate::vmx::hyperv::{self, HypercallRegisters};
use crate::vmx::instruction::VmxFail;
use crate::vmx::msr;
use crate::vmx::mtrr::MtrrMsr;
use crate::vmx::vmcs::fields::{
    EXIT_QUALIFICATION, GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE, GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS, GUEST_RIP, GUEST_SS_ACCESS_RIGHTS,
    IDT_VECTORING_ERROR_CODE, IDT_VECTORING_INFO, VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE, VM_ENTRY_INSTRUCTION_LEN,
    VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO, VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN, VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO, VM_EXIT_REASON,
};
use crate::vmx::vmcs::{self, GuestKind, VmcsError, encode_finished, encode_resume_failed, encode_unexpected};

/// Exits so far per basic reason ([`policy::counter`]), including the
/// current one: for the print policy and the histogram every stop prints.
/// Only the exit handler touches them, with interrupts off, on the one CPU
/// that runs the guest; the atomics just avoid `static mut`.
static EXITS_BY_REASON: [AtomicU64; COUNTERS] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; COUNTERS];

/// Counts an exit of basic reason `basic`, and returns how many there have
/// been, this one included.
fn count_exit(basic: u16) -> u64 {
    EXITS_BY_REASON[policy::counter(basic)].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1
}

/// The counts of [`EXITS_BY_REASON`] as they stand.
fn exits_by_reason() -> [u64; COUNTERS] {
    core::array::from_fn(|slot| EXITS_BY_REASON[slot].load(Ordering::Relaxed))
}

// The `ExitState` that `decide` carries from one exit to the next, one
// atomic per field, for the same reason as `EXITS_BY_REASON`.
static MAIN_VMCALLS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
static NMI_PENDING: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
static NMIS_HANDLED: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
static EPT_WRITES_GRANTED: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

fn load_state() -> ExitState {
    ExitState {
        main_vmcalls: MAIN_VMCALLS.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        nmi_pending: NMI_PENDING.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        nmis_handled: NMIS_HANDLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        ept_writes_granted: EPT_WRITES_GRANTED.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
    }
}

fn store_state(state: ExitState) {
    MAIN_VMCALLS.store(state.main_vmcalls, Ordering::Relaxed);
    NMI_PENDING.store(state.nmi_pending, Ordering::Relaxed);
    NMIS_HANDLED.store(state.nmis_handled, Ordering::Relaxed);
    EPT_WRITES_GRANTED.store(state.ept_writes_granted, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Handler return value that tells the entry stub to resume the guest.
/// Every other value is a stop value (see `vmx/vmcs/launch.rs`).
const RESUME_GUEST: u64 = 0;

/// What the handler returns to the entry stub for `action` at exit
/// `number`: [`RESUME_GUEST`], or the stop value `vmcs::launch` returns.
fn stub_return(action: ExitAction, number: u64, raw_reason: u32) -> u64 {
    match action {
        ExitAction::Resume(_) => RESUME_GUEST,
        ExitAction::Finished => encode_finished(number),
        ExitAction::Unexpected => encode_unexpected(number, raw_reason),
    }
}

/// The guest RIP after an instruction of `length` bytes, or `None` when that would wrap past the top of the
/// address space or land outside the canonical range.
///
/// `rip` is the guest's: a guest kernel can map code in the last bytes of the address space, where the sum
/// overflows (a panic in debug builds, a silent wrap in release). An instruction ending at the last canonical
/// byte of the lower half does not overflow, but gives `0x0000_8000_0000_0000`, and VM entry would then fail its
/// guest-state checks on RIP. The caller stops the guest instead, in both cases.
fn next_rip(rip: u64, length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    rip.checked_add(length).filter(|&next| is_canonical_48(next))
}

/// VM-exit handler: decides what the exit is (`exit_decision::decide`),
/// carries that out, prints the exit over serial, then tells the entry stub
/// what to do. It returns [`RESUME_GUEST`] after preparing the VMCS for the
/// guest to go on (the stub then executes VMRESUME), or, for the test guest,
/// a stop value (the stub then returns it from `vmcs::launch` to bring-up).
/// A stop of the firmware halts here ([`halt_unless_returnable`]).
///
/// Runs on the VM-exit stack with interrupts off. It may only use things
/// that need no firmware: VMREAD/VMWRITE (the VMCS is still current) and the
/// serial port. `uefi::println!` must not be called here; `log!` and the
/// panic handler skip the console once the phase below is set. For an
/// emulated instruction it also writes the result into the guest's registers
/// in `frame`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
extern "efiapi" fn vmexit_handler(frame: *mut RegisterFrame) -> u64 {
    // First, so every line below (and any panic) skips the firmware console.
    // Put back when the guest resumes ([`resume_phase`]). After a stop that
    // returns, bring-up switches it back once it has left VMX operation.
    let phase = crate::output::set_phase(Phase::VmExit);
    #[cfg(feature = "host-fault-test")]
    host::fault_on_purpose();
    #[cfg(feature = "forward-refusal-test")]
    hyperv::refuse_on_purpose();

    let guest = GuestKind::SELECTED;
    let number = stats::update(VcpuStats::count_exit);
    // SAFETY: the entry stub passes a pointer to the frame it just pushed on
    // the exit stack. It stays put until this returns and nothing else
    // touches it meanwhile; the stub pops it into the guest's registers
    // afterwards, so writes here reach the guest.
    let frame = unsafe { &mut *frame };
    let read = read_exit(frame);
    let host_nmi = host::take_pending_nmi();
    let (event, next) = judge(guest, read.exit, host_nmi);
    let outcome = carry_out(event, &read, next, frame);
    if let Outcome::Resumed { plan, .. } = outcome {
        stats::update(|stats| stats.count_resumed(event, plan));
        stats::update_forwarded(|forwarded| forwarded.count(plan.emulate));
    }
    // Before anything prints, so a panic while printing still shows this exit.
    history::record(read.record(number, event));
    let basic = read.reason().map_or(UNREADABLE_REASON, |reason| reason.basic);
    let count = count_exit(basic);
    report_exit(&ExitReport {
        guest,
        number,
        count,
        detail: exit_detail(count, outcome.stops(), read.unreadable(), MAX_LEVEL),
        read: &read,
        host_nmi,
        event,
        next,
        outcome,
    });
    if outcome.stops() {
        report_stop(number, frame, &exits_by_reason());
        halt_unless_returnable(guest);
    } else {
        #[cfg(feature = "host-nmi-test")]
        if event == ExitEvent::MainVmcall {
            wait_for_host_nmi(number);
        }
        // Last, after every VMCS write of this exit.
        keep_nmi_window_for_host_nmi(number);
        crate::output::set_phase(resume_phase(event, phase));
    }
    stub_return(outcome.action(), number, read.raw_reason())
}

/// The output phase the guest resumes in after `event`: the one the exit
/// found (`found`), except after the `ExitBootServices` VMCALL, from which
/// on it is [`Phase::Runtime`] for good: the firmware console is gone.
fn resume_phase(event: ExitEvent, found: Phase) -> Phase {
    if event == ExitEvent::BootServicesEnded {
        Phase::Runtime
    } else {
        found
    }
}

/// Halts after a stop of a `guest` whose stop cannot return to bring-up
/// (`GuestKind::stop_returns_to_bring_up`): the firmware, launched in place,
/// has reused the stack `vmcs::launch_in_place` ran on, and no frame was
/// saved to jump back to. The stop's report is already on serial.
fn halt_unless_returnable(guest: GuestKind) {
    if !guest.stop_returns_to_bring_up() {
        crate::output::halt_forever();
    }
}

/// What [`read_exit`] read about one exit. Each VMCS field keeps its VMREAD
/// result, so the report can show an unreadable one where it belongs.
pub(super) struct ExitRead {
    /// VM_EXIT_REASON.
    pub(super) reason: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO.
    pub(super) interruption_info: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// EXIT_QUALIFICATION.
    pub(super) qualification: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS, read for EPT exits only (`None` for others).
    pub(super) guest_physical: Option<Result<u64, VmcsError>>,
    /// GUEST_SS_ACCESS_RIGHTS, the CPL, read for VMCALL exits only.
    pub(super) ss_access_rights: Option<Result<u64, VmcsError>>,
    /// GUEST_RIP.
    pub(super) rip: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN.
    pub(super) length: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE.
    pub(super) interruptibility: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// IDT_VECTORING_INFO.
    pub(super) idt_vectoring: Result<u64, VmcsError>,
    /// The guest's RAX, RBX, RCX and RDX as the stub saved them, before an
    /// emulated instruction changes them.
    ///
    /// The stub pushed them just below HOST_RSP; after a normal exit they are
    /// the guest's values. After a VM-entry failure (exit reason bit 31) the
    /// guest never ran, so they are whatever was live when entry was
    /// attempted: the host's registers for VMLAUNCH, or the restored guest
    /// registers (the previous exit's) for VMRESUME. Either way, not this
    /// exit's guest.
    pub(super) registers: [u64; 4],
    /// The page EPT protects, for granting write.
    protected: Option<ProtectedPage>,
    /// Everything `decide` needs, `None` if a field it needs was unreadable.
    pub(super) exit: Option<ExitInfo>,
}

impl ExitRead {
    /// The exit reason, if VM_EXIT_REASON was readable.
    pub(super) fn reason(&self) -> Option<ExitReason> {
        self.reason.ok().map(|raw| ExitReason::from_raw(raw as u32))
    }

    /// VM_EXIT_REASON for the stop value, or [`UNREADABLE_REASON`].
    fn raw_reason(&self) -> u32 {
        self.reason.map_or(u32::from(UNREADABLE_REASON), |raw| raw as u32)
    }

    /// This exit, number `number`, as the history keeps it, with what
    /// `decide` made of it (`event`).
    fn record(&self, number: u64, event: ExitEvent) -> ExitRecord {
        ExitRecord {
            number,
            reason: self.reason.ok().map(|raw| raw as u32),
            qualification: self.qualification.ok(),
            rip: self.rip.ok(),
            length: self.length.ok(),
            interruption_info: self.interruption_info.ok().map(|info| info as u32),
            idt_vectoring_info: self.idt_vectoring.ok().map(|info| info as u32),
            registers: self.registers,
            event,
        }
    }

    /// Whether a VMCS field the handler read could not be read.
    fn unreadable(&self) -> bool {
        [
            self.reason,
            self.interruption_info,
            self.qualification,
            self.guest_physical.unwrap_or(Ok(0)),
            self.ss_access_rights.unwrap_or(Ok(0)),
            self.rip,
            self.length,
            self.interruptibility,
            self.idt_vectoring,
        ]
        .iter()
        .any(Result::is_err)
    }
}

/// Reads the exit's VMCS fields and the guest registers, and collects what
/// [`judge`] and [`carry_out`] need. Prints nothing.
fn read_exit(frame: &RegisterFrame) -> ExitRead {
    let reason = read_field(VM_EXIT_REASON);
    let decoded = reason.ok().map(|raw| ExitReason::from_raw(raw as u32));
    let interruption_info = read_field(VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO);
    let qualification = read_field(EXIT_QUALIFICATION);
    let ept_exit = decoded.is_some_and(|reason| {
        !reason.entry_failure && matches!(reason.basic, EXIT_REASON_EPT_VIOLATION | EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG)
    });
    let guest_physical = ept_exit.then(|| read_field(GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS));
    // Only a VMCALL is judged by the CPL; 0 otherwise, which `decide` never
    // looks at, and an unreadable one leaves the VMCALL unjudged.
    let vmcall_exit = decoded.is_some_and(|reason| !reason.entry_failure && reason.basic == EXIT_REASON_VMCALL);
    let ss_access_rights = vmcall_exit.then(|| read_field(GUEST_SS_ACCESS_RIGHTS));
    let guest_cpl = ss_access_rights.map_or(Some(0), |rights| rights.ok().map(cpl_from_ss));
    let rip = read_field(GUEST_RIP);
    let length = read_field(VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN);
    let interruptibility = read_field(GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE);
    let idt_vectoring = read_field(IDT_VECTORING_INFO);
    let protected = ept::protected_page();
    let mtrr = guest_mtrrs::capabilities();

    // Only EPT and I/O exits are judged by EXIT_QUALIFICATION. For any other
    // exit an unreadable one (reported later) does not matter.
    let judged_by_qualification =
        ept_exit || decoded.is_some_and(|reason| !reason.entry_failure && reason.basic == EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION);
    let qualification_for_decide = if judged_by_qualification {
        qualification.ok()
    } else {
        Some(qualification.unwrap_or(0))
    };
    // Meaningful only when idt_vectoring is valid and carries an error code;
    // 0 otherwise, so an unreadable field never stops an exit that ignores it.
    let idt_vectoring_error_code = read_field(IDT_VECTORING_ERROR_CODE).unwrap_or(0) as u32;
    // Meaningful only for EPT exits; decide never looks at it otherwise.
    let guest_physical_for_decide = guest_physical.map_or(Some(0), Result::ok);
    let exit = match (
        decoded,
        interruption_info.ok(),
        interruptibility.ok(),
        idt_vectoring.ok(),
        qualification_for_decide,
        guest_physical_for_decide,
        guest_cpl,
    ) {
        (
            Some(reason),
            Some(info),
            Some(blocking),
            Some(vectoring),
            Some(qualification),
            Some(guest_physical),
            Some(guest_cpl),
        ) => {
            Some(ExitInfo {
                reason,
                interruption_info: InterruptionInfo(info as u32),
                guest_rax: frame.rax,
                guest_rcx: frame.rcx,
                guest_rdx: frame.rdx,
                interruptibility: blocking as u32,
                // IDT_VECTORING_INFO has the interruption-information layout.
                idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(vectoring as u32),
                idt_vectoring_error_code,
                qualification,
                guest_physical,
                protected_page: protected.map_or(0, |page| page.gpa),
                mtrr,
                hyperv: hyperv::offered(),
                guest_cpl,
            })
        }
        // An unreadable field is reported later; without it the exit cannot
        // be judged.
        _ => None,
    };

    ExitRead {
        reason,
        interruption_info,
        qualification,
        guest_physical,
        ss_access_rights,
        rip,
        length,
        interruptibility,
        idt_vectoring,
        registers: [frame.rax, frame.rbx, frame.rcx, frame.rdx],
        protected,
        exit,
    }
}

/// Decides what `exit` of `guest` is with the state kept between exits, and
/// keeps the state for the next one. An NMI that arrived in root operation
/// since the last exit (`host_nmi`) is pending for the guest first. An exit
/// that could not be read is unexpected.
fn judge(guest: GuestKind, exit: Option<ExitInfo>, host_nmi: bool) -> (ExitEvent, ExitState) {
    let state = load_state().with_host_nmi(host_nmi);
    let (event, next) = match exit {
        Some(exit) => decide(guest, state, exit),
        None => (ExitEvent::Unexpected, state),
    };
    store_state(next);
    (event, next)
}

/// What carrying out an exit's event came to.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) enum Outcome {
    /// The guest goes on: the VMCS is prepared as `plan` says.
    Resumed { plan: ResumePlan, resumed: Resumed },
    /// The plan could not be carried out, so the guest stops.
    ResumeFailed(ResumeFailure),
    /// The event itself stops the guest (`Finished` or `Unexpected`).
    Stopped(ExitAction),
}

impl Outcome {
    /// What the entry stub does next.
    pub(super) fn action(self) -> ExitAction {
        match self {
            Self::Resumed { plan, .. } => ExitAction::Resume(plan),
            Self::ResumeFailed(_) => ExitAction::Unexpected,
            Self::Stopped(action) => action,
        }
    }

    /// Whether the guest stops at this exit.
    pub(super) fn stops(self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self, Self::Resumed { .. })
    }
}

/// Carries out `event`: prepares the guest to resume as its plan says, or
/// stops it. `next` is the state after the exit. Prints nothing.
fn carry_out(event: ExitEvent, read: &ExitRead, next: ExitState, frame: &mut RegisterFrame) -> Outcome {
    match event.action() {
        ExitAction::Resume(plan) => {
            let plan = plan.keeping_pending_nmi(next);
            // Re-deliver an event this exit interrupted mid-delivery. The plan
            // refuses when it would also advance RIP or inject its own event,
            // since only one event is injected per VM entry.
            let plan = match read
                .exit
                .and_then(|exit| exit.redelivery(read.length.ok().map(|length| length as u32)))
            {
                Some(redelivery) => plan.redelivering(redelivery),
                None => Some(plan),
            };
            match plan {
                Some(plan) => match prepare_resume(read, plan, frame) {
                    Ok((plan, resumed)) => Outcome::Resumed { plan, resumed },
                    Err(failure) => Outcome::ResumeFailed(failure),
                },
                None => Outcome::ResumeFailed(ResumeFailure::RedeliveryConflict),
            }
        }
        stop => Outcome::Stopped(stop),
    }
}

/// Turns NMI-window exiting on if an NMI arrived in root operation after
/// [`judge`] looked. The host NMI handler turns it on itself, but a write
/// of the primary controls in [`prepare_resume`] may have replaced its
/// write; nothing writes them after this, so the guest exits to take the
/// NMI as soon as it can.
fn keep_nmi_window_for_host_nmi(number: u64) {
    if !host::nmi_pending() {
        return;
    }
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{} VM exit #{number}: an NMI arrived in root operation during this exit; NMI-window exiting on.",
        crate::TAG
    );
    // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS
    // current. `configure_controls` checked that the CPU allows NMI-window
    // exiting.
    if let Err(error) = unsafe { vmcs::set_nmi_window_exiting(true) } {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{} VM exit #{number}: could not turn NMI-window exiting on ({error:?}); the NMI waits for the next exit.",
            crate::TAG
        );
    }
}

/// Waits in root operation, after main VMCALL #1, until an NMI arrives or
/// the guest's own wait would have given up. `run-hyperv.ps1 -InjectNmi`
/// sends its NMI once serial shows the resume line printed just before, so
/// the NMI reaches the host NMI handler instead of the guest.
#[cfg(feature = "host-nmi-test")]
fn wait_for_host_nmi(number: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: host-nmi-test: waiting in VMX root operation for an NMI.");
    let mut rounds = crate::vmx::guest::GUEST_WAIT_ITERATIONS;
    while !host::nmi_pending() && rounds > 0 {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
        rounds -= 1;
    }
    if host::nmi_pending() {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: host-nmi-test: the host NMI handler ran ({} NMI(s) in root operation so far).",
            host::nmis_taken()
        );
    } else {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: host-nmi-test: no NMI arrived; going on.");
    }
}

/// What an emulated instruction did, for the report.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) enum EmulationOutcome {
    /// CPUID `leaf`/`subleaf`: what the processor returned (`raw`) and what
    /// the guest got after `cpuid_policy` (`guest`).
    Cpuid {
        leaf: u32,
        subleaf: u32,
        raw: CpuidResult,
        guest: CpuidResult,
    },
    /// RDMSR of `msr` returned `value`.
    Rdmsr { msr: u32, value: u64 },
    /// WRMSR wrote `value` to `msr`.
    Wrmsr { msr: u32, value: u64 },
    /// RDMSR of the guest's MTRR `msr` returned `value`, from its copy.
    MtrrRead { msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64 },
    /// WRMSR wrote `value` to the guest's MTRR `msr`, in its copy, with
    /// what EPT made of it (`write`). The CPU's own MSR holds `cpu_value`,
    /// read after the write, which it leaves alone.
    MtrrWrite {
        msr: MtrrMsr,
        value: u64,
        cpu_value: u64,
        write: MtrrWrite,
    },
    /// IN of `size` from `port` read `value`.
    In { port: u16, size: IoSize, value: u32 },
    /// OUT of `value` (`size` wide) to `port`.
    Out { port: u16, size: IoSize, value: u32 },
    /// The hypercall with input value `input` went to Hyper-V, which
    /// returned `result` in RAX: the status in bits 15:0, the reps done in
    /// bits 43:32.
    Hypercall { input: u64, result: u64 },
    /// RDMSR of the synthetic MSR `msr` returned `value`, from Hyper-V.
    SyntheticRead { msr: u32, value: u64 },
    /// WRMSR wrote `value` to the synthetic MSR `msr`, at Hyper-V.
    SyntheticWrite { msr: u32, value: u64 },
    /// Hyper-V refused the forwarded `emulation` with `exception`, which the
    /// guest gets at its own instruction instead.
    Refused {
        emulation: Emulation,
        exception: InterruptionInfo,
    },
}

impl EmulationOutcome {
    /// The exception the guest gets when Hyper-V refused the access.
    fn refused(self) -> Option<InterruptionInfo> {
        match self {
            Self::Refused { exception, .. } => Some(exception),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Executes `emulation` in root operation and writes its result into the
/// guest's registers in `frame`. Only an access to the guest's MTRRs can
/// fail; one Hyper-V refuses comes back as [`EmulationOutcome::Refused`],
/// with `frame` unchanged.
fn execute(emulation: Emulation, frame: &mut RegisterFrame) -> Result<EmulationOutcome, ResumeFailure> {
    Ok(match emulation {
        Emulation::Cpuid { leaf, subleaf } => {
            // In root operation CPUID returns the processor's values (under
            // Hyper-V: what Hyper-V shows Aleph0).
            let raw = __cpuid_count(leaf, subleaf);
            let guest = cpuid_policy(leaf, raw);
            // CPUID writes 32-bit registers, which zero-extends them.
            frame.rax = guest.eax.into();
            frame.rbx = guest.ebx.into();
            frame.rcx = guest.ecx.into();
            frame.rdx = guest.edx.into();
            EmulationOutcome::Cpuid {
                leaf,
                subleaf,
                raw,
                guest,
            }
        }
        Emulation::Rdmsr { msr } => {
            // SAFETY: `decide` emulates only INTERCEPTED_MSRS, which exist on
            // every CPU Aleph0 runs on (IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE: every 64-bit
            // CPU) and have no read side effects.
            let value = unsafe { msr::rdmsr(msr) };
            // RDMSR writes EAX and EDX, which zero-extends them.
            frame.rax = value & 0xFFFF_FFFF;
            frame.rdx = value >> 32;
            EmulationOutcome::Rdmsr { msr, value }
        }
        Emulation::Wrmsr { msr, value } => {
            // SAFETY: an intercepted MSR (see Rdmsr), and `decide` checked
            // the value is canonical, so WRMSR cannot fault. VM entry and
            // exit do not switch IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE and Aleph0 never runs
            // SWAPGS, so the guest's value is simply the CPU's.
            unsafe { msr::wrmsr(msr, value) };
            EmulationOutcome::Wrmsr { msr, value }
        }
        Emulation::MtrrRead { msr } => {
            let value = guest_mtrrs::read(msr).map_err(ResumeFailure::GuestMtrrs)?;
            // RDMSR writes EAX and EDX, which zero-extends them.
            frame.rax = value & 0xFFFF_FFFF;
            frame.rdx = value >> 32;
            EmulationOutcome::MtrrRead { msr, value }
        }
        Emulation::MtrrWrite { msr, value } => {
            // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, the guest stopped at
            // this exit.
            let write = unsafe { guest_mtrrs::write(msr, value) }.map_err(ResumeFailure::GuestMtrrs)?;
            // SAFETY: `decide` routes only the MTRR MSRs the CPU has to the
            // copy, and reading one has no side effects. Read for the report,
            // which shows the CPU's untouched.
            let cpu_value = unsafe { msr::rdmsr(msr.address()) };
            EmulationOutcome::MtrrWrite {
                msr,
                value,
                cpu_value,
                write,
            }
        }
        Emulation::In { port, size } => {
            // SAFETY: the guest asked for exactly this access, which it could
            // have made without Aleph0, and IN/OUT at CPL 0 in root operation
            // cannot fault. A 2- or 4-byte access at 0x3FC-0x3FE also touches
            // 0x3FF, so it exits and passes through to COM1's registers at
            // 0x3FC-0x3FE, the guest's own UART (docs/EMULATED_EXITS.md
            // section 5).
            let value = unsafe {
                match size {
                    IoSize::Byte => u32::from(port::inb(port)),
                    IoSize::Word => u32::from(port::inw(port)),
                    IoSize::Dword => port::inl(port),
                }
            };
            frame.rax = merge_in(frame.rax, size, value);
            EmulationOutcome::In { port, size, value }
        }
        Emulation::Out { port, size, value } => {
            // SAFETY: as for In: the guest's own OUT.
            unsafe {
                match size {
                    IoSize::Byte => port::outb(port, value as u8),
                    IoSize::Word => port::outw(port, value as u16),
                    IoSize::Dword => port::outl(port, value),
                }
            }
            EmulationOutcome::Out { port, size, value }
        }
        Emulation::Hypercall { input } => {
            let mut registers = HypercallRegisters {
                rcx: input,
                rdx: frame.rdx,
                r8: frame.r8,
                rax: 0,
            };
            // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation at CPL 0 with the host
            // IDT loaded, the guest stopped at its VMCALL. `decide` forwards
            // only with Hyper-V's interface present and from the guest's CPL
            // 0, so this is a hypercall the guest could have made itself.
            match unsafe { hyperv::forward_hypercall(&mut registers) } {
                Ok(()) => {
                    frame.rax = registers.rax;
                    frame.rcx = registers.rcx;
                    frame.rdx = registers.rdx;
                    frame.r8 = registers.r8;
                    EmulationOutcome::Hypercall {
                        input,
                        result: registers.rax,
                    }
                }
                Err(_) => EmulationOutcome::Refused {
                    emulation,
                    exception: InterruptionInfo::INVALID_OPCODE,
                },
            }
        }
        Emulation::SyntheticRead { msr } => {
            // SAFETY: as for Hypercall, at the guest's RDMSR, which needs CPL
            // 0 to exit at all.
            match unsafe { hyperv::forward_rdmsr(msr) } {
                Ok(value) => {
                    // RDMSR writes EAX and EDX, which zero-extends them.
                    frame.rax = value & 0xFFFF_FFFF;
                    frame.rdx = value >> 32;
                    EmulationOutcome::SyntheticRead { msr, value }
                }
                Err(_) => EmulationOutcome::Refused {
                    emulation,
                    exception: InterruptionInfo::GENERAL_PROTECTION,
                },
            }
        }
        Emulation::SyntheticWrite { msr, value } => {
            // SAFETY: as for SyntheticRead, at the guest's WRMSR.
            match unsafe { hyperv::forward_wrmsr(msr, value) } {
                Ok(()) => EmulationOutcome::SyntheticWrite { msr, value },
                Err(_) => EmulationOutcome::Refused {
                    emulation,
                    exception: InterruptionInfo::GENERAL_PROTECTION,
                },
            }
        }
    })
}

/// How the guest goes on after [`prepare_resume`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct Resumed {
    /// Where the guest resumes.
    pub(super) rip: u64,
    /// The INVEPT type used, if the protected page was made writable.
    pub(super) invept: Option<InveptType>,
    /// What the emulated instruction did, if the plan emulated one.
    pub(super) emulated: Option<EmulationOutcome>,
}

/// Why the guest cannot resume from an exit it was meant to resume from.
/// Its `Display` is the report's line, before "; not resuming.".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum ResumeFailure {
    /// GUEST_RIP could not be read.
    RipUnreadable,
    /// RIP must move past the instruction, but VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN could
    /// not be read.
    LengthUnreadable,
    /// The next RIP would wrap past the top of the address space or be
    /// non-canonical ([`next_rip`]).
    NextRipInvalid,
    /// A VMWRITE the plan needs failed; `what` names the step.
    Write { what: &'static str, error: VmcsError },
    /// The plan makes the protected page writable, but there is none.
    NoProtectedPage,
    /// INVEPT failed after the protected page was made writable.
    GrantWrite(VmxFail),
    /// RDMSR or WRMSR of the guest's MTRRs failed.
    GuestMtrrs(MtrrAccessFailure),
    /// The exit interrupted an event's delivery, but this exit's plan already
    /// advances RIP or injects its own event, so the event cannot be
    /// re-delivered: only one event is injected per VM entry. (A software
    /// event whose instruction length is unreadable fails the same way.)
    RedeliveryConflict,
}

impl fmt::Display for ResumeFailure {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match *self {
            Self::RipUnreadable => f.write_str("guest RIP unreadable"),
            Self::LengthUnreadable => f.write_str("instruction length unreadable"),
            Self::NextRipInvalid => f.write_str("next guest RIP would wrap or be non-canonical"),
            Self::Write { what, error } => write!(f, "could not {what} ({error:?})"),
            Self::NoProtectedPage => f.write_str("no protected page to make writable"),
            Self::GrantWrite(error) => write!(f, "could not make the protected page writable (INVEPT {error:?})"),
            Self::GuestMtrrs(failure) => write!(f, "{failure}"),
            Self::RedeliveryConflict => f.write_str(
                "an interrupted event cannot be re-delivered while the exit advances RIP or injects its own event",
            ),
        }
    }
}

/// VMWRITEs `value` to `field` for a resume plan; `what` names the step if
/// it fails.
fn write_for_resume(field: u32, value: u64, what: &'static str) -> Result<(), ResumeFailure> {
    // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS current.
    unsafe { vmcs::vmwrite(field, value) }.map_err(|error| ResumeFailure::Write { what, error })
}

/// Prepares the VMCS (and EPT) as `plan` says: executes the emulated
/// instruction into `frame`, moves GUEST_RIP past the exiting instruction
/// and ends an STI or MOV SS shadow, queues an NMI or an exception for
/// injection at the next VM entry, turns NMI-window exiting on or off, and
/// makes the protected page writable. Returns the plan carried out, which
/// injects an exception instead of advancing RIP when Hyper-V refused a
/// forwarded access, and how the guest resumes; or why it cannot.
fn prepare_resume(
    read: &ExitRead,
    plan: ResumePlan,
    frame: &mut RegisterFrame,
) -> Result<(ResumePlan, Resumed), ResumeFailure> {
    let rip = read.rip.map_err(|_| ResumeFailure::RipUnreadable)?;
    // Checked before the emulation: with the length unreadable or the new RIP
    // wrapping or non-canonical, a WRMSR or OUT would already have happened
    // when the guest stops, and serial would never show it.
    let advance_to = if plan.advance_rip {
        let length = read.length.map_err(|_| ResumeFailure::LengthUnreadable)?;
        Some(next_rip(rip, length).ok_or(ResumeFailure::NextRipInvalid)?)
    } else {
        None
    };
    // Before RIP moves: the guest resumes past the instruction with its
    // result already in its registers.
    let emulated = plan.emulate.map(|emulation| execute(emulation, frame)).transpose()?;
    // Hyper-V refused a forwarded access: the guest gets the same exception,
    // at its own instruction, as it would without Aleph0.
    let (plan, advance_to) = match emulated.and_then(EmulationOutcome::refused) {
        Some(exception) => (plan.refused_with(exception), None),
        None => (plan, advance_to),
    };
    let ResumePlan {
        inject_nmi,
        nmi_window,
        grant_write,
        inject_exception,
        redeliver,
        ..
    } = plan;

    let resume_rip = if let Some(next) = advance_to {
        write_for_resume(GUEST_RIP, next, "advance guest RIP")?;
        // `exit` is always read here: `decide` only plans a resume for an
        // exit it could judge. Written only when a shadow was set, so most
        // exits pay nothing.
        let interruptibility = read.exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.interruptibility);
        let cleared = after_skipped_instruction(interruptibility);
        if cleared != interruptibility {
            write_for_resume(
                GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE,
                cleared.into(),
                "end the guest's STI/MOV SS blocking",
            )?;
        }
        next
    } else {
        // An NMI exit: the guest goes on at the instruction it was about to
        // run, and the injected NMI is delivered before it. An EPT
        // violation: the faulting write runs again. A #GP or #UD: delivered
        // at the RDMSR, WRMSR or VMCALL, which faults.
        rip
    };

    if inject_nmi {
        write_for_resume(
            VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO,
            InterruptionInfo::NMI.0.into(),
            "queue the NMI for injection",
        )?;
    }
    if let Some(exception) = inject_exception {
        // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS
        // current.
        unsafe { queue_exception(exception) }.map_err(|error| ResumeFailure::Write {
            what: "queue the exception for injection",
            error,
        })?;
    }
    if let Some(redelivery) = redeliver {
        // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS
        // current.
        unsafe { write_redelivery(redelivery) }.map_err(|error| ResumeFailure::Write {
            what: "queue the interrupted event for re-delivery",
            error,
        })?;
    }
    if let Some(on) = nmi_window {
        // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS
        // current. `configure_controls` checked that the CPU allows
        // NMI-window exiting.
        unsafe { vmcs::set_nmi_window_exiting(on) }.map_err(|error| ResumeFailure::Write {
            what: if on {
                "turn NMI-window exiting on"
            } else {
                "turn NMI-window exiting off"
            },
            error,
        })?;
    }
    let invept = if grant_write {
        let page = read.protected.ok_or(ResumeFailure::NoProtectedPage)?;
        // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, guest stopped. `page`
        // came from `ept::protected_page`, so `Ept::build` made the tables,
        // which are never freed.
        Some(unsafe { page.grant_write() }.map_err(ResumeFailure::GrantWrite)?)
    } else {
        None
    };
    Ok((
        plan,
        Resumed {
            rip: resume_rip,
            invept,
            emulated,
        },
    ))
}

/// Queues `exception` for the next VM entry, with error code 0 if it
/// delivers one, through the guest's own IDT at the instruction RIP points
/// to.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// VMX root operation with the guest's VMCS current.
unsafe fn queue_exception(exception: InterruptionInfo) -> Result<(), VmcsError> {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX root operation with a current VMCS.
    unsafe {
        if exception.delivers_error_code() {
            vmcs::vmwrite(VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE, 0)?;
        }
        vmcs::vmwrite(VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO, exception.0.into())
    }
}

/// Queues the event `redelivery` describes for the next VM entry: its
/// interruption info, its error code when it carries one, and its
/// instruction length for a software interrupt or exception. The
/// interruption-information field is written last, as for an injection.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// VMX root operation with the guest's VMCS current.
unsafe fn write_redelivery(redelivery: Redelivery) -> Result<(), VmcsError> {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX root operation with a current VMCS.
    unsafe {
        if let Some(error_code) = redelivery.error_code {
            vmcs::vmwrite(VM_ENTRY_EXCEPTION_ERROR_CODE, error_code.into())?;
        }
        if let Some(length) = redelivery.instruction_len {
            vmcs::vmwrite(VM_ENTRY_INSTRUCTION_LEN, length.into())?;
        }
        vmcs::vmwrite(VM_ENTRY_INTERRUPTION_INFO, redelivery.info.0.into())
    }
}

/// Called by the entry stub when VMRESUME falls through instead of entering
/// the guest; `rflags` is RFLAGS right after it, and `frame` the guest's
/// registers, which the stub pushed again. Prints why, then the same stop
/// report as an exit that stops the guest, and returns the stop value the
/// stub hands back to bring-up, or halts for the firmware.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
extern "efiapi" fn vmresume_failed(rflags: u64, frame: *const RegisterFrame) -> u64 {
    // The handler put the guest's phase back before VMRESUME; this is exit
    // context again.
    crate::output::set_phase(Phase::VmExit);
    let guest = GuestKind::SELECTED;
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    match vmcs::resume_failure(rflags) {
        // SAFETY: a VmFailValid implies VMX operation with a current VMCS,
        // so the error number is readable.
        VmcsError::VmFailValid => match unsafe { vmcs::vm_instruction_error() } {
            Ok(code) => crate::serial_println!(
                "{tag} VMRESUME failed: {} ({code})",
                vmcs::vm_instruction_error_name(code),
            ),
            Err(error) => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VMRESUME failed: VmFailValid, error unreadable ({error:?})"),
        },
        error => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VMRESUME failed: {error:?}"),
    }
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} VMRESUME failed; stopping the guest; {}.", after_stop(guest));
    // SAFETY: the stub passes the frame it just pushed on the exit stack,
    // which stays put until this returns.
    let frame = unsafe { &*frame };
    // The VMRESUME belongs to the last exit, so its number heads the report.
    report_stop(stats::snapshot().exits, frame, &exits_by_reason());
    halt_unless_returnable(guest);
    encode_resume_failed(rflags)
}
```

`src/vmx/vmexit/history.rs`:

```rs
//! The last VM exits, kept to show what led to a stop or a panic.
//!
//! An exit printed in full shows only itself, and past the print policy's
//! limit most exits are not printed at all (`policy.rs`). So the exit handler
//! records every exit in a ring of the last [`HISTORY_LEN`]: what it read
//! (no VMREAD is added for this) and what `decide` made of it. Every stop
//! prints the ring oldest first, after the dump, and so does the panic
//! handler, after its message.

use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::fmt;

use crate::vmx::exit_decision::{ExitEvent, ExitReason, exit_reason_name};

/// Exits the history keeps.
pub const HISTORY_LEN: usize = 64;

/// The last `N` items pushed; once it is full, each push overwrites the
/// oldest.
pub struct Ring<T, const N: usize> {
    items: [T; N],
    /// Items pushed so far, kept or not.
    pushed: u64,
}

impl<T: Copy, const N: usize> Ring<T, N> {
    /// An empty ring. `filler` only fills the slots nothing was pushed to,
    /// which are never read.
    pub const fn new(filler: T) -> Self {
        const { assert!(N > 0) };
        Self {
            items: [filler; N],
            pushed: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Adds `item`, overwriting the oldest once the ring is full.
    pub fn push(&mut self, item: T) {
        self.items[(self.pushed % N as u64) as usize] = item;
        self.pushed += 1;
    }

    /// How many items the ring holds: the pushed ones, up to `N`.
    pub fn kept(&self) -> usize {
        self.pushed.min(N as u64) as usize
    }

    /// How many pushed items are no longer kept.
    pub fn overwritten(&self) -> u64 {
        self.pushed.saturating_sub(N as u64)
    }

    /// The kept items, oldest first.
    pub fn oldest_first(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
        // Once items were overwritten, the oldest kept one is where the next
        // push will go.
        let start = if self.overwritten() > 0 {
            (self.pushed % N as u64) as usize
        } else {
            0
        };
        (0..self.kept()).map(move |index| &self.items[(start + index) % N])
    }
}

/// One exit, as the history keeps it. `None` marks a VMCS field that could
/// not be read.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ExitRecord {
    pub number: u64,
    /// VM_EXIT_REASON.
    pub reason: Option<u32>,
    pub qualification: Option<u64>,
    pub rip: Option<u64>,
    pub length: Option<u64>,
    /// VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO.
    pub interruption_info: Option<u32>,
    /// IDT_VECTORING_INFO.
    pub idt_vectoring_info: Option<u32>,
    /// RAX, RBX, RCX and RDX at the exit.
    pub registers: [u64; 4],
    /// What `decide` made of the exit.
    pub event: ExitEvent,
}

impl ExitRecord {
    /// Fills the slots of an empty history.
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        number: 0,
        reason: None,
        qualification: None,
        rip: None,
        length: None,
        interruption_info: None,
        idt_vectoring_info: None,
        registers: [0; 4],
        event: ExitEvent::Unexpected,
    };
}

/// A field of a record, or `?` when it could not be read.
struct Field {
    value: Option<u64>,
    /// Hexadecimal; decimal otherwise, for a count.
    hex: bool,
}

/// `value` in hexadecimal.
fn hex(value: Option<u64>) -> Field {
    Field { value, hex: true }
}

/// `value`, a count, in decimal.
fn decimal(value: Option<u64>) -> Field {
    Field { value, hex: false }
}

impl fmt::Display for Field {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self.value {
            Some(value) if self.hex => write!(f, "{value:#x}"),
            Some(value) => write!(f, "{value}"),
            None => f.write_str("?"),
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for ExitRecord {
    /// One line: `#3 reason=32 (WRMSR) rip=0x7eae1028 len=2 qual=0x0
    /// info=0x0 vectoring=0x0 rax=0x0 rbx=0x20800 rcx=0xc0000102
    /// rdx=0x7a1e -> Emulated(Wrmsr { .. })`, the event in hexadecimal.
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "#{} ", self.number)?;
        match self.reason.map(ExitReason::from_raw) {
            Some(reason) => write!(
                f,
                "reason={} ({}){}",
                reason.basic,
                exit_reason_name(reason.basic),
                if reason.entry_failure { " [entry failed]" } else { "" },
            )?,
            None => f.write_str("reason=?")?,
        }
        let [rax, rbx, rcx, rdx] = self.registers;
        write!(
            f,
            " rip={} len={} qual={} info={} vectoring={} rax={rax:#x} rbx={rbx:#x} rcx={rcx:#x} rdx={rdx:#x} -> {:x?}",
            hex(self.rip),
            decimal(self.length),
            hex(self.qualification),
            hex(self.interruption_info.map(u64::from)),
            hex(self.idt_vectoring_info.map(u64::from)),
            self.event,
        )
    }
}

/// The history, in a cell the exit handler writes through a shared static.
struct History(UnsafeCell<Ring<ExitRecord, HISTORY_LEN>>);

// SAFETY: Aleph0 runs on one CPU. Only the exit handler writes the history
// ([`record`]), with interrupts off, and the host NMI handler never touches
// it. It is read by the same exit handler at a stop, after its last write,
// and by the panic handler, which runs on that CPU after the code that
// panicked: `record` itself cannot panic, so no reader sees half a record.
unsafe impl Sync for History {}

static HISTORY: History = History(UnsafeCell::new(Ring::new(ExitRecord::EMPTY)));

/// Adds `record` to the history. For the exit handler only.
pub(super) fn record(record: ExitRecord) {
    // SAFETY: the exit handler is the only writer, and no reader runs while
    // it writes (see `History`).
    unsafe { (*HISTORY.0.get()).push(record) };
}

/// Prints the history oldest first, each line after `context` (`VM exit
/// #13`, or `PANIC`). Prints nothing before the first exit.
pub fn report(context: fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
    // SAFETY: a reader runs only when the exit handler is not writing (see
    // `History`).
    let history = unsafe { &*HISTORY.0.get() };
    if history.kept() == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} {context}: the last {} exits, oldest first ({} older not kept):",
        history.kept(),
        history.overwritten(),
    );
    for record in history.oldest_first() {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} {context}:   {record}");
    }
}
```

`src/vmx/vmexit/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! VM-exit host resources: the exit stack, the assembly entry stub, and the
//! exit handler.
//!
//! On every VM exit the CPU loads host state from the VMCS and jumps to
//! HOST_RIP ([`entry_address`]) with RSP = HOST_RSP ([`VmExitStack::top`]).
//! Nothing else is set up for us: interrupts are off (host RFLAGS is forced
//! to 0x2), and the guest's general-purpose registers are still live in the
//! CPU, so the stub saves them before any Rust code can clobber them.
//!
//! `bring_up::run` enters the guest through `vmcs::launch` (the test guest)
//! or `vmcs::launch_in_place` (the firmware), so the guest's first VM exit
//! lands here. The handler (`handler.rs`) prints each exit over
//! serial, and `exit_decision::decide` says what it is: an instruction to
//! execute for the guest (CPUID, RDMSR, WRMSR, IN, OUT), an access to its
//! copy of its MTRRs (`guest_mtrrs.rs`), or a #GP to inject for an MSR it
//! cannot have or a value written to one that the CPU would refuse,
//! a write to the EPT-protected data page to allow and retry, a VMCALL to
//! resume past, an NMI to reinject, an NMI window to inject in, the last
//! planned VMCALL, or something unexpected. To resume, the
//! handler updates the VMCS and returns 0, and the stub executes VMRESUME. To
//! stop the test guest, it returns a stop value, and the stub jumps back
//! into `vmcs::launch`, which returns to bring-up (see `vmx/vmcs/launch.rs`).
//! A stop of the firmware has no launch frame to return to, so the handler
//! halts once it has printed the stop. The
//! lines that only print live in `report.rs`; how much of each exit they
//! print is `policy.rs`'s decision. Every exit is counted in the vCPU's
//! statistics (`stats.rs`). Every stop adds the guest's state and registers
//! (`dump.rs`), the statistics, and the last exits (`history.rs`).

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::page::{PAGE_SIZE, allocate_zeroed_pages};
use super::vmcs::{self, VmcsError};

mod dump;
mod guest_mtrrs;
mod handler;
mod history;
mod policy;
mod report;
mod stats;

pub use guest_mtrrs::{publish as publish_guest_mtrrs, registers as guest_mtrr_registers};
pub use stats::{VcpuStats, snapshot as vcpu_stats};

/// Prints the last VM exits, oldest first, each line after `context`: for
/// the panic handler, so a panic in exit context shows what led to it. Like
/// the panic handler, left out of host tests.
#[cfg(not(test))]
pub use history::report as report_exit_history;

/// VMREADs `field` of the current VMCS. For the exit handler and its
/// reports, which run in exit context only.
fn read_field(field: u32) -> Result<u64, VmcsError> {
    // SAFETY: exit context: VMX root operation, with the guest's VMCS
    // current.
    unsafe { vmcs::vmread(field) }
}

/// 64 KiB. A debug build's exits used 21168 bytes on Hyper-V (an MTRR write
/// that retypes EPT), more than the 16 KiB this once was: nothing guards the
/// page below the stack, so the handler ran on into the guest's data page.
pub const VM_EXIT_STACK_PAGES: usize = 16;
pub const VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE: usize = VM_EXIT_STACK_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VmExitStackError {
    /// Failed to allocate memory for the VM-exit stack.
    AllocationFailed,
}

/// Owns a contiguous stack allocation that must outlive every use of HOST_RSP.
pub struct VmExitStack {
    base: NonNull<u8>,
}

impl VmExitStack {
    /// Allocate a zeroed, page-aligned stack for the host VM-exit path.
    pub fn allocate() -> Result<Self, VmExitStackError> {
        let base = allocate_zeroed_pages(VM_EXIT_STACK_PAGES, VmExitStackError::AllocationFailed)?;
        Ok(Self { base })
    }

    /// Top of the downward-growing stack, for HOST_RSP. The x64 calling
    /// convention the entry stub follows needs it 16-byte aligned.
    pub fn top(&self) -> u64 {
        // SAFETY: the allocation is VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE bytes long, so this is
        // one past its end, which `add` allows.
        let top = unsafe { self.base.as_ptr().add(VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE) } as usize;
        assert_eq!(top % 16, 0);
        top as u64
    }

    /// How many bytes of the stack the exit handler has written, from the
    /// top down to the lowest nonzero word ([`used_bytes`]). The whole size
    /// means the lowest word was written, which an overflow into the page
    /// below does on its way.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// No exit handler may be running on the stack: the guest has stopped.
    pub unsafe fn used(&self) -> usize {
        // SAFETY: the allocation is VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE bytes, page-aligned,
        // and the caller guarantees nothing writes it meanwhile.
        let words = unsafe {
            core::slice::from_raw_parts(self.base.as_ptr().cast::<u64>(), VM_EXIT_STACK_SIZE / size_of::<u64>())
        };
        used_bytes(words)
    }
}

/// Bytes from the lowest nonzero word of `words`, a stack that started
/// zeroed, to its top. A word the handler wrote as zero counts as unused,
/// so this can undercount by the few words below the deepest nonzero one.
fn used_bytes(words: &[u64]) -> usize {
    words
        .iter()
        .position(|&word| word != 0)
        .map_or(0, |lowest| (words.len() - lowest) * size_of::<u64>())
}

#[repr(C)]
struct RegisterFrame {
    rax: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    r8: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r15: u64,
}

// The entry stub pushes r15 first and rax last, so rax ends up at the lowest
// address. Tie the struct layout to that order, so reordering a field or a
// push breaks the build instead of silently mixing up guest registers.
const _: () = {
    assert!(core::mem::size_of::<RegisterFrame>() == 15 * 8);
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(RegisterFrame, rax) == 0);
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(RegisterFrame, r15) == 14 * 8);
};

// Every exit enters here with RSP = HOST_RSP, the top of the exit stack, so
// the stack starts empty on each exit and does not grow across exits.
//
// Stack alignment (Microsoft x64 ABI: RSP is a multiple of 16 at each
// `call`): HOST_RSP is 16-aligned; 15 pushes take 120 bytes, and 40 more
// (32 bytes of shadow space plus 8 of padding) make 160, a multiple of 16.
// After the 15 pops RSP is HOST_RSP again, and the failure path pushes the
// same 15 registers, so the same 40 bytes align its call too.
//
// Only the 15 general-purpose registers are saved, because nothing here
// touches vector state: the x86_64-unknown-uefi target is soft-float with
// MMX/SSE disabled (only `fxsr` is among its vector features), so the handler
// and `core::fmt` never use x87, XMM or MXCSR. If SSE target features are ever
// enabled, the handler would clobber the guest's vector registers, and this
// stub would have to save them (for example with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR) before an OS
// guest can run.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    r#"
    .globl vmexit_entry
vmexit_entry:
    push r15
    push r14
    push r13
    push r12
    push r11
    push r10
    push r9
    push r8
    push rbp
    push rdi
    push rsi
    push rdx
    push rcx
    push rbx
    push rax

    mov rcx, rsp
    sub rsp, 40
    cld
    call vmexit_handler

    // RAX = 0: resume the guest. Anything else is a stop value: return it
    // from vmx_launch (vmx/vmcs/launch.rs), abandoning this stack. Only the
    // test guest's stops get here; the firmware's halt in the handler.
    test rax, rax
    jnz vmx_return_to_launcher

    // Resume: restore the guest's registers in the reverse order of the
    // pushes above; RIP, RSP and RFLAGS come from the VMCS, not from this
    // frame.
    add rsp, 40
    pop rax
    pop rbx
    pop rcx
    pop rdx
    pop rsi
    pop rdi
    pop rbp
    pop r8
    pop r9
    pop r10
    pop r11
    pop r12
    pop r13
    pop r14
    pop r15
    vmresume

    // Reached only if VMRESUME failed; RFLAGS say how. The guest's
    // registers are still live: push them again as a RegisterFrame for the
    // stop's dump. PUSH leaves RFLAGS alone, so PUSHFQ still reads what
    // VMRESUME left. vmresume_failed(rflags = RCX, frame = RDX) returns the
    // stop value in RAX.
    push r15
    push r14
    push r13
    push r12
    push r11
    push r10
    push r9
    push r8
    push rbp
    push rdi
    push rsi
    push rdx
    push rcx
    push rbx
    push rax
    pushfq
    pop rcx
    mov rdx, rsp
    sub rsp, 40
    call vmresume_failed
    jmp vmx_return_to_launcher
"#
);

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn vmexit_entry() -> !;
}

/// The address of the entry stub, for HOST_RIP.
pub fn entry_address() -> u64 {
    vmexit_entry as *const () as usize as u64
}
```

`src/vmx/vmexit/policy.rs`:

```rs
//! How much of each VM exit the handler prints.
//!
//! Under Hyper-V every serial byte is itself an exit to Hyper-V, and an exit
//! printed in full is about five lines. The test guest's 13 exits do not
//! notice. Firmware idling in HLT, or a kernel booting through thousands of
//! CPUID, MSR and HLT exits, would spend most of its time printing. So each
//! exit gets a [`Detail`] from its [`Level`]:
//!
//! | Exit | Level | Detail in the default build |
//! |---|---|---|
//! | stops the guest, or a VMCS field could not be read | error | in full |
//! | one of the first [`FULL_EXITS_PER_REASON`] of its reason | info | in full |
//! | the 32nd, 64th, 128th, ... of its reason | info | one summary line |
//! | any other | trace | nothing |
//!
//! A build prints the levels up to [`MAX_LEVEL`]: info by default, trace
//! with the `trace-exits` Cargo feature, which prints every exit in full.
//! An NMI that arrived while Aleph0 ran is always printed, whatever the
//! exit's detail. Every stop also prints how many exits of each reason there
//! were ([`Histogram`]), so the exits left out still show in the totals.

use core::fmt;

use crate::vmx::exit_decision::exit_reason_name;

/// How much a report line matters.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Level {
    /// The guest stops, or Aleph0 could not read what it needed.
    Error,
    /// What exits did, within the rate limit.
    Info,
    /// Every exit, in full.
    Trace,
}

/// The most detailed level this build prints: trace with the `trace-exits`
/// Cargo feature, info otherwise. Nothing can set a level at run time yet.
pub const MAX_LEVEL: Level = if cfg!(feature = "trace-exits") {
    Level::Trace
} else {
    Level::Info
};

/// Exits of one reason printed in full before the rate limit starts. Each
/// reason in the test guest's run stays well under it (four I/O exits at
/// most), so its exits print exactly as before.
pub const FULL_EXITS_PER_REASON: u64 = 16;

/// How much of one exit is printed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Detail {
    /// Every line: what was read, what it turned out to be, what was done.
    Full,
    /// One line: the exit's number and reason, and how many there were.
    Summary,
    /// Nothing.
    Silent,
}

/// How much of an exit to print: exit `count` of its reason (1 for the
/// first), which `stops` the guest or not, with an `unreadable` VMCS field or
/// not, in a build that prints up to `max_level` ([`MAX_LEVEL`]).
pub fn exit_detail(count: u64, stops: bool, unreadable: bool, max_level: Level) -> Detail {
    let level = if stops || unreadable {
        Level::Error
    } else if count <= FULL_EXITS_PER_REASON {
        Level::Info
    } else {
        Level::Trace
    };
    if level <= max_level {
        Detail::Full
    } else if count.is_power_of_two() && Level::Info <= max_level {
        Detail::Summary
    } else {
        Detail::Silent
    }
}

/// Basic exit reasons with a counter of their own: 0 to 127, well past the
/// highest the SDM defines.
pub const REASON_COUNTERS: usize = 128;
/// The counter every other reason shares: one past the SDM's, or
/// `UNREADABLE_REASON` (`0xFFFF`) when VM_EXIT_REASON could not be read.
pub const OTHER_REASONS: usize = REASON_COUNTERS;
/// Counters in all.
pub const COUNTERS: usize = REASON_COUNTERS + 1;

/// The counter of basic exit reason `basic`. Never past the last one,
/// whatever `basic` is.
pub fn counter(basic: u16) -> usize {
    usize::from(basic).min(OTHER_REASONS)
}

/// The exit counts by reason, as the line every stop prints:
/// `10 (CPUID)=1, 12 (HLT)=1, 18 (VMCALL)=2`, with `other=N` for the shared
/// counter. Reasons without an exit are left out.
pub struct Histogram<'a>(pub &'a [u64; COUNTERS]);

impl fmt::Display for Histogram<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let mut counted = self.0.iter().enumerate().filter(|&(_, &count)| count > 0).peekable();
        if counted.peek().is_none() {
            return f.write_str("none");
        }
        let mut separator = "";
        for (slot, count) in counted {
            if slot == OTHER_REASONS {
                write!(f, "{separator}other={count}")?;
            } else {
                write!(f, "{separator}{slot} ({})={count}", exit_reason_name(slot as u16))?;
            }
            separator = ", ";
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[path = "../../../tests/unit/vmx/vmexit/policy.rs"]
mod tests;
```
