`src/vmx/vmexit/report.rs`:

```rs
//! The VM-exit handler's report lines: what an exit was and what Aleph0 did
//! about it. Kept apart from `handler.rs`, so that file reads as the steps.
//!
//! Like the handler, everything here runs in exit context: only VMREAD and
//! the serial port, never firmware.

use super::guest_mtrrs::{self, MtrrWrite};
use super::handler::{EmulationOutcome, ExitRead, Outcome, Resumed};
use super::policy::{COUNTERS, Detail, Histogram};
use super::stats::Tally;
use super::{RegisterFrame, dump, history, read_field, stats};
use crate::vmx::ept::{Eptp, InveptType, Retyped};
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::{
    EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG, EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI, EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, EXIT_REASON_VMCALL, EXIT_REASON_WRMSR,
    EptQualification, ExitEvent, ExitInfo, ExitState, InterruptionInfo, PLANNED_MAIN_VMCALLS, exit_reason_name,
    expected_main_rax, wrmsr_value,
};
use crate::vmx::guest::{GUEST_DATA_SEED, GUEST_EPT_VALUE};
use crate::vmx::hyperv;
use crate::vmx::mtrr::{self, FIXED_END, MtrrMsr, Mtrrs};
use crate::vmx::page::PAGE_SIZE;
use crate::vmx::vmcs::fields::{EPT_POINTER, GUEST_LINEAR_ADDRESS};
use crate::vmx::vmcs::{GuestKind, VmcsError};

/// One exit, as its report needs it.
pub(super) struct ExitReport<'a> {
    /// The guest it came from.
    pub(super) guest: GuestKind,
    /// The exit's number, from 1.
    pub(super) number: u64,
    /// How many exits of its reason there have been, this one included.
    pub(super) count: u64,
    /// How much of it the print policy prints.
    pub(super) detail: Detail,
    /// What was read about it.
    pub(super) read: &'a ExitRead,
    /// Whether an NMI arrived in root operation since the last exit.
    pub(super) host_nmi: bool,
    /// What it turned out to be.
    pub(super) event: ExitEvent,
    /// The state after it.
    pub(super) next: ExitState,
    /// What came of it.
    pub(super) outcome: Outcome,
}

/// Prints one exit in as much detail as the print policy gives it: what was
/// read about it, an NMI that arrived in root operation meanwhile, what it
/// turned out to be and what came of it. The NMI is printed whatever the
/// detail.
pub(super) fn report_exit(report: &ExitReport<'_>) {
    let ExitReport {
        guest,
        number,
        count,
        detail,
        read,
        host_nmi,
        event,
        next,
        outcome,
    } = *report;
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    match detail {
        Detail::Full => {}
        Detail::Summary => {
            // Only exits that resume are rate-limited, and only readable
            // ones, so the reason is known here.
            let basic = read.reason().map_or(0, |reason| reason.basic);
            crate::serial_println!(
                "{tag} VM exit #{number}: reason={basic} ({}), {count} exits of this reason so far.",
                exit_reason_name(basic),
            );
            report_forwarded(number, basic);
            if host_nmi {
                report_host_nmi(number);
            }
            return;
        }
        Detail::Silent => {
            if host_nmi {
                report_host_nmi(number);
            }
            return;
        }
    }
    report_read(number, read);
    if host_nmi {
        report_host_nmi(number);
    }
    match outcome {
        Outcome::Resumed { resumed, .. } => report_event(guest, number, event, read.exit, next, Some(resumed)),
        Outcome::ResumeFailed(failure) => {
            crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: {failure}; not resuming.")
        }
        Outcome::Stopped(_) => report_event(guest, number, event, read.exit, next, None),
    }
    if outcome.stops() {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: stopping the guest; {}.", after_stop(guest));
    }
}

/// Where a stop of `guest` goes, for its report line.
pub(super) fn after_stop(guest: GuestKind) -> &'static str {
    if guest.stop_returns_to_bring_up() {
        "returning to bring-up"
    } else {
        "halting: the firmware has nothing to return to"
    }
}

/// Prints what [`ExitRead`] holds: the reason, the qualification, an EPT
/// exit's addresses, RIP and instruction length, RAX to RDX, and every field
/// that could not be read.
fn report_read(number: u64, read: &ExitRead) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    match read.reason() {
        Some(reason) => {
            crate::serial_println!(
                "{tag} VM exit #{number}: reason={} ({}){}",
                reason.basic,
                exit_reason_name(reason.basic),
                if reason.entry_failure {
                    " [VM entry failed; guest did not run]"
                } else {
                    ""
                },
            );
            if reason.basic == EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI
                && !reason.entry_failure
                && let Ok(info) = read.interruption_info
            {
                report_exception(number, InterruptionInfo(info as u32));
            }
        }
        None => report_unreadable(number, "VM_EXIT_REASON", read.reason),
    }
    match read.qualification {
        Ok(qualification) => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: qualification={qualification:#018x}"),
        Err(_) => report_unreadable(number, "EXIT_QUALIFICATION", read.qualification),
    }
    if let (Some(reason), Some(guest_physical)) = (read.reason(), read.guest_physical) {
        match guest_physical {
            Ok(guest_physical) => report_ept_exit(
                number,
                reason.basic,
                EptQualification(read.qualification.unwrap_or(0)),
                guest_physical,
            ),
            Err(_) => report_unreadable(number, "GUEST_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS", guest_physical),
        }
    }
    match (read.rip, read.length) {
        (Ok(rip), Ok(length)) => {
            crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest rip={rip:#018x} instruction length={length}")
        }
        (rip, length) => {
            report_unreadable(number, "GUEST_RIP", rip);
            report_unreadable(number, "VM_EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LEN", length);
        }
    }
    let [rax, rbx, rcx, rdx] = read.registers;
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest rax={rax:#018x} rbx={rbx:#018x} rcx={rcx:#018x} rdx={rdx:#018x}"
    );
    report_unreadable(number, "VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO", read.interruption_info);
    report_unreadable(number, "GUEST_INTERRUPTIBILITY_STATE", read.interruptibility);
    report_unreadable(number, "IDT_VECTORING_INFO", read.idt_vectoring);
    if let Some(rights) = read.ss_access_rights {
        report_unreadable(number, "GUEST_SS_ACCESS_RIGHTS", rights);
    }
}

/// Prints that the VMCS field `name` could not be read at exit `number`, if
/// `value` says so; prints nothing for a value that was read.
fn report_unreadable(number: u64, name: &str, value: Result<u64, VmcsError>) {
    if let Err(error) = value {
        crate::serial_println!("{} VM exit #{number}: {name} unreadable ({error:?})", crate::TAG);
    }
}

/// Prints an EPT exit's addresses and what the EPT entries allowed.
fn report_ept_exit(number: u64, basic: u16, qualification: EptQualification, guest_physical: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    if basic == EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT misconfiguration at GPA {guest_physical:#018x}: an EPT entry for it is invalid."
        );
        return;
    }

    let (r, w, x) = qualification.permissions();
    let access = qualification.access_name();
    // The linear address is only valid with qualification bit 7, and only
    // the report needs it, so it is read here.
    match qualification.linear_valid().then(|| read_field(GUEST_LINEAR_ADDRESS)) {
        Some(Ok(linear)) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT violation at GPA {guest_physical:#018x} (linear {linear:#018x}): {access}; page R={r} W={w} X={x}."
        ),
        Some(Err(error)) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT violation at GPA {guest_physical:#018x} (linear address unreadable: {error:?}): {access}; page R={r} W={w} X={x}."
        ),
        None => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT violation at GPA {guest_physical:#018x} (no linear address): {access}; page R={r} W={w} X={x}."
        ),
    }
}

/// Prints the walk of `gpa` through the EPT tables EPT_POINTER names: each
/// entry on its path, what the CPU refuses in it, and how the walk ended
/// (`ept::walk`), as KVM prints the hierarchy of an EPT entry with reserved
/// bits set. The walk reads only Aleph0's own table pages.
fn report_ept_walk(number: u64, gpa: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    let eptp = match read_field(EPT_POINTER) {
        Ok(raw) => Eptp::from_raw(raw),
        Err(error) => {
            crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT_POINTER unreadable ({error:?}); no EPT walk.");
            return;
        }
    };
    let Some(walk) = guest_mtrrs::inspect(|_, tables| tables.walk(eptp, gpa)) else {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: the EPT tables are not available; no EPT walk.");
        return;
    };
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT walk of GPA {gpa:#018x} from EPTP {:#x}:",
        eptp.raw()
    );
    for entry in walk.entries() {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}:   {} entry {:#x} at {:#x} = {:#018x}: {}",
            entry.level.name(),
            entry.index,
            entry.address,
            entry.raw,
            entry.faults,
        );
    }
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}:   {}.", walk.end);
}

/// Prints that an NMI arrived while Aleph0 ran in root operation, and is
/// now pending for the guest. Not "resuming the guest": that text arms
/// `run-hyperv.ps1 -InjectNmi`.
fn report_host_nmi(number: u64) {
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{} VM exit #{number}: an NMI arrived while Aleph0 ran in root operation ({} so far); pending for the guest.",
        crate::TAG,
        crate::vmx::host::nmis_taken(),
    );
}

/// Prints, after the summary line of exit `number`, what Aleph0 forwarded
/// to Hyper-V so far at exits of its reason `basic`: hypercalls by call code
/// for VMCALL, synthetic MSRs for RDMSR and WRMSR. Nothing when none was,
/// or for another reason.
fn report_forwarded(number: u64, basic: u16) {
    let forwarded = stats::forwarded();
    let (what, tally) = match basic {
        EXIT_REASON_VMCALL => ("hypercalls by call code", forwarded.hypercalls),
        EXIT_REASON_RDMSR => ("synthetic MSR reads", forwarded.synthetic_reads),
        EXIT_REASON_WRMSR => ("synthetic MSR writes", forwarded.synthetic_writes),
        _ => return,
    };
    if tally != Tally::EMPTY {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{} VM exit #{number}: forwarded to Hyper-V so far: {what}: {tally}.",
            crate::TAG
        );
    }
}

/// Prints what every stop adds after the lines of exit `number`: the
/// guest's state and registers (`frame`), the vCPU's exit statistics with
/// what was forwarded to Hyper-V, how many exits of each reason there were
/// (`exits_by_reason`), including those the print policy left out, and the
/// last exits, oldest first.
pub(super) fn report_stop(number: u64, frame: &RegisterFrame, exits_by_reason: &[u64; COUNTERS]) {
    dump::report_guest(number, frame);
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: exit statistics: {}.", stats::snapshot());
    let forwarded = stats::forwarded();
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: forwarded to Hyper-V: hypercalls by call code: {}; synthetic MSR reads: {}; synthetic MSR writes: {}.",
        forwarded.hypercalls,
        forwarded.synthetic_reads,
        forwarded.synthetic_writes,
    );
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{} VM exit #{number}: exits by reason: {}.",
        crate::TAG,
        Histogram(exits_by_reason)
    );
    history::report(format_args!("VM exit #{number}"));
}

/// Prints what exit `number` of `guest` turned out to be and what Aleph0
/// does about it. `state` is the state after the exit; `resumed` is how the
/// guest goes on, for events that resume it.
fn report_event(
    guest: GuestKind,
    number: u64,
    event: ExitEvent,
    exit: Option<ExitInfo>,
    state: ExitState,
    resumed: Option<Resumed>,
) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    let rax = exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_rax);
    let rcx = exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_rcx);
    let rip = resumed.map_or(0, |resumed| resumed.rip);
    let nmis_injected = stats::snapshot().nmi_injections;
    match event {
        ExitEvent::EptWriteGranted => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: write to the protected data page: write granted (W=1), INVEPT {}; retrying the write at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            resumed
                .and_then(|resumed| resumed.invept)
                .map_or("not run", InveptType::name),
        ),
        ExitEvent::DataPageMismatch => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: the data page read back rcx={:#x} rdx={:#x}, expected {GUEST_DATA_SEED:#x} and {GUEST_EPT_VALUE:#x}.",
            exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_rcx),
            exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_rdx),
        ),
        ExitEvent::EptWriteMissing => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: main VMCALL (rax={rax:#x}) before any EPT violation: the guest's write to its data page was not caught, so EPT did not protect it."
        ),
        ExitEvent::EptViolation => {
            crate::serial_println!(
                "{tag} VM exit #{number}: an EPT violation Aleph0 does not handle: only the guest's first write to its protected data page is one; the map is wrong for this GPA."
            );
            report_ept_walk(number, exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_physical));
        }
        // The read's line already says an entry is invalid; the walk says
        // which.
        ExitEvent::EptMisconfig => report_ept_walk(number, exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_physical)),
        ExitEvent::MainVmcall => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: expected VMCALL (rax={rax:#x}); resuming the guest at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        ExitEvent::GuestNmiHandler => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest NMI handler ran (rax={rax:#x}); the reinjected NMI was delivered; resuming the guest at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        ExitEvent::NmiInjected => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: NMI (interruption info={:#010x}); reinjecting it into the guest at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.interruption_info.0),
        ),
        ExitEvent::NmiDeferred => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: NMI cannot be injected yet (interruptibility={:#x}); waiting for the NMI window.",
            exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.interruptibility),
        ),
        ExitEvent::NmiWindowInjected => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: NMI window open; reinjecting the pending NMI at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall if nmis_injected == 0 && state.nmis_handled == 0 && !state.nmi_pending => {
            crate::serial_println!(
                "{tag} VM exit #{number}: expected VMCALL (rax={rax:#x}); all {PLANNED_MAIN_VMCALLS} planned VMCALLs handled; no NMI arrived."
            )
        }
        ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: expected VMCALL (rax={rax:#x}); all {PLANNED_MAIN_VMCALLS} planned VMCALLs handled; NMIs: {nmis_injected} reinjected, {} handled by the guest{}.",
            state.nmis_handled,
            // An NMI deferred but never injected before the last VMCALL.
            if state.nmi_pending {
                ", 1 still pending (dropped)"
            } else {
                ""
            },
        ),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(_) => report_emulation(number, resumed.and_then(|resumed| resumed.emulated), rip),
        ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection => report_general_protection(number, exit, rip),
        // Not "resuming the guest": `run-hyperv.ps1 -InjectNmi` waits for
        // that text after main VMCALL #1, and this exit comes before it.
        ExitEvent::Halted => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: HLT; going on at rip={rip:#018x}."),
        ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode => report_invalid_opcode(number, exit, rip),
        ExitEvent::BootServicesEnded => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: VMCALL from Aleph0's ExitBootServices event (rcx={rcx:#x}): boot services are over; output phase now runtime (serial only); going on at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        ExitEvent::TestVmcall => {
            crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: test VMCALL (rcx={rcx:#x}); going on at rip={rip:#018x}.")
        }
        ExitEvent::Unexpected if guest == GuestKind::BuiltInTest => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: NOT an expected exit (the next main VMCALL should have rax={:#x}).",
            expected_main_rax(state),
        ),
        // The firmware has no script: the lines above name the exit.
        ExitEvent::Unexpected => {
            crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: NOT an exit Aleph0 handles for the firmware.")
        }
    }
    if event == ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT: {} write violation(s) on the protected data page, write granted.",
            state.ept_writes_granted,
        );
    }
}

/// Prints what an emulated instruction did and where the guest resumes.
fn report_emulation(number: u64, outcome: Option<EmulationOutcome>, rip: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    match outcome {
        Some(EmulationOutcome::Cpuid {
            leaf,
            subleaf,
            raw,
            guest,
        }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: CPUID leaf={leaf:#x} subleaf={subleaf:#x} -> eax={:#010x} ebx={:#010x} ecx={:#010x} edx={:#010x} (processor ecx={:#010x}); resuming at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            guest.eax,
            guest.ebx,
            guest.ecx,
            guest.edx,
            raw.ecx,
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::Rdmsr { msr, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: RDMSR {msr:#x} -> {value:#018x}; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::Wrmsr { msr, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: WRMSR {msr:#x} <- {value:#018x}; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::MtrrRead { msr, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: RDMSR {:#x} ({msr}) -> {value:#018x}, from the guest's MTRRs; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            msr.address(),
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::MtrrWrite {
            msr,
            value,
            cpu_value,
            write,
        }) => report_mtrr_write(number, msr, value, cpu_value, write, rip),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::In { port, size, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: IN port {port:#x} size={} -> {value:#x}; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            size.bytes(),
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::Out { port, size, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: OUT port {port:#x} size={} value={value:#x}; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            size.bytes(),
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::Hypercall { input, result }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: hypercall {:#06x} (rcx={input:#x}) forwarded to Hyper-V -> status {:#x} (rax={result:#x}); resuming at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            hyperv::call_code(input),
            result as u16,
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::SyntheticRead { msr, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: RDMSR {msr:#x} (synthetic) forwarded to Hyper-V -> {value:#018x}; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::SyntheticWrite { msr, value }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: WRMSR {msr:#x} (synthetic) <- {value:#018x} forwarded to Hyper-V; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        Some(EmulationOutcome::Refused { emulation, exception }) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: Hyper-V refused the forwarded {emulation:?} with {}; injecting it at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            exception_mnemonic(exception),
        ),
        None => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: emulated instruction not executed."),
    }
}

/// `#UD` or `#GP(0)`, the exceptions a forwarded access is refused with.
fn exception_mnemonic(exception: InterruptionInfo) -> &'static str {
    if exception == InterruptionInfo::INVALID_OPCODE {
        "#UD"
    } else {
        "#GP(0)"
    }
}

/// Prints why the guest gets #UD: for a VMCALL, that it came from CPL > 0
/// or that there is no Hyper-V to take it; otherwise, that it is MWAIT or
/// MONITOR.
fn report_invalid_opcode(number: u64, exit: Option<ExitInfo>, rip: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    match exit.filter(|exit| exit.reason.basic == EXIT_REASON_VMCALL) {
        Some(exit) if exit.guest_cpl != 0 => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: VMCALL (rcx={:#x}) from CPL {}, which Hyper-V refuses too; injecting #UD at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            exit.guest_rcx,
            exit.guest_cpl,
        ),
        Some(exit) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: VMCALL (rcx={:#x}) is not Aleph0's, and there is no Hyper-V interface to forward it to; injecting #UD at rip={rip:#018x}.",
            exit.guest_rcx,
        ),
        None => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: MWAIT or MONITOR, which the guest's CPUID does not offer; injecting #UD at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
    }
}

/// Prints why the guest gets a #GP at its RDMSR or WRMSR: for a WRMSR of
/// one of its MTRRs, what the CPU refuses in the value; for an MTRR address
/// the CPU has no MSR at, that; otherwise, that the MSR is outside the MSR
/// bitmap or the value is not canonical.
fn report_general_protection(number: u64, exit: Option<ExitInfo>, rip: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    let msr = exit.map_or(0, |exit| exit.guest_rcx as u32);
    let refused_mtrr = exit
        .filter(|exit| exit.reason.basic == EXIT_REASON_WRMSR)
        .and_then(|exit| {
            let mtrr = exit.mtrr.msr(msr)?;
            let value = wrmsr_value(&exit);
            exit.mtrr.check(mtrr, value).err().map(|error| (mtrr, value, error))
        });
    let absent_mtrr = exit.is_some_and(|exit| mtrr::is_msr_address(msr) && exit.mtrr.msr(msr).is_none());
    match refused_mtrr {
        Some((mtrr, value, error)) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: WRMSR {msr:#x} ({mtrr}) <- {value:#018x} refused: {error}; the guest's MTRRs unchanged; injecting #GP(0) at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        None if absent_mtrr => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: MSR {msr:#x} is an MTRR address this CPU has no MSR at (see IA32_MTRRCAP); injecting #GP(0) at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        None => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: MSR {msr:#x} is outside the MSR bitmap, or the WRMSR value is not canonical; injecting #GP(0) at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
    }
}

/// Prints a WRMSR of the guest's MTRRs: the write, beside the CPU's own
/// MSR, which keeps its value; then, if the types changed, the guest's
/// MTRRs as they now stand and the EPT regions that changed, read back from
/// the PD entries.
fn report_mtrr_write(number: u64, msr: MtrrMsr, value: u64, cpu_value: u64, write: MtrrWrite, rip: u64) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    crate::serial_println!(
        "{tag} VM exit #{number}: WRMSR {:#x} ({msr}) <- {value:#018x}, into the guest's MTRRs; the CPU's {msr} stays {cpu_value:#018x}.",
        msr.address(),
    );
    match write.retyped {
        None => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: every address keeps its memory type; EPT unchanged; resuming at rip={rip:#018x}."
        ),
        Some(retyped) => {
            guest_mtrrs::inspect(|mtrrs, types| {
                report_guest_mtrrs(number, mtrrs, msr.is_fixed());
                report_retyped(number, &retyped, write.invept, types.free_pts());
                if let Some((start, end)) = retyped.span {
                    for run in types.region_runs(start, end) {
                        crate::serial_println!(
                            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT {:#014x}..{:#014x}: {}",
                            run.start,
                            run.end,
                            run.mapping
                        );
                    }
                }
            });
            crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: resuming at rip={rip:#018x}.");
        }
    }
}

/// Prints the guest's MTRRs as bring-up prints the CPU's: whether they are
/// on, the variable ranges in use, and, after a write to a fixed-range MSR
/// (`fixed_written`), the types of the first MiB.
fn report_guest_mtrrs(number: u64, mtrrs: &Mtrrs, fixed_written: bool) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest MTRRs: {mtrrs}.");
    let Mtrrs::Enabled(enabled) = mtrrs else {
        return;
    };
    for range in enabled.variable_ranges() {
        crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest MTRR {range}");
    }
    if fixed_written && enabled.fixed_enabled() {
        for run in mtrrs.runs(FIXED_END, PAGE_SIZE as u64) {
            crate::serial_println!(
                "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest MTRR fixed {:#07x}..{:#07x}: {}",
                run.start,
                run.end,
                run.type_name(),
            );
        }
    }
}

/// Prints what changed in EPT after the guest's MTRRs did, and the spare
/// PTs `free_pts` left.
fn report_retyped(number: u64, retyped: &Retyped, invept: Option<InveptType>, free_pts: usize) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    match invept {
        Some(invept) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT: {} region(s) retyped ({} split into a spare PT, {} merged back into one 2 MiB page); {free_pts} spare PT(s) left; INVEPT {}.",
            retyped.regions,
            retyped.split,
            retyped.merged,
            invept.name(),
        ),
        None => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT unchanged: the types changed only where nothing is mapped."
        ),
    }
    if retyped.uncached > 0 {
        crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: EPT: {} region(s) of mixed types mapped UC as one page: no spare PT left.",
            retyped.uncached,
        );
    }
}

/// Prints the vector of an exception exit, from its VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO
/// `info`. Exit qualification, printed by the caller, holds the faulting
/// address for a page fault (#PF, vector 14). NMI exits share reason 0 but
/// are not exceptions; the event line printed later reports them.
fn report_exception(number: u64, info: InterruptionInfo) {
    let tag = crate::TAG;
    if info.is_nmi() {
        return;
    }
    let raw = info.0;
    match info.vector() {
        Some(vector) => crate::serial_println!(
            "{tag} VM exit #{number}: guest exception vector={vector} (interruption info={raw:#010x})"
        ),
        None => crate::serial_println!("{tag} VM exit #{number}: interruption info not valid ({raw:#010x})"),
    }
}
```

`src/vmx/vmexit/stats.rs`:

```rs
//! Per-vCPU exit statistics, kept the way KVM keeps `struct kvm_vcpu_stat`:
//! plain counters that the exit handler bumps in one place, for any guest,
//! and that no decision ever reads. `exit_decision::decide` says what an exit
//! is; these count what Aleph0 then did about it.
//!
//! Every stop prints them, before the exits by reason (`policy::Histogram`).
//! Once the test guest has finished, bring-up compares them with what that
//! guest does (`guest::expected_stats`), as a KVM selftest checks a vCPU's
//! statistics after its run.
//!
//! What was forwarded to Hyper-V, by call code and by MSR, is counted beside
//! them ([`Forwarded`]), so the counters bring-up compares and carries in an
//! error stay a few words.

use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::fmt;

use crate::vmx::exit_decision::{Emulation, ExitEvent, ResumePlan};
use crate::vmx::hyperv;

/// One vCPU's exit statistics. Each counter is a `u64`: at a billion exits a
/// second, one would take over 500 years to overflow.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VcpuStats {
    /// Every VM exit, handled or not.
    pub exits: u64,
    /// CPUIDs executed for the guest.
    pub cpuid_exits: u64,
    /// RDMSRs executed for the guest.
    pub msr_read_exits: u64,
    /// WRMSRs executed for the guest.
    pub msr_write_exits: u64,
    /// RDMSRs of the guest's MTRRs, answered from its copy.
    pub mtrr_read_exits: u64,
    /// WRMSRs of the guest's MTRRs, written to its copy.
    pub mtrr_write_exits: u64,
    /// INs executed for the guest.
    pub io_in_exits: u64,
    /// OUTs executed for the guest.
    pub io_out_exits: u64,
    /// HLTs the guest was resumed past.
    pub halt_exits: u64,
    /// NMIs injected into the guest.
    pub nmi_injections: u64,
    /// Exceptions injected into the guest (#GP, #UD), those Hyper-V raised
    /// for a forwarded access included.
    pub exception_injections: u64,
    /// Hypercalls forwarded to Hyper-V, refused ones included.
    pub hypercall_exits: u64,
    /// RDMSRs of synthetic MSRs forwarded to Hyper-V, refused ones included.
    pub synthetic_read_exits: u64,
    /// WRMSRs of synthetic MSRs forwarded to Hyper-V, refused ones included.
    pub synthetic_write_exits: u64,
}

impl VcpuStats {
    /// No exit yet.
    pub const ZERO: Self = Self {
        exits: 0,
        cpuid_exits: 0,
        msr_read_exits: 0,
        msr_write_exits: 0,
        mtrr_read_exits: 0,
        mtrr_write_exits: 0,
        io_in_exits: 0,
        io_out_exits: 0,
        halt_exits: 0,
        nmi_injections: 0,
        exception_injections: 0,
        hypercall_exits: 0,
        synthetic_read_exits: 0,
        synthetic_write_exits: 0,
    };

    /// Counts one more exit and returns its number, from 1.
    pub fn count_exit(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.exits += 1;
        self.exits
    }

    /// Counts what Aleph0 did at an exit it resumed from: `event`, carried
    /// out as `plan`. An exit that stops the guest counts in `exits` only,
    /// since what its plan would have done never happened.
    pub fn count_resumed(&mut self, event: ExitEvent, plan: ResumePlan) {
        match plan.emulate {
            Some(Emulation::Cpuid { .. }) => self.cpuid_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::Rdmsr { .. }) => self.msr_read_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::Wrmsr { .. }) => self.msr_write_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::MtrrRead { .. }) => self.mtrr_read_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::MtrrWrite { .. }) => self.mtrr_write_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::In { .. }) => self.io_in_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::Out { .. }) => self.io_out_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::Hypercall { .. }) => self.hypercall_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::SyntheticRead { .. }) => self.synthetic_read_exits += 1,
            Some(Emulation::SyntheticWrite { .. }) => self.synthetic_write_exits += 1,
            None => {}
        }
        // HLT resumes past the instruction like a VMCALL does, so only the
        // event tells it apart.
        if event == ExitEvent::Halted {
            self.halt_exits += 1;
        }
        if plan.inject_nmi {
            self.nmi_injections += 1;
        }
        if plan.inject_exception.is_some() {
            self.exception_injections += 1;
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for VcpuStats {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let Self {
            exits,
            cpuid_exits,
            msr_read_exits,
            msr_write_exits,
            mtrr_read_exits,
            mtrr_write_exits,
            io_in_exits,
            io_out_exits,
            halt_exits,
            nmi_injections,
            exception_injections,
            hypercall_exits,
            synthetic_read_exits,
            synthetic_write_exits,
        } = self;
        write!(
            f,
            "exits={exits} cpuid_exits={cpuid_exits} msr_read_exits={msr_read_exits} \
             msr_write_exits={msr_write_exits} mtrr_read_exits={mtrr_read_exits} \
             mtrr_write_exits={mtrr_write_exits} io_in_exits={io_in_exits} io_out_exits={io_out_exits} \
             halt_exits={halt_exits} nmi_injections={nmi_injections} exception_injections={exception_injections} \
             hypercall_exits={hypercall_exits} synthetic_read_exits={synthetic_read_exits} \
             synthetic_write_exits={synthetic_write_exits}"
        )
    }
}

/// What Aleph0 forwarded to Hyper-V at the exits it resumed from, refused
/// accesses included, as KVM's Hyper-V code counts hypercalls by code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Forwarded {
    /// Hypercalls by call code (RCX bits 15:0).
    pub hypercalls: Tally,
    /// RDMSRs of synthetic MSRs by MSR.
    pub synthetic_reads: Tally,
    /// WRMSRs of synthetic MSRs by MSR.
    pub synthetic_writes: Tally,
}

impl Forwarded {
    /// Nothing forwarded yet.
    pub const NONE: Self = Self {
        hypercalls: Tally::EMPTY,
        synthetic_reads: Tally::EMPTY,
        synthetic_writes: Tally::EMPTY,
    };

    /// Counts what a resumed exit's plan emulated (`emulate`), if it was
    /// forwarded to Hyper-V.
    pub fn count(&mut self, emulate: Option<Emulation>) {
        match emulate {
            Some(Emulation::Hypercall { input }) => self.hypercalls.count(hyperv::call_code(input).into()),
            Some(Emulation::SyntheticRead { msr }) => self.synthetic_reads.count(msr),
            Some(Emulation::SyntheticWrite { msr, .. }) => self.synthetic_writes.count(msr),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

/// Keys a [`Tally`] counts on their own.
pub const TALLY_KEYS: usize = 32;

/// Counts by key, a hypercall's call code or an MSR, for the first
/// [`TALLY_KEYS`] keys seen; later keys share [`Tally::other`]. The
/// firmware's VMBus drivers use a handful of call codes, and a guest with
/// the SynIC writes its 16 SINTx MSRs and a dozen more.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Tally {
    /// `(key, count)`, in the order first seen; the first `len` are used.
    keys: [(u32, u64); TALLY_KEYS],
    len: usize,
    /// Counts of the keys that found no slot.
    pub other: u64,
}

impl Tally {
    /// Nothing counted.
    pub const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        keys: [(0, 0); TALLY_KEYS],
        len: 0,
        other: 0,
    };

    /// Counts one more of `key`.
    pub fn count(&mut self, key: u32) {
        if let Some((_, count)) = self.keys[..self.len].iter_mut().find(|(seen, _)| *seen == key) {
            *count += 1;
        } else if self.len < TALLY_KEYS {
            self.keys[self.len] = (key, 1);
            self.len += 1;
        } else {
            self.other += 1;
        }
    }

    /// The keys counted, with their counts, in the order first seen.
    pub fn counts(&self) -> &[(u32, u64)] {
        &self.keys[..self.len]
    }
}

/// `0x5c=3 0x5d=1`, then `other=N` for the keys without a slot; `none` when
/// nothing was counted.
impl fmt::Display for Tally {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        if *self == Self::EMPTY {
            return f.write_str("none");
        }
        let mut separator = "";
        for (key, count) in self.counts() {
            write!(f, "{separator}{key:#x}={count}")?;
            separator = " ";
        }
        if self.other > 0 {
            write!(f, "{separator}other={}", self.other)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct Stats<T>(UnsafeCell<T>);

// SAFETY: Aleph0 runs one vCPU on one CPU. Only the exit handler writes the
// statistics ([`update`], [`update_forwarded`]), with interrupts off, and
// the host NMI handler never touches them. They are read by that handler
// outside those calls, and by bring-up once the guest has stopped, when no
// exit handler runs.
unsafe impl<T> Sync for Stats<T> {}

static STATS: Stats<VcpuStats> = Stats(UnsafeCell::new(VcpuStats::ZERO));
static FORWARDED: Stats<Forwarded> = Stats(UnsafeCell::new(Forwarded::NONE));

/// Applies `update` to the statistics. For the exit handler only.
pub(super) fn update<R>(update: impl FnOnce(&mut VcpuStats) -> R) -> R {
    // SAFETY: the exit handler is the only writer, and no reader runs while
    // it writes (see `Stats`).
    update(unsafe { &mut *STATS.0.get() })
}

/// Applies `update` to what was forwarded. For the exit handler only.
pub(super) fn update_forwarded(update: impl FnOnce(&mut Forwarded)) {
    // SAFETY: as for `update`.
    update(unsafe { &mut *FORWARDED.0.get() })
}

/// The statistics as they stand.
pub fn snapshot() -> VcpuStats {
    // SAFETY: a reader runs only when the exit handler is not writing (see
    // `Stats`).
    unsafe { *STATS.0.get() }
}

/// What was forwarded so far.
pub fn forwarded() -> Forwarded {
    // SAFETY: as for `snapshot`.
    unsafe { *FORWARDED.0.get() }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "../../../tests/unit/vmx/vmexit/stats.rs"]
mod tests;
```

`src/vmx/vmxon.rs`:

```rs
//! Entering and leaving VMX root operation.
//!
//! [`enter_vmx_root_operation`] checks the region size IA32_VMX_BASIC
//! asks for, allocates the VMXON region (`region::VmxRegion`), sets
//! CR4.VMXE and the CR0/CR4 bits VMX operation fixes, and executes VMXON.
//! [`VmxOperation::leave`] undoes it: VMXOFF, then CR0/CR4 as they were.
//!
//! VMXON takes a memory operand holding the region's physical address,
//! and reports failure through RFLAGS: CF = 1 is VmFailInvalid (bad region,
//! alignment or revision identifier), ZF = 1 is VmFailValid (already in VMX
//! operation, error number 15).
//!
//! The region is resident (`page::RESIDENT_DATA`): the CPU uses it for as
//! long as VMX operation lasts, after `ExitBootServices` too, so the OS must
//! never reclaim it.

use super::cr;
use super::instruction::{VmxFail, vmx_asm};
use super::msr;
use super::page::PAGE_SIZE;
use super::region::VmxRegion;

/// Why entering VMX operation failed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VmxOnError {
    /// UEFI could not provide a page.
    AllocationFailed,
    /// IA32_VMX_BASIC reports a VMX region size outside the allocated page.
    UnsupportedRegionSize,
    /// VMXON reported VmFailInvalid (CF=1).
    VmFailInvalid,
    /// VMXON reported VmFailValid (ZF=1): typically already in VMX operation.
    VmFailValid,
}

impl From<VmxFail> for VmxOnError {
    fn from(fail: VmxFail) -> Self {
        match fail {
            VmxFail::Invalid => Self::VmFailInvalid,
            VmxFail::Valid => Self::VmFailValid,
        }
    }
}

/// VMX root operation, entered by [`enter_vmx_root_operation`]: the VMXON
/// region the CPU uses meanwhile, and CR0/CR4 from before VMXON, which
/// [`VmxOperation::leave`] restores.
///
/// No `Drop`: the region must stay allocated while the CPU is in VMX
/// operation, and leaving should follow a VMCLEAR, which only the owner of
/// the VMCS can do.
pub struct VmxOperation {
    _region: VmxRegion,
    original_cr0: u64,
    original_cr4: u64,
}

impl VmxOperation {
    /// Executes VMXOFF, then restores CR0 and CR4 to their values before
    /// VMXON, which clears CR4.VMXE.
    ///
    /// If VMXOFF fails, the CPU is still in VMX operation, so CR0 and CR4
    /// stay as they are: clearing CR4.VMXE in VMX operation raises #GP, and
    /// CR0 must keep the bits VMX operation fixes.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Every VMCS used on this CPU should be cleared with VMCLEAR first, so
    /// the CPU writes its data back to memory. If one was not (its VMCLEAR
    /// failed), only that VMCS's memory is stale, which is harmless while its
    /// region is never reused. No VMX instruction may run after this
    /// succeeds.
    pub unsafe fn leave(self) -> Result<(), VmxFail> {
        // SAFETY: this value exists only after VMXON succeeded, so the CPU
        // is in VMX root operation; the caller guarantees no VMX instruction
        // follows. CR0/CR4 get back the values the code ran with before
        // VMXON, legal again once VMX operation has ended.
        unsafe {
            vmxoff()?;
            cr::write_cr0(self.original_cr0);
            cr::write_cr4(self.original_cr4);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Forces CR0 and CR4 into the ranges the CPU requires for VMX operation.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The CPU must support VMX (the FIXED MSRs exist only then), and the
/// running code must keep working with the bits VMX operation forces (in
/// practice CR0.PE, CR0.PG, CR0.NE and CR4.VMXE, which UEFI already has, or
/// does not mind).
pub unsafe fn apply_fixed_bits() {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX support, so the FIXED MSRs exist,
    // and that the running code can go on with the bits they force.
    unsafe {
        let cr0 = (cr::read_cr0() | msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_VMX_CR0_FIXED0)) & msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_VMX_CR0_FIXED1);
        let cr4 = (cr::read_cr4() | msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED0)) & msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED1);

        cr::write_cr0(cr0);
        cr::write_cr4(cr4);
    }
}

/// Executes VMXON on `region`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// CR4.VMXE and the fixed CR0/CR4 bits must be set, and `region` must stay
/// allocated for as long as VMX operation lasts.
pub unsafe fn vmxon(region: &VmxRegion) -> Result<(), VmxOnError> {
    // SAFETY: VMXON reads only the 8-byte operand; the caller guarantees the
    // CR0/CR4 state VMXON needs and the region's lifetime.
    Ok(unsafe { vmx_asm!("vmxon [{0}]", in(reg) region.phys_addr_ref()) }?)
}

/// Executes VMXOFF, leaving VMX operation.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The CPU must be in VMX root operation, and no VMX instruction may run
/// after this succeeds.
unsafe fn vmxoff() -> Result<(), VmxFail> {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX root operation, so VMXOFF cannot #UD.
    unsafe { vmx_asm!("vmxoff") }
}

/// The returned [`VmxOperation`] keeps the region allocated for as long as
/// the CPU is in VMX operation, and remembers CR0/CR4 for leaving it.
///
/// If VMXON fails, CR0 and CR4 are restored, so CR4.VMXE is not left set
/// outside VMX operation.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The CPU must support VMX with IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL allowing it outside
/// SMX ([`super::detect`]), and must not be in VMX operation already.
pub unsafe fn enter_vmx_root_operation() -> Result<VmxOperation, VmxOnError> {
    // SAFETY: the caller guarantees VMX support and that this CPU is not
    // in VMX operation yet. CR0/CR4 change only to what VMXON needs, and
    // go back if it fails; the region outlives VMX operation, since
    // `VmxOperation` owns it.
    unsafe {
        let region_size = (msr::rdmsr(msr::IA32_VMX_BASIC) >> 32) & 0x1fff;
        if region_size == 0 || region_size > PAGE_SIZE as u64 {
            return Err(VmxOnError::UnsupportedRegionSize);
        }

        // Allocate before touching CR0/CR4 so VMXON is the only step that
        // can fail with the control registers modified.
        let vmxon_region = VmxRegion::allocate(VmxOnError::AllocationFailed)?;

        let (original_cr0, original_cr4) = (cr::read_cr0(), cr::read_cr4());
        cr::enable_vmxe();
        apply_fixed_bits();
        if let Err(error) = vmxon(&vmxon_region) {
            cr::write_cr0(original_cr0);
            cr::write_cr4(original_cr4);
            return Err(error);
        }
        Ok(VmxOperation {
            _region: vmxon_region,
            original_cr0,
            original_cr4,
        })
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/resident/mod.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

/// Part of the test VM's memory map: the firmware's data, Aleph0's
/// resident pages, free memory up to 2 GiB.
const MAP: [(u64, u64, MemoryType); 3] = [
    (0x7e00_0000, 0x100, MemoryType::BOOT_SERVICES_DATA),
    (0x7e10_0000, 0x20, MemoryType::RUNTIME_SERVICES_DATA),
    (0x7e12_0000, 0x1ee0, MemoryType::CONVENTIONAL),
];

#[test]
fn an_address_has_the_type_of_its_region() {
    let at = |address| memory_type_at(MAP.into_iter(), address);
    assert_eq!(at(0x7e10_0000), Some(MemoryType::RUNTIME_SERVICES_DATA));
    assert_eq!(at(0x7e11_f000), Some(MemoryType::RUNTIME_SERVICES_DATA));
    // The first byte past a region is the next one's.
    assert_eq!(at(0x7e12_0000), Some(MemoryType::CONVENTIONAL));
    assert_eq!(at(0x7e0f_ffff), Some(MemoryType::BOOT_SERVICES_DATA));
}

#[test]
fn an_address_outside_every_region_has_no_type() {
    let at = |address| memory_type_at(MAP.into_iter(), address);
    assert_eq!(at(0x7dff_f000), None);
    assert_eq!(at(0x8000_0000), None);
    // A region whose end would overflow still has its start.
    assert_eq!(
        memory_type_at([(u64::MAX - 0xFFF, u64::MAX, MemoryType::MMIO)].into_iter(), u64::MAX),
        Some(MemoryType::MMIO)
    );
}
```

`tests/unit/resident/pe.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/resident/pe.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

/// Size of the test image: headers, one page with fixups, the table.
const IMAGE_SIZE: usize = 0x3000;
/// Where the PE signature starts.
const SIGNATURE: usize = 0x80;
/// Where the optional header starts.
const OPTIONAL: usize = SIGNATURE + 4 + 20;
/// RVA of the base relocation table.
const TABLE: usize = 0x2000;
/// An address in the image as the linker wrote it, for base 0x1_4000_0000.
const LINKED: u64 = 0x1_4000_1234;

fn put(image: &mut [u8], offset: usize, bytes: &[u8]) {
    image[offset..offset + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
}

/// A loaded PE32+ image whose base relocation table holds one block: page
/// 0x1000, with the given entries. Absolute addresses ([`LINKED`]) sit at
/// 0x1010 and 0x1ff8.
fn image_with(entries: &[u16]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut image = vec![0; IMAGE_SIZE];
    put(&mut image, 0, b"MZ");
    put(&mut image, 0x3C, &(SIGNATURE as u32).to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, SIGNATURE, b"PE\0\0");
    put(&mut image, OPTIONAL, &0x20Bu16.to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, OPTIONAL + 56, &(IMAGE_SIZE as u32).to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, OPTIONAL + 108, &16u32.to_le_bytes());
    let block_size = 8 + 2 * entries.len();
    put(&mut image, OPTIONAL + 152, &(TABLE as u32).to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, OPTIONAL + 156, &(block_size as u32).to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, TABLE, &0x1000u32.to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, TABLE + 4, &(block_size as u32).to_le_bytes());
    for (i, entry) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
        put(&mut image, TABLE + 8 + 2 * i, &entry.to_le_bytes());
    }
    put(&mut image, 0x1010, &LINKED.to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut image, 0x1FF8, &LINKED.to_le_bytes());
    image
}

fn u64_at(image: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes(image[offset..offset + 8].try_into().unwrap())
}

/// DIR64 fixups at page offsets 0x010 and 0xff8, then an ABSOLUTE pad.
const ENTRIES: [u16; 3] = [0xA010, 0xAFF8, 0x0000];

#[test]
fn headers_give_the_image_size_and_the_table() {
    let image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    assert_eq!(
        Headers::parse(&image),
        Ok(Headers {
            size_of_image: IMAGE_SIZE,
            relocations: TABLE..TABLE + 14,
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn every_dir64_fixup_moves_by_the_delta() {
    let mut image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    let table = Headers::parse(&image).unwrap().relocations;
    assert_eq!(relocate(&mut image, table, 0x2000), Ok(2));
    assert_eq!(u64_at(&image, 0x1010), LINKED + 0x2000);
    assert_eq!(u64_at(&image, 0x1FF8), LINKED + 0x2000);
}

#[test]
fn a_copy_below_the_loaded_image_moves_its_addresses_down() {
    // The copy at 0x7e00_0000, the loaded image at 0x7f00_0000: the delta
    // wraps, and adding it subtracts.
    let mut image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    let table = Headers::parse(&image).unwrap().relocations;
    let delta = 0x7e00_0000u64.wrapping_sub(0x7f00_0000);
    relocate(&mut image, table, delta).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(u64_at(&image, 0x1010), LINKED - 0x100_0000);
}

#[test]
fn padding_and_the_rest_of_the_image_stay_as_they_were() {
    let mut image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    let before = image.clone();
    let table = Headers::parse(&image).unwrap().relocations;
    relocate(&mut image, table, 0x1000).unwrap();
    let changed: Vec<usize> = (0..IMAGE_SIZE).filter(|&i| image[i] != before[i]).collect();
    // Only the low bytes of the two addresses: 0x1234 + 0x1000 = 0x2234.
    assert_eq!(changed, [0x1011, 0x1FF9]);
}

#[test]
fn an_image_that_is_not_pe32_plus_is_refused() {
    let mut no_mz = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    no_mz[0] = b'Z';
    let mut pe32 = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    put(&mut pe32, OPTIONAL, &0x10Bu16.to_le_bytes());
    let mut signature_outside = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    put(&mut signature_outside, 0x3C, &0xFFFF_FFF0u32.to_le_bytes());
    for image in [no_mz, pe32, signature_outside, b"MZ".to_vec()] {
        assert_eq!(Headers::parse(&image), Err(PeError::NotPe32Plus));
    }
}

#[test]
fn an_image_without_a_relocation_table_cannot_move() {
    let mut empty = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    put(&mut empty, OPTIONAL + 156, &0u32.to_le_bytes());
    let mut five_directories = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    put(&mut five_directories, OPTIONAL + 108, &5u32.to_le_bytes());
    for image in [empty, five_directories] {
        assert_eq!(Headers::parse(&image), Err(PeError::NoRelocations));
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_table_past_the_image_is_refused() {
    let mut image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    put(&mut image, OPTIONAL + 156, &0x1001u32.to_le_bytes());
    assert_eq!(Headers::parse(&image), Err(PeError::TableOutsideImage));
}

#[test]
fn a_block_that_does_not_fit_its_table_is_refused() {
    // A zeroed table, as if the firmware had not loaded it: size 0.
    for size in [0u32, 7, 13, 16] {
        let mut image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
        put(&mut image, TABLE + 4, &size.to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            relocate(&mut image, TABLE..TABLE + 14, 1),
            Err(PeError::BadBlock { offset: 0 }),
            "block size {size}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_fixup_past_the_image_is_refused() {
    let mut image = image_with(&ENTRIES);
    put(&mut image, TABLE, &0x2FF8u32.to_le_bytes());
    assert_eq!(
        relocate(&mut image, TABLE..TABLE + 14, 1),
        Err(PeError::FixupOutsideImage { rva: 0x3008 })
    );
}

#[test]
fn other_fixup_types_are_refused() {
    // HIGHLOW (3), a 32-bit fixup: never in an x86-64 image.
    let mut image = image_with(&[0x3010, 0x0000]);
    let table = Headers::parse(&image).unwrap().relocations;
    assert_eq!(
        relocate(&mut image, table, 1),
        Err(PeError::UnsupportedFixup { kind: 3, rva: 0x1010 })
    );
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/apic.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::ept::{EPT_READ, EPT_RWX};
use crate::vmx::paging::PageSize;

/// The usual value on the bootstrap processor: base 0xFEE00000, xAPIC mode
/// (EN), BSP.
const XAPIC_BSP: ApicBase = ApicBase(0xFEE0_0900);

#[test]
fn the_mode_follows_en_and_extd() {
    assert_eq!(ApicBase(0xFEE0_0000).mode(), LapicMode::Disabled);
    assert_eq!(ApicBase(0xFEE0_0800).mode(), LapicMode::Xapic);
    assert_eq!(ApicBase(0xFEE0_0C00).mode(), LapicMode::X2apic);
    assert_eq!(ApicBase(0xFEE0_0400).mode(), LapicMode::Invalid);
}

#[test]
fn the_base_address_is_bits_maxphyaddr_to_12() {
    assert_eq!(XAPIC_BSP.address(46), 0xFEE0_0000);
    // A base firmware moved high, then cut at MAXPHYADDR 36.
    let high = ApicBase((1 << 40) | 0x1_2345_6000 | 0x900);
    assert_eq!(high.address(46), (1 << 40) | 0x1_2345_6000);
    assert_eq!(high.address(36), 0x1_2345_6000 & ((1 << 36) - 1));
    assert_eq!(high.address(0), 0);
    assert_eq!(high.address(64), (1 << 40) | 0x1_2345_6000);
}

#[test]
fn the_value_prints_with_its_mode_and_bsp() {
    assert!(XAPIC_BSP.bsp());
    assert_eq!(XAPIC_BSP.to_string(), "0xfee00900 (xAPIC, BSP)");
    assert_eq!(ApicBase(0xFEE0_0C00).to_string(), "0xfee00c00 (x2APIC)");
}

#[test]
fn the_version_range_is_an_integrated_apics() {
    assert!(INTEGRATED_APIC_VERSIONS.contains(&0x14));
    // An 82489DX, and the all-ones of a read that reached nothing.
    assert!(!INTEGRATED_APIC_VERSIONS.contains(&0x01));
    assert!(!INTEGRATED_APIC_VERSIONS.contains(&0xFF));
}

/// The firmware's page tables mapping `physical` there, as `walk_current`
/// gives it.
fn mapped_at(physical: u64) -> Result<Mapping, WalkError> {
    Ok(Mapping {
        physical,
        size: PageSize::Size1G,
        writable: true,
        user: false,
        execute_disable: false,
    })
}

/// EPT mapping the page at `hpa` as `memory_type` with `access`.
fn ept(hpa: u64, access: u64, memory_type: MemoryType) -> WalkEnd {
    WalkEnd::Mapped {
        hpa,
        size: 1 << 30,
        access,
        memory_type,
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_registers_are_readable_through_identity_maps_and_uc() {
    let base = 0xFEE0_0000;
    assert_eq!(
        check_registers(base, mapped_at(base), ept(base, EPT_RWX, MemoryType::Uncacheable)),
        Ok(())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        check_registers(base, mapped_at(base), ept(base, EPT_READ, MemoryType::Uncacheable)),
        Ok(())
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_guests_page_tables_must_map_the_registers_to_themselves() {
    let base = 0xFEE0_0000;
    let uc = ept(base, EPT_RWX, MemoryType::Uncacheable);
    let unmapped = Err(WalkError::NotPresent { level: 3 });
    assert_eq!(
        check_registers(base, unmapped, uc),
        Err(LocalApicError::GuestMapping {
            address: base,
            translation: unmapped
        })
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        check_registers(base, mapped_at(0x8000_0000), uc),
        Err(LocalApicError::GuestMapping { .. })
    ));
}

#[test]
fn ept_must_map_the_registers_to_themselves_uc_and_readable() {
    let base = 0xFEE0_0000;
    for end in [
        WalkEnd::NotPresent,
        WalkEnd::Misconfigured,
        ept(base, EPT_RWX, MemoryType::WriteBack),
        ept(0x8000_0000, EPT_RWX, MemoryType::Uncacheable),
        ept(base, 0, MemoryType::Uncacheable),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            check_registers(base, mapped_at(base), end),
            Err(LocalApicError::EptMapping { address: base, end }),
            "{end:?}"
        );
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/context_tables.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its

use super::*;

/// Base with a distinct byte in every position, so a byte landing in the
/// wrong field is caught.
const BASE: u64 = 0x1122_3344_5566_7788;

#[test]
fn tss_descriptor_layout() {
    let descriptor = tss_descriptor(BASE, 0x67);
    assert_eq!(
        descriptor,
        [
            0x67, 0x00, 0x88, 0x77, 0x66, 0x89, 0x00, 0x55, 0x44, 0x33, 0x22, 0x11, 0, 0, 0, 0
        ],
    );
}

#[test]
fn tss_descriptor_limit_high_bits() {
    let descriptor = tss_descriptor(0, 0xA_BCDE);
    assert_eq!(&descriptor[0..2], &[0xDE, 0xBC]);
    assert_eq!(descriptor[6], 0x0A, "limit 19:16 in the low nibble, flags clear");
}

#[test]
fn tss_descriptor_round_trips_through_gdt_decoder() {
    // Null descriptor, one code descriptor, then the 16-byte TSS at 0x10.
    let mut gdt = [0u8; 32];
    gdt[8..16].copy_from_slice(&0x00AF_9B00_0000_FFFFu64.to_le_bytes());
    gdt[16..32].copy_from_slice(&tss_descriptor(BASE, 0x67));
    let table = DescriptorTable {
        base: gdt.as_ptr() as u64,
        limit: gdt.len() as u16 - 1,
    };

    // SAFETY: `table` describes `gdt`, a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { segment_base_from_gdt(&table, 0x10) }, BASE);
}

#[test]
fn tss_holds_its_interrupt_stacks_and_no_io_bitmap() {
    let tss = Tss::new([0x1000, 0x2000, 0x3000, 0, 0, 0, 0x7000]);
    // Fields of a packed struct are copied out before comparing.
    assert_eq!(({ tss.ist1 }, { tss.ist2 }, { tss.ist3 }), (0x1000, 0x2000, 0x3000));
    assert_eq!(({ tss.ist4 }, { tss.ist7 }), (0, 0x7000));
    assert_eq!(({ tss.rsp0 }, { tss.rsp1 }, { tss.rsp2 }), (0, 0, 0));
    // The I/O map starts past the limit: no I/O permission bitmap.
    assert_eq!({ tss.iomap_base }, 0x68);
}
```
