`tests/unit/vmx/exit_decision.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/exit_decision/mod.rs`: the shared types, the
//! dispatch, and through `decide` the handlers in `scenario.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::scenario::{BLOCKING_BY_MOV_SS, BLOCKING_BY_NMI, BLOCKING_BY_STI};
use super::*;
use crate::vmx::guest::{
    GUEST_DATA_SEED, GUEST_EPT_VALUE, GUEST_IO_VALUE, GUEST_MARKER, GUEST_MSR_VALUE, GUEST_MTRR_BASE, GUEST_NMI_MARKER,
    GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT, expected_stats,
};
use crate::vmx::mtrr::MtrrCapabilities;
use crate::vmx::vmexit::VcpuStats;

const MARKER: u64 = GUEST_MARKER as u64;
const NMI_MARKER: u64 = GUEST_NMI_MARKER as u64;
/// VM_EXIT_INTERRUPTION_INFO of an NMI exit.
const NMI_INFO: InterruptionInfo = InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0202);

/// After the guest's emulated exits, before the EPT violation: the state the
/// scenario's own exits start from.
const START: ExitState = ExitState {
    main_vmcalls: 0,
    nmi_pending: false,
    nmis_handled: 0,
    ept_writes_granted: 0,
};
/// After the EPT violation: the data page is writable, main VMCALL #1 next.
const WRITTEN: ExitState = ExitState {
    ept_writes_granted: 1,
    ..START
};
/// After main VMCALL #1: the guest is in its wait loop.
const WAITING: ExitState = ExitState {
    main_vmcalls: 1,
    ..WRITTEN
};

/// GPA of the guest's read-only data page.
const PROTECTED_PAGE: u64 = 0x7eb1_d000;
/// Exit qualification of the guest's write to it: a write (bit 1) to a page
/// that is readable (bit 3) but not writable or executable, through the
/// guest's linear address (bits 7 and 8). Hyper-V and bare metal may set
/// other bits; only these matter.
const PROTECTED_WRITE: u64 = 0x18A;
/// A page fault: hardware exception (type 3), error code valid, vector 14.
const PAGE_FAULT_INFO: u32 = 0x8000_0B0E;

fn exit(basic: u16) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        reason: ExitReason {
            basic,
            entry_failure: false,
        },
        interruption_info: InterruptionInfo(0),
        guest_rax: 0,
        // What the guest holds at main VMCALL #1 when its data page behaved.
        guest_rcx: GUEST_DATA_SEED.into(),
        guest_rdx: GUEST_EPT_VALUE.into(),
        interruptibility: 0,
        idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(0),
        idt_vectoring_error_code: 0,
        qualification: 0,
        guest_physical: 0,
        protected_page: PROTECTED_PAGE,
        mtrr: MtrrCapabilities::NONE,
        hyperv: false,
        guest_cpl: 0,
    }
}

/// An EPT violation at `gpa` with exit qualification `qualification`.
fn ept_violation(gpa: u64, qualification: u64) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        guest_physical: gpa,
        qualification,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_EPT_VIOLATION)
    }
}

/// The guest's write to its data page, 4 bytes in (any offset counts).
fn protected_write() -> ExitInfo {
    ept_violation(PROTECTED_PAGE + 4, PROTECTED_WRITE)
}

fn vmcall(rax: u64) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        guest_rax: rax,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_VMCALL)
    }
}

/// A VMCALL of the firmware or the OS, with `rcx` in RCX, from CPL 0, under
/// Hyper-V.
fn hypercall(rcx: u64) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        guest_rcx: rcx,
        hyperv: true,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_VMCALL)
    }
}

fn nmi(interruptibility: u32) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        interruption_info: NMI_INFO,
        interruptibility,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI)
    }
}

#[test]
fn injected_nmi_is_valid_type_2_vector_2() {
    assert_eq!(InterruptionInfo::NMI, InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0202));
}

#[test]
fn nmi_info_is_recognised() {
    assert!(InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0202).is_nmi());
    // Bit 12 (NMI unblocking due to IRET) does not change what it is.
    assert!(InterruptionInfo(0x8000_1202).is_nmi());
}

#[test]
fn exceptions_and_invalid_info_are_not_nmis() {
    assert!(!InterruptionInfo(PAGE_FAULT_INFO).is_nmi());
    // NMI bits without the valid bit.
    assert!(!InterruptionInfo(0x0000_0202).is_nmi());
    // Right vector, wrong type: hardware exception (type 3), vector 2.
    assert!(!InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0302).is_nmi());
    // Right type, wrong vector: NMI type, vector 3.
    assert!(!InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0203).is_nmi());
}

#[test]
fn interruption_info_validity_is_bit_31() {
    assert!(InterruptionInfo(PAGE_FAULT_INFO).is_valid());
    assert!(!InterruptionInfo(PAGE_FAULT_INFO & !InterruptionInfo::VALID).is_valid());
}

#[test]
fn ept_qualification_flags_decode() {
    let write = EptQualification(PROTECTED_WRITE);
    assert!(write.is_write());
    assert!(write.linear_valid());
    assert!(write.is_protected_write());
    let read = EptQualification(EPT_ACCESS_READ | EPT_PAGE_READABLE);
    assert!(!read.is_write());
    assert!(!read.linear_valid());
    assert!(!read.is_protected_write());
}

#[test]
fn protected_write_qualification_matches_its_bits() {
    assert_eq!(
        PROTECTED_WRITE,
        EPT_ACCESS_WRITE | EPT_PAGE_READABLE | EPT_LINEAR_VALID | EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS
    );
}

#[test]
fn write_to_the_protected_page_is_granted() {
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, protected_write()),
        (ExitEvent::EptWriteGranted, WRITTEN)
    );
}

#[test]
fn write_to_another_page_stops_with_the_violation() {
    let elsewhere = ept_violation(PROTECTED_PAGE + 0x1000, PROTECTED_WRITE);
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, elsewhere),
        (ExitEvent::EptViolation, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_violation_on_a_device_page_stops_with_the_violation() {
    // The Local APIC's version register: EPT maps it, so a violation there
    // means the map is wrong.
    let read = EPT_ACCESS_READ | EPT_LINEAR_VALID | EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS;
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, ept_violation(0xFEE0_0030, read)),
        (ExitEvent::EptViolation, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn violation_with_nothing_protected_stops_with_the_violation() {
    // Before Ept::build the protected page is 0, and GPA 0 must not match.
    let unprotected = ExitInfo {
        protected_page: 0,
        ..ept_violation(0, PROTECTED_WRITE)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, unprotected),
        (ExitEvent::EptViolation, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn read_or_fetch_violation_stops_with_the_violation() {
    let read = EPT_ACCESS_READ | EPT_PAGE_READABLE | EPT_LINEAR_VALID | EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS;
    let fetch = EPT_ACCESS_FETCH | EPT_PAGE_READABLE | EPT_LINEAR_VALID | EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS;
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, ept_violation(PROTECTED_PAGE, read)).0,
        ExitEvent::EptViolation
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, ept_violation(PROTECTED_PAGE, fetch)).0,
        ExitEvent::EptViolation
    );
}

#[test]

        ExitEvent::EptViolation
    );

#[test]

    assert_eq!(

    );

#[test]
fn second_violation_on_the_page_stops_with_the_violation() {
    // Write was granted once; another violation means the grant did not
    // take effect.
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WRITTEN, protected_write()),
        (ExitEvent::EptViolation, WRITTEN)
    );

#[test]
fn violation_during_nmi_unblocking_iret_stops_with_the_violation() {

#[test]
fn violation_on_a_guest_page_table_access_stops_with_the_violation() {
    // Bit 7 without bit 8: the CPU was reading a guest page table.
    let walk = ept_violation(PROTECTED_PAGE, PROTECTED_WRITE & !EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS);
    assert_eq!(decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, walk).0, ExitEvent::EptViolation);
    let no_linear = ept_violation(
        PROTECTED_PAGE,
        PROTECTED_WRITE & !(EPT_LINEAR_VALID | EPT_TRANSLATED_ACCESS),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, no_linear).0,
        ExitEvent::EptViolation
    );
}

#[test]
fn ept_misconfiguration_stops_with_its_own_event() {
    let misconfig = ExitInfo {
        guest_physical: PROTECTED_PAGE,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, misconfig),
        (ExitEvent::EptMisconfig, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_ept_stops_stop_the_guest() {

        assert_eq!(event.action(), ExitAction::Unexpected, "{event:?}");
    }
}

#[test]

#[test]

#[test]

        },
    );

/// IDT-vectoring info of an NMI (type 2, vector 2) that the exit interrupted.
const VECTORING_NMI: InterruptionInfo = InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0202);

#[test]
fn a_vectoring_exit_is_still_judged_by_its_reason() {
    // Before re-delivery, any valid vectoring field stopped the guest. Now
    // the exit goes to its reason's handler, and the delivery is re-delivered
    // on top of the plan.
    let interrupted = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: VECTORING_NMI,
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WRITTEN, interrupted).0,
        ExitEvent::MainVmcall
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_ept_violation_during_delivery_grants_write_and_re_delivers() {
    // The test guest's reinjected NMI faults on its read-only data page: an
    // EPT violation whose IDT-vectoring field holds the NMI. Grant write,
    // and re-deliver the NMI on the retried entry.
    let interrupted = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: VECTORING_NMI,
        ..protected_write()
    };
    let (event, _) = decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, interrupted);
    assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::EptWriteGranted);
    let plan = match event.action() {
        ExitAction::Resume(plan) => plan,
        other => panic!("expected a resume, got {other:?}"),
    };
    let redelivery = interrupted.redelivery(None).expect("the NMI is re-delivered");
    assert_eq!(redelivery.info, VECTORING_NMI);
    assert_eq!(
        plan.redelivering(redelivery),
        Some(ResumePlan {
            redeliver: Some(redelivery),
            ..ResumePlan::RETRY_AFTER_GRANT
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn no_vectoring_means_no_redelivery() {
    assert_eq!(vmcall(MARKER).redelivery(None), None);
}

#[test]
fn redelivery_clears_bits_30_to_12_and_keeps_the_event() {
    // Bit 12 (NMI unblocking due to IRET) is exit-only; it must not reach the
    // VM-entry field.
    let interrupted = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(0x8000_1202),
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        interrupted.redelivery(None).unwrap().info,
        InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0202)
    );
}

#[test]
fn redelivery_keeps_an_exception_error_code() {
    // A hardware exception (type 3) with the error-code bit (#PF, vector 14).
    let page_fault = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0B0E),
        idt_vectoring_error_code: 0x2,
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    };
    let redelivery = page_fault.redelivery(None).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(redelivery.error_code, Some(0x2));
    assert_eq!(redelivery.instruction_len, None);
    // An exception without the bit (#UD, vector 6) carries no error code.
    let invalid_opcode = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0306),
        idt_vectoring_error_code: 0x2,
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    };
    assert_eq!(invalid_opcode.redelivery(None).unwrap().error_code, None);
}

#[test]
fn a_software_interrupt_re_delivers_with_its_length() {
    // A software interrupt (type 4), e.g. INT 0x80.
    let software = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0480),
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    };
    assert_eq!(software.redelivery(Some(2)).unwrap().instruction_len, Some(2));
    // With the length unreadable, it cannot be re-delivered: the plan stops.
    let redelivery = software.redelivery(None).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(redelivery.instruction_len, None);
    assert_eq!(ResumePlan::RETRY_AFTER_GRANT.redelivering(redelivery), None);
}

#[test]
fn redelivery_conflicts_with_an_advance_or_injection() {
    let redelivery = ExitInfo {
        idt_vectoring: VECTORING_NMI,
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    }
    .redelivery(None)
    .unwrap();
    // A plan that advances RIP, injects an NMI, or injects an exception
    // already uses the single VM-entry injection, so it cannot re-deliver.
    assert_eq!(ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION.redelivering(redelivery), None);
    assert_eq!(ResumePlan::INJECT_NMI.redelivering(redelivery), None);
    assert_eq!(ResumePlan::INJECT_GP.redelivering(redelivery), None);
}

#[test]
fn entry_failure_is_unexpected() {
    let failed = ExitInfo {
        reason: ExitReason {
            basic: EXIT_REASON_VMCALL,
            entry_failure: true,
        },
        ..vmcall(MARKER)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, failed),
        (ExitEvent::Unexpected, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn exception_exit_is_unexpected() {
    let page_fault = ExitInfo {
        interruption_info: InterruptionInfo(PAGE_FAULT_INFO),
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WAITING, page_fault),
        (ExitEvent::Unexpected, WAITING)
    );
}

#[test]
fn each_event_maps_to_its_action() {
    let resume = |advance_rip, inject_nmi, nmi_window, grant_write| {
        ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan {
            advance_rip,
            inject_nmi,
            nmi_window,
            grant_write,
            emulate: None,
            inject_exception: None,
            redeliver: None,
        })
    };
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::MainVmcall.action(), resume(true, false, None, false));
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::GuestNmiHandler.action(), resume(true, false, None, false));
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::NmiInjected.action(), resume(false, true, Some(false), false));
    assert_eq!(
        ExitEvent::NmiWindowInjected.action(),
        resume(false, true, Some(false), false)
    );
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::NmiDeferred.action(), resume(false, false, Some(true), false));
    // RIP not advanced: the write runs again once the page is writable.
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::EptWriteGranted.action(), resume(false, false, None, true));
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall.action(), ExitAction::Finished);
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::EptWriteMissing.action(), ExitAction::Unexpected);
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::DataPageMismatch.action(), ExitAction::Unexpected);
    assert_eq!(ExitEvent::Unexpected.action(), ExitAction::Unexpected);
    let cpuid = Emulation::Cpuid { leaf: 1, subleaf: 0 };
    assert_eq!(
        ExitEvent::Emulated(cpuid).action(),
        ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan {
            emulate: Some(cpuid),
            ..ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection.action(),
        ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::INJECT_GP)
    );
    // A fault: RIP stays on the instruction. A constant, so checked at compile time.
    const { assert!(!ResumePlan::INJECT_GP.advance_rip) };
    assert_eq!(
        ExitEvent::Halted.action(),
        ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode.action(),
        ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::INJECT_UD)
    );
    const { assert!(!ResumePlan::INJECT_UD.advance_rip) };
}

#[test]
fn hlt_resumes_past_the_instruction() {
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, exit(EXIT_REASON_HLT)),
        (ExitEvent::Halted, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn hlt_in_an_sti_shadow_is_decided_the_same() {
    // `sti; hlt`: the exit reports blocking by STI; the decision does not
    // depend on it, the RIP advance ends it.
    let in_shadow = ExitInfo {
        interruptibility: BLOCKING_BY_STI,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_HLT)
    };
    assert_eq!(decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, in_shadow).0, ExitEvent::Halted);
}

#[test]
fn skipping_an_instruction_ends_sti_and_mov_ss_blocking_only() {
    assert_eq!(after_skipped_instruction(BLOCKING_BY_STI), 0);
    assert_eq!(after_skipped_instruction(BLOCKING_BY_MOV_SS), 0);
    // Blocking by SMI (bit 2) and by NMI (bit 3) outlast the instruction.
    assert_eq!(after_skipped_instruction(0b1111), 0b1100);
    assert_eq!(after_skipped_instruction(BLOCKING_BY_NMI), BLOCKING_BY_NMI);
}

        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn injected_invalid_opcode_is_a_hardware_exception_without_error_code() {

    assert!(!InterruptionInfo::INVALID_OPCODE.delivers_error_code());
    assert!(InterruptionInfo::GENERAL_PROTECTION.delivers_error_code());
}

#[test]
fn ept_access_name_prefers_write() {
    assert_eq!(EptQualification(0x18A).access_name(), "write");
    // Hardware may report a read along with the write of a read-modify-write.
    assert_eq!(
        EptQualification(EPT_ACCESS_READ | EPT_ACCESS_WRITE).access_name(),
        "write"
    );
    assert_eq!(EptQualification(EPT_ACCESS_FETCH).access_name(), "instruction fetch");
    assert_eq!(EptQualification(EPT_ACCESS_READ).access_name(), "read");
    assert_eq!(EptQualification(0).access_name(), "no access bit set");
}

#[test]
fn ept_page_permissions_come_from_bits_5_to_3() {
    // The guest's data page: readable only.
    assert_eq!(EptQualification(0x18A).permissions(), (1, 0, 0));
    assert_eq!(EptQualification(0x38).permissions(), (1, 1, 1));
}

/// The exits the guest's emulation block causes, in order.
fn emulated_exits() -> Vec<ExitInfo> {
    let msr = |basic, rax: u64, rdx: u64| ExitInfo {
        guest_rax: rax,
        guest_rcx: 0xC000_0102,
        guest_rdx: rdx,
        ..exit(basic)
    };
    let io = |is_in: bool, rax: u64| ExitInfo {
        qualification: (u64::from(GUEST_SCRATCH_PORT) << 16) | (u64::from(is_in) << 3),
        guest_rax: rax,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION)
    };
    // Hyper-V's MTRRs: fixed ranges, eight variable ranges, MAXPHYADDR 46.
    let mtrr = |basic, msr: u32, value: u64| ExitInfo {
        guest_rax: value & 0xFFFF_FFFF,
        guest_rcx: msr.into(),
        guest_rdx: value >> 32,
        mtrr: MtrrCapabilities::new((1 << 8) | 8, 46).unwrap(),
        ..exit(basic)
    };
    vec![
        ExitInfo {
            guest_rax: 1,
            guest_rcx: 0,
            ..exit(EXIT_REASON_CPUID)
        },
        msr(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, 0, 0),
        msr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, GUEST_MSR_VALUE & 0xFFFF_FFFF, GUEST_MSR_VALUE >> 32),
        msr(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, 0, 0),
        msr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0, 0),
        io(true, 0),
        io(false, GUEST_IO_VALUE.into()),
        io(true, 0),
        io(false, 0),
        ExitInfo {
            guest_rax: 0x8000_0008,
            ..exit(EXIT_REASON_CPUID)
        },
        // Its last variable MTRR, number 7 under Hyper-V: read the pair,
        // turn it off, move it, 2 MiB, read the mask back, 4 KiB, then off
        // and back as it was.
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, 0x20E, 0),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, 0x20F, 0),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20E, GUEST_MTRR_BASE),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, 0x20F, 0),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0x3FFF_FFFF_F800),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20E, 0),
        mtrr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0),
        exit(EXIT_REASON_HLT),
    ]
}

#[test]
fn cpuid_exit_is_dispatched_to_emulation() {
    let cpuid = ExitInfo {
        guest_rax: 1,
        guest_rcx: 0,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_CPUID)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, cpuid).0,
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Cpuid { leaf: 1, subleaf: 0 })
    );
}

#[test]
fn whole_guest_run_finishes_with_the_expected_stats() {
    // As the exit handler counts: every exit, then what a resumed one did.
    let mut state = ExitState::default();
    let mut stats = VcpuStats::ZERO;
    let mut event = ExitEvent::Unexpected;
    for exit in emulated_exits()
        .into_iter()
        .chain([protected_write(), vmcall(MARKER), vmcall(MARKER + 1)])
    {
        stats.count_exit();
        (event, state) = decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, state, exit);
        if let ExitAction::Resume(plan) = event.action() {
            stats.count_resumed(event, plan);
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall);
    assert_eq!(stats, expected_stats(&stats));
    assert_eq!((stats.exits, stats.nmi_injections), (24, 0));
}

#[test]
fn injected_general_protection_is_a_hardware_exception_with_error_code() {
    // Valid (bit 31), error code (bit 11), hardware exception (type 3),
    // vector 13.
    assert_eq!(InterruptionInfo::GENERAL_PROTECTION, InterruptionInfo(0x8000_0B0D));
}

#[test]
fn msr_exits_are_dispatched_to_emulation() {
    // RDX = 0: `exit` defaults it to GUEST_EPT_VALUE, which as the upper half
    // of a WRMSR value would be non-canonical.
    let msr = |basic| ExitInfo {
        guest_rcx: 0xC000_0102,
        guest_rdx: 0,
        ..exit(basic)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, msr(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR)).0,
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr: 0xC000_0102 })
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, msr(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR)).0,
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Wrmsr { msr: 0xC000_0102, .. })
    ));
}

#[test]
fn io_exit_is_dispatched_to_emulation() {
    let byte_in = ExitInfo {
        qualification: (0x3FF << 16) | (1 << 3),
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, START, byte_in).0,
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::In {
            port: 0x3FF,
            size: IoSize::Byte
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_nmi_from_root_operation_becomes_pending() {
    assert_eq!(START.with_host_nmi(false), START);
    assert_eq!(
        START.with_host_nmi(true),
        ExitState {
            nmi_pending: true,
            ..START
        }
    );
    // NMIs do not queue: one already pending stays the only one.
    let pending = START.with_host_nmi(true);
    assert_eq!(pending.with_host_nmi(true), pending);
}

#[test]
fn a_pending_nmi_keeps_the_nmi_window_on() {
    let pending = ExitState {
        nmi_pending: true,
        ..WAITING
    };
    assert_eq!(
        ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION.keeping_pending_nmi(pending),
        ResumePlan {
            nmi_window: Some(true),
            ..ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION
        }
    );
    // An injected #GP leaves the NMI waiting for the window too.
    assert_eq!(
        ResumePlan::INJECT_GP.keeping_pending_nmi(pending).nmi_window,
        Some(true)
    );
}

#[test]
fn without_a_pending_nmi_the_plan_is_unchanged() {
    for plan in [
        ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION,
        ResumePlan::INJECT_NMI,
        ResumePlan::RETRY_AFTER_GRANT,
    ] {
        assert_eq!(plan.keeping_pending_nmi(WAITING), plan);
    }
}

#[test]
fn an_nmi_in_root_operation_at_vmcall_1_reaches_the_guest() {
    // Main VMCALL #1, with an NMI that arrived while Aleph0 handled the EPT
    // violation before it.
    let (event, state) = decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WRITTEN.with_host_nmi(true), vmcall(MARKER));
    assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::MainVmcall);
    assert!(state.nmi_pending);
    let plan = match event.action() {
        ExitAction::Resume(plan) => plan.keeping_pending_nmi(state),
        action => panic!("main VMCALL #1 resumes, not {action:?}"),
    };
    assert_eq!(plan.nmi_window, Some(true));

    // The guest can take it at once: the NMI-window exit injects it, and
    // the run ends as one with a reinjected NMI does.
    let mut state = state;
    let mut event = ExitEvent::Unexpected;
    for exit in [exit(EXIT_REASON_NMI_WINDOW), vmcall(NMI_MARKER), vmcall(MARKER + 1)] {
        (event, state) = decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, state, exit);
        if exit.reason.basic == EXIT_REASON_NMI_WINDOW {
            assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::NmiWindowInjected);
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall);
    assert_eq!((state.nmis_handled, state.nmi_pending), (1, false));
}

/// What `decide` makes of `exit` for the firmware, from `state`.
fn firmware(state: ExitState, exit: ExitInfo) -> ExitAction {
    decide(GuestKind::Firmware, state, exit).0.action()
}

#[test]
fn the_firmware_resumes_from_every_exit_aleph0_handles() {
    // Hyper-V's first synthetic MSR, outside the MSR bitmap: #GP without
    // Hyper-V's interface, forwarded with it, and on either way.
    let synthetic_msr = ExitInfo {
        guest_rcx: 0x4000_0000,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR)
    };
    let forwarded_msr = ExitInfo {
        hyperv: true,
        ..synthetic_msr
    };
    let pending = ExitState {
        nmi_pending: true,
        ..START
    };
    let handled = emulated_exits().into_iter().map(|exit| (START, exit)).chain([
        (START, synthetic_msr),
        (START, forwarded_msr),
        (START, hypercall(0x5C)),
        (START, vmcall(0)),
        (START, exit(EXIT_REASON_MWAIT)),
        (START, exit(EXIT_REASON_MONITOR)),
        (START, nmi(0)),
        (START, nmi(BLOCKING_BY_STI)),
        (pending, exit(EXIT_REASON_NMI_WINDOW)),
    ]);
    for (state, exit) in handled {
        assert!(
            matches!(firmware(state, exit), ExitAction::Resume(_)),
            "reason {} from {state:?}",
            exit.reason.basic
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_firmware_stops_at_its_ept_violations() {
    // No page is the firmware's to write, so every EPT violation means the
    // map is wrong.
    for exit in [protected_write(), ept_violation(0xFEE0_0030, EPT_ACCESS_READ)] {
        assert_eq!(
            firmware(START, exit),
            ExitAction::Unexpected,
            "reason {}",
            exit.reason.basic
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, protected_write()),
        (ExitEvent::EptViolation, START)
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_firmware_resumes_past_aleph0s_own_vmcalls() {
    for (rcx, event) in [
        (vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED, ExitEvent::BootServicesEnded),
        (vmcall::TEST, ExitEvent::TestVmcall),
    ] {
        // Under Hyper-V or not: they are Aleph0's either way.
        for hyperv in [false, true] {
            let exit = ExitInfo {
                hyperv,
                ..hypercall(rcx)
            };
            assert_eq!(decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, exit), (event, START));
        }
        assert_eq!(event.action(), ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION));
    }
}

#[test]
fn aleph0s_vmcalls_have_reserved_hypercall_bits_set() {
    // Bits 63:60 of a hypercall input value are reserved, so no hypercall
    // Hyper-V takes has either value in RCX.
    for rcx in [vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED, vmcall::TEST] {
        assert_ne!(rcx >> 60, 0, "{rcx:#x}");
    }
    assert_ne!(vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED, vmcall::TEST);
    assert_eq!(vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED, 0x416c_6570_6830_4542);
}

#[test]
fn every_other_firmware_vmcall_is_forwarded_under_hyper_v() {
    // HvCallPostMessage and HvCallSignalEvent as the VMBus drivers make
    // them, a fast rep hypercall, and Aleph0's values one bit off or cut to
    // their low half, which are hypercalls too (invalid ones, which Hyper-V
    // answers).
    for rcx in [
        0x5C,
        0x1_005D,
        0x0000_0002_0001_0003,
        vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED ^ 1,
        vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED & 0xFFFF_FFFF,
        vmcall::TEST ^ (1 << 63),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, hypercall(rcx)),
            (ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Hypercall { input: rcx }), START),
            "rcx={rcx:#x}"
        );
    }
    // Aleph0's values in RAX are no call to Aleph0 any more.
    let in_rax = ExitInfo {
        guest_rax: vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED,
        ..hypercall(0x5C)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, in_rax).0,
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5C })
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_forwarded_hypercall_resumes_past_the_vmcall_with_its_result() {
    let event = decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, hypercall(0x5C)).0;
    assert_eq!(
        event.action(),
        ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan {
            emulate: Some(Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5C }),
            ..ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_refused_forward_injects_at_the_instruction_and_keeps_the_rest() {
    let ExitAction::Resume(plan) = ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5C }).action() else {
        panic!("a forwarded hypercall resumes");
    };
    let plan = plan.keeping_pending_nmi(ExitState {
        nmi_pending: true,
        ..START
    });
    let refused = plan.refused_with(InterruptionInfo::INVALID_OPCODE);
    assert!(!refused.advance_rip);
    assert_eq!(refused.inject_exception, Some(InterruptionInfo::INVALID_OPCODE));
    assert_eq!(
        (refused.nmi_window, refused.emulate),
        (Some(true), Some(Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5C }))
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_vmcall_without_hyper_v_gets_invalid_opcode() {
    // As on hardware without a hypervisor: VMCALL outside VMX non-root
    // operation is #UD.
    let exit = ExitInfo {
        hyperv: false,
        ..hypercall(0x5C)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, exit),
        (ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode, START)
    );
    assert_eq!(firmware(START, exit), ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::INJECT_UD));
}

#[test]
fn a_vmcall_from_cpl_3_gets_invalid_opcode_whatever_rcx_holds() {
    // Hyper-V refuses a hypercall from CPL > 0 with #UD; forwarding it from
    // root operation would make it at CPL 0 instead. Aleph0's own need CPL 0
    // too.
    for cpl in 1..=3 {
        for rcx in [0x5C, vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED, vmcall::TEST] {
            let exit = ExitInfo {
                guest_cpl: cpl,
                ..hypercall(rcx)
            };
            assert_eq!(
                decide(GuestKind::Firmware, START, exit).0,
                ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode,
                "cpl={cpl} rcx={rcx:#x}"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_cpl_is_the_dpl_of_ss() {
    // A 64-bit kernel data segment (0xC093) and a user one (0xC0F3).
    assert_eq!(cpl_from_ss(0xC093), 0);
    assert_eq!(cpl_from_ss(0xC0F3), 3);
    assert_eq!(cpl_from_ss(0x1_C0B3), 1);
}

#[test]
fn the_test_guest_keeps_its_script_under_hyper_v() {
    // Its VMCALLs are its script's: Aleph0's values and hypercalls stop the
    // run, and its markers in RAX do what they always did.
    for rcx in [vmcall::BOOT_SERVICES_ENDED, vmcall::TEST, 0x5C] {
        assert_eq!(
            decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WRITTEN, hypercall(rcx)).0,
            ExitEvent::Unexpected,
            "rcx={rcx:#x}"
        );
    }
    let marked = |rax| ExitInfo {
        hyperv: true,
        ..vmcall(rax)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WRITTEN, marked(MARKER)).0,
        ExitEvent::MainVmcall
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WAITING, marked(NMI_MARKER)).0,
        ExitEvent::GuestNmiHandler
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decide(GuestKind::BuiltInTest, WAITING, marked(MARKER + 1)).0,
        ExitEvent::LastMainVmcall
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_firmware_stops_at_an_unhandled_exit() {
    let page_fault = ExitInfo {
        interruption_info: InterruptionInfo(PAGE_FAULT_INFO),
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_EXCEPTION_OR_NMI)
    };
    let entry_failure = ExitInfo {
        reason: ExitReason {
            basic: 33,
            entry_failure: true,
        },
        ..exit(33)
    };
    // A triple fault (2), a CR access (28), an EPT misconfiguration (49).
    for exit in [
        page_fault,
        entry_failure,
        exit(2),
        exit(28),
        exit(EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            firmware(START, exit),
            ExitAction::Unexpected,
            "reason {}",
            exit.reason.basic
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_firmware_never_finishes() {
    // Every basic reason and the test guest's markers, from every state its
    // run passes through, the last main VMCALL's included.
    for state in [START, WRITTEN, WAITING] {
        for basic in 0..=u16::from(u8::MAX) {
            for rax in [0, MARKER, MARKER + 1, NMI_MARKER] {
                let exit = ExitInfo {
                    guest_rax: rax,
                    ..exit(basic)
                };
                assert_ne!(
                    firmware(state, exit),
                    ExitAction::Finished,
                    "reason {basic} rax={rax:#x}"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/exit_decision/emulation.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/exit_decision/emulation.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::{
    EXIT_REASON_CPUID, EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION, EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, ExitReason, InterruptionInfo,
};
use crate::vmx::mtrr::{self, MtrrCapabilities};

/// CPUID leaf 1 as a Hyper-V guest with nested virtualization sees it: VMX
/// (ECX bit 5) set.
const LEAF_1: CpuidResult = CpuidResult {
    eax: 0x0009_06EA,
    ebx: 0x0010_0800,
    ecx: 0xFEDA_32A3,
    edx: 0x1F8B_FBFF,
};

/// An exit with reason `basic` and every other field zero.
fn exit(basic: u16) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        reason: ExitReason {
            basic,
            entry_failure: false,
        },
        interruption_info: InterruptionInfo(0),
        guest_rax: 0,
        guest_rcx: 0,
        guest_rdx: 0,
        interruptibility: 0,
        idt_vectoring: InterruptionInfo(0),
        idt_vectoring_error_code: 0,
        qualification: 0,
        guest_physical: 0,
        protected_page: 0,
        mtrr: MtrrCapabilities::NONE,
        hyperv: false,
        guest_cpl: 0,
    }
}

#[test]
fn leaf_1_hides_vmx_and_nothing_else() {
    assert_ne!(LEAF_1.ecx & (1 << 5), 0);
    let guest = cpuid_policy(1, LEAF_1);
    assert_eq!(guest.ecx, LEAF_1.ecx & !(1 << 5));
    assert_eq!((guest.eax, guest.ebx, guest.edx), (LEAF_1.eax, LEAF_1.ebx, LEAF_1.edx));
}

#[test]
fn leaf_1_without_vmx_is_unchanged() {
    let no_vmx = CpuidResult {
        ecx: LEAF_1.ecx & !(1 << 5),
        ..LEAF_1
    };
    assert_eq!(cpuid_policy(1, no_vmx), no_vmx);
}

#[test]
fn other_leaves_pass_through() {
    for leaf in [0, 7, 0xD, 0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0001] {
        assert_eq!(cpuid_policy(leaf, LEAF_1), LEAF_1, "leaf {leaf:#x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn cpuid_takes_leaf_and_subleaf_from_the_low_halves_of_rax_and_rcx() {
    let cpuid_exit = ExitInfo {
        guest_rax: 0xFFFF_FFFF_0000_0007,
        guest_rcx: 0x0000_0001_0000_0001,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_CPUID)
    };
    assert_eq!(
        cpuid(&cpuid_exit),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Cpuid { leaf: 7, subleaf: 1 })
    );
}

const KERNEL_GS_BASE: u32 = 0xC000_0102;

fn msr_exit(basic: u16, msr: u64, rax: u64, rdx: u64) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        guest_rcx: msr,
        guest_rax: rax,
        guest_rdx: rdx,
        ..exit(basic)
    }
}

#[test]
fn rdmsr_of_an_intercepted_msr_is_emulated() {
    assert_eq!(
        rdmsr(&msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, KERNEL_GS_BASE.into(), 0, 0)),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr: KERNEL_GS_BASE })
    );
}

#[test]
fn rdmsr_ignores_the_upper_half_of_rcx() {
    let exit = msr_exit(
        EXIT_REASON_RDMSR,
        0xFFFF_FFFF_0000_0000 | u64::from(KERNEL_GS_BASE),
        0,
        0,
    );
    assert_eq!(
        rdmsr(&exit),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr: KERNEL_GS_BASE })
    );

#[test]
fn msrs_outside_the_bitmap_get_a_general_protection_fault() {
    // Hyper-V's synthetic MSRs start at 0x40000000; neither range covers
    // them, and without Hyper-V's interface nothing forwards them.
    for msr in [0x4000_0000, 0x4000_0020, 0xC000_2000] {
        assert_eq!(
            rdmsr(&msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, msr, 0, 0)),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection
        );
        assert_eq!(
            wrmsr(&msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, msr, 0, 0)),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection
        );
    }
}

/// `exit` from a guest that has Hyper-V's interface.
fn under_hyperv(exit: ExitInfo) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo { hyperv: true, ..exit }
}

#[test]
fn synthetic_msrs_are_forwarded_under_hyper_v() {
    // HV_X64_MSR_TIME_REF_COUNT, the firmware's first; the first and last
    // of the range.
    for msr in [0x4000_0020, 0x4000_0000, 0x4000_FFFF] {
        assert_eq!(
            rdmsr(&under_hyperv(msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, msr.into(), 0, 0))),
            ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::SyntheticRead { msr }),
            "{msr:#x}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_synthetic_wrmsr_is_forwarded_with_any_value() {
    // HV_X64_MSR_HYPERCALL with a page GPA and the enable bit, and a value
    // that is no canonical address: Hyper-V checks it, not Aleph0.
    for value in [0x7FF2_0001, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000] {
        let exit = under_hyperv(msr_exit(
            EXIT_REASON_WRMSR,
            0x4000_0001,
            value & 0xFFFF_FFFF,
            value >> 32,
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            wrmsr(&exit),
            ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::SyntheticWrite {
                msr: 0x4000_0001,
                value
            }),
            "{value:#x}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]

    for msr in [0x3FFF_FFFF, 0x4001_0000, 0xC000_2000] {
        assert_eq!(
            rdmsr(&under_hyperv(msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, msr, 0, 0))),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,

        assert_eq!(
            wrmsr(&under_hyperv(msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, msr, 0, 0))),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
            "{msr:#x}"
        );
    }

#[test]

    }

#[test]
fn an_msr_in_range_but_not_intercepted_means_a_broken_bitmap() {

#[test]
fn canonical_means_bits_63_to_47_all_equal() {
    assert!(is_canonical_48(0));
    assert!(is_canonical_48(0x0000_7FFF_FFFF_FFFF));
    assert!(is_canonical_48(0xFFFF_8000_0000_0000));
    assert!(is_canonical_48(u64::MAX));
    assert!(!is_canonical_48(0x0000_8000_0000_0000));

/// Exit qualification of an I/O instruction: size − 1 in bits 2:0, IN in
/// bit 3, string in bit 4, REP in bit 5, port in bits 31:16.
fn io_qualification(port: u16, size_minus_1: u64, is_in: bool) -> u64 {
    (u64::from(port) << 16) | (u64::from(is_in) << 3) | size_minus_1
}

fn io_exit(qualification: u64, rax: u64) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        qualification,
        guest_rax: rax,
        ..exit(EXIT_REASON_IO_INSTRUCTION)
    }
}

#[test]
fn io_qualification_decodes_size_direction_and_port() {
    let byte_in = IoQualification(io_qualification(0x3FF, 0, true));
    assert_eq!(byte_in.size(), Some(IoSize::Byte));
    assert!(byte_in.is_in());
    assert!(!byte_in.is_string());
    assert!(!byte_in.is_rep());
    assert_eq!(byte_in.port(), 0x3FF);
    let dword_out = IoQualification(io_qualification(0xCF8, 3, false));
    assert_eq!(dword_out.size(), Some(IoSize::Dword));
    assert!(!dword_out.is_in());
    assert_eq!(dword_out.port(), 0xCF8);
    assert_eq!(
        IoQualification(io_qualification(0x60, 1, true)).size(),
        Some(IoSize::Word)
    );
}

#[test]
fn unused_size_encodings_have_no_size() {
    for size_minus_1 in [2, 4, 5, 6, 7] {
        assert_eq!(IoQualification(size_minus_1).size(), None, "{size_minus_1}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn string_and_rep_bits_decode() {
    assert!(IoQualification(1 << 4).is_string());
    assert!(IoQualification(1 << 5).is_rep());
}

#[test]
fn byte_and_word_in_keep_the_rest_of_rax() {
    let rax = 0x1122_3344_5566_7788;
    assert_eq!(merge_in(rax, IoSize::Byte, 0xA5), 0x1122_3344_5566_77A5);
    assert_eq!(merge_in(rax, IoSize::Word, 0xBEEF), 0x1122_3344_5566_BEEF);
}

#[test]
fn dword_in_zero_extends_into_rax() {
    assert_eq!(merge_in(0x1122_3344_5566_7788, IoSize::Dword, 0xDEAD_BEEF), 0xDEAD_BEEF);
}

#[test]
fn out_value_takes_al_ax_or_eax() {
    let rax = 0x1122_3344_5566_7788;
    assert_eq!(out_value(rax, IoSize::Byte), 0x88);
    assert_eq!(out_value(rax, IoSize::Word), 0x7788);
    assert_eq!(out_value(rax, IoSize::Dword), 0x5566_7788);
}

#[test]
fn in_is_emulated() {
    assert_eq!(
        io(&io_exit(io_qualification(0x3FF, 0, true), 0)),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::In {
            port: 0x3FF,
            size: IoSize::Byte
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn out_is_emulated_with_the_value_from_rax() {
    assert_eq!(
        io(&io_exit(io_qualification(0x3FF, 0, false), 0xFFFF_FF00 | 0xA5)),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Out {
            port: 0x3FF,
            size: IoSize::Byte,
            value: 0xA5
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn string_or_rep_io_stops_the_guest() {
    let string = io_qualification(0x3FF, 0, true) | (1 << 4);
    let rep = string | (1 << 5);
    for qualification in [string, rep] {
        assert_eq!(io(&io_exit(qualification, 0)), ExitEvent::Unexpected);
    }
}

#[test]
fn io_with_an_unused_size_stops_the_guest() {
    assert_eq!(io(&io_exit(io_qualification(0x3FF, 2, true), 0)), ExitEvent::Unexpected);
}

/// Every MSR index the bitmap covers: the two ranges whose bits the CPU consults.
fn bitmap_msr_indexes() -> impl Iterator<Item = u32> {
    (0u32..=0x1FFF).chain(0xC000_0000..=0xC000_1FFF)
}

#[test]
fn rdmsr_is_emulated_only_for_the_intercepted_msrs() {
    for msr in bitmap_msr_indexes() {
        let event = rdmsr(&msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, msr.into(), 0, 0));
        if INTERCEPTED_MSRS.contains(&msr) {
            assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr }), "MSR {msr:#x}");
        } else if mtrr::is_msr_address(msr) {
            // An MTRR address, none of which this guest (no MTRRs) has.
            assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection, "MSR {msr:#x}");
        } else {
            // In range with its bit clear: it should never have exited, so the bitmap is broken.
            assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::Unexpected, "MSR {msr:#x}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn wrmsr_is_emulated_only_for_the_intercepted_msrs() {
    for msr in bitmap_msr_indexes() {
        // RAX and RDX are zero, so the value is 0, which is canonical.
        let event = wrmsr(&msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, msr.into(), 0, 0));
        if INTERCEPTED_MSRS.contains(&msr) {
            assert_eq!(
                event,
                ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Wrmsr { msr, value: 0 }),
                "MSR {msr:#x}"
            );
        } else if mtrr::is_msr_address(msr) {
            assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection, "MSR {msr:#x}");
        } else {
            assert_eq!(event, ExitEvent::Unexpected, "MSR {msr:#x}");
        }
    }
}

/// The MTRR MSRs of the Hyper-V VM: the fixed ranges, eight variable
/// ranges, MAXPHYADDR 46.
fn hyper_v_mtrrs() -> MtrrCapabilities {
    MtrrCapabilities::new((1 << 8) | 8, 46).unwrap()
}

/// An RDMSR or WRMSR exit of a guest with Hyper-V's MTRRs, writing `value`.
fn mtrr_exit(basic: u16, msr: u32, value: u64) -> ExitInfo {
    ExitInfo {
        mtrr: hyper_v_mtrrs(),
        ..msr_exit(basic, msr.into(), value & 0xFFFF_FFFF, value >> 32)
    }
}

#[test]
fn rdmsr_of_an_mtrr_reads_the_guests_copy() {
    for address in [0x2FF, 0x250, 0x26F, 0x200, 0x20F] {
        assert_eq!(
            rdmsr(&mtrr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, address, 0)),
            ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::MtrrRead {
                msr: hyper_v_mtrrs().msr(address).unwrap()
            }),
            "{address:#x}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn wrmsr_of_an_mtrr_writes_the_guests_copy() {
    // Variable range 7's mask: 2 MiB, valid.
    let exit = mtrr_exit(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800);
    assert_eq!(
        wrmsr(&exit),
        ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::MtrrWrite {
            msr: hyper_v_mtrrs().msr(0x20F).unwrap(),
            value: 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_mtrr_value_the_cpu_refuses_gets_a_general_protection_fault() {
    for (address, value) in [
        // Bit 8 of IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.
        (0x2FF, 0xD00),
        // A reserved type in a range that is off: refused all the same.
        (0x20E, 0x20_0000 | 2),
        // Bit 46, past MAXPHYADDR.
        (0x20F, (1 << 46) | 0x800),
        // A reserved type in one byte of a fixed-range MSR.
        (0x26F, 0x0606_0606_0606_0607),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            wrmsr(&mtrr_exit(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, address, value)),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
            "{address:#x} <- {value:#x}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn mtrr_addresses_the_cpu_has_no_msr_at_get_a_general_protection_fault() {
    let without_fixed = MtrrCapabilities::new(8, 46).unwrap();
    for (mtrr, msr) in [
        // Variable ranges 8 and 31 with eight ranges.
        (hyper_v_mtrrs(), 0x210),
        (hyper_v_mtrrs(), 0x23F),
        // A fixed-range MSR without IA32_MTRRCAP.FIX.
        (without_fixed, 0x250),
        // Any of them on a CPU without MTRRs.
        (MtrrCapabilities::NONE, 0x2FF),
        (MtrrCapabilities::NONE, 0x200),
    ] {
        let access = |basic| ExitInfo {
            mtrr,
            ..msr_exit(basic, msr, 0, 0)
        };
        assert_eq!(
            rdmsr(&access(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR)),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
            "{msr:#x}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            wrmsr(&access(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR)),
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection,
            "{msr:#x}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn msrs_next_to_the_mtrrs_that_are_not_intercepted_mean_a_broken_bitmap() {
    // IA32_MTRRCAP stays the guest's, and 0x240 is past the variable ranges
    // Aleph0 keeps: neither should ever exit.
    for msr in [0xFE, 0x240] {
        let access = |basic| ExitInfo {
            mtrr: hyper_v_mtrrs(),
            ..msr_exit(basic, msr, 0, 0)
        };
        assert_eq!(rdmsr(&access(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR)), ExitEvent::Unexpected, "{msr:#x}");
        assert_eq!(wrmsr(&access(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR)), ExitEvent::Unexpected, "{msr:#x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn each_bitmap_msr_is_passed_through_kept_in_the_mtrr_copy_refused_or_never_exits() {
    let mtrrs = hyper_v_mtrrs();
    for msr in bitmap_msr_indexes() {
        let event = rdmsr(&mtrr_exit(EXIT_REASON_RDMSR, msr, 0));
        let expected = if INTERCEPTED_MSRS.contains(&msr) {
            ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr })
        } else if let Some(mtrr) = mtrrs.msr(msr) {
            ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::MtrrRead { msr: mtrr })
        } else if mtrr::is_msr_address(msr) {
            ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection
        } else {
            ExitEvent::Unexpected
        };
        assert_eq!(event, expected, "MSR {msr:#x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_wrmsr_value_is_edx_eax() {
    let exit = msr_exit(EXIT_REASON_WRMSR, 0x20F, 0xFFFF_FFFF_0000_0800, 0xFFFF_FFFF_0000_3FFF);
    assert_eq!(wrmsr_value(&exit), 0x3FFF_0000_0800);
}
```

```rs
#[test]
fn the_mtrr_base_is_uc_in_a_physbase_and_2_mib_aligned() {
    // `mov eax` loads it whole: it fits in 32 bits, with the type, UC (0),
    // in bits 7:0.
    let physbase = GUEST_MTRR_BASE | crate::vmx::mtrr::MemoryType::Uncacheable as u64;
    assert_eq!(physbase, 0x20_0000);
    assert!(GUEST_MTRR_BASE.is_multiple_of(SIZE_2M));

/// A supervisor, writable, executable 4 KiB page.
fn kernel_page() -> Mapping {
    Mapping {
        physical: 0x7eb1_9000,
        size: paging::PageSize::Size4K,
        writable: true,
        user: false,
        execute_disable: false,
    }
}

const SMEP_AND_SMAP: u64 = cr::CR4_SMEP | cr::CR4_SMAP;

#[test]
fn identity_mapped_page_passes() {
    assert_eq!(check_identity(0x7eb1_9000, &kernel_page()), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn page_mapped_elsewhere_is_refused() {
    assert_eq!(
        check_identity(0xffff_8000_7eb1_9000, &kernel_page()),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::NotIdentityMapped {
            virtual_address: 0xffff_8000_7eb1_9000,
            physical: 0x7eb1_9000,
        }),
    );
}

#[test]
fn kernel_pages_pass_even_with_smep_and_smap() {
    assert_eq!(check_permissions(&kernel_page(), &kernel_page(), SMEP_AND_SMAP), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn code_with_xd_is_refused() {
    let code = Mapping {
        execute_disable: true,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(
        check_permissions(&code, &kernel_page(), 0),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::CodeNotExecutable)
    );
}

#[test]
fn user_code_is_refused_only_under_smep() {
    let code = Mapping {
        user: true,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(check_permissions(&code, &kernel_page(), 0), Ok(()));
    assert_eq!(
        check_permissions(&code, &kernel_page(), cr::CR4_SMEP),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::CodeBlockedBySmep),
    );
}

#[test]
fn read_only_stack_is_refused() {
    let stack = Mapping {
        writable: false,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(
        check_permissions(&kernel_page(), &stack, 0),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::StackNotWritable)
    );
}

#[test]
fn user_stack_is_refused_only_under_smap() {
    let stack = Mapping {
        user: true,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(check_permissions(&kernel_page(), &stack, 0), Ok(()));
    assert_eq!(
        check_permissions(&kernel_page(), &stack, cr::CR4_SMAP),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::StackBlockedBySmap),
    );
}

#[test]
fn kernel_idt_passes_under_smap() {
    assert_eq!(check_idt_permissions(&kernel_page(), SMEP_AND_SMAP), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn writable_kernel_data_page_passes_under_smap() {
    assert_eq!(check_data_permissions(&kernel_page(), SMEP_AND_SMAP), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn read_only_data_page_is_refused() {
    let data = Mapping {
        writable: false,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(check_data_permissions(&data, 0), Err(GuestMemoryError::DataNotWritable));
}

#[test]
fn user_data_page_is_refused_only_under_smap() {
    let data = Mapping {
        user: true,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(check_data_permissions(&data, 0), Ok(()));
    assert_eq!(
        check_data_permissions(&data, cr::CR4_SMAP),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::DataBlockedBySmap)
    );
}

#[test]
fn user_idt_is_refused_only_under_smap() {
    let idt = Mapping {
        user: true,
        ..kernel_page()
    };
    assert_eq!(check_idt_permissions(&idt, 0), Ok(()));
    assert_eq!(
        check_idt_permissions(&idt, cr::CR4_SMAP),
        Err(GuestMemoryError::IdtBlockedBySmap)
    );
}

#[test]
fn expected_stats_keep_what_an_nmi_changes_and_nothing_else() {
    // A run with -InjectNmi: two more exits, one NMI injected.
    let with_nmi = VcpuStats {
        exits: 15,
        nmi_injections: 1,
        ..expected_stats(&VcpuStats::ZERO)
    };
    assert_eq!(expected_stats(&with_nmi), with_nmi);
    // A run whose HLT never exited, or that got a #GP it should not have.
    for wrong in [
        VcpuStats {
            halt_exits: 0,
            ..with_nmi
        },
        VcpuStats {
            exception_injections: 1,
            ..with_nmi
        },
    ] {
        assert_ne!(expected_stats(&wrong), wrong);
    }
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/guest_state.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/guest_state.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

const FLAT_CODE_64: u64 = 0x00AF_9B00_0000_FFFF;
/// Flat data descriptor with the accessed bit clear (type 0x2).
const FLAT_DATA_NOT_ACCESSED: u64 = 0x00CF_9200_0000_FFFF;
/// Busy 64-bit TSS descriptor, low 8 bytes: limit 0x67, type 0xB, P = 1.
const BUSY_TSS: u64 = 0x0000_8B00_0000_0067;

/// The Hyper-V firmware's IDT.
const FIRMWARE_IDT: DescriptorTable = DescriptorTable {
    base: 0x7f0a_4018,
    limit: 0xfff,
};

#[test]
fn the_test_guest_starts_at_its_code_with_interrupts_off_and_its_own_idt() {
    let idt = DescriptorTable {
        base: 0x7eae_e000,
        limit: 0x2f,
    };
    let entry = GuestEntry::At {
        rip: 0x7eae_c000,
        rsp: 0x7eae_f000,
        idtr: idt,
    };
    assert_eq!(entry.registers(), (0x7eae_c000, 0x7eae_f000, 0x2));
    assert_eq!(entry.idtr(), idt);
}

#[test]
fn in_place_keeps_the_firmware_idt_and_leaves_rip_rsp_and_rflags_to_vmlaunch() {
    let entry = GuestEntry::InPlace { idtr: FIRMWARE_IDT };
    // Placeholders: `launch_in_place` writes the real ones at VMLAUNCH.
    assert_eq!(entry.registers(), (0, 0, 0x2));
    assert_eq!(entry.idtr(), FIRMWARE_IDT);
}

#[test]
fn data_segment_gets_accessed_bit() {
    let segment = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x30, SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_DATA_NOT_ACCESSED), 0);
    assert_eq!(segment.access_rights, 0xC093);
    assert_eq!(segment.limit, 0xFFFF_FFFF);
}

#[test]
fn system_segment_type_is_left_alone() {
    // Bit 0 of a system type is not "accessed": type 0xA would be a
    // different descriptor kind, so it must not be touched.
    let segment = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x40, SegmentDescriptor(0x0000_8A00_0000_0067), 0x1000);
    assert_eq!(segment.access_rights, 0x008A);
}

#[test]
fn null_selector_is_unusable_but_keeps_base() {
    let segment = GuestSegment::unusable(0, 0xFFFF_8000_0000_0000);
    assert!(!segment.is_usable());
    assert_eq!(segment.base, 0xFFFF_8000_0000_0000);
}

#[test]
fn long_mode_cs_and_busy_tss_pass() {
    let cs = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x38, SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_CODE_64), 0);
    let tr = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x50, SegmentDescriptor(BUSY_TSS), 0x1000);
    assert_eq!(check_segments(&cs, &tr), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn compatibility_mode_cs_is_refused() {
    // Same code descriptor with L = 0, D/B = 1: 32-bit code.
    let cs = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x38, SegmentDescriptor(0x00CF_9B00_0000_FFFF), 0);
    let tr = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x50, SegmentDescriptor(BUSY_TSS), 0x1000);
    assert_eq!(
        check_segments(&cs, &tr),
        Err(GuestStateError::CsNot64Bit { access_rights: 0xC09B })
    );
}

#[test]
fn available_tss_is_refused() {
    // Type 0x9: a TSS that LTR has not marked busy.
    let cs = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x38, SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_CODE_64), 0);
    let tr = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x50, SegmentDescriptor(0x0000_8900_0000_0067), 0x1000);
    assert_eq!(
        check_segments(&cs, &tr),
        Err(GuestStateError::TrNotBusyTss { access_rights: 0x0089 })
    );
}

#[test]
fn unusable_tr_is_refused() {
    let cs = GuestSegment::from_descriptor(0x38, SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_CODE_64), 0);
    let tr = GuestSegment::unusable(0, 0);
    assert!(matches!(
        check_segments(&cs, &tr),
        Err(GuestStateError::TrNotBusyTss { .. })
    ));
}

#[test]
fn the_segment_table_lists_the_registers_in_the_sdm_order() {
    // The SDM numbers each kind of segment field ES, CS, SS, DS, FS, GS, LDTR,
    // TR, two apart; `GuestState::segments` lists the registers the same way.
    for (index, fields) in SEGMENT_FIELDS.iter().enumerate() {
        let step = 2 * index as u32;
        assert_eq!(fields.selector, fields::GUEST_ES_SELECTOR + step, "register {index}");
        assert_eq!(fields.base, fields::GUEST_ES_BASE + step, "register {index}");
        assert_eq!(fields.limit, fields::GUEST_ES_LIMIT + step, "register {index}");
        assert_eq!(
            fields.access_rights,
            fields::GUEST_ES_ACCESS_RIGHTS + step,
            "register {index}"
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(SEGMENT_FIELDS[1].selector, fields::GUEST_CS_SELECTOR);
    assert_eq!(SEGMENT_FIELDS[7].access_rights, fields::GUEST_TR_ACCESS_RIGHTS);
}

#[test]
fn a_segment_prints_as_the_guest_state_line_shows_it() {
    // The Hyper-V firmware's CS.
    let cs = GuestSegment {
        selector: 0x28,
        base: 0,
        limit: 0xffff_ffff,
        access_rights: 0xa09b,
    };
    assert_eq!(
        cs.to_string(),
        "selector=0x0028 base=0x0000000000000000 limit=0xffffffff access=0x0a09b"
    );
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/host/gdt.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/host/gdt.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::segment::{SegmentDescriptor, system_descriptor_base};

/// The selectors the Hyper-V firmware runs with.
const HYPER_V: FirmwareSelectors = FirmwareSelectors {
    cs: 0x28,
    ss: 0x08,
    ds: 0x08,
    es: 0x08,
    fs: 0x08,
    gs: 0x08,
};

/// A TSS base with a distinct byte in every position.
const TSS_BASE: u64 = 0x1122_3344_5566_7788;

fn encoded(layout: &GdtLayout) -> [u64; SLOTS] {
    let mut gdt = [u64::MAX; SLOTS];
    encode(layout, TSS_BASE, &mut gdt);
    gdt
}

#[test]
fn hyper_v_selectors_put_the_tss_after_the_code_descriptor() {
    let layout = layout(HYPER_V).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        layout.selectors,
        HostSelectors {
            cs: 0x28,
            ss: 0x08,
            ds: 0x08,
            es: 0x08,
            fs: 0x08,
            gs: 0x08,
            tr: 0x30,
        }
    );
    // Slots 0-7: the TSS takes 6 and 7.
    assert_eq!(layout.limit, 0x3F);
}

#[test]
fn every_slot_holds_what_its_selector_names() {
    let gdt = encoded(&layout(HYPER_V).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(gdt[0], 0, "null");
    assert_eq!(gdt[1], DATA);
    assert_eq!(gdt[2..5], [0; 3], "unused slots are null");
    assert_eq!(gdt[5], CODE_64);
    let tss: [u8; 16] = [gdt[6].to_le_bytes(), gdt[7].to_le_bytes()]
        .concat()
        .try_into()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(system_descriptor_base(&tss), TSS_BASE);
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(gdt[6]).limit(), 0x67);
    assert!(gdt[8..].iter().all(|&slot| slot == 0), "nothing past the TSS");
}

#[test]
fn code_descriptor_is_flat_64_bit_ring_0() {
    let code = SegmentDescriptor(CODE_64);
    // VMCS access-rights format: G = 1, L = 1, P = 1, DPL 0, S = 1, type
    // 0xB. What the Hyper-V firmware's CS shows, accessed bit included.
    assert_eq!(code.access_rights(), 0xA09B);
    assert_eq!(code.base(), 0);
    assert_eq!(code.limit(), 0xFFFF_FFFF);
}

#[test]
fn data_descriptor_is_flat_read_write_ring_0() {
    let data = SegmentDescriptor(DATA);
    // G = 1, D/B = 1, P = 1, DPL 0, S = 1, type 0x3: the Hyper-V
    // firmware's data segments.
    assert_eq!(data.access_rights(), 0xC093);
    assert_eq!(data.base(), 0);
    assert_eq!(data.limit(), 0xFFFF_FFFF);
}

#[test]
fn null_data_selectors_stay_null() {
    let firmware = FirmwareSelectors {
        fs: 0,
        gs: 0,
        ..HYPER_V
    };
    let layout = layout(firmware).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((layout.selectors.fs, layout.selectors.gs), (0, 0));
    let gdt = encoded(&layout);
    assert_eq!(gdt[0], 0, "a null selector writes no descriptor");
}

#[test]
fn each_distinct_data_selector_gets_a_data_descriptor() {
    let firmware = FirmwareSelectors {
        ss: 0x30,
        ds: 0x10,
        ..HYPER_V
    };
    let layout = layout(firmware).unwrap();
    // The TSS goes above the highest slot used, here SS's.
    assert_eq!(layout.selectors.tr, 0x38);
    let gdt = encoded(&layout);
    assert_eq!((gdt[1], gdt[2], gdt[6]), (DATA, DATA, DATA));
    assert_eq!(gdt[5], CODE_64);
}

#[test]
fn a_null_code_selector_is_refused() {
    let firmware = FirmwareSelectors { cs: 0, ..HYPER_V };
    assert_eq!(layout(firmware), Err(GdtLayoutError::NullCode));
}

#[test]
fn a_selector_with_rpl_or_ti_set_is_refused() {
    for selector in [0x0B, 0x0C] {
        let firmware = FirmwareSelectors {
            ds: selector,
            ..HYPER_V
        };
        assert_eq!(layout(firmware), Err(GdtLayoutError::NotRing0Gdt { selector }));
    }
}

#[test]
fn data_in_the_code_slot_is_refused() {
    let firmware = FirmwareSelectors { ss: 0x28, ..HYPER_V };
    assert_eq!(layout(firmware), Err(GdtLayoutError::DataInCodeSlot { selector: 0x28 }));
}

#[test]
fn a_gdt_past_one_page_is_refused() {
    // Slot 510 leaves one slot, but the TSS needs two.
    let firmware = FirmwareSelectors { cs: 510 * 8, ..HYPER_V };
    assert_eq!(layout(firmware), Err(GdtLayoutError::TooLarge));
    let firmware = FirmwareSelectors { cs: 509 * 8, ..HYPER_V };
    assert_eq!(layout(firmware).map(|layout| layout.limit), Ok(4095));
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/host/handlers.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/host/handlers.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items. The fault stubs are assembled into the test binary too,
//! so their bytes are checked here.

use super::*;

/// The bytes a stub starts with: `push $0` when the CPU pushes no error
/// code, then `push $vector`, as a sign-extended byte below 128 and a
/// 32-bit immediate from 128 on.
fn expected_prefix(vector: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    if !has_error_code(vector) {
        bytes.extend([0x6A, 0x00]);
    }
    if vector < 128 {
        bytes.extend([0x6A, vector]);
    } else {
        bytes.extend([0x68, vector, 0, 0, 0]);
    }
    bytes
}

#[test]
fn every_stub_pushes_its_error_code_slot_and_vector() {
    let stubs = stubs();
    for vector in 0..=u8::MAX {
        let start = usize::from(vector) * STUB_SIZE as usize;
        let prefix = expected_prefix(vector);
        assert_eq!(
            &stubs[start..start + prefix.len()],
            prefix.as_slice(),
            "stub of vector {vector}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn every_stub_then_jumps_to_the_common_part() {
    let stubs = stubs();
    for vector in 0..=u8::MAX {
        let start = usize::from(vector) * STUB_SIZE as usize;
        let jump = stubs[start + expected_prefix(vector).len()];
        // JMP rel8 or JMP rel32.
        assert!(matches!(jump, 0xEB | 0xE9), "stub of vector {vector}: {jump:#04x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn gates_point_at_the_nmi_entry_and_the_fault_stubs() {
    assert_eq!(handler_address(NMI_VECTOR), host_nmi_entry as *const () as u64);
    let stubs = (&raw const host_vector_stubs) as u64;
    assert_eq!(handler_address(0), stubs);
    assert_eq!(handler_address(13), stubs + 13 * 16);
    assert_eq!(handler_address(255), stubs + 255 * 16);
}

#[test]
fn a_pending_nmi_is_taken_once() {
    NMI_PENDING.store(true, Ordering::Release);
    assert!(nmi_pending());
    assert!(take_pending_nmi());
    assert!(!nmi_pending());
    assert!(!take_pending_nmi());
}

#[test]
fn the_exception_frame_matches_what_the_stubs_and_the_cpu_push() {
    // The stub's two pushes, then the CPU's five, lowest address first.
    assert_eq!(core::mem::size_of::<ExceptionFrame>(), 7 * 8);
    assert_eq!(core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionFrame, error_code), 8);
    assert_eq!(core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionFrame, rip), 16);
    assert_eq!(core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionFrame, ss), 48);
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/host/idt.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/host/idt.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

/// Made-up handler addresses: 16 bytes apart, like the fault stubs.
fn handler(vector: u8) -> u64 {
    0x7e00_0000 + u64::from(vector) * 16
}

fn filled() -> Box<[[u8; GATE_SIZE]; VECTORS]> {
    let mut idt = Box::new([[0xAA; GATE_SIZE]; VECTORS]);
    fill(&mut idt, 0x28, handler);
    idt
}

#[test]
fn nmi_double_fault_and_machine_check_have_stacks_of_their_own() {
    assert_eq!(interrupt_stack(2), Some(InterruptStack::Nmi));
    assert_eq!(interrupt_stack(8), Some(InterruptStack::DoubleFault));
    assert_eq!(interrupt_stack(18), Some(InterruptStack::MachineCheck));
    for vector in (0..=u8::MAX).filter(|vector| ![2, 8, 18].contains(vector)) {
        assert_eq!(interrupt_stack(vector), None, "vector {vector}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn each_interrupt_stack_has_its_own_ist_number() {
    let ists = InterruptStack::ALL.map(InterruptStack::ist);
    assert_eq!(ists, [1, 2, 3]);
}

#[test]
fn every_gate_points_to_its_handler_through_the_code_selector() {
    let idt = filled();
    for vector in 0..=u8::MAX {
        let ist = interrupt_stack(vector).map_or(0, InterruptStack::ist);
        assert_eq!(
            idt[usize::from(vector)],
            interrupt_gate(handler(vector), 0x28, ist),
            "vector {vector}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_gates_name_their_ist_in_byte_4() {
    let idt = filled();
    assert_eq!(idt[2][4], 1, "NMI on IST1");
    assert_eq!(idt[8][4], 2, "#DF on IST2");
    assert_eq!(idt[18][4], 3, "#MC on IST3");
    assert_eq!(idt[14][4], 0, "#PF on the current stack");
}

#[test]
fn exactly_the_architectural_vectors_have_an_error_code() {
    let with_code: Vec<u8> = (0..=u8::MAX).filter(|&vector| has_error_code(vector)).collect();
    assert_eq!(with_code, [8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 21, 29, 30]);
}

#[test]
fn exceptions_are_named_by_mnemonic() {
    assert_eq!(exception_name(13), "#GP general protection");
    assert_eq!(exception_name(14), "#PF page fault");
    assert_eq!(exception_name(2), "NMI");
    assert_eq!(exception_name(15), "reserved exception");
    assert_eq!(exception_name(31), "reserved exception");
    assert_eq!(exception_name(32), "interrupt");
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/host/page_tables.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/host/page_tables.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.
//!
//! The tables are built in vectors at made-up physical addresses, then
//! walked with `paging::walk`, the same walker bring-up runs on the
//! firmware's tables, so the tests check what the CPU would resolve.

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::ept::SIZE_2M;
use crate::vmx::paging::{self, Mapping};

/// Made-up physical addresses of the tables: the PML4, the PDPT, then the
/// PDs back to back.
const PML4: u64 = 0x10_0000;
const PDPT: u64 = 0x10_1000;
const PDS: u64 = 0x10_2000;

/// A map of `gibs` GiB in `page_size` pages, filled by `fill_identity_map`.
struct Built {
    pml4: Vec<HostEntry<Pml4>>,
    pdpt: Vec<HostEntry<Pdpt>>,
    pds: Vec<HostEntry<Pd>>,
}

impl Built {
    fn new(gibs: usize, page_size: PageSize) -> Self {
        let pd_pages = table_pages(gibs, page_size) - 2;
        let mut built = Self {
            pml4: vec![HostEntry::from_raw(0); ENTRIES],
            pdpt: vec![HostEntry::from_raw(0); ENTRIES],
            pds: vec![HostEntry::from_raw(0); pd_pages * ENTRIES],
        };
        let tables = Tables {
            pml4: &mut built.pml4,
            pdpt: &mut built.pdpt,
            pds: &mut built.pds,
            pdpt_address: PDPT,
            pds_address: PDS,
        };
        fill_identity_map(tables, gibs, page_size);
        built
    }

    /// The entry at physical address `address`, as the walker reads it.
    fn read(&self, address: u64) -> u64 {
        let index = |base: u64| ((address - base) / 8) as usize;
        match address {
            PML4..PDPT => self.pml4[index(PML4)].raw,
            PDPT..PDS => self.pdpt[index(PDPT)].raw,
            _ => self.pds[index(PDS)].raw,
        }
    }

    fn walk(&self, address: u64) -> Result<Mapping, paging::WalkError> {
        paging::walk(PML4, address, |entry| self.read(entry))
    }
}

/// Addresses across a 4 GiB map: both ends of the first page and of each
/// GiB, and one inside a 2 MiB page.
const SAMPLES: [u64; 7] = [
    0,
    0xFFF,
    0x7eb1_9123,
    SIZE_1G - 1,
    SIZE_1G,
    3 * SIZE_1G + 5 * SIZE_2M + 0x42,
    4 * SIZE_1G - 1,
];

/// Checks that `mapping`, the walk of `address`, maps it to itself and lets
/// the ring-0 host read, write and execute it.
fn assert_identity(address: u64, mapping: Mapping, size: paging::PageSize) {
    assert_eq!(mapping.physical, address, "{address:#x} maps to itself");
    assert_eq!(mapping.size, size);
    assert!(mapping.writable, "{address:#x} writable");
    assert!(!mapping.user, "{address:#x} supervisor only");
    assert!(
        !mapping.execute_disable,
        "{address:#x} executable whatever EFER.NXE says"
    );
}

#[test]
fn one_gib_pages_map_every_address_to_itself() {
    let built = Built::new(4, PageSize::Huge1G);
    for address in SAMPLES {
        assert_identity(address, built.walk(address).unwrap(), paging::PageSize::Size1G);
    }
}

#[test]
fn two_mib_pages_map_every_address_to_itself() {
    let built = Built::new(4, PageSize::Large2M);
    for address in SAMPLES {
        assert_identity(address, built.walk(address).unwrap(), paging::PageSize::Size2M);
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_map_ends_at_its_last_gib() {
    for page_size in [PageSize::Huge1G, PageSize::Large2M] {
        let built = Built::new(4, page_size);
        assert_eq!(
            built.walk(4 * SIZE_1G),
            Err(paging::WalkError::NotPresent { level: 3 }),
            "{page_size:?}: no PDPT entry past the end"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn only_the_first_pml4_entry_is_used() {
    let built = Built::new(512, PageSize::Huge1G);
    assert_eq!(built.pml4[0], HostEntry::table(PDPT));
    assert!(built.pml4[1..].iter().all(|entry| entry.raw == 0));
}

#[test]
fn one_gib_pages_need_no_pds() {
    assert_eq!(table_pages(2, PageSize::Huge1G), 2);
    assert_eq!(table_pages(512, PageSize::Huge1G), 2);
    assert!(Built::new(2, PageSize::Huge1G).pds.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn two_mib_pages_need_a_pd_per_gib() {
    assert_eq!(table_pages(2, PageSize::Large2M), 4);
    let built = Built::new(2, PageSize::Large2M);
    // The second GiB's PD is the second page after PDS.
    assert_eq!(built.pdpt[1], HostEntry::table(PDS + 0x1000));
    // PD entry 513 across both PDs: the second GiB's second 2 MiB page.
    assert_eq!(built.pds[513], HostEntry::large_page(SIZE_1G + SIZE_2M));
}

#[test]
fn table_entries_are_present_writable_and_accessed() {
    // P (bit 0), R/W (bit 1), A (bit 5); U/S (bit 2) and XD (bit 63) clear.
    assert_eq!(HostEntry::<Pml4>::table(0x7000).raw, 0x7000 | 0x23);
}

#[test]
fn large_pages_are_dirty_and_have_ps_set() {
    // As tables, plus D (bit 6) and PS (bit 7); PAT, PCD and PWT 0 (WB).
    assert_eq!(HostEntry::<Pdpt>::huge_page(SIZE_1G).raw, SIZE_1G | 0xE3);
    assert_eq!(HostEntry::<Pd>::large_page(SIZE_2M).raw, SIZE_2M | 0xE3);
}

#[test]
fn the_end_must_be_whole_gibs_up_to_one_pdpt() {
    assert_eq!(gibs(SIZE_1G), Ok(1));
    assert_eq!(gibs(PDPT_SPAN), Ok(512));
    for end in [0, SIZE_1G + SIZE_2M, PDPT_SPAN + SIZE_1G] {
        assert_eq!(gibs(end), Err(HostPagingError::InvalidEnd { end }));
    }
}

#[test]
fn five_level_paging_is_refused() {
    assert_eq!(check_paging_mode(CR4_LA57), Err(HostPagingError::FiveLevelPaging));
    // The CR4 the Hyper-V firmware runs with (no LA57).
    assert_eq!(check_paging_mode(0x2668), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn page_size_follows_the_cpu() {
    assert_eq!(PageSize::for_cpu(true), PageSize::Huge1G);
    assert_eq!(PageSize::for_cpu(false), PageSize::Large2M);
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/hyperv.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/hyperv.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items. The forwarders are assembled into the test binary too, so
//! the recovery points are checked against their bytes.

use super::*;

/// CPUID.1:ECX as Hyper-V showed it to Aleph0 (ROADMAP.md), bit 31 set.
const HYPERV_LEAF1_ECX: u32 = 0xf7fa_3223;
/// CPUID.40000000H:EAX, the highest hypervisor leaf, as Hyper-V showed it
/// to Aleph0 (docs/HYPERV_INTERFACE.md).
const HYPERV_MAX_LEAF: u32 = 0x4000_000B;

#[test]
fn hyper_v_offers_its_interface() {
    assert!(offers_interface(HYPERV_LEAF1_ECX, HYPERV_MAX_LEAF, INTERFACE_SIGNATURE));
    assert_eq!(INTERFACE_SIGNATURE, 0x3123_7648);
}

#[test]
fn no_interface_without_the_hypervisor_present_bit() {
    // Bare metal: leaves from 0x40000000 answer with the highest basic leaf's
    // data, which could hold anything.
    assert!(!offers_interface(
        HYPERV_LEAF1_ECX & !(1 << 31),
        HYPERV_MAX_LEAF,
        INTERFACE_SIGNATURE
    ));
}

#[test]
fn no_interface_when_the_interface_leaf_is_past_the_highest() {
    assert!(!offers_interface(HYPERV_LEAF1_ECX, VENDOR_LEAF, INTERFACE_SIGNATURE));
}

#[test]
fn no_interface_for_another_signature() {
    // Another hypervisor's interface leaf, or none: "Hv#0", 0.
    for interface in [u32::from_le_bytes(*b"Hv#0"), 0] {
        assert!(!offers_interface(HYPERV_LEAF1_ECX, HYPERV_MAX_LEAF, interface));
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_vendor_reads_ebx_ecx_edx() {
    let detection = Detection {
        leaf1_ecx: HYPERV_LEAF1_ECX,
        vendor: CpuidResult {
            eax: HYPERV_MAX_LEAF,
            ebx: 0x7263_694D,
            ecx: 0x666F_736F,
            edx: 0x7648_2074,
        },
        interface: INTERFACE_SIGNATURE,
    };
    assert_eq!(&detection.vendor_bytes(), b"Microsoft Hv");
    assert!(detection.offers_interface());
}

#[test]
fn the_call_code_is_bits_15_to_0() {
    // HvCallPostMessage (0x5c), fast, with a rep count of 2.
    assert_eq!(call_code(0x0000_0002_0001_005C), 0x5C);
}

#[test]
fn the_synthetic_range_covers_hyper_v_and_nothing_in_the_bitmap() {
    use crate::vmx::exit_bitmaps::{MsrAccess, msr_bit};
    // Guest OS ID, the reference counter, TSC invariant control, the
    // nested SynIC control.
    for msr in [0x4000_0000, 0x4000_0020, 0x4000_0118, 0x4000_1080] {
        assert!(SYNTHETIC_MSRS.contains(&msr), "{msr:#x}");
    }
    for msr in [0x3FFF_FFFF, 0x4001_0000] {
        assert!(!SYNTHETIC_MSRS.contains(&msr), "{msr:#x}");
    }
    // Every one of them exits, whatever the bitmap says.
    for msr in [*SYNTHETIC_MSRS.start(), *SYNTHETIC_MSRS.end()] {
        assert_eq!(msr_bit(msr, MsrAccess::Read), None);
    }
}

/// The address of a forwarder's label.
fn address(label: *const u8) -> u64 {
    label as u64
}

#[test]
fn each_forwarding_instruction_recovers_from_its_own_exception() {
    for (instruction, vector, refused) in [
        (
            &raw const hyperv_hypercall_instruction,
            INVALID_OPCODE,
            &raw const hyperv_hypercall_refused,
        ),
        (
            &raw const hyperv_rdmsr_instruction,
            GENERAL_PROTECTION,
            &raw const hyperv_rdmsr_refused,
        ),
        (
            &raw const hyperv_wrmsr_instruction,
            GENERAL_PROTECTION,
            &raw const hyperv_wrmsr_refused,
        ),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(recovery(address(instruction), vector), Some(address(refused)));
        // Any other exception there is still a bug, and so is the right
        // exception one byte off.
        let other = if vector == INVALID_OPCODE {
            GENERAL_PROTECTION
        } else {
            INVALID_OPCODE
        };
        assert_eq!(recovery(address(instruction), other), None);
        assert_eq!(recovery(address(instruction) + 1, vector), None);
        assert_eq!(recovery(address(refused), vector), None);
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_recovery_elsewhere() {
    assert_eq!(recovery(0, GENERAL_PROTECTION), None);
    assert_eq!(recovery(recovery as *const () as u64, INVALID_OPCODE), None);
}

#[test]
fn the_recovery_points_sit_on_the_instructions() {
    // VMCALL is 0F 01 C1, RDMSR 0F 32, WRMSR 0F 30: the RIP the CPU reports
    // for the fault is the label's.
    // SAFETY: each label is in the forwarders' assembled code, which is in
    // the test binary's text for as long as it runs and never written; each
    // instruction is at least as long as the bytes read.
    let (vmcall, rdmsr, wrmsr) = unsafe {
        (
            *(&raw const hyperv_hypercall_instruction).cast::<[u8; 3]>(),
            *(&raw const hyperv_rdmsr_instruction).cast::<[u8; 2]>(),
            *(&raw const hyperv_wrmsr_instruction).cast::<[u8; 2]>(),
        )
    };
    assert_eq!(vmcall, [0x0F, 0x01, 0xC1]);
    assert_eq!(rdmsr, [0x0F, 0x32]);
    assert_eq!(wrmsr, [0x0F, 0x30]);
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/instruction.rs`.

//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with

use super::*;

const CF: u64 = 1 << 0;
const ZF: u64 = 1 << 6;
/// RFLAGS bit 1 always reads as 1.

#[test]

    assert_eq!(check_rflags(RESERVED), Ok(()));

    assert_eq!(check_rflags(RESERVED | ZF), Err(VmxFail::Valid));
}

#[test]

    assert_eq!(check_rflags(CF | ZF), Err(VmxFail::Invalid));
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/msr.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/msr.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

/// Build a capability MSR from its required (low) and allowed (high) halves.
fn capability(required: u32, allowed: u32) -> ControlCapability {
    ControlCapability((u64::from(allowed) << 32) | u64::from(required))
}

#[test]
fn halves_split_required_and_allowed() {
    let capability = capability(0x16, 0x8000_00FF);
    assert_eq!(capability.required(), 0x16);
    assert_eq!(capability.allowed(), 0x8000_00FF);
}

#[test]
fn allows_needs_every_bit() {
    let capability = capability(0, 0b0110);
    assert!(capability.allows(0b0010));
    assert!(capability.allows(0b0110));
    assert!(!capability.allows(0b0001));
    assert!(!capability.allows(0b0011), "one allowed bit is not enough");
}

#[test]
fn required_bits_are_added() {
    assert_eq!(capability(0x16, 0xFF).choose(0), Ok(0x16));
}

#[test]
fn allowed_desired_bits_are_kept() {
    assert_eq!(capability(0x16, 0xFFFF).choose(0x200), Ok(0x216));
}

#[test]
fn desired_bit_not_allowed_is_rejected() {
    assert_eq!(capability(0x16, 0xFF).choose(0x200), Err(UnsupportedControl));
}

#[test]
fn required_bit_not_allowed_is_rejected() {
    // (low, high) = (1, 0) is inconsistent: required but not allowed.
    assert_eq!(capability(0x1, 0x0).choose(0), Err(UnsupportedControl));
}
```
