`tests/unit/vmx/mtrr.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/mtrr/mod.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items. The helpers that build MSR values are `pub(crate)`, for
//! the EPT tests.

use super::MemoryType::{Uncacheable as UC, WriteBack as WB, WriteCombining as WC, WriteThrough as WT};
use super::*;
use crate::vmx::ept::{SIZE_1G, SIZE_2M};

/// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE with the MTRRs enabled, fixed ranges off, and
/// `default` as the default type.
pub(crate) fn enabled(default: MemoryType) -> u64 {
    DEF_TYPE_ENABLE | default.raw()
}

/// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE with the MTRRs and the fixed ranges enabled, and
/// `default` as the default type.
pub(crate) fn enabled_with_fixed(default: MemoryType) -> u64 {
    enabled(default) | DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE
}

/// The PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK pair of a valid range of `size` bytes (a power of
/// two) at `base`, on a CPU with 39 physical-address bits.
pub(crate) fn range(base: u64, size: u64, memory_type: MemoryType) -> (u64, u64) {
    let mask = ((1 << 39) - 1) & !(size - 1);
    (base | memory_type.raw(), mask | PHYSMASK_VALID)
}

/// MTRRs with `default` and the variable ranges `variable`, no fixed ones.
fn mtrrs(default: MemoryType, variable: &[(u64, u64)]) -> Mtrrs {
    Mtrrs::decode(enabled(default), None, variable).unwrap()
}

/// The ranges of MTRRs that are on; panics if they are not.
fn as_enabled(mtrrs: &Mtrrs) -> &EnabledMtrrs {
    let Mtrrs::Enabled(enabled) = mtrrs else {
        panic!("MTRRs not enabled: {mtrrs:?}");
    };
    enabled
}

/// Every byte of a fixed-range MSR set to `memory_type`.
fn fixed_all(memory_type: MemoryType) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes([memory_type.raw() as u8; 8])
}

/// The usual first MiB: RAM (WB) up to 0xA0000, the legacy VGA window
/// 0xA0000..0xC0000 UC, then the option ROMs and BIOS 0xC0000..0x100000 WP.
pub(crate) fn pc_fixed() -> [u64; FIXED_MSRS] {
    let mut fixed = [fixed_all(MemoryType::WriteProtected); FIXED_MSRS];
    fixed[0] = fixed_all(WB);
    fixed[1] = fixed_all(WB);
    fixed[2] = fixed_all(UC);
    fixed
}

#[test]
fn only_the_five_architectural_types_decode() {
    for (value, memory_type) in [
        (0, Some(UC)),
        (1, Some(WC)),
        (2, None),
        (3, None),
        (4, Some(WT)),
        (5, Some(MemoryType::WriteProtected)),
        (6, Some(WB)),
        (7, None),
        (0xFF, None),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(MemoryType::from_raw(value), memory_type, "type {value}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn types_encode_as_the_sdm_numbers_them() {
    assert_eq!(UC.raw(), 0);
    assert_eq!(WC.raw(), 1);
    assert_eq!(WT.raw(), 4);
    assert_eq!(MemoryType::WriteProtected.raw(), 5);
    assert_eq!(WB.raw(), 6);
    assert_eq!(WB.name(), "WB");
}

#[test]
fn disabled_mtrrs_make_everything_uncacheable() {
    // E clear: the default type, the fixed and the variable ranges are all
    // ignored, even a reserved type in them.
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(
        DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE | WB.raw(),
        Some([fixed_all(WB); FIXED_MSRS]),
        &[(7, PHYSMASK_VALID)],
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mtrrs, Mtrrs::Disabled);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x7eb0_1000), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0, SIZE_2M), Some(UC));
}

#[test]
fn without_mtrrs_everything_is_write_back() {
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::Unsupported;
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xA_0000), WB);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xFEE0_0000), WB);
}

#[test]
fn an_address_no_range_covers_gets_the_default_type() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[range(0, 2 * SIZE_1G, WB)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x7FFF_F000), WB);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(2 * SIZE_1G), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xFEE0_0000), UC);
}

#[test]
fn a_range_without_the_valid_bit_is_ignored() {
    let (base, mask) = range(0, 2 * SIZE_1G, WB);
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[(base, mask & !PHYSMASK_VALID)]);
    assert_eq!(as_enabled(&mtrrs).variable_count(), 1);
    assert!(as_enabled(&mtrrs).variable_ranges().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x1000_0000), UC);
}

#[test]
fn ranges_keep_their_number_base_mask_and_type() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(
        UC,
        &[(0, 0), range(0x8000_0000, 0x1000_0000, WC), range(0, SIZE_1G, WB)],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        as_enabled(&mtrrs).variable_ranges(),
        [
            VariableRange {
                number: 1,
                base: 0x8000_0000,
                mask: 0x7F_F000_0000,
                memory_type: WC,
            },
            VariableRange {
                number: 2,
                base: 0,
                mask: 0x7F_C000_0000,
                memory_type: WB,
            },
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn uncacheable_wins_an_overlap() {
    // A UC hole for MMIO inside a WB range, the common firmware layout.
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(WB, &[range(0, 4 * SIZE_1G, WB), range(0xC000_0000, SIZE_1G, UC)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xBFFF_F000), WB);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xC000_0000), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xFEE0_0000), UC);
}

#[test]
fn write_through_wins_over_write_back() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[range(0, SIZE_1G, WB), range(0, SIZE_2M, WT)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x1000), WT);
}

#[test]
fn an_undefined_overlap_is_uncacheable() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(WB, &[range(0, SIZE_1G, WC), range(0, SIZE_2M, WT)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x1000), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(SIZE_2M), WC);
}

#[test]
fn three_overlapping_ranges_combine_the_same_in_any_order() {
    for ([a, b, c], expected) in [
        ([WT, WB, WB], WT),
        ([WB, WT, UC], UC),
        ([WC, WC, WB], UC),
        ([WB, WB, WB], WB),
    ] {
        for order in [[a, b, c], [a, c, b], [b, a, c], [b, c, a], [c, a, b], [c, b, a]] {
            let variable = order.map(|memory_type| range(0, SIZE_2M, memory_type));
            assert_eq!(mtrrs(WB, &variable).memory_type(0x1000), expected, "{order:?}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn identical_overlapping_types_stay() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[range(0, SIZE_1G, WC), range(0, SIZE_2M, WC)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x1000), WC);
}

#[test]
fn the_fixed_ranges_decide_the_first_mib() {
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(UC), Some(pc_fixed()), &[range(0, SIZE_1G, WB)]).unwrap();
    assert!(as_enabled(&mtrrs).fixed_enabled());
    // The variable range covers all of these too; the fixed ranges win.
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0x9_F000), WB);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xA_0000), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xB_F000), UC);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xC_0000), MemoryType::WriteProtected);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(0xF_F000), MemoryType::WriteProtected);
    // From 1 MiB on, the variable ranges again.
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.memory_type(FIXED_END), WB);
}

#[test]
fn each_fixed_range_reads_its_own_byte() {
    // Byte n of each MSR holds type 6 for n even, 0 for n odd.
    let alternating = u64::from_le_bytes([6, 0, 6, 0, 6, 0, 6, 0]);
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(UC), Some([alternating; FIXED_MSRS]), &[]).unwrap();
    for (msr, start, size) in FIXED_RANGES {
        for n in 0..8 {
            let expected = if n % 2 == 0 { WB } else { UC };
            for address in [start + n * size, start + (n + 1) * size - PAGE_SIZE as u64] {
                assert_eq!(
                    mtrrs.memory_type(address),
                    expected,
                    "MSR {msr:#x} range {n} at {address:#x}"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn fixed_ranges_are_ignored_while_disabled_or_missing() {
    let disabled = Mtrrs::decode(enabled(WB), Some([fixed_all(UC); FIXED_MSRS]), &[]).unwrap();
    assert!(!as_enabled(&disabled).fixed_enabled());
    assert_eq!(disabled.memory_type(0xA_0000), WB);

    let missing = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(WB), None, &[]).unwrap();
    assert!(!as_enabled(&missing).fixed_enabled());
    assert_eq!(missing.memory_type(0xA_0000), WB);
}

#[test]
fn a_reserved_type_in_use_is_refused_with_its_msr() {
    assert_eq!(
        Mtrrs::decode(DEF_TYPE_ENABLE | 2, None, &[]),
        Err(MtrrError::ReservedType {
            msr: IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE,
            value: 2
        })
    );

    let mut fixed = [fixed_all(WB); FIXED_MSRS];
    fixed[4] = u64::from_le_bytes([6, 6, 6, 7, 6, 6, 6, 6]);
    assert_eq!(
        Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(WB), Some(fixed), &[]),
        Err(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr: 0x269, value: 7 })
    );

    assert_eq!(
        Mtrrs::decode(enabled(WB), None, &[(0, 0), (3, PHYSMASK_VALID)]),
        Err(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr: 0x202, value: 3 })
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_reserved_type_out_of_use_is_accepted() {
    // A disabled fixed range and an invalid variable range: the CPU never
    // reads their types.
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled(WB), Some([fixed_all(UC) | 2; FIXED_MSRS]), &[(3, 0)]);
    assert!(mtrrs.is_ok());
}

#[test]
fn more_variable_ranges_than_kept_are_refused() {
    let variable = [(0, 0); MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES + 1];
    assert_eq!(
        Mtrrs::decode(enabled(WB), None, &variable),
        Err(MtrrError::TooManyVariableRanges {
            count: MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES + 1
        })
    );
    assert!(Mtrrs::decode(enabled(WB), None, &variable[..MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES]).is_ok());
}

#[test]
fn a_block_inside_one_range_has_its_type() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[range(0, 2 * SIZE_1G, WB)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0x4000_0000, SIZE_2M), Some(WB));
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(2 * SIZE_1G, SIZE_2M), Some(UC));
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0, SIZE_1G), Some(WB));
}

#[test]
fn a_block_a_range_covers_in_part_is_mixed() {
    // A 1 MiB UC range in the upper half of the 2 MiB block at 0x7FE0_0000.
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[range(0, 2 * SIZE_1G, WB), range(0x7FF0_0000, 0x10_0000, UC)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0x7FE0_0000, SIZE_2M), None);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0x7FC0_0000, SIZE_2M), Some(WB));
    // The same range, looked at in 4 KiB blocks, has one type per block.
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0x7FEF_F000, PAGE_SIZE as u64), Some(WB));
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0x7FF0_0000, PAGE_SIZE as u64), Some(UC));
}

#[test]
fn a_small_range_elsewhere_leaves_a_block_uniform() {
    // The UC range's mask tests bits inside a 2 MiB block, but its upper
    // bits do not match this block, so it covers none of it.
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(UC, &[range(0, 2 * SIZE_1G, WB), range(0x7FF0_0000, 0x10_0000, UC)]);
    let small = as_enabled(&mtrrs).variable_ranges()[1];
    assert!(small.may_split(0x7FE0_0000, SIZE_2M));
    assert!(!small.may_split(0x4000_0000, SIZE_2M));
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0x4000_0000, SIZE_2M), Some(WB));
}

#[test]
fn a_partial_range_of_the_same_type_leaves_a_block_uniform() {
    let mtrrs = mtrrs(WB, &[range(0x10_0000, 0x10_0000, WB)]);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0, SIZE_2M), Some(WB));
}

#[test]
fn the_first_block_is_mixed_when_the_fixed_ranges_differ() {
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(WB), Some(pc_fixed()), &[]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0, SIZE_2M), None);
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(SIZE_2M, SIZE_2M), Some(WB));
}

#[test]
fn the_first_block_is_uniform_when_the_fixed_ranges_agree() {
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(WB), Some([fixed_all(WB); FIXED_MSRS]), &[]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mtrrs.block_type(0, SIZE_2M), Some(WB));
}

#[test]
fn runs_merge_blocks_of_the_same_type() {
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(
        enabled_with_fixed(UC),
        Some(pc_fixed()),
        &[range(0, 2 * SIZE_1G, WB), range(0x7FF0_0000, 0x10_0000, UC)],
    )
    .unwrap();
    let runs: Vec<_> = mtrrs.runs(4 * SIZE_1G, SIZE_2M).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        runs,
        [
            TypeRun {
                start: 0,
                end: SIZE_2M,
                memory_type: None,
            },
            TypeRun {
                start: SIZE_2M,
                end: 0x7FE0_0000,
                memory_type: Some(WB),
            },
            TypeRun {
                start: 0x7FE0_0000,
                end: 2 * SIZE_1G,
                memory_type: None,
            },
            TypeRun {
                start: 2 * SIZE_1G,
                end: 4 * SIZE_1G,
                memory_type: Some(UC),
            },
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn runs_in_4k_blocks_show_the_fixed_ranges() {
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(UC), Some(pc_fixed()), &[]).unwrap();
    let runs: Vec<_> = mtrrs
        .runs(FIXED_END, PAGE_SIZE as u64)
        .map(|run| (run.start, run.end, run.memory_type))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        runs,
        [
            (0, 0xA_0000, Some(WB)),
            (0xA_0000, 0xC_0000, Some(UC)),
            (0xC_0000, FIXED_END, Some(MemoryType::WriteProtected)),
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn no_runs_for_an_empty_span() {
    assert_eq!(mtrrs(WB, &[]).runs(0, SIZE_2M).count(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn mtrrs_print_as_bring_up_reports_them() {
    assert_eq!(
        Mtrrs::Unsupported.to_string(),
        "not supported (CPUID); all memory is treated as WB"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        Mtrrs::Disabled.to_string(),
        "disabled (IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.E=0); all memory is UC"
    );
    // Hyper-V's layout: eight variable ranges, the first making 4 GiB WB.
    let mut variable = [(0, 0); 8];
    variable[0] = range(0, 4 * SIZE_1G, WB);
    let mtrrs = Mtrrs::decode(enabled_with_fixed(UC), Some(pc_fixed()), &variable).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        mtrrs.to_string(),
        "enabled, default type UC; fixed ranges enabled; 8 variable ranges, 1 in use"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        as_enabled(&mtrrs).variable_ranges()[0].to_string(),
        "variable range 0: base=0x000000000000 mask=0x007f00000000 WB"
    );
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/mtrr/registers.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::mtrr::MemoryType::{self, Uncacheable as UC, WriteBack as WB};

/// IA32_MTRRCAP of the Hyper-V VM: eight variable ranges, the fixed ranges,
/// and WC (bit 10), which nothing here reads.
const HYPER_V_MTRRCAP: u64 = (1 << 10) | CAP_FIXED | 8;
/// MAXPHYADDR of the Hyper-V VM: its PHYSMASK0 stops at bit 45.
const HYPER_V_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 46;

/// IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE as Hyper-V's firmware leaves it: MTRRs and fixed
/// ranges on, default type UC.
const HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE: u64 = DEF_TYPE_ENABLE | DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE;
/// Hyper-V's variable range 0: the first 4 GiB, WB.
const HYPER_V_PHYSBASE0: u64 = 0x6;
const HYPER_V_PHYSMASK0: u64 = 0x3FFF_0000_0800;

fn hyper_v() -> MtrrCapabilities {
    MtrrCapabilities::new(HYPER_V_MTRRCAP, HYPER_V_ADDRESS_BITS).unwrap()
}

/// The MTRR MSR at `address`; panics if `capabilities` has none there.
fn msr(capabilities: MtrrCapabilities, address: u32) -> MtrrMsr {
    capabilities
        .msr(address)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no MTRR MSR {address:#x}"))
}

/// Hyper-V's MTRRs, as the guest's copy starts.
fn hyper_v_state() -> MtrrState {
    MtrrState::new(MtrrRegisters::read_with(hyper_v(), |msr| hyper_v_value(msr.address())).unwrap()).unwrap()
}

/// Every byte of a fixed-range MSR set to `memory_type`.
fn fixed_all(memory_type: MemoryType) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes([memory_type.raw() as u8; 8])
}

/// The value Hyper-V's firmware leaves in the MTRR MSR at `address`: WB
/// below 0xA0000 and UC up to 1 MiB in the fixed ranges, variable range 0
/// for the first 4 GiB, the other ranges unused.
fn hyper_v_value(address: u32) -> u64 {
    match address {
        IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE => HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE,
        0x250 | 0x258 => fixed_all(WB),
        0x259..=0x26F => fixed_all(UC),
        0x200 => HYPER_V_PHYSBASE0,
        0x201 => HYPER_V_PHYSMASK0,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

#[test]
fn mtrrcap_gives_the_variable_count_and_the_fixed_ranges() {
    let capabilities = hyper_v();
    assert_eq!(capabilities.variable_count(), 8);
    assert!(capabilities.fixed);
    assert!(!MtrrCapabilities::new(10, 46).unwrap().fixed);
}

#[test]
fn more_variable_ranges_than_kept_are_refused() {
    assert_eq!(
        MtrrCapabilities::new(MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES as u64 + 1, 46),
        Err(MtrrError::TooManyVariableRanges {
            count: MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES + 1
        })
    );
    assert!(MtrrCapabilities::new(MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES as u64, 46).is_ok());
}

#[test]
fn the_msrs_are_def_type_the_fixed_ones_then_each_pair() {
    let addresses: Vec<u32> = hyper_v().msrs().map(MtrrMsr::address).collect();
    let mut expected = vec![0x2FF, 0x250, 0x258, 0x259];
    expected.extend(0x268..=0x26F);
    expected.extend(0x200..=0x20F);
    assert_eq!(addresses, expected);
}

#[test]
fn without_fixed_ranges_only_def_type_and_the_pairs_exist() {

        .unwrap()
        .msrs()
        .map(MtrrMsr::address)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(addresses, [0x2FF, 0x200, 0x201, 0x202, 0x203]);

#[test]
fn a_cpu_without_mtrrs_has_no_mtrr_msr() {
    assert_eq!(MtrrCapabilities::NONE.msrs().count(), 0);

#[test]
fn mtrrcap_itself_is_not_among_the_msrs() {
    // Read-only: WRMSR to it always faults, and the guest reads the CPU's.
    assert!(hyper_v().msrs().all(|msr| msr.address() != IA32_MTRRCAP));
    assert!(!is_msr_address(IA32_MTRRCAP));
}

#[test]
fn every_mtrr_address_is_def_type_the_fixed_ones_and_32_pairs() {
    let addresses: Vec<u32> = every_msr_address().collect();
    assert_eq!(addresses.len(), 1 + 11 + 64);
    assert_eq!(addresses[..2], [0x2FF, 0x250]);
    assert_eq!(addresses[11..13], [0x26F, 0x200]);
    assert_eq!(addresses.last(), Some(&0x23F));
    // Exactly the addresses `is_msr_address` accepts, in the MSR bitmap's
    // low range.
    for address in 0..0x2000 {
        assert_eq!(is_msr_address(address), addresses.contains(&address), "{address:#x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn every_msr_a_cpu_can_have_is_an_mtrr_address() {
    let widest = MtrrCapabilities::new((1 << 8) | MAX_VARIABLE_RANGES as u64, 52).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(widest.msrs().count(), every_msr_address().count());
    assert!(widest.msrs().all(|msr| is_msr_address(msr.address())));
    // Its neighbours are not: IA32_PAT, and IA32_MC0_CTL2 above the fixed
    // ranges.
    assert!(!is_msr_address(0x277));
    assert!(!is_msr_address(0x280));
}

#[test]
fn def_type_takes_a_type_and_the_two_enable_bits() {
    let def_type = msr(hyper_v(), IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    for value in [
        0,
        HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE,
        DEF_TYPE_ENABLE | WB.raw(),
        DEF_TYPE_FIXED_ENABLE | 1,
    ] {
        assert_eq!(hyper_v().check(def_type, value), Ok(()), "{value:#x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn def_type_refuses_reserved_bits_and_types() {
    let def_type = msr(hyper_v(), IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    // Bits 9:8 lie between the type and FE; bit 12 is past E.
    for bits in [0x300, 1 << 12, 1 << 63] {
        assert_eq!(
            hyper_v().check(def_type, HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE | bits),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedBits { msr: 0x2FF, bits })
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        hyper_v().check(def_type, DEF_TYPE_ENABLE | 2),
        Err(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr: 0x2FF, value: 2 })
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_fixed_range_msr_refuses_a_reserved_type_in_any_byte() {
    let capabilities = hyper_v();
    let fix4k = msr(capabilities, 0x26A);
    assert_eq!(capabilities.check(fix4k, fixed_all(WB)), Ok(()));
    for byte in 0..8 {
        let mut bytes = [WB.raw() as u8; 8];
        bytes[byte] = 7;
        assert_eq!(
            capabilities.check(fix4k, u64::from_le_bytes(bytes)),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr: 0x26A, value: 7 }),
            "byte {byte}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn physbase_takes_a_type_and_an_address_below_maxphyaddr() {
    let physbase = msr(hyper_v(), 0x20E);
    assert_eq!(hyper_v().check(physbase, 0x3FFF_FFFF_F000 | WB.raw()), Ok(()));
    // Bits 11:8, then bit 46, the first one past MAXPHYADDR.
    for bits in [0xF00, 1 << 46, 1 << 63] {
        assert_eq!(
            hyper_v().check(physbase, 0x20_0000 | bits),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedBits { msr: 0x20E, bits })
        );
    }
}

#[test]

    let physbase = msr(hyper_v(), 0x20E);

#[test]

        assert_eq!(hyper_v().check(physmask, value), Ok(()), "{value:#x}");

#[test]
fn reading_refuses_what_wrmsr_would_have_refused() {
    // Variable range 7 is off, so decoding alone would accept its reserved
    // type; no CPU can hold it, so it comes from a broken VMM below Aleph0.
    let reserved_type = MtrrRegisters::read_with(hyper_v(), |msr| match msr.address() {
        0x20E => 2,
        address => hyper_v_value(address),
    });
    assert_eq!(reserved_type, Err(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr: 0x20E, value: 2 }));
    let reserved_bits = MtrrRegisters::read_with(hyper_v(), |msr| match msr.address() {
        0x2FF => HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE | 0x100,
        address => hyper_v_value(address),
    });
    assert_eq!(
        reserved_bits,
        Err(MtrrError::ReservedBits {
            msr: 0x2FF,
            bits: 0x100
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn msr_finds_every_mtrr_msr_the_cpu_has_and_nothing_else() {
    for capabilities in [hyper_v(), MtrrCapabilities::new(2, 39).unwrap(), MtrrCapabilities::NONE] {
        let listed: Vec<MtrrMsr> = capabilities.msrs().collect();
        for address in 0..0x1000 {
            let expected = listed.iter().copied().find(|msr| msr.address() == address);
            assert_eq!(capabilities.msr(address), expected, "{address:#x} in {capabilities:?}");
        }
    }
    // IA32_PAT sits between the fixed-range MSRs and IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE.
    assert_eq!(hyper_v().msr(0x277), None);
    // Variable range 8 does not exist with eight ranges.
    assert_eq!(hyper_v().msr(0x210), None);
}

#[test]
fn mtrr_msrs_are_named_as_the_sdm_names_them() {
    let capabilities = hyper_v();
    for (address, name) in [
        (0x2FF, "IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE"),
        (0x250, "IA32_MTRR_FIX64K_00000"),
        (0x259, "IA32_MTRR_FIX16K_A0000"),
        (0x26F, "IA32_MTRR_FIX4K_F8000"),
        (0x200, "IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0"),
        (0x20F, "IA32_MTRR_PHYSMASK7"),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(msr(capabilities, address).to_string(), name);
    }
    assert!(msr(capabilities, 0x268).is_fixed());
    assert!(!msr(capabilities, 0x2FF).is_fixed());

#[test]
fn rdmsr_reads_back_what_wrmsr_wrote() {
    let mut registers = MtrrRegisters::read_with(hyper_v(), |msr| hyper_v_value(msr.address())).unwrap();
    let physmask = msr(hyper_v(), 0x20F);
    assert_eq!(registers.get(physmask), 0);
    registers.write(physmask, 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(registers.get(physmask), 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800);
    assert_eq!(registers.get(msr(hyper_v(), 0x201)), HYPER_V_PHYSMASK0);
}

#[test]
fn a_refused_write_leaves_every_value_as_it_was() {
    let mut state = hyper_v_state();
    let before = state.clone();
    for (address, value) in [(0x2FF, HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE | 0x200), (0x258, 2), (0x201, 1 << 50)] {
        assert!(state.write(msr(hyper_v(), address), value).is_err(), "{address:#x}");
        assert_eq!(state, before);
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_write_that_moves_a_range_changes_the_types() {
    let mut state = hyper_v_state();
    // Variable range 7: 2 MiB at 2 MiB, UC. Off until its mask is valid.
    assert_eq!(state.write(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20E), 0x20_0000), Ok(false));
    assert_eq!(state.write(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20F), 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800), Ok(true));
    assert_eq!(state.mtrrs().memory_type(0x20_0000), UC);
    assert_eq!(state.mtrrs().memory_type(0x40_0000), WB);
    assert_eq!(state.registers().get(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20F)), 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800);
}

#[test]
fn writing_the_value_already_there_changes_no_type() {
    let mut state = hyper_v_state();
    assert_eq!(state.write(msr(hyper_v(), 0x201), HYPER_V_PHYSMASK0), Ok(false));
    assert_eq!(state, hyper_v_state());
}

#[test]
fn only_the_write_that_sets_e_again_changes_the_types() {
    // An OS's MTRR update: clear E (all memory UC), write the ranges, set E.
    let mut state = hyper_v_state();
    let def_type = msr(hyper_v(), IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    assert_eq!(state.write(def_type, 0), Ok(true));
    assert_eq!(state.mtrrs(), &Mtrrs::Disabled);
    assert_eq!(state.write(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20E), 0x20_0000), Ok(false));
    assert_eq!(state.write(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20F), 0x3FFF_FFE0_0800), Ok(false));
    assert_eq!(state.write(def_type, HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE), Ok(true));
    assert_eq!(state.mtrrs().memory_type(0x20_0000), UC);
    assert_eq!(state.mtrrs().memory_type(0x9_F000), WB);
}

#[test]
fn a_bad_physbase_faults_at_its_own_write_while_the_mtrrs_are_off() {
    // With E clear nothing decodes the ranges, so `Mtrrs::decode` alone
    // would take a reserved type here, and refuse only the write that sets
    // E again. The CPU refuses it at once.
    let mut state = hyper_v_state();
    let def_type = msr(hyper_v(), IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    state.write(def_type, 0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        state.write(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20E), 0x20_0000 | 2),
        Err(MtrrError::ReservedType { msr: 0x20E, value: 2 })
    );
    assert_eq!(state.registers().get(msr(hyper_v(), 0x20E)), 0);
    assert_eq!(state.write(def_type, HYPER_V_DEF_TYPE), Ok(true));
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/paging.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/paging.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use std::collections::HashMap;

const P_RW: u64 = PRESENT | WRITABLE;
const PML4: u64 = 0x1000;
const PDPT: u64 = 0x2000;
const PD: u64 = 0x3000;
const PT: u64 = 0x4000;

/// Builds a virtual address from its table indices and page offset.
fn va(pml4: u64, pdpt: u64, pd: u64, pt: u64, offset: u64) -> u64 {
    (pml4 << 39) | (pdpt << 30) | (pd << 21) | (pt << 12) | offset
}

/// Fake physical memory holding page-table entries; unset entries read 0.
struct Tables(HashMap<u64, u64>);

impl Tables {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self(HashMap::new())
    }
    fn set(&mut self, table: u64, index: u64, entry: u64) -> &mut Self {
        self.0.insert(table + index * 8, entry);
        self
    }
    fn walk(&self, cr3: u64, virtual_address: u64) -> Result<Mapping, WalkError> {
        walk(cr3, virtual_address, |address| {
            self.0.get(&address).copied().unwrap_or(0)
        })
    }
}

/// PML4[1] -> PDPT[2] -> PD[3] -> PT[4] -> page 0x0012_3000, all P|RW.
fn four_level_tables() -> Tables {
    let mut tables = Tables::new();
    tables
        .set(PML4, 1, PDPT | P_RW)
        .set(PDPT, 2, PD | P_RW)
        .set(PD, 3, PT | P_RW)
        .set(PT, 4, 0x0012_3000 | P_RW);
    tables
}

#[test]
fn four_kib_page_translates_with_offset() {
    let mapping = four_level_tables().walk(PML4, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0xABC)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        mapping,
        Mapping {
            physical: 0x0012_3ABC,
            size: PageSize::Size4K,
            writable: true,
            user: false,
            execute_disable: false,
        },
    );
}

#[test]
fn user_only_when_set_at_every_level() {
    let mut tables = Tables::new();
    tables
        .set(PML4, 1, PDPT | P_RW | USER)
        .set(PDPT, 2, PD | P_RW | USER)
        .set(PD, 3, PT | P_RW | USER)
        .set(PT, 4, 0x0012_3000 | P_RW | USER);
    assert!(tables.walk(PML4, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0)).unwrap().user);

    // One supervisor entry anywhere makes it a supervisor page.
    tables.set(PDPT, 2, PD | P_RW);
    assert!(!tables.walk(PML4, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0)).unwrap().user);
}

#[test]
fn cr3_low_bits_are_ignored() {
    let mapping = four_level_tables().walk(PML4 | 0x18, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mapping.physical, 0x0012_3000);
}

#[test]
fn read_only_at_any_level_makes_page_read_only() {
    let mut tables = four_level_tables();
    tables.set(PDPT, 2, PD | PRESENT);
    assert!(!tables.walk(PML4, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0)).unwrap().writable);
}

#[test]
fn execute_disable_at_any_level_is_reported() {
    let mut tables = four_level_tables();
    tables.set(PML4, 1, PDPT | P_RW | EXECUTE_DISABLE);
    let mapping = tables.walk(PML4, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0)).unwrap();
    assert!(mapping.execute_disable);
    // XD is a flag, not part of the address.
    assert_eq!(mapping.physical, 0x0012_3000);
}

#[test]
fn two_mib_page_keeps_offset_and_drops_pat_bit() {
    let mut tables = Tables::new();
    tables
        .set(PML4, 0, PDPT | P_RW)
        .set(PDPT, 0, PD | P_RW)
        // Bit 12 is PAT in a large-page entry, not an address bit.
        .set(PD, 5, 0x4020_0000 | (1 << 12) | PAGE_SIZE_BIT | P_RW);
    let mapping = tables.walk(PML4, va(0, 0, 5, 0x1F, 0x123)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mapping.size, PageSize::Size2M);
    assert_eq!(mapping.physical, 0x4020_0000 | (0x1F << 12) | 0x123);
}

#[test]
fn one_gib_page_keeps_offset() {
    let mut tables = Tables::new();
    tables
        .set(PML4, 0, PDPT | P_RW)
        .set(PDPT, 1, 0x8000_0000 | PAGE_SIZE_BIT | P_RW);
    let mapping = tables.walk(PML4, va(0, 1, 7, 9, 0x42)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mapping.size, PageSize::Size1G);
    assert_eq!(mapping.physical, 0x8000_0000 | (7 << 21) | (9 << 12) | 0x42);
}

#[test]
fn missing_entry_reports_its_level() {
    let mut tables = four_level_tables();
    tables.set(PD, 3, 0);
    assert_eq!(
        tables.walk(PML4, va(1, 2, 3, 4, 0)),
        Err(WalkError::NotPresent { level: 2 })
    );
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/segment.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/segment.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

/// Describe `gdt` the way GDTR would.
fn table(gdt: &[u8]) -> DescriptorTable {
    DescriptorTable {
        base: gdt.as_ptr() as u64,
        limit: gdt.len() as u16 - 1,
    }
}

#[test]
fn null_and_ldt_selectors_return_zero() {
    let gdt = [0xFFu8; 32];
    let gdt = table(&gdt);
    for selector in [0x0, 0x1, 0x3] {
        assert_eq!(
            // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
            unsafe { segment_base_from_gdt(&gdt, selector) },
            0,
            "selector {selector:#x}"
        );
    }
    // TI=1 names the LDT, which this decoder does not read.
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { segment_base_from_gdt(&gdt, 0x0C) }, 0);
}

#[test]
fn selector_past_limit_returns_zero() {
    // The 16-byte TSS descriptor at 0x10 needs 16 bytes; only 8 are inside
    // the limit.
    let gdt = [0xFFu8; 24];
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { segment_base_from_gdt(&table(&gdt), 0x10) }, 0);
}

#[test]
fn rpl_bits_are_ignored() {
    let mut gdt = [0u8; 32];
    gdt[0x10 + 2] = 0x78;
    gdt[0x10 + 3] = 0x56;
    gdt[0x10 + 4] = 0x34;
    gdt[0x10 + 7] = 0x12;
    let gdt = table(&gdt);
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { segment_base_from_gdt(&gdt, 0x10) }, 0x1234_5678);
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { segment_base_from_gdt(&gdt, 0x13) }, 0x1234_5678);
}

/// The usual flat 64-bit code descriptor: base 0, limit 0xFFFFF with
/// G = 1, L = 1, present, DPL 0, execute/read, accessed.
const FLAT_CODE_64: u64 = 0x00AF_9B00_0000_FFFF;
/// The usual flat data descriptor: G = 1, D/B = 1, read/write, accessed.
const FLAT_DATA: u64 = 0x00CF_9300_0000_FFFF;

#[test]
fn flat_code_descriptor_decodes() {
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_CODE_64).base(), 0);
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_CODE_64).limit(), 0xFFFF_FFFF);
    // G=1 L=1 | P=1 DPL=0 S=1 type=0xB
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_CODE_64).access_rights(), 0xA09B);
}

#[test]
fn flat_data_descriptor_decodes() {
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_DATA).limit(), 0xFFFF_FFFF);
    // G=1 D/B=1 | P=1 DPL=0 S=1 type=0x3
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_DATA).access_rights(), 0xC093);
}

#[test]
fn scattered_base_and_byte_limit_decode() {
    // base 0x1234_5678, limit 0x1_2345 with G=0, P S type=0x3.
    let descriptor = 0x1201_9334_5678_2345;
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(descriptor).base(), 0x1234_5678);
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(descriptor).limit(), 0x1_2345);
    // Limit bits 19:16 sit between the two access-rights halves; they
    // must not leak into access-rights bits 11:8.
    assert_eq!(SegmentDescriptor(descriptor).access_rights(), 0x0093);
}

#[test]
fn read_descriptor_rejects_null_ldt_and_out_of_range() {
    let gdt = [0xFFu8; 24];
    let gdt = table(&gdt);
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { read_descriptor(&gdt, 0x00) }, None);
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { read_descriptor(&gdt, 0x03) }, None, "null with RPL 3");
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { read_descriptor(&gdt, 0x0C) }, None, "TI=1 names the LDT");
    // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
    assert_eq!(unsafe { read_descriptor(&gdt, 0x18) }, None, "past the limit");
}

#[test]
fn read_descriptor_ignores_rpl() {
    let mut gdt = [0u8; 24];
    gdt[0x10..0x18].copy_from_slice(&FLAT_DATA.to_le_bytes());
    let gdt = table(&gdt);
    assert_eq!(
        // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
        unsafe { read_descriptor(&gdt, 0x10) },
        Some(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_DATA))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        // SAFETY: `gdt` describes a live local array.
        unsafe { read_descriptor(&gdt, 0x13) },
        Some(SegmentDescriptor(FLAT_DATA))
    );
}

#[test]
fn descriptor_table_operand_is_limit_then_base() {
    let table = DescriptorTable {
        base: 0x1122_3344_5566_7788,
        limit: 0xABCD,
    };
    assert_eq!(
        table.to_operand(),
        [0xCD, 0xAB, 0x88, 0x77, 0x66, 0x55, 0x44, 0x33, 0x22, 0x11],
    );
}

#[test]
fn descriptor_table_operand_round_trips() {
    let table = DescriptorTable {
        base: 0x1122_3344_5566_7788,
        limit: 0x004F,
    };
    let operand = table.to_operand();
    assert_eq!(operand, [0x4F, 0x00, 0x88, 0x77, 0x66, 0x55, 0x44, 0x33, 0x22, 0x11]);
    assert_eq!(DescriptorTable::from_operand(operand), table);
}

#[test]
fn descriptor_offset_rules() {
    let gdt = DescriptorTable {
        base: 0x1000,
        limit: 0x4F,
    }; // 80 bytes
    assert_eq!(descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x00, 8), None, "null selector");
    assert_eq!(descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x03, 8), None, "null selector with RPL 3");
    assert_eq!(descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x2C, 8), None, "TI = 1 names the LDT");
    assert_eq!(descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x28, 8), Some(0x28));
    assert_eq!(descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x2B, 8), Some(0x28), "RPL bits are ignored");
    assert_eq!(
        descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x40, 16),
        Some(0x40),
        "16 bytes end exactly at the limit"
    );
    assert_eq!(descriptor_offset(&gdt, 0x48, 16), None, "16 bytes past the limit");
}

#[test]
fn system_descriptor_base_joins_all_four_pieces() {
    let mut bytes = [0u8; 16];
    bytes[2] = 0x88;
    bytes[3] = 0x77;
    bytes[4] = 0x66;
    bytes[7] = 0x55;
    bytes[8..12].copy_from_slice(&0x1122_3344u32.to_le_bytes());
    assert_eq!(system_descriptor_base(&bytes), 0x1122_3344_5566_7788);
}

#[test]
fn interrupt_gate_splits_a_low_handler_address() {
    assert_eq!(
        interrupt_gate(0x7eb0_f020, 0x28, 0),
        [0x20, 0xF0, 0x28, 0x00, 0x00, 0x8E, 0xB0, 0x7E, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    );
}

#[test]
fn interrupt_gate_keeps_the_high_handler_bits() {
    assert_eq!(
        interrupt_gate(0xFFFF_8000_1234_5678, 0x28, 0),
        [
            0x78, 0x56, 0x28, 0x00, 0x00, 0x8E, 0x34, 0x12, 0x00, 0x80, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0, 0
        ],
    );
}

#[test]
fn interrupt_gate_puts_the_ist_index_in_byte_4() {
    assert_eq!(interrupt_gate(0x1000, 0x28, 3)[4], 3);
    // Only 3 bits exist; the rest of byte 4 stays reserved (0).
    assert_eq!(interrupt_gate(0x1000, 0x28, 0xFF)[4], 7);
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmcs/mod.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::msr::ControlCapability;

#[test]
fn an_unsupported_control_is_a_vmcs_error() {
    assert_eq!(VmcsError::from(UnsupportedControl), VmcsError::UnsupportedControlValue);
}

const CF: u64 = 1 << 0;
const ZF: u64 = 1 << 6;
/// RFLAGS bit 1 always reads as 1.
const RESERVED: u64 = 1 << 1;

#[test]
fn launch_with_cf_is_fail_invalid() {
    assert_eq!(launch_failure(RESERVED | CF), VmcsError::VmFailInvalid);
}

#[test]
fn launch_with_zf_is_fail_valid() {
    assert_eq!(launch_failure(RESERVED | ZF), VmcsError::VmFailValid);
}

#[test]
fn launch_falling_through_with_clear_flags_is_still_a_failure() {
    // A successful VMLAUNCH never reaches the next instruction, so
    // clear flags here must not be read as success.
    assert_eq!(launch_failure(RESERVED), VmcsError::LaunchReturned);
}

#[test]
fn resume_with_cf_is_fail_invalid() {
    assert_eq!(resume_failure(RESERVED | CF), VmcsError::VmFailInvalid);
}

#[test]
fn resume_with_zf_is_fail_valid() {
    assert_eq!(resume_failure(RESERVED | ZF), VmcsError::VmFailValid);
}

#[test]
fn resume_falling_through_with_clear_flags_is_still_a_failure() {
    // A successful VMRESUME never reaches the next instruction either.
    assert_eq!(resume_failure(RESERVED), VmcsError::ResumeReturned);
}

#[test]
fn only_vm_fail_valid_has_an_instruction_error_to_read() {
    // Every other error returns before the VMREAD, which would fault outside
    // VMX operation (as it would here, on the host).
    for error in [
        VmcsError::VmFailInvalid,
        VmcsError::LaunchReturned,
        VmcsError::ResumeReturned,
        VmcsError::AllocationFailed,
    ] {
        // SAFETY: none of these is VmFailValid, so no VMREAD runs.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { instruction_error_for(error) }, None);
    }
}

#[test]
fn secondary_controls_activate_primary_bit_31() {
    let desired = DesiredControls::minimal_64_bit_guest(GuestKind::BuiltInTest);
    assert_eq!(desired.secondary, SECONDARY_ENABLE_EPT);
    assert_eq!(primary_request(desired), desired.primary | (1 << 31));
}

#[test]
fn no_secondary_controls_leave_the_primary_request_alone() {
    let desired = DesiredControls {
        primary: 0x10,
        secondary: 0,
        ..DesiredControls::minimal_64_bit_guest(GuestKind::BuiltInTest)
    };
    assert_eq!(primary_request(desired), 0x10);
}

#[test]
fn nmi_window_on_sets_only_bit_22() {
    assert_eq!(with_nmi_window_exiting(0x8401_E172, true), 0x8441_E172);
}

#[test]
fn nmi_window_off_clears_only_bit_22() {
    assert_eq!(with_nmi_window_exiting(0x8441_E172, false), 0x8401_E172);
}

#[test]
fn the_guest_requests_hlt_exiting_and_the_msr_and_io_bitmaps() {
    let desired = DesiredControls::minimal_64_bit_guest(GuestKind::BuiltInTest);
    assert_eq!(desired.primary, (1 << 7) | (1 << 25) | (1 << 28));
}

#[test]
fn every_exception_of_the_built_in_test_guest_exits() {
    assert_eq!(exception_bitmap(GuestKind::BuiltInTest), u32::MAX);
    assert_eq!(
        DesiredControls::minimal_64_bit_guest(GuestKind::BuiltInTest).exception_bitmap,
        u32::MAX
    );
}

#[test]
fn only_a_stop_of_the_test_guest_returns_to_bring_up() {
    assert!(GuestKind::BuiltInTest.stop_returns_to_bring_up());
    assert!(!GuestKind::Firmware.stop_returns_to_bring_up());
}

#[test]
fn the_firmware_takes_its_own_exceptions() {
    assert_eq!(exception_bitmap(GuestKind::Firmware), 0);
    assert_eq!(
        DesiredControls::minimal_64_bit_guest(GuestKind::Firmware).exception_bitmap,
        0
    );
}

/// Capability MSRs that allow exactly the VM-exit controls `exit` and the
/// VM-entry controls `entry`, and require none.
fn allowing(exit: u32, entry: u32) -> VmcsControlMsrs {
    VmcsControlMsrs {
        basic: 0,
        pinbased: ControlCapability(0),
        primary: ControlCapability(0),
        exit: ControlCapability(u64::from(exit) << 32),
        entry: ControlCapability(u64::from(entry) << 32),
        secondary: ControlCapability(0),
        ept_vpid_cap: 0,
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_pat_is_switched_when_the_cpu_allows_all_three_controls() {
    // Exit bits 18 (save IA32_PAT) and 19 (load IA32_PAT), entry bit 14
    // (load IA32_PAT).
    let save_and_load = (1 << 18) | (1 << 19);
    assert_eq!(pat_switch(&allowing(save_and_load, 1 << 14)), (save_and_load, 1 << 14));
    // With any one missing, none: the guest's writes would be lost at VM
    // entry, or one PAT would still serve both.
    for (exit, entry) in [(1 << 19, 1 << 14), (1 << 18, 1 << 14), (save_and_load, 0)] {
        assert_eq!(
            pat_switch(&allowing(exit, entry)),
            (0, 0),
            "exit={exit:#x} entry={entry:#x}"
        );
    }
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/vmcs/launch.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmcs/launch.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;

const CF: u64 = 1 << 0;
const ZF: u64 = 1 << 6;
/// RFLAGS bit 1 always reads as 1.
const RESERVED: u64 = 1 << 1;
/// RFLAGS.IF: firmware calls the launch with interrupts on.
const IF: u64 = 1 << 9;

const VMCALL: ExitReason = ExitReason {
    basic: 18,
    entry_failure: false,
};

#[test]
fn rflags_from_a_failed_vmlaunch_decode_as_launch_failed() {
    // The launch stub returns RFLAGS unencoded (kind 0).
    assert_eq!(
        decode(RESERVED | IF | CF),
        GuestStop::LaunchFailed {
            error: VmcsError::VmFailInvalid,
            instruction_error: None
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decode(RESERVED | IF | ZF),
        GuestStop::LaunchFailed {
            error: VmcsError::VmFailValid,
            instruction_error: None
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decode(RESERVED | IF),
        GuestStop::LaunchFailed {
            error: VmcsError::LaunchReturned,
            instruction_error: None
        },
    );
}

#[test]
fn finished_keeps_the_exit_count() {
    assert_eq!(decode(encode_finished(2)), GuestStop::Finished { exits: 2 });
}

#[test]
fn unexpected_keeps_the_exit_number_and_reason() {
    assert_eq!(
        decode(encode_unexpected(3, 0x8000_0021)),
        GuestStop::Unexpected {
            number: 3,
            reason: ExitReason {
                basic: 33,
                entry_failure: true
            }
        },
    );
}

#[test]
fn unexpected_keeps_the_largest_exit_number_that_fits() {
    let largest = (1 << 30) - 1;
    assert_eq!(
        decode(encode_unexpected(largest, 18)),
        GuestStop::Unexpected {
            number: largest,
            reason: VMCALL
        },
    );
}

#[test]
fn oversized_exit_number_cannot_change_the_kind() {
    // Only the low 30 bits are kept, so bits 63:62 still say "unexpected".
    assert!(matches!(
        decode(encode_unexpected(u64::MAX, 18)),
        GuestStop::Unexpected { reason: VMCALL, .. },
    ));
}

#[test]
fn failed_vmresume_keeps_its_flags() {
    assert_eq!(
        decode(encode_resume_failed(RESERVED | ZF)),
        GuestStop::ResumeFailed {
            error: VmcsError::VmFailValid,
            instruction_error: None
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decode(encode_resume_failed(RESERVED)),
        GuestStop::ResumeFailed {
            error: VmcsError::ResumeReturned,
            instruction_error: None
        },
    );
}

#[test]
fn zero_from_the_in_place_launch_means_it_runs_on_as_the_guest() {
    assert_eq!(decode_in_place(0), Ok(()));
}

#[test]
fn rflags_from_a_failed_in_place_launch_say_how_it_failed() {
    assert_eq!(decode_in_place(RESERVED | IF | CF), Err(VmcsError::VmFailInvalid));
    assert_eq!(decode_in_place(RESERVED | IF | ZF), Err(VmcsError::VmFailValid));
    // Clear flags still mean VMLAUNCH fell through, never that it ran.
    assert_eq!(decode_in_place(RESERVED | IF), Err(VmcsError::LaunchReturned));
}

#[test]
fn no_stop_value_is_zero() {
    // The exit handler returns 0 to mean "resume the guest".
    assert_ne!(encode_finished(0), 0);
    assert_ne!(encode_unexpected(0, 0), 0);
    assert_ne!(encode_resume_failed(0), 0);
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/mod.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its

use super::*;

#[test]
fn an_untouched_stack_is_unused() {
    assert_eq!(used_bytes(&[0; 4]), 0);
}

#[test]
fn use_counts_from_the_lowest_nonzero_word_to_the_top() {
    // The stack grows down: the last word is its top, written first.
    assert_eq!(used_bytes(&[0, 0, 0, 7]), 8);
    // A zero word above the lowest written one still counts as used.
    assert_eq!(used_bytes(&[0, 5, 0, 7]), 24);
}

#[test]
fn a_written_lowest_word_is_the_whole_stack() {
    assert_eq!(used_bytes(&[1, 0, 0, 0]), 32);
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/dump.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use std::collections::HashSet;

/// The VM-exit controls of the Hyper-V runs: the required bits
/// (`0x00036ffb`, which include "host address-space size"). No save or load
/// control for DR7, PAT or EFER is among them.
const HYPER_V_EXIT: u64 = 0x0003_6ffb;
/// The VM-entry controls of the Hyper-V runs: the required bits
/// (`0x000011fb`) and "IA-32e mode guest" (bit 9).
const HYPER_V_ENTRY: u64 = 0x0000_11fb | (1 << 9);

#[test]
fn every_dumped_field_appears_once() {
    let encodings: Vec<u32> = DUMP_LINES
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|line| line.fields)
        .map(|&(_, field)| field)
        .collect();
    let unique: HashSet<u32> = encodings.iter().copied().collect();
    assert_eq!(unique.len(), encodings.len(), "a VMCS field is dumped twice");
}

#[test]
fn every_dump_line_names_its_fields_apart() {
    for line in &DUMP_LINES {
        let names: HashSet<&str> = line.fields.iter().map(|&(name, _)| name).collect();
        assert_eq!(names.len(), line.fields.len(), "line {}", line.label);
        assert!(line.fields.len() <= MAX_FIELDS, "line {}", line.label);
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_dump_includes_the_new_error_code_fields() {
    let encodings: HashSet<u32> = DUMP_LINES
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|line| line.fields)
        .map(|&(_, field)| field)
        .collect();
    assert!(encodings.contains(&0x4406), "VM-exit interruption error code");
    assert!(encodings.contains(&0x440A), "IDT-vectoring error code");
}

#[test]
fn under_hyper_v_dr7_is_lost_and_pat_and_efer_are_still_in_their_msrs() {
    assert_eq!(
        saved_registers(HYPER_V_ENTRY, HYPER_V_EXIT),
        [
            ("dr7", Source::NotSaved),
            ("pat", Source::Msr(IA32_PAT)),
            ("efer", Source::Msr(IA32_EFER)),
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_save_controls_put_the_registers_in_the_vmcs() {
    let saving = HYPER_V_EXIT | VM_EXIT_SAVE_DEBUG_CONTROLS | VM_EXIT_SAVE_IA32_PAT | VM_EXIT_SAVE_IA32_EFER;
    assert_eq!(
        saved_registers(HYPER_V_ENTRY, saving),
        [
            ("dr7", Source::Vmcs(GUEST_DR7)),
            ("pat", Source::Vmcs(GUEST_IA32_PAT)),
            ("efer", Source::Vmcs(GUEST_IA32_EFER)),
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_register_loaded_on_entry_or_exit_but_not_saved_is_lost() {
    let entry_loads_pat = HYPER_V_ENTRY | VM_ENTRY_LOAD_IA32_PAT;
    assert_eq!(
        saved_registers(entry_loads_pat, HYPER_V_EXIT)[1],
        ("pat", Source::NotSaved)
    );
    let exit_loads_efer = HYPER_V_EXIT | VM_EXIT_LOAD_IA32_EFER;
    assert_eq!(
        saved_registers(HYPER_V_ENTRY, exit_loads_efer)[2],
        ("efer", Source::NotSaved)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_dump_line_prints_each_field_by_name() {
    let line = &DUMP_LINES[1];
    let values = [Ok(0x8000_0b0e), Err(VmcsError::VmFailValid)];
    assert_eq!(
        DumpValues { line, values: &values }.to_string(),
        "queued injection: info=0x80000b0e error_code=unreadable (VmFailValid)"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_dump_line_with_too_few_values_prints_the_rest_as_unreadable() {
    let line = &DUMP_LINES[3];
    let values = [Ok(0x7eae_2000)];
    assert_eq!(
        DumpValues { line, values: &values }.to_string(),
        "addresses: guest_linear=0x7eae2000 guest_physical=unreadable (VmFailInvalid)"
    );
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/vmexit/guest_mtrrs.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/guest_mtrrs.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.
//!
//! The copy is one static, never published on the host (`publish` needs the
//! tables of a real `Ept::build`), so a single test covers it.

use super::*;

#[test]
fn the_copy_is_refused_while_lent_out_and_before_it_is_published() {
    let def_type = MtrrCapabilities::new(8, 46).unwrap().msr(0x2FF).unwrap();
    // As inside another call's closure.
    GUEST_MTRRS.in_use.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    assert_eq!(with(|_| ()), Err(Unavailable::InUse));
    assert_eq!(read(def_type), Err(MtrrAccessFailure::InUse));
    assert_eq!(capabilities(), MtrrCapabilities::NONE);
    GUEST_MTRRS.in_use.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);

    assert_eq!(with(|_| ()), Err(Unavailable::NotPublished));
    assert_eq!(read(def_type), Err(MtrrAccessFailure::NotPublished));
    assert!(registers().is_none());
    // A refused call leaves the copy free for the next one.
    assert!(!GUEST_MTRRS.in_use.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/handler.rs`.

//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with

use super::*;

const RESUME: ExitAction = ExitAction::Resume(ResumePlan::PAST_INSTRUCTION);

#[test]
fn resume_tells_the_stub_to_resume() {
    assert_eq!(stub_return(RESUME, 1, 18), RESUME_GUEST);
    assert_eq!(RESUME_GUEST, 0);
}

#[test]
fn finished_stops_with_the_exit_count() {
    // Four exits: two main VMCALLs, an NMI, the guest NMI handler's VMCALL.
    assert_eq!(stub_return(ExitAction::Finished, 4, 18), vmcs::encode_finished(4));
}

#[test]
fn unexpected_stops_with_the_exit_and_its_reason() {
    assert_eq!(
        stub_return(ExitAction::Unexpected, 1, 10),
        vmcs::encode_unexpected(1, 10)
    );
}

#[test]
fn next_rip_adds_the_instruction_length() {
    assert_eq!(next_rip(0x1000, 3), Some(0x1003));
}

#[test]
fn next_rip_may_reach_the_last_address() {
    // A 15-byte instruction at ...FFF0 ends at ...FFFE; the next RIP is then the last representable address.
    assert_eq!(next_rip(u64::MAX - 15, 15), Some(u64::MAX));
}

#[test]
fn next_rip_past_the_top_of_the_address_space_is_refused() {
    assert_eq!(next_rip(u64::MAX - 14, 15), None);
    assert_eq!(next_rip(0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFE, 3), None);
}

#[test]
fn next_rip_may_reach_the_last_canonical_address_of_the_lower_half() {
    assert_eq!(next_rip(0x0000_7FFF_FFFF_FFFC, 3), Some(0x0000_7FFF_FFFF_FFFF));
}

#[test]
fn next_rip_past_the_lower_half_is_refused() {
    // A 1-byte instruction at the last canonical byte of the lower half: the add does not overflow, but
    // 0x0000_8000_0000_0000 is non-canonical.
    assert_eq!(next_rip(0x0000_7FFF_FFFF_FFFF, 1), None);
    assert_eq!(next_rip(0x0000_7FFF_FFFF_FFF1, 15), None);
}

#[test]
fn resume_failures_read_as_the_report_has_always_printed_them() {
    // The report adds "; not resuming." after each.
    assert_eq!(ResumeFailure::RipUnreadable.to_string(), "guest RIP unreadable");
    assert_eq!(
        ResumeFailure::NextRipInvalid.to_string(),
        "next guest RIP would wrap or be non-canonical"
    );
    let write = ResumeFailure::Write {
        what: "advance guest RIP",
        error: VmcsError::VmFailValid,
    };
    assert_eq!(write.to_string(), "could not advance guest RIP (VmFailValid)");
    assert_eq!(
        ResumeFailure::GrantWrite(VmxFail::Invalid).to_string(),
        "could not make the protected page writable (INVEPT Invalid)"
    );
}

#[test]
fn only_a_resumed_outcome_lets_the_guest_go_on() {
    assert!(Outcome::ResumeFailed(ResumeFailure::NoProtectedPage).stops());
    assert_eq!(
        Outcome::ResumeFailed(ResumeFailure::NoProtectedPage).action(),
        ExitAction::Unexpected
    );
    assert!(Outcome::Stopped(ExitAction::Finished).stops());
    assert_eq!(Outcome::Stopped(ExitAction::Finished).action(), ExitAction::Finished);
}

#[test]
fn guest_mtrr_failures_say_what_went_wrong() {
    assert_eq!(
        ResumeFailure::GuestMtrrs(MtrrAccessFailure::NotPublished).to_string(),
        "the guest's MTRRs were never set up"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ResumeFailure::GuestMtrrs(MtrrAccessFailure::Invept(VmxFail::Invalid)).to_string(),
        "EPT took the guest's MTRR types, but INVEPT failed (Invalid)"
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_guest_resumes_in_the_phase_the_exit_found() {
    for found in [Phase::BootServices, Phase::Runtime] {
        assert_eq!(resume_phase(ExitEvent::Halted, found), found);
        assert_eq!(resume_phase(ExitEvent::TestVmcall, found), found);
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_exit_boot_services_vmcall_starts_the_runtime_phase_for_good() {
    assert_eq!(
        resume_phase(ExitEvent::BootServicesEnded, Phase::BootServices),
        Phase::Runtime
    );
    // A second one, faked by the guest, changes nothing.
    assert_eq!(
        resume_phase(ExitEvent::BootServicesEnded, Phase::Runtime),
        Phase::Runtime
    );
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/history.rs`.

//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::Emulation;

fn kept<const N: usize>(ring: &Ring<u32, N>) -> Vec<u32> {
    ring.oldest_first().copied().collect()
}

#[test]
fn an_empty_ring_keeps_nothing() {
    let ring: Ring<u32, 4> = Ring::new(0);
    assert_eq!(ring.kept(), 0);
    assert_eq!(ring.overwritten(), 0);
    assert!(kept(&ring).is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn a_ring_keeps_everything_until_full() {
    let mut ring: Ring<u32, 4> = Ring::new(0);
    for item in 1..=4 {
        ring.push(item);
    }
    assert_eq!(kept(&ring), [1, 2, 3, 4]);
    assert_eq!(ring.overwritten(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn a_full_ring_overwrites_the_oldest_and_keeps_the_order() {
    let mut ring: Ring<u32, 4> = Ring::new(0);
    for item in 1..=6 {
        ring.push(item);
    }
    assert_eq!(kept(&ring), [3, 4, 5, 6]);
    assert_eq!(ring.overwritten(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn a_ring_wraps_any_number_of_times() {
    let mut ring: Ring<u32, 64> = Ring::new(0);
    for item in 1..=1000 {
        ring.push(item);
    }
    assert_eq!(kept(&ring), (937..=1000).collect::<Vec<u32>>());
    assert_eq!(ring.overwritten(), 1000 - 64);
}

#[test]
fn a_record_prints_as_one_line() {
    // Exit #3 of the Hyper-V runs: WRMSR of IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE.
    let record = ExitRecord {
        number: 3,
        reason: Some(32),
        qualification: Some(0),
        rip: Some(0x7eae_1028),
        length: Some(2),
        interruption_info: Some(0),
        idt_vectoring_info: Some(0),
        registers: [0, 0x2_0800, 0xc000_0102, 0x7a1e],
        event: ExitEvent::Emulated(Emulation::Wrmsr {
            msr: 0xc000_0102,
            value: 0x7a1e_0000_0000,
        }),
    };
    assert_eq!(
        record.to_string(),
        "#3 reason=32 (WRMSR) rip=0x7eae1028 len=2 qual=0x0 info=0x0 vectoring=0x0 \
         rax=0x0 rbx=0x20800 rcx=0xc0000102 rdx=0x7a1e -> Emulated(Wrmsr { msr: c0000102, value: 7a1e00000000 })"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_record_marks_unreadable_fields_and_failed_entries() {
    let record = ExitRecord {
        number: 1,
        reason: Some(33 | 1 << 31),
        rip: None,
        ..ExitRecord::EMPTY
    };
    assert_eq!(
        record.to_string(),
        "#1 reason=33 (VM-entry failure: invalid guest state) [entry failed] rip=? len=? qual=? info=? \
         vectoring=? rax=0x0 rbx=0x0 rcx=0x0 rdx=0x0 -> Unexpected"
    );
    let unread = ExitRecord {
        number: 2,
        ..ExitRecord::EMPTY
    };
    assert!(unread.to_string().starts_with("#2 reason=? rip=?"));
}
```

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/policy.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::UNREADABLE_REASON;

/// The details of exits 1 to `last` of one reason, none of which stops the
/// guest, in a build printing up to `max_level`.
fn details(last: u64, max_level: Level) -> Vec<Detail> {
    (1..=last)
        .map(|count| exit_detail(count, false, false, max_level))
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn the_first_exits_of_a_reason_print_in_full() {
    assert!(
        details(FULL_EXITS_PER_REASON, Level::Info)
            .iter()
            .all(|&detail| detail == Detail::Full)
    );
}

#[test]
fn after_the_first_exits_only_powers_of_two_print_a_summary() {
    let printed: Vec<(u64, Detail)> = (FULL_EXITS_PER_REASON + 1..=4096)
        .map(|count| (count, exit_detail(count, false, false, Level::Info)))
        .filter(|&(_, detail)| detail != Detail::Silent)
        .collect();
    let summaries: Vec<u64> = printed.iter().map(|&(count, _)| count).collect();
    assert_eq!(summaries, [32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096]);
    assert!(printed.iter().all(|&(_, detail)| detail == Detail::Summary));
}

#[test]
fn a_stop_always_prints_in_full() {
    for count in [1, 17, 33, 1_000_000] {
        assert_eq!(
            exit_detail(count, true, false, Level::Info),
            Detail::Full,
            "count {count}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn an_unreadable_field_always_prints_in_full() {
    assert_eq!(exit_detail(33, false, true, Level::Info), Detail::Full);
}

#[test]
fn trace_prints_every_exit_in_full() {
    assert!(details(5000, Level::Trace).iter().all(|&detail| detail == Detail::Full));
}

#[test]
fn the_test_guest_runs_print_every_exit_in_full() {
    // The basic reasons of the recorded runs, in order: nine emulated exits,
    // HLT, the EPT violation, then the VMCALLs; with -InjectNmi an NMI exit
    // and the guest NMI handler's VMCALL come before the last one.
    let plain = [10, 31, 32, 31, 32, 30, 30, 30, 30, 12, 48, 18, 18];
    let inject_nmi = [10, 31, 32, 31, 32, 30, 30, 30, 30, 12, 48, 18, 0, 18, 18];
    for run in [&plain[..], &inject_nmi[..]] {
        let mut counts = [0u64; COUNTERS];
        for (number, &basic) in run.iter().enumerate() {
            counts[counter(basic)] += 1;
            let stops = number == run.len() - 1;
            let detail = exit_detail(counts[counter(basic)], stops, false, MAX_LEVEL);
            assert_eq!(detail, Detail::Full, "exit #{}", number + 1);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn every_reason_has_a_counter_and_none_is_out_of_bounds() {
    assert_eq!(counter(10), 10);
    assert_eq!(counter(127), 127);
    assert_eq!(counter(128), OTHER_REASONS);
    assert_eq!(counter(UNREADABLE_REASON), OTHER_REASONS);
    assert!(counter(u16::MAX) < COUNTERS);
}

#[test]
fn the_histogram_lists_each_counted_reason_with_its_name() {
    // The plain run's counts.
    let mut counts = [0u64; COUNTERS];
    for (basic, count) in [(10, 1), (12, 1), (18, 2), (30, 4), (31, 2), (32, 2), (48, 1)] {
        counts[counter(basic)] = count;
    }
    assert_eq!(
        Histogram(&counts).to_string(),
        "10 (CPUID)=1, 12 (HLT)=1, 18 (VMCALL)=2, 30 (I/O instruction)=4, 31 (RDMSR)=2, 32 (WRMSR)=2, 48 (EPT violation)=1"
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_histogram_names_the_shared_counter_other() {
    let mut counts = [0u64; COUNTERS];
    counts[counter(0)] = 1;
    counts[counter(UNREADABLE_REASON)] = 2;
    assert_eq!(Histogram(&counts).to_string(), "0 (exception or NMI)=1, other=2");
    assert_eq!(Histogram(&[0; COUNTERS]).to_string(), "none");
}

#[test]
fn the_default_build_prints_up_to_info() {
    assert_eq!(MAX_LEVEL == Level::Trace, cfg!(feature = "trace-exits"));
}
```

`tests/unit/vmx/vmexit/stats.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit tests for `src/vmx/vmexit/stats.rs`.
//!
//! Compiled only by `cargo test-host`. That file includes this one with
//! `#[path]` as its child module `tests`, so `use super::*` reaches its
//! private items.

use super::*;
use crate::vmx::exit_decision::{ExitAction, IoSize};
use crate::vmx::mtrr::MtrrCapabilities;

/// The statistics after one resumed exit of `event`, with its own plan.
fn after(event: ExitEvent) -> VcpuStats {
    let ExitAction::Resume(plan) = event.action() else {
        panic!("{event:?} does not resume");
    };
    let mut stats = VcpuStats::ZERO;
    stats.count_resumed(event, plan);
    stats
}

#[test]
fn exits_are_numbered_from_one() {
    let mut stats = VcpuStats::ZERO;
    assert_eq!([stats.count_exit(), stats.count_exit()], [1, 2]);
    assert_eq!(stats.exits, 2);
}

#[test]
fn each_emulated_instruction_has_its_own_counter() {
    let emulated = |emulation| after(ExitEvent::Emulated(emulation));
    let port = 0x3FF;
    let size = IoSize::Byte;
    let def_type = MtrrCapabilities::new(8, 46).unwrap().msr(0x2FF).unwrap();
    for (stats, counter) in [
        (emulated(Emulation::Cpuid { leaf: 1, subleaf: 0 }), "cpuid_exits"),
        (emulated(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr: 0xC000_0102 }), "msr_read_exits"),
        (
            emulated(Emulation::Wrmsr {
                msr: 0xC000_0102,
                value: 0,
            }),
            "msr_write_exits",
        ),
        (emulated(Emulation::MtrrRead { msr: def_type }), "mtrr_read_exits"),
        (
            emulated(Emulation::MtrrWrite {
                msr: def_type,
                value: 0xC06,
            }),
            "mtrr_write_exits",
        ),
        (emulated(Emulation::In { port, size }), "io_in_exits"),
        (emulated(Emulation::Out { port, size, value: 0 }), "io_out_exits"),
        (after(ExitEvent::Halted), "halt_exits"),
        (after(ExitEvent::NmiInjected), "nmi_injections"),
        (after(ExitEvent::NmiWindowInjected), "nmi_injections"),
        (after(ExitEvent::GuestGeneralProtection), "exception_injections"),
        (after(ExitEvent::GuestInvalidOpcode), "exception_injections"),
    ] {
        // Exactly that counter is 1, and no other.
        let line = stats.to_string();
        let ones: Vec<&str> = line.split(' ').filter(|field| field.ends_with("=1")).collect();
        assert_eq!(ones, [format!("{counter}=1")], "{line}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn exits_that_do_nothing_for_the_guest_count_nothing_more() {
    for event in [
        ExitEvent::MainVmcall,
        ExitEvent::GuestNmiHandler,
        ExitEvent::NmiDeferred,
        ExitEvent::EptWriteGranted,
    ] {
        assert_eq!(after(event), VcpuStats::ZERO, "{event:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn stats_print_as_one_line_of_named_counters() {
    let stats = VcpuStats {
        exits: 13,
        cpuid_exits: 1,
        msr_read_exits: 2,
        msr_write_exits: 2,
        io_in_exits: 2,
        io_out_exits: 2,
        halt_exits: 1,
        ..VcpuStats::ZERO
    };
    assert_eq!(
        stats.to_string(),
        "exits=13 cpuid_exits=1 msr_read_exits=2 msr_write_exits=2 mtrr_read_exits=0 mtrr_write_exits=0 \
         io_in_exits=2 io_out_exits=2 halt_exits=1 nmi_injections=0 exception_injections=0 \
         hypercall_exits=0 synthetic_read_exits=0 synthetic_write_exits=0"
    );
}

#[test]
fn forwarded_accesses_count_by_call_code_and_msr() {
    let mut stats = VcpuStats::ZERO;
    let mut forwarded = Forwarded::NONE;
    for emulation in [
        // HvCallPostMessage twice, once fast with a rep count; HvCallSignalEvent.
        Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5C },
        Emulation::Hypercall {
            input: 0x0000_0002_0001_005C,
        },
        Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5D },
        Emulation::SyntheticRead { msr: 0x4000_0020 },
        Emulation::SyntheticRead { msr: 0x4000_0020 },
        Emulation::SyntheticWrite {
            msr: 0x4000_0001,
            value: 0x7FF2_0001,
        },
    ] {
        let event = ExitEvent::Emulated(emulation);
        let ExitAction::Resume(plan) = event.action() else {
            panic!("{event:?} does not resume");
        };
        stats.count_resumed(event, plan);
        forwarded.count(plan.emulate);
    }
    assert_eq!(
        (
            stats.hypercall_exits,
            stats.synthetic_read_exits,
            stats.synthetic_write_exits
        ),
        (3, 2, 1)
    );
    assert_eq!(forwarded.hypercalls.counts(), [(0x5C, 2), (0x5D, 1)]);
    assert_eq!(forwarded.synthetic_reads.to_string(), "0x40000020=2");
    assert_eq!(forwarded.synthetic_writes.to_string(), "0x40000001=1");
}

#[test]
fn nothing_else_is_forwarded() {
    let mut forwarded = Forwarded::NONE;
    for emulate in [
        None,
        Some(Emulation::Cpuid {
            leaf: 0x4000_0000,
            subleaf: 0,
        }),
        Some(Emulation::Rdmsr { msr: 0xC000_0102 }),
    ] {
        forwarded.count(emulate);
    }
    assert_eq!(forwarded, Forwarded::NONE);
}

#[test]
fn a_refused_forward_counts_the_access_and_the_exception() {
    // The plan `prepare_resume` carries out when Hyper-V refuses a hypercall.
    let emulation = Emulation::Hypercall { input: 0x5C };
    let plan = ResumePlan {
        advance_rip: false,
        emulate: Some(emulation),
        ..ResumePlan::INJECT_UD
    };
    let mut stats = VcpuStats::ZERO;
    stats.count_resumed(ExitEvent::Emulated(emulation), plan);
    assert_eq!((stats.hypercall_exits, stats.exception_injections), (1, 1));
}

#[test]
fn a_tally_shares_one_counter_past_its_keys() {
    let mut tally = Tally::EMPTY;
    assert_eq!(tally.to_string(), "none");
    for key in 0..TALLY_KEYS as u32 + 2 {
        tally.count(key);
    }
    tally.count(0);
    assert_eq!(tally.counts().len(), TALLY_KEYS);
    assert_eq!(tally.counts()[0], (0, 2));
    assert_eq!(tally.other, 2);
    assert!(tally.to_string().ends_with(" 0x1f=1 other=2"), "{tally}");
}
```
